confirmed.title: render_pipe snapshot: the instanced-state table is fixed at 128 slots and never grows, so the 129th distinct instanced pose in one packet spins forever on the main thread
confirmed.bug_class: unbounded open-addressing probe on a full table (hang)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: CONFIRMED (harness test of the class copied verbatim). BuildSnapshot runs `b.stateTable.Reset(64);` (line 496). PointerTable::Reset sizes the table to the first power of two >= 2*expected (128) and only grows in Reset. AdmitMesh then inserts one key per distinct live InstancedAnimationState: `int32_t s = b.stateTable.Find(live, stateIndex);` (line 256). Nothing bounds the count by 128. Find's loop `for (;;) { Slot& s = _slots[i]; if (s.gen != _gen) {...return -1;} if (s.key == key) return s.index; i = (i + 1) & mask; }` (146-158) has no exit when every slot holds the current generation and the key is absent. A state is one (AnimationManager::Instance, clip frame) pair: `_instances._data[(handle >> 8) & 0xff]._states._data[handle & 0xff]` (199-200), with one AnimationState per clip frame. Every single-layer animation is instanced (AnimationState::Update sets `_instanced = true` when layerCount == 1 && handle >= 0). Citizens and animals walking, carrying and working at different phases of 30+-frame clips across several skeletons easily reach more than 128 distinct (clip, frame) states among the drawn and shadow-pass items of one frame. Harness output: capacity 128, 128 of 129 inserted after 2 s, 129th never returns.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit: call BuildSnapshot (or PointerTable directly) on a Renderer whose items reference 129 MeshInstances with distinct instanced handles; it never returns. Live: ext.render_pipe on a >=3-core machine with the overlap governor engaged (Android P13 or a heavy emit), a mid-size town with many citizens or animals walking on screen; the main thread hangs in BuildSnapshot and the watchdog writes standalone_hang.log. Fix: grow stateTable on insert (or Reset it with the number of instanced items as the bound, as `geometries` uses itemCount).

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: hang (main thread, ext.render_pipe ON with the overlap snapshot engaged)
verdict.proof:
Read on origin/main (<worktree>, last touched by ddd862312). Not in the review_20261103 ledger: grep for stateTable / PointerTable there finds nothing.

1. Capacity is always 128. BuildSnapshot calls `b.stateTable.Reset(64);` (snapshot.cpp:496) with a constant. In PointerTable::Reset (128-139), want=64, and `while (want < expected*2) want *= 2;` gives 128. Slots are only (re)assigned in Reset, and only when they need to grow, so the table never has more than 128 slots. Find never grows it.

2. A full table loops forever. Find (143-158) stops only when it reaches a slot with gen != _gen (absent) or a slot whose key matches. Once all 128 slots hold the current generation, a key that is not in the table steps `i = (i+1) & mask` forever. There is no probe-count bound.

3. Nothing caps inserts at 128. AdmitMesh (253-266) inserts one key per distinct live InstancedAnimationState, i.e. `&_instances[(h>>8)&0xff]._states[h&0xff]`. In AnimationManager (animationstate_transforms.cpp:930-1000) there is one Instance per (AnimationGroup, clip), and each holds `clip._instanceCount` baked states. The number of distinct states is therefore the sum of the (clip, baked frame) pairs in use. Nothing limits that to 128. The only per-packet bound, itemCount, sizes `geometries` (Reset(itemCount+16)), not `stateTable`. No refusal path in pass A counts states.

4. The path can be reached. render_pipe.cpp:549-556: MainHalf calls Freeze, and Freeze calls BuildSnapshot whenever the governor sets next.snapshot. Every single-layer animation with a handle is instanced (wave27_lane_gfxbig.cpp:763-766). With enough citizens and animals on screen at different phases of different clips, the frame needs 129 or more distinct states. The 129th new state then spins in Find, on the main thread, inside BuildSnapshot.

Not shown by a run: the state count a real town reaches. The defect (a fixed 128-slot table with an unbounded probe) can be checked line by line, and the finder reports a harness test of the class copied verbatim that hangs on insert 129. This only affects ext.render_pipe, which is default OFF, so faithful behaviour is untouched.
verdict.minimal_fix: In BuildSnapshot, size the state table by the same bound as the geometry table. The number of distinct states cannot exceed the number of admitted meshes, which pass A bounds by itemCount plus the followed meshes of EdgeMeshInstances. So `b.stateTable.Reset(64);` becomes `b.stateTable.Reset(itemCount + 16);`. Load stays at 0.5 or below, and Find always meets an empty slot. Optionally add a probe-count guard that refuses the snapshot (result.refused = "state table full") instead of spinning.

confirmed.title: render_pipe snapshot re-points the WorldGeometry's chunk/water/run/strip items at the arena copy, against its own design; better_water then allocates a strip slot (with GPU buffers) per arena address until all 4 are taken, and never frees them
confirmed.bug_class: dangling/aliased pointer into a reusable arena; per-address side table never freed (C1 / C13)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (code reading). Pass A admits the WorldGeometry only from decal/road items and skips its other modes: `if (mode != kModeDecal && mode != kModeRoad) continue;   // the live object (2.2)` (519). Pass C re-points EVERY item whose geometry is in the table, with no mode test: `const int32_t index = b.geometries.Find(item._geometry, -1); if (index >= 0) item._geometry = b.entries[...].copy;` (565-566). So whenever a decal or road is drawn, the terrain chunk, water, contour, ext.terrain_batch run and ext.better_water strip items of the same WorldGeometry draw from the arena copy. P13_OVERLAP.md 2.2 says these modes are 'not copied: the live object' because a copied embedded VertexBuffer 'would be bound by pointer, cached by the Context across frames and could alias a later arena object'. That is exactly what happens: WorldGeometry::Draw binds `&_waterVertexBuffer` / `&_waterIndexBuffer` / `&_vertexBuffer` of `this` (geometry_draw.cpp:444-445), and arena.storage.reset() frees those addresses when the arena grows. Concrete fallout in ext code that keys on the geometry's address: Ext::BetterWater::StripFor(copy) does not find `&copy` in FindStrip, takes a free slot (`s->owner = &geo;`, better_water.cpp:248), builds the strip and uploads a new VertexBuffer + IndexBuffer. The copy's address changes with the slot (two arenas) and with its admission offset, so after 4 distinct addresses every StripSlot is owned by an arena address. Forget(live) in ~WorldGeometry never matches those slots: their buffers leak, and the strip disappears for the live geometry too (StripFor returns null), for the rest of the process, later worlds included. Ext::TerrainBatch::DrawRun(copy) misses FindReady (owner is the live geometry) and silently falls back to the per-chunk draw. The RenderPipeCopy shadow does not see it: HashFrame(ownPointers=false) leaves the geometry pointer out.
confirmed.repro_idea: ext.render_pipe (threaded, overlap governor on) + ext.better_water mode >= 2 in a map with a river and roads on screen: stderr shows '[BetterWater] strip built' lines repeating, with a new slot per frame address, then the shore strip vanishes. Unit: BuildSnapshot on a Renderer holding one road item and one water item of the same WorldGeometry; assert the water item still points at the live object (it points at the copy). Fix: in pass C, re-point a WorldGeometry item only when its key mode is 0x2000 / 0x4000.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: resource (GPU buffer leak plus the shore strip vanishing); ext only: needs ext.render_pipe on, and ext.better_water Fancy for the strip consequence. Faithful profile unaffected.
verdict.proof:
Static reasoning on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>); each step can be checked line by line.
1) WorldGeometry::AddDrawItems (src/game/Game/geometry_draw.cpp:268, 287, 296, 305, 328, 352) passes the same `this` for every item: terrain chunks, contour ranges 0x6000/0x8000, the better_water strip (kStripDrawKey = 0x6000|0x1fff), decals 0x2000 and roads 0x4000.
2) Pass A (snapshot.cpp:516-528) admits the WorldGeometry only from a decal or road item (`if (mode != kModeDecal && mode != kModeRoad) continue;`). Admit (snapshot.cpp:331-332) then inserts the live pointer into b.geometries.
3) Pass C (snapshot.cpp:560-568) does `b.geometries.Find(item._geometry, -1)` with no mode test. Find with insert=-1 is a pure lookup that returns the stored index (lines 143-158). So every chunk, water, contour, terrain_batch run and strip item of that WorldGeometry is re-pointed at the arena copy as soon as one decal or road is drawn. That contradicts the file header (lines 19-22: "Its other modes keep the live object") and P13_OVERLAP.md 2.2, line 79 ("not copied: the live object").
4) WorldGeometry::Draw (geometry_draw.cpp:441-445, 513-518) then binds &_waterVertexBuffer, &_waterIndexBuffer and &_vertexBuffer of the copy, which are memcpy'd embedded objects inside arena storage that arena.storage.reset() frees on growth (snapshot.cpp:541-545). For the 0x6000/0x1fff item it calls Ext::BetterWater::DrawStrip(*this = copy).
5) better_water.cpp:234-249 StripFor(copy): FindStrip compares owner == &geo, misses, takes a free slot and sets owner = &copy. UploadStrip then allocates a new VertexBuffer and IndexBuffer (lines 206-216). The copy's address is arena base + entry offset. It differs between the two alternating arenas (g_arenas[slot&1]) and after every arena regrowth, and the offset moves with admission order. So slots fill up with arena addresses. Forget(live) (lines 438-447), called from ~WorldGeometry, matches only &live, so those slots are never freed: their buffers leak for the process lifetime. Once all 4 slots hold stale arena owners, StripFor returns null (line 246) and the strip is no longer drawn for any geometry, later worlds included.
6) Ext::TerrainBatch::DrawRun(copy) likewise misses FindReady (terrain_batch.cpp:65-67, owner is the live geometry) and silently falls back.
Nothing in src/ext/render_pipe special-cases BetterWater or TerrainBatch (grep finds no reference).
Not in the ledger: README F-001..F-217 / S-001, findings_p3p4.json and findings_p8.json hold no snapshot pass-C or WorldGeometry re-point entry. The only snapshot.cpp items are P0_MAP's DeepCopy cursor pattern and the SunLight / max_shadow_res finding, both different defects.
The headline defect (pass C re-points modes the design keeps live) is airtight by reading. How fast the 4 slots run out depends on how many distinct copy addresses occur at run time, but the two alternating arenas alone already create 2 owner slots that are never freed.
verdict.minimal_fix: In pass C (src/ext/render_pipe/snapshot.cpp:565), re-point a WorldGeometry item only when its key mode is decal or road. For example: `if (index >= 0) { if (typeid(*item._geometry) == typeid(WorldGeometry)) { const uint32_t mode = item._arg5 & kModeMask; if (mode != kModeDecal && mode != kModeRoad) continue; } item._geometry = b.entries[index].copy; }` (formatted one statement per line). This keeps the chunk, water, contour, terrain_batch run and better_water strip items on the live object, as P13_OVERLAP 2.2 specifies. A unit test: BuildSnapshot on a Renderer holding one road item and one water item of the same WorldGeometry asserts that the water item still points at the live object.

confirmed.title: sharp_ui: the art is matched by SpriteInfo width/height but placed into the UV-derived rectangle, so a sheet whose UV span differs from its width/height reads past the art's RGBA buffer
confirmed.bug_class: out-of-bounds read (size check on one rectangle, copy over another)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (code reading; the input is a modded or malformed Dialog/SpriteSheet.rsc). StartJob builds each sprite's rectangle from its UVs: `job->sprites[i].rect = RectFromUvs(s.u0, s.v0, s.u1, s.v1, w, h);`. It picks the art by the record's own size: `FindArt(table, tableCount, s.name._data, s.width, s.height, factor)` (318-319). FindArt checks only `table[i].width == baseW * scale && table[i].height == baseH * scale` against s.width / s.height (sharp_sheet.cpp:140). BuildScaledSheet then calls PlaceArt(out, w, h, ScaleRect(sprites[i].rect, scale), art, ...) (sharp_sheet.cpp:209). PlaceArt indexes the art by the RECT's size: `ay = Clamp(y - r.y, 0, r.height - 1); ax = Clamp(x - r.x, 0, r.width - 1); s = rgba + (ay * r.width + ax) * 4;` (sharp_sheet.cpp:184-187). When the UV rectangle is wider or taller than width x height (RectFromUvs also does not clip x + width to the sheet), the read runs up to (rect.w*rect.h - art.w*art.h)*4 bytes past the baked static array: the next sprite's pixels, or past the end of kSprites/kExtSprites for the last one. Writes stay in bounds (PadRect clips), and UpscaleRect is safe because its rectangle goes through PadRect against the base sheet.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit (tests/unit/ext_sharp_sheet_test.cpp style): BuildScaledSheet with one ScaledSprite whose rect is 6x6 and whose art points at a 4x4*scale RGBA buffer under ASan: heap/global-buffer-overflow in PlaceArt. Live: a UI mod replacing Dialog/SpriteSheet.rsc whose sprite named like one of ours (e.g. a menu button) keeps the retail width/height but has UVs one texel larger, at sharp_ui 'Text + icons' 2x/4x. Fix: in StartJob, use the art only when RectFromUvs' width/height equal s.width/s.height (or pass the art's size to PlaceArt and clamp to it).

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: memory (global-buffer over-read, ext.sharp_ui on + modded/malformed Dialog or Extensions SpriteSheet.rsc)
verdict.proof:
The over-read is real, and it is not already recorded or fixed. Each step below can be checked line by line against origin/main (<worktree>). The line numbers in the finding are off: the code is at sharp_scaled.cpp:247-249, not 318.

1. src/ext/sharp_ui/sharp_scaled.cpp:247 sets `rect = RectFromUvs(s.u0, s.v0, s.u1, s.v1, w, h)`. The size comes from the UVs only: width = lround(u1*W) - lround(u0*W), clamped to [0, W] (sharp_sheet.cpp:23-28).
2. sharp_scaled.cpp:248 calls `FindArt(table, tableCount, s.name._data, s.width, s.height, factor)`. That function (sharp_sheet.cpp:43-52) returns the art only when `table[i].width == s.width*factor && table[i].height == s.height*factor`. So the art's RGBA buffer holds exactly s.width*s.height*factor^2*4 bytes. The UV rectangle is never compared with s.width / s.height.
3. BuildScaledSheet (sharp_sheet.cpp:117) calls `PlaceArt(out, w, h, ScaleRect(rect, scale), art, pad*scale)`. Here r.width = rectW*f and r.height = rectH*f.
4. PlaceArt (sharp_sheet.cpp:89-103) reads `rgba + (ay*r.width + ax)*4`, with ay clamped to [0, r.height-1] and ax clamped to [0, r.width-1]. The PadRect pad only re-clamps to the edge, so every (ax, ay) inside the rectangle is visited. The largest byte offset read is (rectW*rectH*f^2 - 1)*4 + 3. That is past the art buffer whenever rectW*rectH > s.width*s.height.
5. Nothing on the input side ties the two fields together. SpriteInfo's u0/v0/u1/v1 and width/height are separate serialized fields (src/engine/ui/spritesheet_vtable.cpp:382 reads the floats directly), with no check that they agree. A mod's Dialog/SpriteSheet.rsc that keeps one of our sprite names and its retail width/height but has a larger UV span therefore makes the worker thread read past a baked static array (the next sprite's pixels, or past the end of the table).
6. The writes stay in bounds: PadRect clips them to dstW x dstH, and UpscaleRect clips against the base sheet. Only the read is out of bounds, as the finding says.

Ledger: grep for PlaceArt / FindArt / RectFromUvs / sharp_sheet in docs/history/review_20261103 finds nothing. The only sharp_ui hits in findings_p8.json are font-raster findings, which are a different defect.

Off-switch: the code runs only when ext.sharp_ui is on at 2x or 4x, so faithful play is unaffected.

Build proof is cheap if wanted: a unit test calling BuildScaledSheet with a 6x6 rect, scale 2, and art sized 4x4x2x2x4 bytes, run under ASan, should report a global/heap-buffer-overflow in PlaceArt.
verdict.minimal_fix: In StartJob (src/ext/sharp_ui/sharp_scaled.cpp:248), use the art only when the UV rectangle matches the record's size: compute the rect first, then call FindArt only if `rect.width == s.width && rect.height == s.height`; otherwise leave art = nullptr so the sprite is just upscaled. Plain hardening against hostile input, with a comment saying a sheet whose UVs disagree with its width/height gets no art. Add a unit test in tests/unit/ext_sharp_sheet_test.cpp for the mismatched case.

confirmed.title: ext.sharp_ui PlaceArt reads our art with the UV-derived rectangle's stride and size, but FindArt matched the art by the record's width/height: heap/global buffer over-read
confirmed.bug_class: out-of-bounds read (size checked against a different field than the one used)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: FindArt (line 48) accepts art when `table[i].width != baseW * scale || table[i].height != baseH * scale` is false, with baseW/baseH = SpriteInfo::width/height (sharp_scaled.cpp:535 passes s.width, s.height). The rectangle PlaceArt walks comes from the UVs instead: StartJob sets `rect = RectFromUvs(s.u0, s.v0, s.u1, s.v1, w, h)` (sharp_scaled.cpp:534), and BuildScaledSheet calls `PlaceArt(out.data(), w, h, ScaleRect(sprites[i].rect, scale), sprites[i].art, pad * scale)`. PlaceArt then reads `rgba + (ay * r.width + ax) * 4` for ay < r.height, ax < r.width (line 97). Nothing checks that the UV extent equals the record's width/height, so a modded Dialog/SpriteSheet.rsc (or Extensions sheet) with a sprite named like one of ours, whose UV rectangle is larger than its width/height fields, reads past the end of the baked art array (static data in sharp_sprites_data_{2x,4x}.h). RectFromUvs also clamps x and width independently (x + width can reach 2 x sheetW). CONFIRMED: ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ at sharp_sheet.cpp:97 in sheet_poc mode 2 (art 16x16 as FindArt accepts it for an 8x8 record at 2x; UVs give a 16x16 base rect, so 32x32 is read).
confirmed.repro_idea: sheet_poc.cpp mode 2. In game: a mod Dialog/SpriteSheet.rsc whose sprite "<a name in kSprites>" has width/height W x H but u1-u0 > W/sheetW; run with ext.sharp_ui on at Text + icons and the UI scale at 75% (2x copy). Minimal fix: in StartJob, give a sprite art only when rect.width == s.width && rect.height == s.height (or pass the rect's size to FindArt).

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: memory (OOB read of static art data; only with ext.sharp_ui on and a modded sprite sheet)
verdict.proof:
The finding holds by static reasoning on origin/main fa150cf7f. Nothing upstream touches src/ext/sharp_ui, and no ledger entry mentions PlaceArt, FindArt or sharp_sheet. The only sharp-related entries in findings_p8 are font_raster items.
The proof, line by line:
(1) sharp_sheet.h:35-41 and the generated sharp_sprites_data_2x.h: ArtSprite::rgba is exactly width*height*4 bytes. Example: kRgba_0_GoalFail[4096] is 32x32x4.
(2) sharp_scaled.cpp:247-248 (StartJob): rect = RectFromUvs(s.u0,s.v0,s.u1,s.v1,w,h), but art = FindArt(table,n,name,s.width,s.height,factor). FindArt (sharp_sheet.cpp:48) only checks table.width == s.width*scale and table.height == s.height*scale. So the art buffer is (s.width*scale)*(s.height*scale)*4 bytes.
(3) BuildScaledSheet (sharp_sheet.cpp:117) passes ScaleRect(rect, scale) to PlaceArt. Its width and height are (lround(u1*w)-lround(u0*w))*scale and the same for v, up to sheetW*scale. They come only from the UVs, and nothing ties them to s.width or s.height.
(4) PlaceArt (sharp_sheet.cpp:92-95) reads rgba + (ay*r.width + ax)*4 with ay up to r.height-1 and ax up to r.width-1.
So if the UV extent exceeds width/height, the highest offset read, (r.height*r.width-1)*4, is past the end of the art array. A modded Dialog/SpriteSheet.rsc (or Extensions sheet) controls the UVs and width/height of each SpriteInfo separately. A record named like one of ours, with a correct width/height and larger UVs, reaches this read when ext.sharp_ui is on.
If the UV extent is smaller, the read stays in bounds but uses the wrong stride, so the art is drawn skewed: a logic defect, not memory.
Faithful behaviour is not affected: this is ext-only code (ext.sharp_ui is off by default). The sheet_poc ASan report was not reproduced here. The static chain above does not depend on it.
verdict.minimal_fix: In StartJob (src/ext/sharp_ui/sharp_scaled.cpp:247-249), give a sprite art only when the UV rectangle matches the record: after computing rect, set art = (rect.width == s.width && rect.height == s.height) ? FindArt(...) : nullptr. An alternative is to pass rect.width/rect.height to FindArt instead of s.width/s.height. Add a unit case to tests/unit/ext_sharp_sheet_test.cpp: an 8x8 record whose UVs span 16x16 gets no art.

confirmed.title: ext.sharp_ui FindArt: `baseW * scale` signed int overflow on a sprite record's width/height from the sheet file
confirmed.bug_class: signed integer overflow
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: `if (table[i].width != baseW * scale || table[i].height != baseH * scale) return nullptr;` where baseW/baseH are SpriteInfo::width/height read from the loaded sprite sheet (sharp_scaled.cpp:535) and scale is 2 or 4. A record width >= 2^29 (scale 4) or 2^30 (scale 2) with a name in our art table overflows int. CONFIRMED: UBSan `signed integer overflow: 1073741824 * 2 cannot be represented in type 'int'` at sharp_sheet.cpp:48 (sheet_poc mode 0).
confirmed.repro_idea: sheet_poc.cpp mode 0: FindArt(table, 1, "Button", 0x40000000, 1, 2). Fix: compare in int64 (`static_cast<int64_t>(baseW) * scale`), with a NOT RETAIL comment.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (low: hostile/corrupt sprite-sheet resource with ext.sharp_ui on)
verdict.proof: Static reasoning, checkable line by line in <worktree> (origin/main, code added in e0dfb6569 / #155 and not changed since). (1) src/engine/ui/spritesheet_vtable.cpp:376-377 serializes SpriteInfo::width / height (int32_t at +0x1c / +0x20, SpriteHeader SpriteSheet.h:115-116) straight from the resource stream with no range check. (2) src/ext/sharp_ui/sharp_scaled.cpp:243-248 (StartJob) passes s.width, s.height for every record of the loaded sheet, with factor taken from ArtFor (2 or 4), into FindArt. (3) src/ext/sharp_ui/sharp_sheet.cpp:48: after strcmp matches the name against our art table, it evaluates `baseW * scale` / `baseH * scale` in plain int. With width >= 0x40000000 and scale 2 (or >= 0x20000000 and scale 4, or a large negative value) the product cannot be represented in int, which is signed overflow UB. Nothing between the deserialize and the multiply bounds the value. Reaching it needs a sheet record whose name matches an art-table entry, for example a mod that overrides the dialog / extensions sheet, and ext.sharp_ui switched on. Faithful behaviour is not affected because the code is NOT RETAIL ext code. Ledger check: there is no row for sharp_sheet.cpp, FindArt or baseW in README.md, P0_MAP.md, findings_p3p4.json or findings_p8.json. The only sharp_ui rows in findings_p8 are about LoadPrivateFace in the font rasteriser, so this is not a duplicate. The finder's UBSan PoC (sheet_poc mode 0) is not in the tree and was not re-run here, but the static chain needs no runtime proof.
verdict.minimal_fix: In FindArt, compare in 64 bits: `if (table[i].width != static_cast<int64_t>(baseW) * scale || table[i].height != static_cast<int64_t>(baseH) * scale) return nullptr;` and add a comment saying the sheet record's width / height come unbounded from the resource. The file is already NOT RETAIL, so plain hardening is enough. Add a unit test in tests/unit with FindArt(table, 1, name, 0x40000000, 1, 2) returning nullptr.

confirmed.title: ext.sharp_ui RectFromUvs: `x1 - x0` / `y1 - y0` signed overflow for out-of-range UVs (and lround of NaN/inf)
confirmed.bug_class: signed integer overflow / out-of-range lround
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: `const int x0 = static_cast<int>(std::lround(u0 * sheetW)); ... const int x1 = ...; return SheetRect{Clamp(x0,0,sheetW), ..., Clamp(x1 - x0, 0, sheetW), Clamp(y1 - y0, 0, sheetH)};` (the header line is 115 in the concatenated read; the subtraction is at line 28 of the file). The UVs are SpriteInfo::u0..v1 from the sheet file, and the difference is taken before clamping. CONFIRMED: UBSan `signed integer overflow: 2000000000 - -2000000000 cannot be represented in type 'int'` at sharp_sheet.cpp:28:75 (sheet_poc mode 3, u0 = -1953125, u1 = 1953125 on a 1024 sheet). On Windows, where long is 32-bit, lround(NaN / +-inf / |u*W| > 2^31) also returns LONG_MIN, and `0 - INT_MIN` overflows the same way.
confirmed.repro_idea: sheet_poc.cpp mode 3. Fix: clamp x0/x1/y0/y1 to [0, sheet] before subtracting (or reject non-finite UVs): the width then stays within the sheet, which also bounds the PlaceArt rectangle.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (low: needs a hostile or corrupt sprite sheet, with ext.sharp_ui on)
verdict.proof:
Checked against <worktree>/src/ext/sharp_ui/sharp_sheet.cpp:23-29 on origin/main. The function computes `x0/y0/x1/y1 = static_cast<int>(std::lround(u * sheetW))`, then returns `SheetRect{Clamp(x0,0,W), Clamp(y0,0,H), Clamp(x1 - x0, 0, W), Clamp(y1 - y0, 0, H)}`. The int subtraction runs on the unclamped values before Clamp, so x0 = -2e9 and x1 = 2e9 overflow int, which is UB. There is also a second route. On Windows long is 32-bit, and lround of NaN, +-inf or anything past 2^31 has an unspecified result (in practice LONG_MIN = INT_MIN), so `0 - INT_MIN` overflows too.

The bad values can reach this code. Its only caller is sharp_scaled.cpp:247, which passes UI::SpriteInfo u0..v1 straight through. Those values are deserialized raw from the sprite sheet resource at spritesheet_vtable.cpp:380-382 (`ser->Serialize(e->u0 / e->u1 ...)`), and no load path validates or clamps them. A mod's .rsc sheet is part of the input surface, and the path is live only when ext.sharp_ui is on. The function is NOT RETAIL, so retail has nothing to diff against.

The finding also cites a UBSan report from sheet_poc mode 3: `signed integer overflow: 2000000000 - -2000000000` at sharp_sheet.cpp:28:75. That matches the code exactly. It is not a duplicate: the ledger (docs/history/review_20261103 *.md and the findings JSON) only has sharp_ui font-raster rows, nothing on RectFromUvs, lround or this subtraction. PadRect at lines 35-40 is not affected, because it subtracts values that are already clamped.
verdict.minimal_fix: In RectFromUvs, clamp each corner to [0, sheetW] or [0, sheetH] before subtracting: `const int cx0 = Clamp(x0,0,sheetW); const int cx1 = Clamp(x1,0,sheetW);` and the same for y, then `width = cx1 > cx0 ? cx1 - cx0 : 0`. For a NaN, inf or out-of-range UV, either clamp the float to [0,1] before lround or return an empty rect when `!std::isfinite`. Add a "NOT RETAIL:" note on the hardening and a unit test in tests/unit with u0=-1953125, u1=1953125 and a NaN UV on a 1024 sheet.

confirmed.title: ext.render_pipe: the window-owning main thread blocks in plain condition-variable waits while the render thread calls IDXGISwapChain::Present. In exclusive fullscreen, DXGI may send window messages synchronously from Present, so the frame can deadlock
confirmed.bug_class: wait without wakeup / cross-thread deadlock (DXGI sends window messages synchronously from a thread that does not own the window, while the owner thread is parked)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (static only). Render thread: src/render/dx11/render_pipe_finish.cpp:84 `HRESULT hr = dd->swapChain->Present(sync, 0);` runs inside EngineOps::Finish on ext.render_pipe's RenderThread. The HWND belongs to the main thread, which pumps it in MainLoop::Frame through Platform::Pump. While that Present runs, the main thread can be parked in Handoff::WaitIdle (handoff.h:129-134: `_idle.wait(lk, [this] { return !_busy.load(...); });`). It reaches that wait from the hand-off (pipe_driver.h:357 Join -> WaitIdle), from SettleTail (:330, the tail a RENDERPIPE_FENCE release left in flight is exactly EndCommands + Present) and from BeforeTransition. It can also be parked in WaitReleased (:138-142) or ClaimSteps (:103-108). None of these waits dispatch sent messages: they are std::condition_variable waits, not MsgWaitForMultipleObjects. Microsoft's DXGI guidance ('Multithread considerations') warns that in full-screen mode Present on a render thread may call SetWindowPos / SetWindowLong, which SendMessage to the window-owning thread, so a message-pump thread that waits on the render thread deadlocks. The authors flagged this as unproven in docs/extensions/handins/RENDERPIPE1.md section 10 item 4 ('If it hangs, the fix is a message-aware wait on the main thread'). docs/runtime_port/NEXT_SESSION.md still lists it as a by-hand leftover ('an alt-tab in exclusive fullscreen with ext.render_pipe on ... a hang reads exit 4'). It is not in the F-*/S-* ledger. S-010 is the opposite direction (a Resize run on the main thread from WM_ACTIVATE) and does not cover the main thread being parked.
confirmed.repro_idea: Windows, DX11, fullscreen=1 in settings.cfg (exclusive), ext.render_pipe on, >= 3 physical cores (the thread is up), a town busy enough that frames pipeline without stepping. Alt-tab out and back repeatedly, or switch the desktop resolution, during play. Expect exit 4 with standalone_hang.log showing the main thread in Handoff::WaitIdle and the render thread inside IDXGISwapChain::Present / NtUserSetWindowPos. A deterministic harness: on the render thread, call SetWindowPos on the main HWND inside Emit (standing in for DXGI's send) and confirm the hang. Fix direction: have the main thread wait with MsgWaitForMultipleObjects(QS_SENDMESSAGE) plus PeekMessage(PM_QS_SENDMESSAGE) in a Platform:: hook while the hand-off is busy.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: hang (exit 4), only with ext.render_pipe on, the render thread running, DX11 exclusive fullscreen
verdict.proof:
The code reading holds, but whether the hang can happen is unproven, so the finding cannot be confirmed or refuted from the source alone.

What holds: in <worktree>/src/ext/render_pipe/handoff.h, WaitIdle (:129-134), WaitReleased (:138-142) and ClaimSteps (:103-108) are plain std::condition_variable waits. None of them dispatches sent messages. The swap chain's Present runs on the render thread inside Emit/Finish (render_pipe_finish.cpp). The HWND belongs to the main thread, which only pumps in Platform::Pump. So the main thread does not pump while it is parked in one of these waits.

What is open: the hang needs DXGI to SendMessage to the window from inside Present during an exclusive-fullscreen transition. The port mirrors retail's factory->MakeWindowAssociation(hwnd, DXGI_MWA_NO_WINDOW_CHANGES) (devicedata.cpp:1272). That flag stops DXGI watching the message queue, so it lowers the odds of a send from Present. It does not provably remove them: an occlusion or mode loss can still reach SetWindowPos / SetWindowLong inside DXGI. Only a run can settle this: alt-tab in DX11 fullscreen=1 with the row on, or the proposed harness that calls SetWindowPos on the main HWND from Emit.

Not a duplicate: S-010 (findings_p8.json:2566) is a data race from a Resize on the main thread in WM_ACTIVATE. The ForceVideoContextReset entry (findings_p8.json:~2410, main.cpp:652) is a race on the Context. F-158 is steps overlapping BeginCommands. None of these covers a main thread parked in a hand-off wait while DXGI sends to it. The risk is already written up as an open by-hand test, not as a ledger row: docs/extensions/handins/RENDERPIPE1.md section 10 item 4 and docs/runtime_port/NEXT_SESSION.md:158.

No retail comparison applies: retail has no render thread.
verdict.minimal_fix: If a run shows the hang, follow the handin's own direction: while the hand-off is busy, the main thread waits through a Platform:: hook. On Windows that hook loops on MsgWaitForMultipleObjects(QS_SENDMESSAGE) plus PeekMessage(PM_QS_SENDMESSAGE | PM_NOREMOVE), so it dispatches only sent messages. The posix and darwin twins keep the plain cv wait. The emit stays unchanged.

proof_run.proof:
The deadlock mechanism is confirmed by a failing Windows unit test. The DXGI trigger is not reproduced.

**Test.** tests/unit/review_render_pipe_sent_message_test.cpp, built in worktree <worktree> on base fa150cf7f with `tools/build.sh unit debug --jobs 2`, run with `unit.exe --filter review_render_pipe`. It uses the real `Ext::RenderPipe::Handoff` from src/ext/render_pipe/handoff.h. The test thread owns a hidden WS_POPUP HWND that is never shown, as the main thread owns the game window. A job on a std::thread sends to that HWND, standing in for DXGI's SetWindowPos / SetWindowLong inside Present.

1. `review_render_pipe_waitidle_services_sent_messages`: main parks in `Handoff::WaitIdle`, the path of Join, SettleTail and BeforeTransition. The job calls `SetWindowPos(hwnd, ...)`. That call never returns. After 2 s a watchdog finds the job still inside SetWindowPos, records the hang and calls `Done()` to free main. Once main pumps with `PeekMessage(PM_QS_SENDMESSAGE)`, the pending WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING is dispatched and the job finishes. Output: `WaitIdle: hung=1 posChanging=1`, then `FAIL ... :121: !hung.load()`.
2. `review_render_pipe_waitreleased_services_sent_messages`: main parks in `Handoff::WaitReleased` (THE FENCE, FenceReleased). The job calls `SendMessageTimeoutW(hwnd, WM_APP+7, ..., 2000 ms)`, which times out. Output: `WaitReleased: send ok=0 err=1460 result=0` (1460 is ERROR_TIMEOUT), then `FAIL :149 ok != 0` and `FAIL :150 err != ERROR_TIMEOUT`.
3. Control `review_render_pipe_message_aware_wait_control`: the same SendMessageTimeoutW plus SetWindowPos, with main waiting through MsgWaitForMultipleObjects(QS_SENDMESSAGE) plus PeekMessageW(PM_NOREMOVE | PM_QS_SENDMESSAGE) while `Busy()`. It passes: `send ok=1 result=42 in 2-16 ms`.

Full unit suite: 2002 tests, 3 failures. All 3 are these CHECKs; nothing else broke.

**What this proves.** The hand-off waits are std::condition_variable waits and never dispatch sent messages. A cross-thread send from the render thread to the main HWND therefore blocks for as long as main is parked. In the game that means WaitIdle never returns and the watchdog reads exit 4. ClaimSteps uses the same `_idle` cv wait, so it has the same property; it is not tested separately.

**What is not proven.** That IDXGISwapChain::Present (or EndCommands) on the render thread actually sends to the window in DX11 exclusive fullscreen. That premise comes from Microsoft's DXGI multithreading guidance. It is not observed here, and the port's MakeWindowAssociation(DXGI_MWA_NO_WINDOW_CHANGES) may make it rarer. An alt-tab run in exclusive fullscreen was not done: it switches the user's display mode and takes focus. That run remains the by-hand test listed in RENDERPIPE1.md §10 item 4 and NEXT_SESSION.md.

**History in the tree.** The same class of deadlock has happened before through a different sender. SunLight.h:183-207 and optionsdialog.cpp:1004-1006 record FAA-MENU, where a render-thread DeviceData_Resize (AdjustDisplay SetWindowPos) deadlocked render_pipe twice. Today's code avoids that path: settingsChanged frames run sequentially, and the fence or ClaimSteps waits for BeginCommands before the pump can raise it. The Present tail is the remaining unguarded sender.

**Artefacts.** In scratchpad/phase2/proofs/render-pipe-sent-msg/: the test file (review_render_pipe_sent_message_test.cpp) and the run output (unit_run.log). The full build log is scratchpad/sentmsg_build.log.
proof_run.minimal_fix: Add a Platform:: hook declared in src/platform/common/ (for example `Platform::WaitDispatchingSent(pred)`). It is used by Handoff::WaitIdle, WaitReleased and ClaimSteps on the main thread. On Windows (src/platform/win/) it loops while the predicate is false: MsgWaitForMultipleObjects(0, nullptr, FALSE, 1, QS_SENDMESSAGE), then PeekMessageW(&m, nullptr, 0, 0, PM_NOREMOVE | PM_QS_SENDMESSAGE). That dispatches only sent (nonqueued) messages, never posted input, so SDL's queue order is untouched. It finishes with the existing locked cv check for the acquire. The posix and darwin twins keep the plain cv wait. The render-thread side and the emit are unchanged. Retail has no render thread, so the change sits only in ext.render_pipe's code paths, which run only with the row on; faithful behaviour stays byte-identical. Note the re-entrancy this opens: a sent message dispatched during the wait runs the SDL WndProc on main while the job is in flight, so it must not touch the render context. The SDL proc only queues events and WindowProc runs later from Platform::Pump, which keeps this safe. The control test (review_render_pipe_message_aware_wait_control) passes with this wait shape.

confirmed.title: With P13 overlap engaged, class-A Sync hooks write plain function-pointer seams (Renderer::_extDrawItemList, MaterialInstance::_extAfterSetup) on the main thread while the render thread's pass 2 reads them: a data race (UB) on non-atomic statics
confirmed.bug_class: data race on a non-atomic static seam pointer (write in a step, read on the render thread during overlapped pass 2)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (static only; no TSan run). Under P13_OVERLAP, Handoff::ClaimSteps lets the fixed steps run while the render thread is still in Pass2 (packet.h: Pass2 comes before Gate). The steps include the UI update, where the Extensions / Enhanced dialog applies a class-A toggle: SetAndRecord -> Sync. That Sync writes plain statics. draw_batch.cpp:476 `Graphics::Renderer::_extDrawItemList = want ? &ExtDrawItemList : nullptr;` is read in pass 2 at engine/graphics/batchc_gfx_leaves.cpp:696-697 `if (_extDrawItemList != nullptr) { _extDrawItemList(*this, context, ...); }`. blossom_draw.cpp:106 `Graphics::MaterialInstance::_extAfterSetup = on ? &AfterSetup : nullptr;` (from better_trees.cpp:69 Sync) is read at engine/graphics/wave21_lane_gfxbody.cpp:342-343 on every material Setup in pass 2. Neither pointer is std::atomic, so a concurrent unsynchronised write and read is UB. The compiler may also reload the pointer between the null test and the call: a toggle-off between the two loads would call through null. draw_gather.cpp:311-314 states the assumption this breaks: 'that toggle comes from the UI pump inside a step, so the render thread is idle and no pass 1 is running'. That held before RENDERPIPE_FENCE / P13_OVERLAP. With overlap, pass 2 can be running during that step. The backend halves of the same toggles are already mutex / atomic guarded (foliage_aa_stage.cpp, billboard_shadow_stage.cpp, smoke_vs_stage.cpp g_extDrawBatchVs), so only these engine seams are left unsynchronised.
confirmed.repro_idea: TSan (Linux, Vulkan, ext.render_pipe on): get the overlap governor on with a busy town (`[RenderPipe] overlap on` in stderr). Then toggle ext.draw_batch, or natural tree growth in the Enhanced tab, several times. TSan should report the write in DrawBatch::Sync / SyncBlossom against the read in Renderer::DrawItemList / MaterialInstance::Setup on the render thread. Minimal fix: make the two seams std::atomic with relaxed load/store (one load per call, kept in a local), or defer the Sync writes to the main half after the join, as is done for MeshInstance::_extInstancedState in Host::BeforePublish.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (data race on a non-atomic static function pointer; the practical effect is at worst one frame where the old or the new hook is used, but under the C++ memory model it is UB)
verdict.proof:
I could not refute this. The reading of the code holds line by line. It is not in the ledger: neither seam appears in README.md, P0_MAP.md, findings_p3p4.json or findings_p8.json. S-028 (SunLight::ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync during overlapped steps) is the same race shape on a different seam, so this is a sibling of S-028, not a duplicate of it. Nothing on origin/main fixes it.

The static chain:
1. The render thread can be in pass 2 while the steps run. In src/ext/render_pipe/pipe_driver.h:132-150, BeforeSteps calls Handoff::ClaimSteps when `_held.overlap` is set and returns without fencing. ClaimSteps (handoff.h:96-106) waits only for the emit's BeginCommands (`_begunUs != 0`), then sets `_gate=false`. packet.h:113-114 runs `ops.Pass2(p)` before `ops.Gate(p)`, so pass 2 runs beside the steps. The gate is reopened only in Tail (pipe_driver.h:185).
2. The steps can reach SetAndRecord. The Options dialog's Enhanced tab (src/ext/enhanced_tab/enhanced_tab.h) is applied from OptionsDialog::OnApply. That dialog is reachable in a game. better_trees.cpp:48 calls `SetAndRecord(row, on)`. registry_boot.cpp:299-304 SetAndRecord calls DrawBatch::Sync() and BetterTrees::Sync() unconditionally. BetterTrees::Sync calls SyncBlossom(p.naturalGrowth) (better_trees.cpp:69), which writes the plain static `Graphics::MaterialInstance::_extAfterSetup` (blossom_draw.cpp:106). DrawBatch::Sync writes the plain static `Graphics::Renderer::_extDrawItemList` (draw_batch.cpp:476) whenever ext.draw_batch changed.
3. The readers run on the render thread in pass 2: batchc_gfx_leaves.cpp:696-697 (Renderer::DrawItemList) and wave21_lane_gfxbody.cpp:342-343 (MaterialInstance::Setup). Neither static is std::atomic, and no lock covers them. The comment at draw_gather.cpp:311-314 assumes the toggle runs while "the render thread is idle". The overlap path in point 1 breaks that assumption.

Why this is not CONFIRMED: there is no TSan report. Statically I also cannot show that the overlap governor stays engaged while the in-game Options dialog is open. The game is paused then and the steps are short, so overlap_governor.h may switch the snapshot off. Reaching the race needs a TSan run on Linux/Vulkan with ext.render_pipe on and `[RenderPipe] overlap on` logged, then a toggle of natural tree growth or ext.draw_batch.
verdict.minimal_fix: The simplest fix follows MeshInstance::_extInstancedState: defer both seam writes to Host::BeforePublish or the Frame tail, where the render thread is joined. Sync would then only record the wanted state. The alternative is to declare `_extDrawItemList` and `_extAfterSetup` as std::atomic with relaxed store in Sync and relaxed load into a local at the read site. In both cases, also report the seam with S-028 as the same overlap-during-steps family.

proof_run.proof:
TSan (clang-19, WSL) reports a data race on the real code. The harness compiles three things unchanged from worktree fa150cf7f: Ext::RenderPipe::Driver and Handoff from src/ext/render_pipe/pipe_driver.h and handoff.h (the actual P13 overlap protocol), and src/ext/better_trees/blossom_draw.cpp, which holds the actual writer Ext::BetterTrees::SyncBlossom. That writer is the one SetAndRecord -> BetterTrees::Sync calls from an in-step UI apply.

The host forces packet.overlap on. This is the governor-on state, and kHoldFrames = 120 holds it for at least 2 s once it switches on. The render-thread Emit calls NoteBegun, then runs a 200 us "pass 2" that repeatedly runs the exact seam test from wave21_lane_gfxbody.cpp:342 (`if (Graphics::MaterialInstance::_extAfterSetup != nullptr)`), then reaches the Gate (PassGate/WaitGate) and Release. The main thread runs BeforeSteps. When driver.Overlapping() is true it toggles via SyncBlossom, as the Enhanced-tab apply does inside a step, and then runs Tail.

Result in mode "bug": 1999 toggles ran during overlapped steps, and 1988 of them landed while pass 2 was in flight. TSan output:
"WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race ... Write of size 8 ... by main thread: #0 Ext::BetterTrees::SyncBlossom(bool) src/ext/better_trees/blossom_draw.cpp:106:48 ... Previous read of size 8 ... by thread T1: #0 Host::Emit ... #1 Driver<Host>::WorkerLoop pipe_driver.h:226 ... Location is global 'Graphics::MaterialInstance::_extAfterSetup'". The process exits with code 66.

Mode "fixed" runs the same schedule, but the step only records the wish and SyncBlossom runs in Host::BeforePublish, where the render thread is joined. That run gives 0 TSan warnings and exit 0.

_extDrawItemList (Camera.h:671, a plain static; written at draw_batch.cpp:476 by DrawBatch::Sync, which SetAndRecord calls on the same path) has the same declaration and the same writer/reader timing, so it is the same race. That case is shown by code reading, not by a separate TSan run: DrawBatch::Sync drags in too much of the engine to link standalone.

Stand-ins, all marked in the harness: the seam's storage definition (identical declaration), the reader as the transcribed null test without the call, GetPath/RtMemFree link stubs that are never run, and the host. Not shown: an in-game run with `[RenderPipe] overlap on` logged and a toggle made while the dialog is open.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
Defer the seam writes out of the step, following the MeshInstance::_extInstancedState pattern. DrawBatch::Sync and BetterTrees::SyncBlossom would only record the wanted state (a main-thread-only bool). The two plain-static stores (`Graphics::Renderer::_extDrawItemList = ...`, draw_batch.cpp:476, and `Graphics::MaterialInstance::_extAfterSetup = ...`, blossom_draw.cpp:106) would then be applied from a point where the render thread is joined: Host::BeforePublish (render_pipe.cpp:632) or the Frame tail, and directly when render_pipe is not threaded. This is the shape verified clean by the harness's "fixed" mode.

The alternative is to make both statics std::atomic and use a relaxed store in Sync and a single relaxed load into a local at each read site (batchc_gfx_leaves.cpp:696, wave21_lane_gfxbody.cpp:342). Each site gets a "NOT RETAIL:" comment.

Either way, file it in the same overlap-during-steps family as S-028 (SunLight::ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync).
proof_run.repro_path: scratchpad/phase2/proofs/seam-overlap-race/ (seam_race.cpp harness, build_tsan.sh WSL build script [run as: sed 's/\r$//' build_tsan.sh > ~/seamrace_build.sh && bash ~/seamrace_build.sh; then ~/seamrace_obj/seam_race bug|fixed], tsan_bug.log = race report, tsan_fixed.log = clean)

confirmed.title: Options Apply raises Device::settingsChanged under the faithful profile through the max_shadow_res seam, so a full video restart is followed by an extra swap-chain Resize
confirmed.bug_class: off-switch: an ext seam runs and changes device state while the row is off or the profile is faithful
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence:
optionsdialog.cpp:1007 calls `::Graphics::SunLight::ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync();` unconditionally in Apply. Under the faithful profile, registry_boot.cpp:202 leaves `SunLight::_extMaxShadowRes = nullptr`. SunLight::AddDrawItems (wave28_lane_partsys.cpp:900) then never calls ExtSyncMaxShadowRes, so `g_extSunLight` stays null. sunlight.cpp:322-325 does:
  `if (g_extSunLight != nullptr) g_extSunLight->ExtSyncMaxShadowRes(true);
   else if (Video::Device::_singleton != nullptr) Video::Device::_singleton->settingsChanged = 1;`
On the needsFullRestart path, Apply has already run OnVideoError / ReleaseDynamic / Shutdown; it then calls Startup + RecreateDynamic. No code in Device::Startup (device_startup.cpp:482, PlatformStartup) clears settingsChanged; only DeviceData_Resize sets it back to 0 (devicedata.cpp:877). So the first BeginCommands after the restart (contextdata.cpp:442) runs a full DeviceData_Resize: ResizeTarget, ResizeBuffers, SetFullscreenState, new colour and depth buffers, RecreateDynamic. Retail's OnApply has no such write. The same branch also runs in the default profile while no SunLight has drawn yet, for example Options opened from a menu without a sun. On the non-restart path ApplyChangedSettings (device.cpp:295) sets the flag anyway, so the effect is limited to the restart path.
confirmed.repro_idea: Run with /profile:faithful on a machine with two adapters, or with a renderer combo that reports needsFullRestart. Change the adapter in Options and Apply. Count DeviceData_Resize entries (g_resizeTraceCalls / the TraceGeom 'entry' line) on the first frame after Startup: the port should show one more than a run with the call guarded by `_extMaxShadowRes != nullptr`. A minimal fix: return from ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync when `_extMaxShadowRes == nullptr`, or guard the call site the same way.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: off-switch (low impact: one redundant swap-chain Resize, only on the full-restart Apply path)
verdict.proof:
Static reasoning on origin/main (<worktree>); each step can be checked line by line. Not in the ledger: S-028 covers a race on the descriptor rewrite while ext.render_pipe is on, and F-158 covers the render_pipe overlap race. Neither covers the write that runs under the faithful profile.
1. src/ext/registry_boot.cpp:202-203: `SunLight::_extMaxShadowRes = CurrentProfile()==Profile::Faithful ? nullptr : &Ext().max_shadow_res;`. Under the faithful profile the seam is null for the whole run.
2. Only one place assigns g_extSunLight: SunLight::ExtSyncMaxShadowRes (sunlight.cpp:328). It is called from AddDrawItems only `if (_extMaxShadowRes != nullptr)` (wave28_lane_partsys.cpp:900), and from ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync only when g_extSunLight is already non-null. Under the faithful profile g_extSunLight therefore stays nullptr for the whole run.
3. src/game/Dialog/optionsdialog.cpp:1007 calls `::Graphics::SunLight::ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync();` with no guard, after the early return for "nothing changed". The comment marks it "EXT SEAM (NOT RETAIL)".
4. sunlight.cpp:322-325: when g_extSunLight is null, it falls to `else if (Video::Device::_singleton != nullptr) Video::Device::_singleton->settingsChanged = 1;`. So every effective Apply under the faithful profile writes Device+0x9C from an ext seam.
5. On the non-restart path, ApplyChangedSettings (device.cpp:295) sets settingsChanged = 1 anyway, so that write makes no difference there. On the needsFullRestart path (renderer or adapter changed), Apply first runs OnVideoError, ReleaseDynamic and Shutdown, then Startup, which is a thunk to PlatformStartup (device_startup.cpp:482-486), then RecreateDynamic and OnVideoRestart. None of these clear settingsChanged. The only place that clears it is a successful Dx11_DeviceData_Resize (devicedata.cpp:877). The first BeginCommands after the restart (contextdata.cpp:442) therefore runs a full Dx11_DeviceData_Resize: ResizeTarget, ResizeBuffers, SetFullscreenState, new colour and depth buffers, and RecreateDynamic. Retail's Apply never asks for that.
Caveat: if a WM_SIZE during the restart makes SizeWindow (device_window.cpp:76) raise the flag anyway, the extra write changes nothing. That depends on the window size changing, so in the normal case (same size) the port does one more rebuild than retail. The faithful-profile purity rule is broken in every case, because a NOT RETAIL seam writes device state while its row is unregistered. The same write also happens under the default profile when no SunLight has drawn yet, which is harmless there because the row may be on.
verdict.minimal_fix: In SunLight::ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync (src/engine/graphics/sunlight.cpp:322), return straight away when `_extMaxShadowRes == nullptr`, so the seam does nothing under the faithful profile. The alternative is to guard the call at optionsdialog.cpp:1007 with `if (::Graphics::SunLight::_extMaxShadowRes != nullptr)`. The registry_boot.cpp:311/326 callers only run for a registered row, so they are unaffected.

confirmed.title: ext.sharp_ui PlaceArt reads our baked art using the sprite's UV-derived rect, while FindArt matched the art on the record's width/height: a sheet whose UVs disagree with its record reads past the art array
confirmed.bug_class: heap/static buffer over-read from malformed sprite-sheet input (unchecked size agreement)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: CONFIRMED (ASan). sharp_scaled.cpp:247-248 StartJob: `rect = RectFromUvs(s.u0, s.v0, s.u1, s.v1, w, h)` and `art = FindArt(table, tableCount, s.name._data, s.width, s.height, factor)`. FindArt (sharp_sheet.cpp) checks only `table[i].width == baseW * scale` against the record's s.width/s.height. PlaceArt (sharp_sheet.cpp:92-99) then indexes the art as `rgba + (ay * r.width + ax) * 4` with r = ScaleRect(UV rect), `ax = Clamp(x - r.x, 0, r.width - 1)`. If the UV rect is larger than the record, it reads past the end. If it is degenerate (u1 <= u0 gives width 0, clamped), Clamp(...,0,-1) returns -1 and it reads before the start. ASan on repro.cpp: mode 0 (record 4x4, UVs 20x20 texels) gives `heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 1 ... 2 bytes after 256-byte region` at sharp_sheet.cpp:97. Mode 1 (u1==u0, pad 1) gives UBSan `addition of unsigned offset ... overflowed` at :95, then a heap-buffer-overflow before the region. In the exe the art is a constexpr array in .rdata (sharp_sprites_data_2x/4x.h), so this reads neighbouring art or crashes at a page edge on the worker thread. Fix: also require the UV rect to equal the record size (or the art size to equal rect*factor) before taking the art; otherwise upscale.
confirmed.repro_idea: A mod's Dialog/SpriteSheet.rsc (or a twin) whose sprite named like one of ours (e.g. a menu chrome sprite) has record width/height equal to the retail ones but UVs covering a larger or empty rectangle; turn on ext.sharp_ui with Text + icons at a UI scale that picks 2x. Unit form: the scratchpad repro.cpp, or add a case to tests/unit/ext_sharp_sheet_test.cpp under ASan.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: memory (heap/.rdata over-read on the sharp_ui worker thread; ext.sharp_ui on + a malformed or modded SpriteSheet only)
verdict.proof:
Checked line by line on origin/main fa150cf7f in <worktree>. The finding could not be refuted.
1) sharp_scaled.cpp:247-249 (StartJob) sets rect = RectFromUvs(s.u0,s.v0,s.u1,s.v1,w,h) from the UVs. It picks art = FindArt(..., s.width, s.height, factor) from the record size. Nothing in StartJob or anywhere else in src/ext/sharp_ui checks that rect.width/height equal s.width/s.height (grep shows no such comparison).
2) FindArt (sharp_sheet.cpp:43-52) only checks table[i].width == baseW*scale and table[i].height == baseH*scale. So the art buffer holds exactly (s.width*f)*(s.height*f)*4 bytes.
3) BuildScaledSheet (sharp_sheet.cpp:117) calls PlaceArt with r = ScaleRect(rect, scale), which comes from the UVs. PlaceArt (89-104) reads rgba + (ay*r.width + ax)*4, with ay in [0, r.height-1] and ax in [0, r.width-1]. The highest offset it reads is (r.width*r.height - 1)*4. That is past the art's end whenever the UV rect is larger than the record, in either dimension or in total area.
4) If the UVs are degenerate (u1 <= u0), RectFromUvs clamps the width to 0. PlaceArt then calls Clamp(x - r.x, 0, -1). Clamp tests v<lo first and v>hi second, so for x >= r.x it returns -1 and the read lands before the start of the art. With pad>0, PadRect still gives a non-empty loop range.
The UV/record mismatch comes only from the sheet data (a mod's Dialog/SpriteSheet or a twin). It is not in the ledger: the review_20261103 hits for sharp_ui are only the font_raster LoadPrivateFace findings. It is also not fixed on main. This is hostile non-UB-in-retail input reaching NOT RETAIL ext code, so the ruling calls for plain hardening. The ASan report the sweep cites was not re-run here. The static path is airtight without it.
verdict.minimal_fix: In StartJob (sharp_scaled.cpp:248), take the art only when the UV rect matches the record: if (rect.width != s.width || rect.height != s.height) art = nullptr; (the sprite then goes through UpscaleRect like any non-art sprite). An equivalent fix is to have PlaceArt / BuildScaledSheet take the art's width and height and skip the sprite when ScaleRect(rect) differs. Add a case to tests/unit/ext_sharp_sheet_test.cpp: record 4x4 with UVs that are 20x20 texels, and a second with u1==u0 and pad 1.

confirmed.title: ext.sharp_ui Finish narrows the built atlas / BC3 level size (size_t) to int for Array::SetSize, then memcpys the full size_t length: a big enough mod sheet overflows the level buffer
confirmed.bug_class: size_t->int truncation in an allocation size followed by a full-length memcpy (resource / hostile texture size)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED. `levels[0].SetSize(static_cast<int>(job.atlas.size())); std::memcpy(levels[0].GetData(), job.atlas.data(), job.atlas.size());` (and line 274-275 for each BC3 level: `levels[i].SetSize(static_cast<int>(end - at)); std::memcpy(..., end - at)`). The atlas is (W*factor)*(H*factor)*4 bytes, and W/H come from the sheet's own texture (ScaledSheetMaterial only checks `_format == 5` and `> 0`). At factor 2 (BGRA8, no compression) a sheet of 11586 x 11586 or more gives an atlas of 2^31 bytes or more, so the int is negative or wraps (16384^2 at 2x = exactly 4 GiB -> 0). SetSize gets a negative or small size, and memcpy writes GBs into it. Nothing caps W*factor at the device's maximum texture size before the worker runs: the texture Create that would refuse 23172 x 23172 only runs after the copy. A related problem at factor 4: an 8192 sheet needs a 4 GiB atlas plus a ~5.3 GiB mip chain on the detached worker. A std::bad_alloc there has no handler in RunJob, so std::terminate ends the process.
confirmed.repro_idea: A mod replaces Dialog/SpriteSheet.rsc with a 12288 x 12288 BGRA8 sheet; ext.sharp_ui on at Text + icons, UI scale that picks factor 2 (px/unit between ~1.01 and 2). Expect a crash in Finish's memcpy on the first selection after the worker finishes. Fix: refuse a build whose scaled width/height exceed the backend's max texture size, or whose byte size exceeds INT_MAX, before StartJob, and catch bad_alloc in RunJob.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: crash (null-destination memcpy of GBs) on a hostile or oversized mod sheet with ext.sharp_ui on; not a heap overflow as worded
verdict.proof:
Checked against origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>). The ledger has no matching entry: the only sharp_ui hits in docs/history/review_20261103 are the font_raster LoadPrivateFace items in findings_p8.json.

Each step can be checked line by line:
1. ScaledSheetMaterial (src/ext/sharp_ui/sharp_scaled.cpp:348) checks only that `_format == 5` and that width and height are greater than 0. There is no upper bound. The readback buffer is sized in size_t (line 358).
2. kCompressFrom = 4 (line 49), so factor 2 (SpritesData2x::kScale) takes the uncompressed BGRA8 path. BuildScaledSheet (sharp_sheet.cpp:107-109) sizes the atlas as size_t(w)*h*4 with w = baseW*2. A 12288 x 12288 sheet, which is within the DX11 16384 limit, gives 24576^2*4 = 2,415,919,104 bytes. That is more than INT_MAX.
3. Finish line 279 runs `levels[0].SetSize(static_cast<int>(job.atlas.size()))`. The value is negative, or 0 for a 16384 sheet (exactly 4 GiB). SetSizeCore (src/engine/collection/array.cpp:2255) clamps a negative size to 0 (NOT RETAIL F-012). A fresh level array has _size 0, so `newSize == oldSizeI` returns early with _data == nullptr.
4. Line 280 `std::memcpy(levels[0].GetData() /*nullptr*/, job.atlas.data(), job.atlas.size() /*>2 GiB*/)` writes through a null pointer, which is UB and an access violation.
The same pattern is at lines 274-275 for the BC3 levels at factor 4. Base 12288 gives a 49152^2 level 0 = 2.4 GB of BC3, which is negative; base 16384 gives 4 GiB, which wraps to 0. Both reach the same null memcpy.

Correction to the finding: with this SetSizeCore, a size_t above INT_MAX always ends with a null (or empty) destination, never a small heap buffer. The atlas is at most 4 GiB at 2x because base width and height are 16384 or less, so the int is negative or 0. The failure is a guaranteed crash on the first selection after the worker finishes. It is not a heap overflow.

Smaller point: the multi-GB allocations in RunJob (atlas, mip chain) have no bad_alloc handler on the detached thread, so std::terminate ends the process. The finding states this, and it holds.

Reachability: ext.sharp_ui is on (default OFF), a mod supplies a BGRA8 Dialog/SpriteSheet.rsc or ExtensionsSprites.rsc of about 11586 px or more per side at factor 2 (about 8192 or more at factor 4), and the UI scale picks that factor.

Not run: there is no test or sanitizer run. The line-by-line proof is complete except for the resource loader accepting a texture that large, and DX11 allows textures up to 16384.
verdict.minimal_fix: In ScaledSheetMaterial, before the readback, refuse the build (push it to g_failed, log once and draw retail's sheet) when int64(_width)*factor or int64(_height)*factor exceeds the device's maximum texture size (16384), or when int64(w*factor)*(h*factor)*4 > INT_MAX. This keeps every later SetSize/memcpy length within an int. Optionally wrap the body of RunJob in try/catch(std::bad_alloc), mark the job failed, and let Finish treat a failed job as a failed build.

confirmed.title: ext.sharp_ui font-variant arithmetic overflows int for a mod font that claims the FrancophilSans face with a huge _lineHeight
confirmed.bug_class: signed integer overflow from untrusted resource field
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: CONFIRMED (UBSan). `static int RoundThirds(int baseHeight, int num) { return (2 * num * baseHeight + 3) / 6; }` is reached from SelectFont via PickFontHeight(base->_lineHeight, ...). The only gate is SameFace (the face name string), which a mod font can carry. font_repro.cpp calling PickFontHeight(300000000, 1.5f, 1.0f, &keep) prints `sharp_math.cpp:51:21: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 8 * 300000000 cannot be represented in type 'int'`. PickVariantHeight also loops over every height from VariantLow to VariantHigh, about baseHeight*2/3 iterations at each selection. Minimal fix: in SelectFont, keep the retail draw when _lineHeight is outside a sane range (for example 1..512).
confirmed.repro_idea: Run the scratchpad font_repro.cpp under -fsanitize=undefined. In game: a mod Font/Font.rsc with face FrancophilSans and _lineHeight 300000000, with ext.sharp_ui on.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (low: needs a hostile mod font, ext.sharp_ui on, and a UI ratio other than 1)
verdict.proof: Static reasoning on origin/main fa150cf7f, which the finding's UBSan line agrees with. The finding is not in the ledger: the only sharp_ui hits in findings_p8.json are about font_raster LoadPrivateFace, which is a different defect. (1) font.cpp:274 `ScalarInt(rw, _lineHeight)` reads the field straight from the .rsc with no range check. (2) sharp_ui.cpp:137-144: SelectFont loads Font/<Font|FontSmall|FontMedium|FontLarge>.rsc. Its only gate is SameFace, which is strcmp(_string20, "FrancophilSans") and lies inside the resource. It then calls PickFontHeight(base->_lineHeight, pxPerUnit, density, &keep). (3) sharp_math.cpp:173-188: both branches reach PickVariantHeight. The retina branch reaches it through PickRetinaVariantHeight at line 101. (4) PickVariantHeight returns early only for baseHeight<=0 or |base*pxPerUnit - base| < 0.5 (lines 73-75). Any ratio other than 1 (UI slider not at 100 %, or density > 1) with a huge base passes both checks. Line 79 then evaluates VariantHigh(baseHeight) = RoundThirds(b,4) = (2*4*b+3)/6. For b > INT_MAX/8 (about 268,435,455; 300,000,000 is the finding's value) 8*b overflows int, which is UB (line 51). RetinaHigh, with num=8, overflows from about 134M up (lines 92, 105). Separately, a large in-range base (for example 100M) makes the loop at line 79 run about 2b/3 iterations, each calling IsVariantHeight, at every font selection, so the game stalls there. Faithful behaviour is unaffected: SelectFont runs only with ext.sharp_ui on.
verdict.minimal_fix: In SelectFont (src/ext/sharp_ui/sharp_ui.cpp, after `const int height = base->_lineHeight;`), keep retail's draw when the height is outside a sane range. Example: `if (height < 1 || height > 512) { std::snprintf(text, 32, "%s->retail(range)", kFontNames[k]); return; }`. Alternatively, clamp in PickFontHeight / PickVariantHeight (return baseHeight when baseHeight > kMaxFontHeight) so the pure math is safe for every caller. Add a unit test in tests/unit with PickFontHeight(300000000, 1.5f, 1.0f, &keep), expecting the base height back and no UBSan report.

confirmed.title: ext.better_water retries the strip buffer upload and writes a stderr line every frame when the device refuses the buffers
confirmed.bug_class: error path retried per frame with a log line (hot-path log, resource churn)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED. DrawStrip (every frame the water draws with better_water_mode >= 2) calls StripFor, which runs `if (!s->ready && !UploadStrip(*s)) return nullptr;`. When ib->Create / vb->Create fails, UploadStrip prints `[BetterWater] the strip's buffers (%d + %d bytes) were not made` and leaves ready false. The next frame does UnlinkStrip + PlatformConstruct + Create + fprintf again. When platformData is null it returns false silently but still destructs and reconstructs both buffers every frame. Nothing records the failure (unlike ShorePixel's g_shorePixelTried), so a persistent refusal (device out of memory, a backend that rejects the size) writes one stderr file line per frame for the rest of the session, against the AGENTS.md §3 hot-path rule. Fix: mark the slot failed for this key (as `tried`) and only retry after OnVideoError / a key change.
confirmed.repro_idea: Force Video::IndexBuffer::Create to return false (debug fault injection, or a backend stub returning false), enable ext.better_water mode Fancy, load a map with water and watch standalone_error.log grow by one line per frame.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (ext.better_water Fancy mode only, and only when the device refuses the buffers. The result is one stderr file write and a destroy/re-create of both buffers per frame for the rest of the session)
verdict.proof:
Checked in <worktree> at fa150cf7f. This is not in the ledger: grep finds no better_water, UploadStrip or strip entry in README.md, findings_p3p4.json or findings_p8.json, and P0_MAP.md lists better_water only for QueryInterface and the constant-buffer size asserts. The trace, line by line:
(1) geometry_draw.cpp:471 calls Ext::BetterWater::DrawStrip(*this, context) from WorldGeometry's water draw, which runs every frame. DrawStrip (better_water.cpp:395-403) takes g_stripMutex and calls StripFor(geo) every frame.
(2) In StripFor (234-266) the rebuild block runs only when `!same || !s->tried`. It sets tried=true and ready=false. On later frames with the same key the block is skipped, but line 265, `if (!s->ready && !UploadStrip(*s)) return nullptr;`, still runs whenever ready is false.
(3) UploadStrip (204-231) sets ready=true only at line 229, after both Create calls succeed. On the failure paths, ready stays false and nothing records that the attempt failed:
  - If platformData is null (line 220), it returns false silently.
  - If ib->Create or vb->Create fails (222-227), it does fprintf(stderr, "[BetterWater] the strip's buffers (%d + %d bytes) were not made") and returns false.
(4) On the next frame s->vb != nullptr, so the else branch (213-217) runs UnlinkStrip (PlatformDestruct on both buffers, because linked was set true at 218), then PlatformConstruct on both, then Create again.
So a persistent refusal destroys and re-creates the buffers and writes one stderr line every frame for the rest of the session. That breaks AGENTS.md §3: fprintf(stderr) ships in perf and release, and this is a per-frame path with no Opt() gate, no _DEBUG guard and no count cap.
The empty-mesh return at line 206 is also retried every frame, but it is cheap and silent, so it is not part of this defect.
Scope: ext.* default OFF, so faithful behaviour is unaffected. It needs better_water on with better_water_mode >= 2 and a device that keeps refusing the buffers.
verdict.minimal_fix: Add `bool failed = false;` to StripSlot. In StripFor, clear it in the key-change block. Change line 265 to `if (!s->ready && (s->failed || !UploadStrip(*s))) return nullptr;`, and set s->failed = true when UploadStrip returns false with a non-empty mesh. Clear `failed` in the OnVideoError/device-restart seam so a new device gets one retry. Alternatively, cap the fprintf at a single print per slot.

confirmed.title: Font raster cache is keyed by (kit, px) only: rebuilding a variant after a mod change indexes rf->glyphs past its end
confirmed.bug_class: out-of-bounds read / stale cache (C1-style side table outliving its source)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: Rasterised() (line 102-118) looks up `c.fonts.find(std::make_pair(kit, px))` and returns the cached RasterFont whatever codepoint list it was built from. The cache never invalidates, and RasterizeFont sizes the glyph list from the FIRST call: font_raster_win.cpp:167 / font_raster_freetype.cpp:312 `out.glyphs.resize(count)`. BuildVariant then loops `for (int32_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) { const RasterGlyph& g = rf->glyphs[static_cast<size_t>(i)]; bitmaps[i] = g.alpha.data(); widths[i] = g.width; ... }` (lines 159-165, and again at 198-202 and 208-213), where `count = baseSheet->m_sprites._size` of the CURRENT base font. Provided objects are rebuilt: Modification::SetupFileSystem (modification_setupfilesystem.cpp:614) calls ExternalFactory::ForceUnload for every loaded External with no compiled file on disk, and the provided Sharp* fonts have none. The next lookup therefore runs BuildVariant again over whatever Font/<Kit>.rsc the new mod set mounts. If that base is still face FrancophilSans (the only check, line 129) but its sheet has more sprites than the first build, std::vector::operator[] reads past the end. g.alpha.data() is then a garbage pointer, and BuildFontSheet copies w*h bytes from it (font_sheet.cpp:81-83). With an equal count but different codepoints, every glyph silently gets another glyph's bitmap and metrics.
confirmed.repro_idea: Boot with ext.sharp_ui on and no mods, so the variants are built at N glyphs. Then enable a mod that ships Font/FontSmall.rsc with _fontName FrancophilSans and an extended glyph table (more c<codepoint> sprites, for example a translation mod). Apply in the Mods dialog and open any UI that uses the Sharp variant. Under ASan, expect a heap-buffer-overflow read in BuildVariant. Fix: key the cache on (kit, px, codepoint list or its hash), or drop the entry when rf->glyphs.size() != count.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: memory (heap OOB read in ext.sharp_ui, ext ON only, needs a mod that remounts Font/<Kit>.rsc with a FrancophilSans face and a different glyph table)
verdict.proof:
Checked line by line in <worktree> (origin/main):
1. src/ext/resources/font_provider.cpp:63-69: Cache::fonts is std::map<pair<kit,px>, RasterFont>. Nothing in src/ext/resources ever erases or clears it (grep finds no fonts.clear/erase), so an entry lasts for the whole process.
2. Rasterised() (102-118): on a hit at line 106 it returns the cached RasterFont and never compares it with `cps`. On a miss, RasterizeFont sizes the result from the first call's list: font_raster_win.cpp:167 and font_raster_freetype.cpp:312 both do `out.glyphs.resize(count)`.
3. BuildVariant (136-165, 198-202, 208-213): it takes `count = baseSheet->m_sprites._size` from the base font loaded now and indexes `rf->glyphs[i]` for i < count. It never checks against rf->glyphs.size(). The only guards are the face-name check at 129 and count == base->_glyphs._size at 137, and neither involves the cache.
4. A rebuild with a different base can happen. ProvideFont (232-245) rebuilds whenever FindAs misses. src/engine/io/modification_setupfilesystem.cpp:611-613 (act 3) ForceUnloads every loaded External whose compiled file is neither in a package nor on disk. The provided Sharp* objects have no such file, so a mod change drops them. resources.cpp:90 also says only the whole-cache flush and ForceUnload evict pinned objects. The base Font/<Kit>.rsc is then served by whatever packages the new mod set mounts.
Result: if the new base keeps _string20 == FrancophilSans and has more c<cp> sprites than the first build, rf->glyphs[i] reads past the vector's end. The garbage g.alpha.data() and width/height then reach BuildFontSheet's copy. If the count is equal but the codepoints differ, every glyph silently gets another glyph's bitmap and metrics.
Not in the ledger: the font_raster entries in findings_p8.json cover the FacePath / LoadPrivateFace face caches, not this (kit, px) raster cache. Not fixed on main.
Reachability is narrow but real: ext.sharp_ui on, plus a mod (for example a translation) that ships a FrancophilSans-face Font/FontSmall.rsc with an extended glyph table, applied after the variants were first built. No ASan run was made; the defect is shown by the missing size/key check, not by a crash trace.
verdict.minimal_fix: In Rasterised(), treat a hit as valid only when the cached entry was built from the same codepoint list. Store the cps vector with the RasterFont, or compare `it->second.glyphs.size() == cps.size()` and each glyphs[i].codepoint == cps[i]. On a mismatch, erase the entry and rasterise again. As a safety net, BuildVariant can also return nullptr when rf->glyphs.size() != static_cast<size_t>(count).

confirmed.title: BackgroundSave::Join polls PersistenceWorker::_status through a volatile cast; the S-033 fix (atomic acquire) was applied to saveload_update.cpp but not to this sibling
confirmed.bug_class: data race (volatile used as synchronisation)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: saveload_update.cpp:1001 now reads `__atomic_load_n(&persistence->_worker._status, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)` for the same hand-off (ledger S-033). background_save.cpp:322 still reads `*static_cast<const volatile int32_t*>(&p->_worker._status) == 0`, and line 326 reads `p->_worker._status` plainly for the log line. The persistence worker writes the field with plain stores (persistence_saveinfo_job.cpp:187-300, persistence_worker.cpp:294/333/417). This is a C++ data race (UB). There is also no acquire: whatever the worker wrote before setting _status is not ordered before the main thread's teardown. P0_MAP concurrency section 3 item 1 lists this site, but no F- or S- row covers it.
confirmed.repro_idea: TSan on a harness that runs Join(true) while a save job completes. Expect a race report on PersistenceWorker::_status between the worker's store and background_save.cpp:322. Fix: the same __atomic_load_n(..., __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) used at saveload_update.cpp:1001, on both reads.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: race (UB under the C++ memory model; ext.background_save is off by default, so a player only reaches it with the row switched on, at a quit or teardown during a save)
verdict.proof:
I could not refute this. It is not a duplicate, and origin/main has not fixed it.

What the code does now (<worktree>):
1. Join(true) is at src/ext/background_save/background_save.cpp:302-327. It calls sl->UpdateSaveTail(), which queues the SaveJob on the persistence worker. It then polls `*static_cast<const volatile int32_t*>(&p->_worker._status) == 0` at line 322, a non-atomic volatile load, while that job runs. Line 326 reads `p->_worker._status` again with a plain load for the ErrLine.
2. The worker thread's SaveJob writes the same field at src/engine/io/persistence_worker.cpp:658/660 with `__atomic_store_n(&_status, ..., __ATOMIC_RELEASE)`. PR #148 (F-147) added that. Before it, the store was plain.
3. Under [intro.races], two conflicting accesses on different threads are a data race unless both are atomic or one happens-before the other. Here the reader is not atomic and nothing orders the two accesses, so this is UB. The volatile cast does not make the load atomic or acquire. So the worker's file work and buffer reads are not ordered before the teardown that follows on the main thread. That teardown frees the SaveLoad and the embedded metadata block the job reads, which is the very purpose of the wait (comment at lines 313-315).

One correction to the finding's evidence: the SaveJob store that matters is already a release atomic store. It is not a plain store. The plain `_status = 0` stores at persistence_worker.cpp:294/333/417 are on the enqueue path. The plain stores in persistence_saveinfo_job.cpp:187-300 belong to the info job, not this hand-off. The race still holds, because only the read side is missing its atomic access.

Ledger check: S-033 (README:306, findings_p8.json:2998) names only saveload_update.cpp:999, and its "also" list is empty. That site now uses `__atomic_load_n(..., __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)` (saveload_update.cpp:1001). F-147 covers saveload.cpp:799 (SaveLoad::Update). P0_MAP.md:468 names background_save.cpp:322, but only as an inventory item, and no F- or S- row covers it. `git log -- src/ext/background_save/background_save.cpp` shows no change since the review fixes. So this is an uncovered sibling of S-033/F-147.

Why the verdict is needs_build_proof and not confirmed: the static reasoning holds line by line. But the campaign standard confirms a race with a TSan report, as F-147 was. In practice x86 TSO and ARMv8's control dependency on the loop exit make a visible failure unlikely, so only a sanitizer run can show the defect.
verdict.minimal_fix: In src/ext/background_save/background_save.cpp, replace the volatile cast at line 322 with `__atomic_load_n(&p->_worker._status, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == 0`. Load the value at line 326 the same way, or keep the value the loop last loaded. Add a `// NOT RETAIL (review S-033 sibling):` comment. Faithful code is unchanged, because the row is ext.* and off by default.

proof_run.proof:
TSan confirms the race (clang++-19 -fsanitize=thread under WSL). The repro does not stand in its own struct for IO::Persistence: it compiles against the worktree's real src/engine/io/Persistence.h (worktree at fa150cf7f, which matches origin/main). Both access expressions are copied word for word. The worker side is the SaveJob tail store from persistence_worker.cpp:658, `__atomic_store_n(&_status, wroteAll ? 1 : 2, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)`, preceded by a plain write that stands in for the job's file and metadata work. The main thread runs the Join(true) poll from background_save.cpp:321-326: the `*static_cast<const volatile int32_t*>(&p->_worker._status) == 0` loop, then a plain `p->_worker._status` read for the log line, then a read of the job's data, which models the teardown that follows.

Buggy build: "ThreadSanitizer: reported 2 warnings", exit 66.
(1) Data race on PersistenceWorker::_status (heap offset 0x48 = Persistence+0x10+0x38). "Atomic write of size 4 by thread T1 at bgsave_join_tsan.cpp:25 [the :658 store]" against "Previous read of size 4 by main thread at bgsave_join_tsan.cpp:32 [the :322 volatile poll]". The volatile cast is a non-atomic access, so this is UB under [intro.races].
(2) Data race on the job's payload. The worker's write before the release store is not ordered before the main thread's read after the poll exits, because the volatile load carries no acquire. This is the concrete hazard for the teardown that frees the SaveLoad and metadata block the job reads.

Fixed build (-DFIXED): the poll uses `__atomic_load_n(&p->_worker._status, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)` and the log line reuses the value the loop last loaded. TSan reports nothing; output is "status=1 payload=42", exit 0.

Limits of the proof:
- It is a pattern repro on the real type layout. It does not run the full Join/SaveLoad path.
- ext.background_save is off by default, so a player meets this only with the row switched on, at a quit during a background save.
