- One correction to the finding: the SaveJob writer already uses a release atomic store (F-147). Only the read side at :322/:326 is missing its atomic access.
- No worktree source was changed.

Files are in scratchpad/phase2/proofs/bgsave-join-status/: bgsave_join_tsan.cpp (the repro), run.sh (the WSL build and run of both variants) and tsan.log (the full output).
proof_run.minimal_fix: In src/ext/background_save/background_save.cpp Join(), keep the polled value in a local, `int32_t status = -1;`. Write the loop as `while (p != nullptr && (status = __atomic_load_n(&p->_worker._status, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) == 0 && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) sleep_for(1ms);`, one statement per line. Print `status` in the ErrLine instead of the plain `p->_worker._status` read. Add the comment `// NOT RETAIL (review S-033 sibling): acquire load; the persistence worker publishes _status with a release store (persistence_worker.cpp:658), and the teardown after this wait frees what the job reads.` The row is ext.* and off by default, so faithful behaviour is unchanged.

confirmed.title: create_on_demand ReadLevels leaves a stale pending.image key: a later image at the same address on the same thread takes another texture's level locators
confirmed.bug_class: dangling pointer used as identity key (ABA) in a thread-local side table
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: On success, ReadLevels sets `pending.image = ℑ` (line 99) and relies on the backend's Create to take and clear it. dx11 imagebufferdata.cpp reaches DeferTexture only after `if (!::Video::ImageBuffer::FormatInRange(ib->_format)) return false;`, and a create that never reaches ImageBufferData::Create also skips it. pending_levels.h itself admits that 'A Create that does not take them ... leaves them to the next image's reader, which replaces them'. That reader does not always replace them: the early exits `if (count <= 0 || image._kind != 2 || image.Width() == 0 || image.Height() == 0) return false;` (line 40) and `if (drop == 0) return false;` (line 49) return before `pending.Clear()` (line 55). If the first ImageBuffer is freed and a new one is allocated at the same address on the loader thread, and that new image takes one of those exits (for example, its stream is not locatable) but is still kind 2 with levels, then Create's `HasPendingLevels(ib)` test (`p.image == owner && !p.levels.empty()`, lazy_create.cpp:298) matches the stale pointer. DeferTexture then records the old image's Locators against the new image's D3D11 desc: the wrong texels, and a level count or sizes that no longer match the new image's pitches.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit-test the shape: call ReadLevels successfully on image A, skip the Create that would take the levels (A's create fails, for example an out-of-range _format in a mod .rsc), placement-new image B at A's address, have ReadLevels return false through the line-49 exit, then assert HasPendingLevels(&B) is false. It is currently true. Fix: call pending.Clear() at ReadLevels entry (and/or clear it in the engine seam after Create).

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (logic; ext.create_on_demand on, needs a malformed .rsc plus same-thread address reuse)
verdict.proof:
Checked line by line against origin/main in <worktree>. Nothing for level_source, PendingLevels or pending.image appears in the review_20261103 ledger (README, P0_MAP, findings_*.json).

1) A stale entry is left behind. On success, level_source.cpp:99 sets `pending.image = &image` with levels non-empty. PlatformSerialize (imagebuffer_platform_serialize.cpp:340-345) then calls RecreateFromFields -> ImageBuffer::Create (buffers.cpp:324), which goes straight to `_data->Create(levels)`. In dx11 ImageBufferData::Create, `if (!FormatInRange(ib->_format)) return false;` (imagebufferdata.cpp:595) returns before the only consumer, `HasPendingLevels`/`DeferTexture` (689/702). DeferTexture is what moves the levels out and calls p.Clear() (lazy_create.cpp:307-308). Vulkan does the same: companions.cpp returns false on VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED before its HasPendingLevels at :423. So an image whose `_format` is out of range (a malformed mod .rsc) leaves pending = {&A, levels}. pending_levels.h's banner admits this ("leaves them to the next image's reader, which replaces them").

2) The next reader does not always replace them. ReadLevels returns false at :40 (count <= 0, for example a count that the F-072 hardening capped to 0) or at :49 (stream not locatable, drop == 0) before `pending.Clear()` at :55. Nothing else clears the thread_local: HasPendingLevels is read-only, and DeferTexture runs only when the pointer matches.

3) The stale entry is matched by pointer alone. HasPendingLevels (lazy_create.cpp:297-299) is `p.image == owner && !p.levels.empty()`. Suppose A is freed and image B is allocated at the same address on the same loader thread, B is kind 2 with an in-range format and non-zero size, and B's ReadLevels takes exit :40 or :49 with no successful ReadLevels in between. Then ImageBufferData::Create(B) sees `levels != nullptr && kind == 2 && HasPendingLevels(ib)` as true. DeferTexture records A's Locators against B's desc and pitches, and B's own eagerly read level arrays are ignored. The result is wrong texels, or a level count or sizes that do not match B. (The `(void)count` at lazy_create.cpp:310 shows there is no size check.)

Limits: the trigger needs hostile input (a format >= 8, which retail would read past the tables anyway), and the ABA reuse depends on the allocator. The defect itself, a stale key that survives an early-exit read, is deterministic and can be reproduced with placement-new in a unit test, as the finding proposes.
verdict.minimal_fix: In src/ext/create_on_demand/level_source.cpp, call `::CreateOnDemand::ThreadPendingLevels().Clear();` at ReadLevels entry, before the :40 early return, so that no reader exit leaves an earlier image's entry. Optionally also clear it after the Create call in the engine seam. Add a unit test: ReadLevels succeeds on A, A's Create is skipped, then for B at the same address ReadLevels returns false through :49, and HasPendingLevels(&B) must be false.

confirmed.title: StreamCache SegmentStream::Read / Skip advance the int32 _pos with a plain signed add; a crafted cached record lets a read end at 0x80000000 (signed overflow)
confirmed.bug_class: signed integer overflow (UB) on a hostile cache file
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (static only). segment_stream.cpp:129-131: `if (_record->Read(static_cast<uint32_t>(_pos), static_cast<uint32_t>(n), ...)) { _pos += n; ...}` and :159 `_pos += len;` (Skip), with `int32_t _pos` (segment_stream.h:70). The record comes from derived.dat; the attacker can recompute its XXH64 checks, so it is hostile input in the same sense as F-036 / F-039. Bundle::AddChunk (stream_record.cpp:479-491) caps blockCount at 0x10000 through DirectoryTotal, which returns `(n - 1) * 0x8000 + last` with `last` an unchecked u16. A record's total can therefore be 0x80000000 (n = 0x10000, last = 0x8000) or up to 0x80007FFF, and AddChunk accepts any segment with seg.pos + seg.len <= total. AltLocate -> RangeInStream (payload.cpp:136-147) also allows pos + len <= 0x80000000. So an AltSkip followed by a Read that RecordView::Read serves can move _pos past INT32_MAX. Example: a size field in the record says 0x7FFFFFF8, Skip runs, then Serialize(int) reads 4 bytes from a segment [0x7FFFFFFC, 4); `_pos += 4` gives 0x80000000. The fallback branch `_fallback->_position += len` (:156) has the same shape.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit test (ext_stream_cache_test, standard C++ only): build a chunk with blockCount 0x10000, last-block uncompressedSize 0x8000 (total 0x80000000), id.size >= 0x80004 and one segment [0x7FFFFFFC, 4). AddChunk it, construct a SegmentStream over the RecordView, call SetCurrentPos(0x7FFFFFFC) (or Skip from 0), then Read(4). Built with -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow, UBSan reports `_pos += n`. Minimal fix: in AddChunk, refuse a record whose total exceeds INT32_MAX (no int32 stream is longer). Alternatively, do the add in int64 in Read/Skip and fail past INT32_MAX, with a NOT RETAIL comment.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (signed overflow, ext.stream_cache + ext.create_on_demand on, hostile derived cache)
verdict.proof:
Not refuted, and not in the ledger. Checked against origin/main fa150cf7f in <worktree>. The ledger has only F-039 (the AddChunk reserve OOM) and P0_MAP:335 for stream_cache. F-142 has the same shape but is in BinaryReader::Skip, which is a different site. The code has not been fixed.

Code facts:
- segment_stream.h:70: `int32_t _pos`.
- segment_stream.cpp:130 `_pos += n;` (Read), :82 `_pos += len;` (Skip), :80 `_fallback->_position += len;`. None of them has a bound.
- stream_record.cpp:55-61, DirectoryTotal: n is capped at 0x10000, but `last` is an unchecked u16, so the total can go up to 0xFFFF*0x8000+0xFFFF = 0x80007FFF.
- AddChunk (:259, :269) only requires DirectoryTotal(head)==total and seg.pos+seg.len <= total. Nothing caps the total at INT32_MAX.
- The record's head is trusted on a hit. stream_cache.cpp:264-271: Bundle::Find matches only (offset, size). The head is compared with the package only under the SHADOW harness flag (:161-165).
- AltLocate (stream_cache.cpp:443-458) checks only RangeInStream(record head, ...). payload.cpp:136-148 caps last.uncompressedSize at 0x8000, so length can be (0x10000-1)*0x8000+0x8000 = 0x80000000. It accepts pos+len <= 0x80000000.

Concrete path (ext.create_on_demand on): level_source.cpp:61-66 reads `size` from the stream, which here are the hostile record's bytes. It then calls Locate (which goes to AltLocate) and then CreateOnDemand::Skip(stream, size), which goes to AltSkip and then SegmentStream::Skip, giving `_pos += size`. If the record directory has n=0x10000 with last block 0x8000, and size = 0x80000000 - pos, RangeInStream passes and `_pos += len` lands on exactly 0x80000000. That is signed overflow at segment_stream.cpp:82. The Read site at :130 is reachable the same way: a segment ending above 0x7FFFFFFF is allowed by AddChunk when total is above 0x80000000.

Preconditions:
- The package entry the record matches has id.size >= 4+0x10000*8 = 0x80004, which AddChunk:257 requires.
- The derived cache is hostile. This is the same threat model as F-039.
- The build does not use -fwrapv. No -fwrapv appears in CMakeLists.txt.

This is a reasoning proof only. Under the campaign's standard, a UB finding needs a UBSan report before it can be confirmed.

Repro: in ext_stream_cache_test, build a chunk with id.size 0x80004, blockCount 0x10000, last directory entry uncompressedSize 0x8000, total 0x80000000 and one segment [0,4). Wrap it in a SegmentStream, call Read(4) to set _pos=4, then Skip(0x7FFFFFFC). Build with -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow; it should report segment_stream.cpp:82.
verdict.minimal_fix: In Bundle::AddChunk (stream_record.cpp, after the DirectoryTotal check at :259), add `if (v.total > 0x7FFFFFFFu) return false;` with a "NOT RETAIL:" comment: no int32 stream is longer than INT32_MAX. Every segment, and the length RangeInStream gets from the same head, is then <= INT32_MAX, so pos+len <= INT32_MAX on the Read, Skip and fallback paths. Alternative: in SegmentStream::Read and Skip, do the add in int64 and fail (or set _failed) past INT32_MAX.

proof_run.proof:
Confirmed on fa150cf7f with a build in worktree <worktree>.

New unit test: ext_stream_cache_bundle_refuses_a_total_past_int32 in tests/unit/ext_stream_cache_test.cpp. It builds one record with:
- blockCount 0x10000 and a last directory entry with uncompressedSize 0x8000, so the total is 0x80000000;
- id.size 0x80004;
- two segments, [0,4) and [0x7FFFFFFC,4).

Without the fix, AddChunk accepts the record. The test then runs a SegmentStream through Read(4), Skip(0x7FFFFFF8) and Read(4).

(1) Plain debug suite (tools/build.sh unit debug --jobs 2): FAIL ext_stream_cache_test.cpp:943 `!added`. Result: 2000 tests, 1 failure.

(2) Sanitizer build. Its configure line: CXXFLAGS="-fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow -fsanitize-trap=signed-integer-overflow" BANISHED_SANITIZE=check. Trap mode was used because WinLibs ships no libubsan, and WSL was blocked by worktree isolation. `unit.exe --filter ext_stream_cache_bundle_refuses_a_total_past_int32` dies with SIGILL (exit 132). gdb shows:
"SIGILL ... Ext::StreamCache::SegmentStream::Read (n=4) at src/ext/stream_cache/segment_stream.cpp:54: `_pos += n;`", called from ext_stream_cache_test.cpp:941.
That is the signed-overflow trap: 0x7FFFFFFC + 4 in int32. The finding cites :130; in this tree the same statement is at :54. Skip's `_pos += len` at :82 has the same shape, and one more step reaches it.

(3) With the minimal fix:
- trap build: 15 ext_stream_cache tests, 0 failures, exit 0;
- plain debug suite: 2000 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped.

Artefacts are in scratchpad/phase2/proofs/streamcache-pos-overflow/:
- test file
- fix_and_test.diff
- sc_trap_gdb.log
- sc_trap_run.log
- sc_trap_fixed.log
- unfixed_debug_unit.log
- fixed_debug_unit.log

The changes are uncommitted in the worktree, and no PR was opened. third_party was robocopied from openba-review because the submodule command was refused by isolation; it is not to be committed.

confirmed.title: Sharp-font glyph cache is keyed by (kit, px) only; a rebuild over a base font with more sprites indexes the cached RasterFont past its end
confirmed.bug_class: heap out-of-bounds read (stale cache sized by an old input)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (static only; reachability depends on a provided variant being evicted). Rasterised() (:102-118) returns the cached `c.fonts[(kit, px)]` without comparing it to `cps`. The codepoints and their count come from the CURRENT base sheet (:136-149, `count = baseSheet->m_sprites._size`), but on a cache hit `rf->glyphs` has the size from the first build. BuildVariant then loops `for (i < count) rf->glyphs[static_cast<size_t>(i)]` at :160, :199 and :209. The banner says the cache exists for 'a rebuild after ExternalFactory::Clean'. If, between the two builds, Font/<Kit>.rsc came from a different source (a mod that keeps _string20 == FrancophilSans but ships a larger glyph set, such as a translation adding accented letters), then count > rf->glyphs.size() reads past the vector. With an equal count the variant silently gets the old codepoints' glyphs, while _charToGlyph is copied from the new base.
confirmed.repro_idea: With ext.sharp_ui on, build Font/SharpFont_32.rsc once (base with N sprites). Swap in a Font/Font.rsc whose face is FrancophilSans and which has N+k sprites (a mod package), then evict the variant (whole-cache flush or ForceUnload) and request the variant again; under ASan the read of rf->glyphs[N] is reported. Fix: key the cache on the codepoint list as well (or store it and compare `rf->glyphs.size() == cps.size()` plus the codepoints), and re-rasterise on a mismatch.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: memory (heap OOB read, ext.sharp_ui on only); with an equal count, silent wrong glyphs
verdict.proof:
Not refuted. Read on origin/main (<worktree>/src/ext/resources/font_provider.cpp).

The defect, line by line:
- Cache::fonts (:65) is a function-static std::map keyed only by (kit, px). Nothing in the file erases or invalidates it, and nothing outside the file can reach it (it sits in an anonymous namespace).
- Rasterised (:102-106) returns the cached RasterFont on a key hit and never looks at `cps`.
- BuildVariant takes `count = baseSheet->m_sprites._size` (:136) from the base font it has just loaded (:127). It then indexes `rf->glyphs[i]` for i < count at :160, :199 and :209. There is no check that `rf->glyphs.size() == count`.
- On a first build, RasterizeFont fills one glyph per codepoint (font_raster.h:56, "in the order of `codepoints`"). The cached size is therefore the old base's sprite count.
- So if a later build sees a base sheet with more sprites, std::vector operator[] reads past the end. If the count is the same but the codepoints differ, the variant gets the old glyph metrics and bitmaps, while :194-196 copies `_charToGlyph` from the new base.

Reachability (plausible, not run):
- The base can change within one process. ModDialog::Apply (src/game/Dialog/moddialog.cpp:541-598, retail 0x14006ea70) calls CloseAndReload, which reloads with a different mod/package set. fix.mods_persist (#156) also keeps that path usable in a game.
- The static cache survives that reload.
- The provided variant objects belong to the factory, so the reload's eviction makes the next request go through ProvideFont -> BuildVariant again (FindAs at :243 misses). That rebuild hits the stale cache.
- The face guard at :129 only requires `_string20 == "FrancophilSans"`. A mod that ships a Font/<Kit>.rsc with the same face name and a larger sprite set (for example extra accented glyphs) passes it.

What is still unproven, which is why this is not "confirmed": that the reload actually evicts the Sharp variant objects, and a run under ASan/_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS. The ledger (README F-001..F-217, findings_p3p4.json, findings_p8.json) has only the FacePath / LoadPrivateFace face-cache findings for font_raster. None of them covers this (kit, px) glyph-cache staleness, so this is not a duplicate. Not fixed on origin/main: the last commits touching the file are d1d140d51 and 525c53dcc, and neither adds a check.
verdict.minimal_fix: In Rasterised (font_provider.cpp:105-106), treat a cache entry as a hit only if it was built from the same codepoint list. Either store the cps vector in the cache entry, or compare `it->second.glyphs.size() == cps.size()` and each glyph's `codepoint == cps[i]`. On a mismatch, erase the entry and re-rasterise. Also add a defensive `if (rf->glyphs.size() != static_cast<size_t>(count)) return nullptr;` in BuildVariant after :153, with a one-line [ExtRes] message.

proof_run.proof:
Confirmed by a unit test that fails on origin/main (fa150cf7f). A new test, tests/unit/ext_font_provider_cache_test.cpp, compiles font_provider.cpp into the unit binary. The rasteriser is swapped for a stub through a macro rename of RasterizeFont, so no font face is needed. The ExternalFactory and Resources seams (Find, FindOrLoad, _singleton, Register, BuildFontSheet, SetPath, Publish) are linker stubs that the test never calls. The test then calls the real Rasterised(kit=0, px=977, cps) three times:
1. 3 codepoints {65,66,67}: rasterises 3 glyphs.
2. 5 codepoints {65,66,67,0xE9,0xE8}: this simulates a rebuild over a base sheet with more sprites.
3. 5 different codepoints: same count as call 2, different list.

Result on the unmodified tree (`bash tools/build.sh unit debug --jobs 2`, log unit_before_fix.log):
  FAIL ext_font_provider_cache_test.cpp:64: b->glyphs.size() == second.size()
  FAIL ext_font_provider_cache_test.cpp:75: c->glyphs.size() == third.size()
  FAIL ext_font_provider_cache_matches_the_base_codepoints

So the cache hands back a RasterFont of 3 glyphs when the caller has 5 codepoints. BuildVariant sets `count = baseSheet->m_sprites._size` (5) and indexes `rf->glyphs[i]` for i < count at :160, :199 and :209, which reads past the end of the vector (a heap OOB read). When the count is equal, the variant gets the old codepoints' glyphs.

With the minimal fix (fix.diff) the test passes: `ok ext_font_provider_cache_matches_the_base_codepoints` (unit_after_fix.log). The only other failure in both runs is sysmisc_timer_ticks_after_eleven_days, which this change does not touch.

Still not shown: that a mod reload evicts the provided variant objects in a real game run. The stale cache itself is shown.
proof_run.minimal_fix: In Rasterised (src/ext/resources/font_provider.cpp:105), a cached entry counts as a hit only when it matches the current codepoint list: `it->second.glyphs.size() == cps.size()` and every `glyphs[i].codepoint == cps[i]`. On a mismatch, `c.fonts.erase(it)` and rasterise again. The diff is in the worktree <worktree> (uncommitted), and the regression test is tests/unit/ext_font_provider_cache_test.cpp.

confirmed.title: background_save calls PlayerToolManager::UpdateCamera on a raw byte copy of a polymorphic object that was never constructed
confirmed.bug_class: type-punned access / object lifetime (member call on storage holding no object)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (static only; the code marks it CAST-OK, but it is undefined under [basic.life]). :298-299 `std::memcpy(job->shadowStorage, static_cast<const void*>(loop->m_toolManager), sizeof(PlayerToolManager)); job->shadow = reinterpret_cast<PlayerToolManager*>(job->shadowStorage);` and :363 `job->shadow->UpdateCamera(...)`. PlayerToolManager is polymorphic (it has a vptr), so it is not an implicit-lifetime type: memcpy creates no object, and every member call and field access through `shadow` (:197-202, :363) is UB. UBSan's vptr check will not catch it, because the copied vptr bytes point to the real vtable. The behaviour today rests on GCC treating the bytes as an object; an optimiser may assume the shadow and the real manager do not alias, or drop the stores.
confirmed.repro_idea: No sanitizer detects this. Reviewable by reading the code: the storage is alignas(PlayerToolManager) uint8_t[] filled by memcpy, then used through reinterpret_cast. Minimal fix: copy only the three camera floats (+0x3c/+0x40/+0x44) and run UpdateCamera on the real manager between a save of the real floats and their restore. Or, if UpdateCamera's body touches only those floats and the controller, move its camera half into a free function that takes the three floats by reference. Either way, add a NOT RETAIL comment.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (formal; low practical risk; ext.background_save is off by default)
verdict.proof:
The conclusion holds, but the finding's reason for it is wrong. Checked on origin/main fa150cf7f in <worktree>.

1) What the finding gets wrong: PlayerToolManager (src/game/Game/PlayerToolManager.h:148) has no virtual member at all; grep finds no "virtual" in the header. +0x00 is an InternalPtr<UI::DialogInstance> field, not a vptr. So "polymorphic, has a vptr" is false, and the UBSan-vptr argument does not apply.

2) Why it is still UB, step by step:
- The class has a user-provided default constructor (PlayerToolManager();), so it is not an aggregate.
- Its member `PlayerCameraViewArray cameraViews` (+0x70) is a Collection::Array, and Collection::Array declares a user-provided `~Array();` (src/engine/collection/Collection.h, about line 377) with a real body.
- That makes PlayerToolManager's implicit destructor non-trivial. The header comment "No destructor runs in C++" is about retail's call pattern, not about C++ triviality.
- A non-aggregate class with a non-trivial destructor is not an implicit-lifetime type ([class.prop]/9). So the memcpy into `alignas(PlayerToolManager) uint8_t shadowStorage[]` (background_save.cpp:73, :228) does not implicitly create a PlayerToolManager object ([intro.object]/10).
- Every use through `job->shadow` (from the reinterpret_cast at :229) therefore touches storage that holds no PlayerToolManager object. Under [basic.life] that is UB. The uses are:
  - the reads at :129-132 (`job->shadow->field_0x3C/40/44`);
  - the member call at :293 (`job->shadow->UpdateCamera(...)`), whose body (camera_input.cpp:122ff) reads and writes this->field_0x38/3C/40/44/A4/A8/AC.
- The memcpy also reads a non-trivially-copyable object bytewise. The `static_cast<const void*>` exists only to silence -Wclass-memaccess.

Ledger: not recorded. The only background_save entries in docs/history/review_20261103 are P0_MAP concurrency notes (:430, :471) and findings_p8 references to its persistence wait. None mentions the shadow copy. F-187 is the UpdateCamera z-clamp drift and is unrelated. Not fixed on origin/main.

Practical impact: GCC does not miscompile this today, because the shadow is never aliased with the real manager in one function. This is a formal-UB finding under the campaign ruling (every UB gets a minimal fix), not an observed failure.

confirmed.title: With fix.save_failure_notice OFF, SaveJob publishes status 1 before it closes the save file; retail closes first, then stores 1
confirmed.bug_class: fix OFF state does not restore retail order (port drift)
confirmed.label: port
confirmed.evidence: Port, with viaTemp == false (fix off): the writes finish, then `__atomic_store_n(&_status, wroteAll ? 1 : 2, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);` (:658), and only after that the shared tail `if (bfs._file.handle != -1) Fs()->CloseFile(bfs._file);` (:670). The file closes before the status store only in the fix-ON branch (:647). Retail Runtime 0x1800b6e00 (Ghidra), success arm: `if ((int)local_68.DebugInfo != -1) { IO::FileSystem::CloseFile(IO::FileSystem::_singleton,(FileInfo *)&local_68); } *(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x38) = 1;`. Retail closes the file first and then stores status 1. Its failure arms store 2 first and close in the tail, which the port matches. So the fix's OFF state is not retail's order: a reader that sees status 1 can find the save handle still open. The retail readers (SaveLoad::Update, the load arms at saveload_update.cpp:1606/1626) test IsWorking() first, so they cannot see this. BackgroundSave::Join (background_save.cpp:321-324) polls _status alone and goes on to teardown as soon as it is non-zero. With fix.save_failure_notice off and ext.background_save on, a quit during a save can therefore start freeing the engine while the worker still runs Fs()->CloseFile on the save handle.
confirmed.repro_idea: Static, Ghidra-proven. Minimal fix: in the !viaTemp success path, close the file (`if (bfs._file.handle != -1) Fs()->CloseFile(bfs._file);`) before the release store of 1, as retail does; the tail close then has nothing left to do. Dynamic check: settings fix.save_failure_notice=0 and ext.background_save=1. Quit from the pause menu while a large-town background save runs, with a sleep injected after the status store in a debug build. Fs()->CloseFile then runs after Join returned.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: minor
verdict.proof: Retail Runtime-x64.dll 0x1800b6e00 (Ghidra decompile, fresh) has this full-write success arm: `if ((int)local_68.DebugInfo != -1) { IO::FileSystem::CloseFile(IO::FileSystem::_singleton,(FileInfo *)&local_68); } *(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x38) = 1;`. The failure arms (`LAB_1800b7028` and the three earlier short-write else branches, plus the !Create branch) store 2 only, and the shared tail closes the handle. Port <worktree>/src/engine/io/persistence_worker.cpp with viaTemp == false (fix.save_failure_notice OFF): the write loop ends, then `__atomic_store_n(&_status, wroteAll ? 1 : 2, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);` (:658), and only after that `if (bfs._file.handle != -1) Fs()->CloseFile(bfs._file);` (:670). On success the port therefore stores 1 before the close, and retail closes before it stores 1. The banner at :663-669 claims that 'a full write success already matches (nothing above closed it yet, so this is where retail's real close happens)'. The decompile contradicts it: retail has a second, inner CloseFile in the success arm. That makes the OFF state of the fix not byte-faithful in ordering, so this is port drift. The failure arms match. Not a duplicate. F-147 / findings_p8.json:3009 is about the plain-vs-atomic store (the data race), and the release store at :658 already fixes it. The S-0xx rows on persistence teardown (worker dtor UAF) and the CloseFile counters (S-029) are separate defects. None of them records the close/store order. Impact note: the BackgroundSave::Join teardown consequence is plausible but secondary. Even in retail the worker still runs ~BinaryFileStream frees after storing 1, so the post-status window exists in retail too. The port widens it with an Fs()->CloseFile (a platform close of the save handle). The verdict rests on the Ghidra order diff alone.
verdict.minimal_fix: In SaveJob's non-viaTemp path, close the file before the status store when every byte was written, as retail does. For example, just before :658 add `if (!viaTemp && wroteAll && bfs._file.handle != -1) Fs()->CloseFile(bfs._file);`, keeping one statement per line. Keep the tail close, which retail also has and which handles the short-write case. Correct the :663-669 banner: retail closes inside the success arm and then stores 1, and the tail close only handles the failure arms.

confirmed.title: BackgroundSave::Join polls the persistence worker's _status with a volatile plain read while the worker stores it atomically (the F-147 pattern, not fixed at this site)
confirmed.bug_class: data race (non-atomic read of a word another thread writes)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: `while (p != nullptr && *static_cast<const volatile int32_t*>(&p->_worker._status) == 0 && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) std::this_thread::sleep_for(...)` and then the plain read `p != nullptr ? p->_worker._status : -1` in the ErrLine at :326. Meanwhile PersistenceWorker::SaveJob on the worker thread does `__atomic_store_n(&_status, ..., __ATOMIC_RELEASE)` (persistence_worker.cpp:658/660). Review F-147 replaced exactly this volatile read with `__atomic_load_n(..., __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)` at saveload_update.cpp:1001, and its comment says a volatile read of a word the worker writes is still a data race. Join is the remaining copy. Without acquire ordering, Join's caller (GameUpdateLoop::Shutdown) can also go on to free the SaveLoad blocks with no happens-before edge to the worker's last reads of them. SUSPECTED: static only, no TSan report attached.
confirmed.repro_idea: TSan unit: one thread runs a SaveJob-like body ending in the release store to _status, while another spins with Join's volatile loop; TSan reports the pair. Real run: ext.background_save=1, quit from the pause menu while a save's worker runs, under a TSan build (Linux). Fix: `__atomic_load_n(&p->_worker._status, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)` in the loop and in the log line.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: race (UB under the C++ memory model; only reachable with ext.background_save on; harmless on x86 TSO, unordered on aarch64)
verdict.duplicate_of: Not a duplicate. This is a leftover site of the F-147 pattern. F-147's fix converted saveload_update.cpp:1001 and the worker's stores but missed this one. P0_MAP.md:406 and :468 name background_save.cpp:322 as one of the two volatile-as-sync pollers, but F-147's root_cause list does not include it, and origin/main fa150cf7f still has it.
verdict.proof:
I checked this on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>), and the code supports the finding.

1. The racing reads are still there. In background_save.cpp:321-326, Join reads `p->_worker._status` through `*static_cast<const volatile int32_t*>(...)` in the poll loop, then reads it again with a plain read inside the ErrLine argument. Both are non-atomic accesses.

2. The worker writes the same word at the same time. persistence_worker.cpp:658/660 does `__atomic_store_n(&_status, wroteAll ? 1 : 2, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)` from inside SaveJob on the worker thread. The overlap comes from Join itself. UpdateSaveTail (line 319) queues the save, which sets _status to 0. Join then spins while the worker's SaveJob runs and eventually stores 1 or 2. Neither side orders the two accesses: the main thread takes no event or mutex inside the loop. One access is non-atomic and the other conflicts with it, so by [intro.races] this is a data race, which is UB.

3. The project already ruled on this exact pattern. F-147 was confirmed with a TSan report, and its fix comment at saveload_update.cpp:999-1001 says: "a volatile read of a word the worker writes is still a data race". The only thing that differs at this site is the spelling of the read.

4. The ordering problem is real. With no acquire load, the worker's earlier reads of the queued blocks (the embedded metadata buffer and the save state, persistence_worker.cpp ~602-630, all before the release store) are not ordered before the main thread's later teardown. GameUpdateLoop teardown frees the SaveLoad and _embeddedState._data, so on aarch64 that teardown has no happens-before edge to the worker's reads.

5. The faithful build is unaffected. Join only reaches this block when the ext job exists (`g_job != nullptr`), so with ext.background_save off nothing changes. That is why the label is ext and not port/retail.
verdict.minimal_fix: In background_save.cpp:322, replace `*static_cast<const volatile int32_t*>(&p->_worker._status) == 0` with `__atomic_load_n(&p->_worker._status, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == 0`. In the ErrLine at :326, either print a local holding the last value the acquire load returned, or use another `__atomic_load_n(..., __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)`. Add a comment citing review F-147 (the paired release store is SaveJob's). The field layout stays as it is.

confirmed.title: Font variant provider accepts non-canonical pixel spellings ("_032", "+32", on LP64 "_4294967328") and returns the already-registered canonical object, which the provide seam then re-paths and re-Adds under the alias
confirmed.bug_class: lenient parse of a resource path / alias registration
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: ParseVariantPath: `const int32_t px = static_cast<int32_t>(std::strtol(num, &end, 10)); if (end == num || px <= 0 || px > 999) return false;`. strtol skips whitespace and takes a sign and leading zeros. On 64-bit-long hosts (Linux, macOS, Android) a value past 2^32 truncates into range before the check, e.g. 4294967328 -> 32. MakeVariantNames(kit, px) then names the canonical "Font/SharpFont_32.rsc:..." paths. ProvideFont (font_provider.cpp:243): `if (Object::External* existing = FindAs<Object::External>(own)) return existing;`. Provide is reached only after the factory missed the ASKED path, so this branch fires exactly when the asked spelling differs from `own`. Provide() then runs Pin(obj, path) (resources.cpp:118-124 of the file): `obj->_path = System::Filename(expandedPath); ... f->Add(obj); ... f->Add(obj);`. The object already in the resource tree under "SharpFont_32" gets its _path rewritten to "SharpFont_032" and is added a second time. When the canonical variant is not built yet, BuildVariant registers material/texture/sheet under the _32 names and the font under the alias, so a later canonical request builds and Publishes a second set under the same paths.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit: ParseVariantPath("Font/SharpFont_032.rsc", vp) returns true with px 32; on Linux, ParseVariantPath("Font/SharpFont_4294967328.rsc", vp) also returns true with px 32. In game (ext.sharp_ui on): FindOrLoad("Font/SharpFont_32.rsc"), then FindOrLoad("Font/SharpFont_032.rsc") (e.g. from a mod .rsc reference). The second returns the first object, now with _path "Font\SharpFont_032.rsc:resource" and present under two keys; then exercise ExternalFactory::Clean. Fix: require the digits to round-trip (no sign, no leading zero, length <= 3) and treat a FindAs hit on a different spelling as not provided.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (logic / hostile-input hardening; reachable only with ext.sharp_ui on and a resource reference spelled non-canonically, e.g. from a mod .rsc; faithful profile registers no provider)
verdict.proof:
Line-by-line, in <worktree> on origin/main.
1) src/ext/resources/font_tables.cpp:46-51: `px = static_cast<int32_t>(std::strtol(num, &end, 10)); if (end == num || px <= 0 || px > 999) return false; ... if (std::strcmp(end, tail) != 0) return false;`. strtol accepts leading whitespace, a '+' sign and leading zeros, so "Font/SharpFont_032.rsc" and "Font/SharpFont_+32.rsc" parse to kit Font, px 32. On LP64 hosts (Linux, macOS, Android: 64-bit long) "_4294967328" gives long 4294967328, which the cast to int32 wraps to 32 (GCC modular conversion) before the range check. On Windows (32-bit long) strtol saturates to LONG_MAX and the cast gives -1, so that spelling is rejected there; the "_032" / "_+32" aliases apply on every platform. The unit tests (tests/unit/ext_font_raster_test.cpp:56-70) cover no such spelling.
2) font_provider.cpp:239-243: ProvideFont rebuilds the CANONICAL names from (kit, px) and does `if (Object::External* existing = FindAs<Object::External>(own)) return existing;`. ProvideFont is reached only from the FindOrLoad miss branch (external_compiled.cpp:276-277, after External::Load found nothing for the ASKED path). So a FindAs hit on `own` means the asked spelling was different from `own`, and the already-registered canonical object is returned for the alias.
3) resources.cpp:146-149 then calls Pin(obj, path) with the alias path. Pin (resources.cpp:120-129) writes `obj->_path = System::Filename(expandedPath)` (the alias) and calls f->Add(obj) twice. FindOrLoad (external_compiled.cpp:287-289) writes `loaded->_path = expanded` (the alias again) and Adds once more. The canonical object, still in the resource tree under "Font\SharpFont_32.rsc:resource", now has _path "Font\SharpFont_032.rsc:resource" and is also inserted under the alias key. When the canonical variant has not been built yet, BuildVariant registers material/texture/sheet under the _32 names and the font under the alias only; a later canonical request misses FindAs(own) for the font and runs BuildVariant again, publishing a second set under the same canonical paths.
Not in the ledger: the only font-related rows in findings_p8.json are the FacePath / LoadPrivateFace face-cache findings (font_raster), not path parsing; README.md, P0_MAP.md and findings_p3p4.json have no ParseVariantPath / strtol-alias entry. Not fixed on origin/main.
What stays unproven without a build: whether the double row plus the _path mismatch leads to a dangling row or double free on ExternalFactory::Clean / the whole-cache flush. The parse leniency and the re-path / re-Add follow directly from the code, so the logic defect is confirmed; the memory-safety consequence would need a test.
verdict.minimal_fix: In ParseVariantPath accept only canonical digits: require 1-3 ASCII digits with no sign, no whitespace and no leading zero (parse by hand or check isdigit(num[0]) && num[0] != '0' and that end - num <= 3) before the strcmp of the tail. Optionally, in ProvideFont, return nullptr when FindAs(own) hits but the normalised asked path differs from `own`, so an alias is never re-pathed. Add unit cases: "Font/SharpFont_032.rsc", "Font/SharpFont_+32.rsc", "Font/SharpFont_ 32.rsc" and "Font/SharpFont_4294967328.rsc" must all return false.

confirmed.title: DerivedCache::LoadIndex sizes a vector from derived.idx's file size before validating a single record: an oversized or sparse index aborts every boot
confirmed.bug_class: unbounded allocation from a file size
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: `const uint64_t count = (static_cast<uint64_t>(idxSize) - kHeaderSize) / sizeof(IndexRecord); std::vector<IndexRecord> all(static_cast<size_t>(count)); if (count != 0 && !ReadAt(_idx, kHeaderSize, all.data(), count * sizeof(IndexRecord))) return false;`. Only the 32-byte headers are checked first (magic, format, record size). Every valid record needs at least one payload byte inside derived.dat (`r.size == 0` breaks), so at most datSize - 32 records can survive. Yet a derived.idx with a valid header and a huge (e.g. sparse 64 GiB) length makes this allocate idxSize bytes, and std::bad_alloc terminates the process. The file persists in <Documents>\Banished\Cache, so the crash repeats at every start with any cache consumer on (package_cache, stream_cache, compress_ao) until the folder is deleted by hand. The 'Clear cache' button cannot help: the run dies first. F-036 fixed only the offset+size wrap in the per-record loop.
confirmed.repro_idea: In the Cache folder, write a derived.idx whose 32-byte header is a valid 'OBADCIDX' format-2 header (generation equal to derived.dat's), then `truncate -s 64G derived.idx` (sparse). Start with ext.package_cache on: the process aborts in LoadIndex. Unit-testable with Store::Open over a temp dir. Fix: clamp count to (datSize - kHeaderSize) or read and validate records in bounded chunks.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (resource / DoS from a planted or corrupted local cache file; ext.* consumers only, off by default)
verdict.proof: Checked line by line in <worktree>/src/ext/derived_cache/derived_cache.cpp (origin/main). In Store::LoadIndex (:381), the only checks before the allocation are: both sizes >= 32, a 32-byte read of each header, HeaderIs(dh,"OBADCDAT",0) and HeaderIs(ih,"OBADCIDX",sizeof(IndexRecord)) (:388-391), and on a generation mismatch either FinishInterruptedRewrite or verifyPayloads=true (:407-417). Nothing bounds idxSize. Then :419 computes count=(idxSize-32)/sizeof(IndexRecord), and :420 `std::vector<IndexRecord> all(static_cast<size_t>(count));` value-initialises count*sizeof(IndexRecord), which is about idxSize bytes. No record has been validated at that point. Nothing in src/ext/derived_cache has a try/catch (grep for try|catch|bad_alloc finds none), and the callers at :292 and :327 call LoadIndex() directly. So an index whose header is valid and whose length is huge (a sparse file of 1 TiB, which NTFS and ext4 both allow) makes operator new throw std::bad_alloc, and with no handler the process terminates. On Linux with overcommit, the zero-fill instead touches the whole size, and the OOM killer ends the process. The record loop (:426-441) shows the size is wasted: any record with r.size == 0 or r.offset != end stops the loop, and offsets are contiguous from 32, so at most datSize-32 records can survive. That makes clamping count to (datSize-32), or reading in bounded chunks, safe. Ledger: F-036 (README.md:87) and the matching findings_p3p4.json entry cover only the offset+size wrap inside the per-record loop, now fixed at :430-431. P0_MAP.md:334 describes LoadIndex validation but does not raise the idxSize allocation. Neither is this finding, so it is not a duplicate. The file is under the user's Cache dir and persists, so the abort repeats at every boot while a cache consumer is on. Recorded as confirmed on static reasoning. A unit test (Store::Open over a temp dir with a sparse derived.idx after a valid header) would turn it into a reproducer, but the defect does not depend on that test.
verdict.minimal_fix: In Store::LoadIndex, before the allocation at derived_cache.cpp:419-420, clamp the record count to what derived.dat can back. Each surviving record needs at least one payload byte, so `uint64_t count = (idxSize - kHeaderSize) / sizeof(IndexRecord); count = std::min<uint64_t>(count, static_cast<uint64_t>(datSize) - kHeaderSize);` is safe; a comment should say why (a forged or sparse index length must not size an allocation). The later `records.size() != all.size() || idxSize != indexEnd` test (:461-462) already truncates the index to the valid prefix in the writable case. An alternative is to read and validate records in bounded chunks. Add a unit test in ext_derived_cache_test that opens a store whose derived.idx has a valid header followed by a large sparse tail.

confirmed.title: PackageCache::Decode does not check that a node's value entry names the same path as its key (nor the node count), and a payload Decode refuses is never replaced
confirmed.bug_class: incomplete validation of a cached structure
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: Decode validates only `ValidEntry(packs, keyPack, keyFile) || !ValidEntry(packs, valuePack, valueFile)`, the children bits, a depth <= 64, and strict in-order key order (InOrderStrict). The value pair is taken as is: `const RtIO::PackfileIndexPair pair{ packs[keyPack].entries[keyFile].name, { valuePack, valueFile } };`. A node keyed "a.rsc" whose value points at the entry for "b.rsc" passes, and so does a tree that omits entries (nodes < distinct names). The mounted directory then silently resolves paths to the wrong entry or to nothing. The loop always pairs a key with an entry of the same _stricmp name, so `StrICmp(key, packs[valuePack].entries[valueFile].name._data) == 0` per node is a cheap complete check. Separately, when Decode does refuse a hash-valid payload, Restore leaves g_pending.valid set and Built Puts a fresh encode. But Store::WriteOne drops any Put whose key is already stored (`if (_stats.writeFailed || Lookup(p.key) != nullptr) return;`, derived_cache.cpp:936), so the bad payload is fetched, hashed and refused at every mount and never healed. Reachable only through a forged or damaged derived.dat whose XXH64 record and payload hashes were recomputed, or a future Encode/Decode skew without a kVersion bump.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit (tests/unit ext_package_cache): Encode a small tree, swap one record's valueFile for another valid entry with a different name (and/or drop the last record and decrement the node count, fixing the children bits), Decode: it returns true. Then Store::Put a corrected payload under the same Key and Find: the old payload comes back.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: minor (hardening: forged local cache only, no UB, values stay in bounds)
verdict.proof:
Read on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>).
(1) src/ext/package_cache/index_codec.cpp Decode (:152-243). Each record is checked with ValidEntry(key), ValidEntry(value), children <= 3, the root/stack invariant (:173-178), depth <= kMaxDepth (:192) and, after the loop, InOrderStrict (:221). InOrderStrict (:59-77) compares only node->element.key._data. The pair is built as `{ packs[keyPack].entries[keyFile].name, { valuePack, valueFile } }` (:197) and nothing compares the value entry's name with the key's. A record keyed "a.rsc" whose value is the in-range entry of "b.rsc" passes every check, so IndexFind("a.rsc") then resolves to b's pack/file. The values stay in range, so this is a wrong-file result, not a memory error. Encode (:107-150) always writes a value whose entry has the key's name (case-insensitively; the key buffer can come from an earlier pack than the winning value). So `rtcrt::StrICmp(key, packs[valuePack].entries[valueFile].name._data) == 0` holds for every real payload and is a safe extra check.
(2) Never healed. package_cache.cpp Restore (:78-104) sets g_pending.valid = true before Find. When Decode refuses a payload whose hash is valid, it returns false with valid still set. Built (:106-120) then Encodes and calls store->Put(g_pending.key, ...). Store::WriteOne (derived_cache.cpp:936) does `if (_stats.writeFailed || Lookup(p.key) != nullptr) return;`. Store::Find (:724-774) drops a record only when its payload hash does not match (:752-766). So a payload that passes the hash but fails Decode stays stored forever: every mount fetches it, hashes it, refuses it and rebuilds the directory by the loop. The cache benefit is lost for good.
Reachability: only a forged derived.dat with recomputed XXH64 hashes, the same local-cache threat model already accepted for F-037. The finding is not a duplicate: F-037 covers tree shape and depth (now kMaxDepth), not key/value consistency or the no-replace path. The omitted-entries half (node count lower than the number of distinct names) is real but weaker. key.shape[1] counts entries, not distinct names, so a cheap check needs the distinct-name count and was not part of this proof. Under the campaign ruling this is hostile non-UB input, so it gets plain hardening.
verdict.minimal_fix: In Decode, after the ValidEntry checks, refuse the record (FreeAll, return false) when rtcrt::StrICmp(packs[keyPack].entries[keyFile].name._data, packs[valuePack].entries[valueFile].name._data) != 0. For healing, have Restore drop the record when Decode refuses the payload, through a Store method that erases that key's record and adds its size to garbage (the path Find already takes on a hash mismatch), so that Built's Put is stored. Optionally, compare `nodes` with the distinct-name count of the packs. Add unit cases to ext_package_cache_test: a swapped value entry must be refused, and a re-Put after a refused Decode must replace the payload.

confirmed.title: ext.terrain_edit: Undo removes a planted resource by comparing raw entity addresses, so a different entity later allocated at the same address on that cell is removed (ABA)
confirmed.bug_class: dangling pointer compared as identity (C1 side table outlives the entity)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: PlantStroke records `g_undo.RecordPlanted(idx, reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(entity))` (line 1210). UndoLast later does `ComponentEntity* standing = map->cells.GetData()[p.cell].occupant.Get(); if (standing != nullptr && reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(standing) == p.entity) { RemoveNaturalResource(standing); ...}` (lines 1585-1589). The comment says a resource 'chopped, mined or replaced since is left alone'. That holds only if the freed 0x48-byte ComponentEntity block is never reused. Every ComponentEntity is MemAlloc(0x48, 8) (PlantAt :1144, componententity.cpp:722), so a tree cut by a woodcutter and a sapling a forester then plants on the same cell can occupy the same block. The undo then marks the forester's sapling (or any new occupant at that address) for removal. A stroke stays undoable for up to kMaxUndoStrokes = 30 strokes and indefinitely in time. ComponentEntity carries `_entityId` (+0x18), which would tell the two apart.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit-level: plant with the Plant tool, RemoveEntity the planted tree, allocate a new ComponentEntity of the same description (the allocator hands back the freed block) and place it on that cell, then UndoLast: the new entity is removed. In game: plant trees inside a forester's radius, let woodcutters clear them and the forester replant, then press Undo. Fix: record the entity's _entityId (or a handle) alongside the pointer and require both to match.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: logic (ext.terrain_edit only, default OFF; wrongly removes one natural resource, no crash or UB)
verdict.proof:
Not refuted, and not in the ledger. A grep of docs/history/review_20261103 (README, P0_MAP, findings_p3p4.json, findings_p8.json) finds no terrain_edit planted/undo identity entry. S-017 has the same C1 shape (an address-keyed latch, ABA), but it concerns GameUpdateLoop::Load, so this finding is not a duplicate of it. P0_MAP lists f9178b6a0 (the refused-undo flag cleared in ForgetWorld), which is a different defect.

The code supports the mechanism:
- terrain_undo.h:38-41: `struct PlantedResource { int cell; uintptr_t entity; }`. The comment says "compared, never dereferenced". The stroke stores only the raw address and holds no reference.
- brush_tool.cpp:1144-1146 (PlantAt): the entity comes from `MemAlloc(0x48, 8)`. 1210: `g_undo.RecordPlanted(idx, reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(entity))`.
- brush_tool.cpp:1583-1589 (UndoLast): `standing = cells[p.cell].occupant.Get(); if (standing != nullptr && reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(standing) == p.entity) RemoveNaturalResource(standing);`. The comment at 1580-1581 says a resource "chopped, mined or replaced since is left alone".
- The stack is cleared only by ForgetWorld (brush_tool.cpp:143-151), which runs on a world change: a different map, height buffer or stride, or a new lock epoch. Nothing clears it as game time passes. Up to kMaxUndoStrokes = 30 strokes stay undoable (terrain_undo.h:27, 178), and the simulation keeps running in between.

So the "replaced since" promise holds only while the freed 0x48 block is not handed back for a new occupant of the same cell. An example: a woodcutter chops the planted tree, its ComponentEntity is freed, and a forester's sapling (also MemAlloc(0x48, 8), componententity.cpp:722) lands at the same address on that cell. Undo then removes the sapling. ComponentEntity::_entityId (+0x18) would tell the two apart.

Why this is not CONFIRMED: the wrong removal needs the bin allocator to return that exact block to an entity placed on that exact cell. That is plausible (S-017 notes the LIFO bin head) but depends on allocation order. A reader cannot check it line by line, and no test, fuzz input or sanitizer report exists yet. Suggested test: plant through PlantAt, RemoveEntity the tree, construct a new ComponentEntity (the allocator returns the freed block), place it on that cell, call UndoLast, and assert the new entity still stands.
verdict.minimal_fix: Record the entity's _entityId with the address (PlantedResource { int cell; uintptr_t entity; uint32_t entityId; }), filled from entity->_entityId in PlantStroke. In UndoLast, require both the address and standing->_entityId to match before RemoveNaturalResource. Reading _entityId of the live occupant is safe because `standing` is the cell's current, valid occupant. Change only ext.terrain_edit; nothing on the faithful path changes.

proof_run.proof:
A failing unit test confirms the finding. The test is tests/unit/review_terrain_undo_aba_test.cpp, in worktree <worktree>, built with `tools/build.sh unit debug --jobs 2` on base fa150cf7f.

What the test does:
1. It starts the real System::MemoryAllocator (Startup(1,0), as ext_heap_slack_test does).
2. It allocates 64 live 0x48/8 blocks, then the "planted" block (PlantAt's MemAlloc(0x48, 8)), then 64 more.
3. It records the planted block through UndoStack::RecordPlanted (cell, address), as PlantStroke does.
4. It frees the planted block (the woodcutter chops the tree), then allocates the next 0x48/8 block (the forester's sapling).
5. It applies UndoLast's exact predicate: `standing != nullptr && reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(standing) == p.entity`.

Observed output:
`[aba] planted=0000021903d71408 sapling=0000021903d71408 undoRemoves=1`
`FAIL ...review_terrain_undo_aba_test.cpp:51: !undoRemoves`
Totals: 2000 tests, 1 failure (this one).

The allocator hands the freed block straight back on the next same-size allocation (LIFO), even with live neighbours on both sides. So Undo would call RemoveNaturalResource on the new occupant. This breaks the promise in the comment that a resource "chopped, mined or replaced since is left alone".

Caveat on the verifier's suggested fix: ComponentEntity::_entityId (+0x18) is not a stable identity. It is the master-array index. EntityList sets it to masterArray._size on register (componententity.cpp:681). Swap-removal rewrites it when another entity is removed (entitylist.cpp:1439, 1618). So a planted tree's id can change, which would make Undo refuse a tree that is still standing. A new entity can also get both the same address and the same id.

A sound identity already exists. Object::Internal::_generation (+0x0c, `GetGeneration()`, Internal.h:552/560) is drawn from InternalFactory::_random.Rand() when each object is born. It is the generation half of the {index, generation} pair that save pointers use. Reading it has no side effect.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
Change only ext.terrain_edit, which is off by default, so the faithful path is untouched.
- terrain_undo.h: add a field so the struct is `struct PlantedResource { int cell; uintptr_t entity; uint32_t generation; };`, and add a generation argument to RecordPlanted.
- PlantStroke: record `entity->GetGeneration()` along with the address.
- UndoLast: remove `standing` only when `reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(standing) == p.entity && standing->GetGeneration() == p.generation`. `standing` is the cell's live occupant, so reading it is safe.

Do not use `_entityId`. It is the master-array index and swap-removal rewrites it. Extend the unit test so it writes distinct generations into the two blocks and checks that the predicate no longer matches.

confirmed.title: fix/ext.restricted_foods save-tail Decode has no cap on the entry count and a quadratic duplicate check, so a crafted save hangs the load
confirmed.bug_class: hostile input: unbounded quadratic work (DoS)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: Decode bounds `count` only by `count > r.left / kMinEntryBytes` (line 81; kMinEntryBytes = 6). For every entry it compares the folded path against every earlier one: `for (const std::string& seen : folded) { if (seen == key) return false; }` (lines 96-99). The save tail has no payload size limit (savetail.h payloadLength is a u32), so a payload of N bytes yields up to N/6 one-byte-path entries and about (N/6)^2/2 string comparisons. 6 MB gives about 5e11 comparisons, and the load never finishes. The sibling codec item_priority/save_state.cpp caps the same loop with `count > kMaxItems` (4096). restricted_foods has no such cap. The payload is CRC-checked, but the CRC is not a secret (it is recomputed by the writer).
confirmed.repro_idea: Fuzz/unit: call Codec().decode on a v1 payload of u32 count=1,000,000 followed by 1e6 entries {kind 1, len 1, distinct byte}. The bytes can only vary over 0x20..0xFF, so make the paths distinct with 2-3 byte paths. Decode runs for minutes. Fix: cap count (e.g. 4096, as item_priority) and/or use an unordered_set for the folded keys.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: resource (hostile shared .sav: load hangs, no memory-safety impact)
verdict.proof:
Not refuted. The code matches the finding on origin/main (<worktree>, last touched by 1da67b67d). It is not in the ledger: P0_MAP.md:272 only lists restricted_foods/save_state.cpp:118 as a codec entry point, and README P4 reports "savetail ... clean". libFuzzer's default input length is small, so a 20-minute run would not reach a multi-MB quadratic input. No F-/S- row covers it.

Reasoning, line by line:
(1) ExtSave_ReadTail (src/game/Game/gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp ~810) reads every byte from the block-1 position to the end of the decompressed stream into `bytes(size - pos)`. There is no size cap.
(2) SaveTail::Decode (savetail.cpp:128-134) accepts any u32 payloadLength that fits in the body. The trailer CRC is recomputed by any writer, so it is not a barrier.
(3) restricted_foods Decode bounds `count` only by `count > r.left / kMinEntryBytes` (save_state.cpp:81, kMinEntryBytes = 6). There is no kMaxItems cap. The sibling item_priority/save_state.cpp:100 has `count > kMaxItems (4096)`.
(4) Each entry passes PathIsValid (length 1..1024, bytes >= 0x20). It is then Fold()-ed and compared against every earlier folded key with a linear loop (lines 96-100), and only then pushed. Every entry must be distinct after folding, or Decode returns false early. Distinct folded 3-byte paths number about 198^3, roughly 7.7M, so they are plentiful. Each such entry is 1+4+3 = 8 bytes.
(5) An 8 MB payload therefore gives about 1e6 entries and about 5e11 std::string == calls. Each call checks the size (equal), then memcmp of 3 bytes, a few ns each. That is about 15-40 minutes of single-threaded work on the load path before ReplaceBlockedPaths, so the load effectively hangs (the hang watchdog may fire).

A note on step (5): this is a timing claim, so the campaign's proof standard requires a measured test, not arithmetic alone. Hence needs_build_proof, not confirmed.

Suggested proof: a unit test in tests/unit/ext_restricted_foods_test.cpp that builds a v1 payload of 1,000,000 distinct 3-byte paths and times Codec().decode.
verdict.minimal_fix: In src/ext/restricted_foods/save_state.cpp, add `constexpr uint32_t kMaxItems = 4096;` (a list longer than any town's materials is damage), mirroring item_priority. Then change line 81 to `if (count > kMaxItems || count > r.left / kMinEntryBytes) return false;` and update the wire-format comment to read `u32 count 0..kMaxItems`. Optionally replace the linear folded-key scan with a std::unordered_set<std::string>. The cap alone bounds the work to about 8M comparisons. Plain hardening: hostile non-UB input, ext code, no NOT RETAIL comment needed beyond the existing file header.

proof_run.proof:

What it does: it builds a v1 payload of 60,000 distinct 3-byte paths. The path bytes are 0x80..0xFF, so folding to lower case cannot make two of them equal. Each entry is 8 bytes, so the payload is 480,004 bytes. The test then times `Codec().decode` and checks that it takes under 1 s.

confirmed.title: fix.cancel_refund: a ComponentEntity built for an overflow pile is leaked when its material has no RawMaterialComponent
confirmed.bug_class: leak on error path
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: PlaceOverflow: `void* mem = MemAlloc(0x48, 8); ComponentEntity* pile = ::new (mem) ComponentEntity(material); Object::InternalPtr<ComponentEntity> hold(pile); RawMaterialComponent* raw = pile->FindComponent<RawMaterialComponent>(); if (raw == nullptr) break;`. On that break the constructed entity and its components are neither registered nor destroyed and freed. InternalPtr does not own (CheckPtr/AssignId are no-ops), so the block leaks. terrain_edit's PlantAt (brush_tool.cpp:1150) has the same pattern (`if (nr == nullptr || model == nullptr) return nullptr;`), but there the description is pre-checked, so it is unreachable. Reachable here only for a cost material whose template lacks a RawMaterialComponent (a mod template), so the impact is small.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit: PlaceOverflow with a ComponentDescription that has no RawMaterial sub-description and a free rim cell. With a counting allocator or LSan, one 0x48 block plus its components leak per call. Fix: test the description for a RawMaterialDescription before allocating, or destroy and MemFree the entity on the break.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: minor (needs mod data to reach; one leaked 0x48 ComponentEntity plus its components per scatter call)
verdict.proof:
Checked line by line against origin/main (<worktree>). Neither the ledger (docs/history/review_20261103/) nor any later commit mentions cancel_refund or PlaceOverflow, so this is not a duplicate.

1. src/ext/cancel_refund/cancel_refund.cpp lines 66-71: `MemAlloc(0x48, 8)`, then a placement-new `ComponentEntity(material)` (which builds the entity's components from the template), then `Object::InternalPtr<ComponentEntity> hold(pile)`, then `if (raw == nullptr) break;`.
2. InternalPtr does not own anything. src/engine/object/Internal.h:354-362 has `~InternalPtr() = default;` over InternalBasePtr's eight bytes, so it frees nothing. On the break the entity is never registered (RegisterEntity at line 76 is skipped), never destroyed and never freed. Nothing else holds a pointer to it, so the memory leaks.
3. The path can be reached. The only caller is DestroyComponent::ScatterContents (src/game/Component/destroycomponent_states.cpp:425-430). It calls PlaceOverflow when `remaining > 0 && Ext::Fix().cancel_refund`, and it computes `rmDesc = FindRawMatDescInTemplate(tmpl)`, which may be null (`weight = rmDesc ? rmDesc->_weight : 0`). PileSize's `weight <= 0` branch shows that a null rmDesc was expected there.
   - The faithful footprint loop above it only dereferences rmDesc (`100 / rmDesc->_weight`, retail 0x14011ca59) on a valid cell: blocker null, terrainType 2, height in [0, 0.2).
   - So if the footprint has no valid cell (for example, every cell is non-land terrain), a cost or storage material whose template has no RawMaterialDescription gets through to PlaceOverflow with its full `remaining`.
   - FindDropCell then finds a rim cell, an entity is built, FindComponent<RawMaterialComponent> returns null (the template has no RawMaterial sub-description), and the code breaks out of the loop: one leak per call.
   - Vanilla cost materials are all raw materials, so only mod templates hit this. fix.cancel_refund is ON by default (fix.*), so the faithful profile alone does not avoid it.

It is not undefined behaviour and not port drift: retail drops the overflow and never runs this ext code. It is plain hardening under the campaign rulings. Optional build proof: a unit test that runs PlaceOverflow with a template that has no RawMaterialDescription, under a counting allocator or LSan.
verdict.minimal_fix: Do not allocate when the template has no RawMaterialDescription. In ScatterContents (destroycomponent_states.cpp:425), change the condition to `if (remaining > 0 && Ext::Fix().cancel_refund && rmDesc != nullptr)`. Alternatively, in PlaceOverflow, check the description before MemAlloc. Destroying and freeing the entity on the break also removes the leak, but the pre-check is simpler and never builds an entity it would only throw away.

confirmed.title: ext.terrain_edit: signed overflow in `start + count` lets a saved water draw range read past _contourIndices
confirmed.bug_class: UB-signed-overflow -> heap out-of-bounds read
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: Status SUSPECTED (found by reading the code). ScanWaterQuads (:305 and :340), GatherRiverCover (:404), GatherUvAnchors (:453) and NearestRiver (:501) all guard a range with `const int start = ranges[r].values[0]; ... const int count = ranges[r].values[3]; if (start < 0 || base < 0 || start + count > terrain->_contourIndices.size) continue;` and then read `idx[start + k]` / `idx[start + k + j]` for k < count. `values[]` are raw int32 loaded from the save (geometry_serialize.cpp:88-100, SerializeDrawRanges for _contourRangesA/B) with no check. With start = 0x7FFFFF00 and count = 0x200, `start + count` is signed overflow (UB). In practice it wraps negative, the guard passes, and the loop reads idx[0x7FFFFF00 + k], about 4 GB past the uint16 array. Retail only passes these ranges to the GPU (geometry_draw.cpp DrawContourRange), so this CPU read is new in the ext. Minimal fix: compare in 64 bits (`(int64_t)start + count > size`) or test `count > size - start`, and also reject count < 0.
confirmed.repro_idea: Edit a save (or set the field in a unit harness that builds a WorldGeometry) so that _contourRangesB[0] = {0x7FFFFF00, 0, 0, 0x200}, with a small index and vertex array. Load the save, open the Terrain page and paint one stroke: ScanWaterQuads runs from AddWaterForStroke. Under UBSan, -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow reports brush_tool.cpp:305. Without it, the idx[] read faults. Lifting ScanWaterQuads out of the anonymous namespace (or calling it through FinishStroke) would allow a fuzz target over the four range values.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: memory (hostile save only; ext.terrain_edit is off by default, so faithful play is not affected)
verdict.proof:
The bug is real. This was checked by reading the code in <worktree> on origin/main; nothing was built or run.

1. A save can set any range value. src/game/Game/geometry_serialize.cpp:88-100 (SerializeDrawRanges, called at :288-289 for _contourRangesA and _contourRangesB) reads the count and then four raw int32 per record, with no check on the values.

2. The guard can overflow. src/ext/terrain_edit/brush_tool.cpp:302-305 (ScanWaterQuads) sets `start = values[0]`, `base = values[1]`, `count = values[3]`, then tests `if (start < 0 || base < 0 || start + count > terrain->_contourIndices.size) continue;`. The guard only requires start >= 0. Nothing bounds count above. So with start = 0x7FFFFF00 and count = 0x200, `start + count` is greater than INT_MAX. That is signed overflow, which is UB. On the usual wrap it becomes negative, the test passes, and the loop at :306-308 reads `idx[start + k]` far past the uint16 _contourIndices buffer.

3. The same guard appears four more times: :340 (river ranges in ScanWaterQuads), :404 (GatherRiverCover), :453 (GatherUvAnchors) and :501 (NearestRiver).

4. A negative count is harmless. The loop condition `k + 5 < count` is false at once, so nothing is read.

5. The path is new in the ext. Retail only hands these ranges to the GPU, so there is no retail behaviour to preserve here.

Ledger check: the CodeQL triage (static/codeql_size_taint_triage.tsv rows 291 and 448) flags only the array count `c` in SerializeDrawRanges, not the per-record start/count values or the ext's guard. No F-, S- or P0_MAP entry covers ScanWaterQuads or these guards. The terrain_edit P0_MAP note (f9178b6a0, ForgetWorld and the undo flag) is a different defect. So this is not a duplicate.

Each line of the proof can be checked by reading. Run evidence (a UBSan report or a unit test that builds a WorldGeometry with these values) would still strengthen the ledger entry.
verdict.minimal_fix: Apply the same change at all five guards in src/ext/terrain_edit/brush_tool.cpp (:305, :340, :404, :453, :501). Replace `start + count > terrain->_contourIndices.size` with `count < 0 || count > terrain->_contourIndices.size - start`. This is safe because start >= 0 is already checked and size >= 0, so the subtraction cannot overflow. A 64-bit compare also works: `(int64_t)start + count > terrain->_contourIndices.size`. This is a hardening fix for hostile non-UB input, but it also removes UB, so per the campaign rule it carries a short "NOT RETAIL:" comment. It changes nothing on the faithful path.

confirmed.title: ext.terrain_edit: `base + idx[...]` can overflow negative and pass the `v >= size` check, so verts[] is read at a negative index
confirmed.bug_class: UB-signed-overflow -> heap out-of-bounds read (negative index)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: Status SUSPECTED (found by reading the code). GatherRiverCover (:407), GatherUvAnchors (:456) and NearestRiver (:504) compute `for (int j = 0; j < 3; ++j) v[j] = base + idx[start + k + j];` and then only check `if (v[0] >= terrain->_contourVertices.size || ...) continue;`. There is no lower bound. The river-range edit check in ScanWaterQuads (:341, `if (base + idx[start] >= terrain->_contourVertices.size) continue;` followed by `verts[base + idx[start]]` at :342) has the same gap. `base` (values[1]) is a raw int32 from the save, checked only for `base >= 0`. With base = INT32_MAX - 10 and an index word above 10, the add is signed overflow (UB). In practice it wraps to a large negative v, which passes `v >= size`, and `verts[v[j]].position[0]` reads about 32 GB before the vertex array. The quad scan at :314/:351 does test `v < 0`, which shows the triangle paths lack the same check. A retail-mirrored path does not exist here: retail does not read contour vertices on the CPU through these ranges.
confirmed.repro_idea: Edit a save so that _contourRangesA[0] = {0, 0x7FFFFFF5, 3, 3}, the first three contour indices are {0x20, 0x21, 0x22} and the vertex array is small. Load it, start the brush and paint a stroke that makes water: AddWaterForStroke calls NearestRiver, then GatherRiverCover. UBSan's signed-integer-overflow check fires at :504 or :407; without it the verts[] read faults. Fix: compute v in int64 and reject v < 0 as well as v >= size.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low-medium: an out-of-bounds heap read (negative index) from a hostile save. It needs ext.terrain_edit switched ON (off by default) and a brush stroke. Faithful play is unaffected.
verdict.proof:
Read on origin/main fa150cf7f. I could not refute it. The ledger has no entry for it: docs/history/review_20261103 mentions terrain_edit only for f9178b6a0 (undo flag) and the S-0xx Metal replaceRegion entry. Nothing on main fixes it.

1) The input is raw. geometry_serialize.cpp:88-100 SerializeDrawRanges reads `values[0..3]` of _contourRangesA and _contourRangesB from the save, each as int32, and nothing validates them. WorldGeometry::BuildWaterBodies, the only producer of sane `values[1] = vtxAcc->size` (water_contour_mesh.cpp:606/674), runs only from the generator at :773. Load keeps the saved ranges, and nothing in src/game rechecks `values[1]`.

2) The arithmetic overflows. brush_tool.cpp GatherRiverCover (:407), GatherUvAnchors (:456) and NearestRiver (:504) each compute `v[j] = base + idx[start+k+j]`. `base` is an int that is only checked `>= 0`, and `idx` is a uint16_t promoted to int. With base > INT32_MAX - idx the add is signed overflow (UB). The bounds check that follows is only `v[j] >= _contourVertices.size`. A wrapped negative v passes it, and `verts[v[j]].position/uv/normal` reads before the array. ScanWaterQuads' river branch (:341-342) has the same one-sided check before `verts[base + idx[start]]`.

3) The finding is slightly off on one point. The quad loops at :314 and :351 do test `v < 0`, but only after the same overflowing `base + idx` add, so the UB is there too. The fix should cover those sites as well.

4) The path is reachable. With the ext ON, FinishStroke (:1001) calls AddWaterForStroke. That calls ScanWaterQuads (:582), NearestRiver (:637) and GatherRiverCover (:676) over every _contourRangesA entry, and none of these screens `base`. No retail mirror exists, because this is ext code that reads GPU contour data on the CPU, so no Ghidra diff applies.

A UBSan run on a crafted save with _contourRangesA[0] = {0, 0x7FFFFFF5, 3, 3} and indices {0x20,0x21,0x22} would turn this into a sanitizer proof, but the line-by-line reasoning above does not depend on one.
verdict.minimal_fix: In brush_tool.cpp, compute each vertex index as `const int64_t v = static_cast<int64_t>(base) + idx[...]` and reject it when `v < 0 || v >= _contourVertices.size`. That covers GatherRiverCover, GatherUvAnchors, NearestRiver, ScanWaterQuads' river first-vertex check (:341) and both quad corner loops (:314, :351). A simpler alternative: skip any range whose `base > _contourVertices.size`. Then `base + idx` is at most size + 65535, which cannot overflow, and the existing `>= size` checks become sufficient. This is plain hardening of hostile input, not retail code.

confirmed.title: fix.foundation_piles writes one uncapped stderr line per pile it moves, in shipped builds
confirmed.bug_class: log on a sim path (AGENTS.md section 3)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: Relocate() ends every successful move with an unconditional `std::fprintf(stderr, "[FoundationPiles] pile %p (%d) at %d,%d -> %d,%d (site %d,%d %dx%d)\n", ...); return 2;`. The row is a fix, default ON. The call runs from ClearArea::Execute phase 3 (cleararea.cpp:655), once for each pile it moves. log_strip.h removes only unqualified printf, so this fprintf(stderr) is in the perf and release builds, and each line is a file write to standalone_error.log. AGENTS.md section 3 says a stderr line on a sim path must sit under _DEBUG, behind an Opt() field that defaults off, or under a hard cap on its total count. The two sibling fix rows in this area do this: cancel_refund.cpp:31-32,82 and stranded_wade.cpp:41-42,388 both use `s_logged < kLogCap` with kLogCap = 16 and cite AGENTS.md section 3. foundation_piles has no cap, so the number of lines over a session grows with the number of piles moved. The line also prints a heap address (%p), so two runs of one save cannot be diffed. Status: SUSPECTED (found by reading the code; no failing test).
confirmed.repro_idea: Start a town and fill every storage. Place a town hall over a dense patch of trees and rocks, and let the foresters and stonecutters fell and cut it so the footprint holds only logs and stone. Run the release exe (tools/build.sh build release, functional game dir). Grep standalone_error.log for '[FoundationPiles]': one line for each pile moved, with no ceiling. Fix: copy cancel_refund's `static int s_logged; constexpr int kLogCap = 16; if (s_logged < kLogCap) { ++s_logged; ... }` around the fprintf.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: minor
verdict.proof:
Checked line by line against origin/main (<worktree>):
1. src/ext/foundation_piles/foundation_piles.cpp:201-204: Relocate() ends every successful relocation with an unconditional `std::fprintf(stderr, "[FoundationPiles] pile %p (%d) at ...", ...); return 2;`. No _DEBUG, no Opt() gate and no counter anywhere in the file. A grep for fprintf/s_logged/kLogCap/_DEBUG/Opt() in the file finds only line 201.
2. src/app/log_strip.h:12 and :29 only `#define printf(...) ((void)0)`. The comment there says fprintf(stderr) is not stripped, so the line ships in the perf and release builds.
3. The row is ON by default: src/ext/registry.h:72 has `bool foundation_piles = true;` and registry.cpp:130 registers it as Tier::Fix, default true.
4. It runs on the sim path: src/game/Work/cleararea.cpp:626 gates on Ext::Fix().foundation_piles, and :655 calls Relocate() once for each pile tile in ClearArea phase 3. Each time Relocate returns 2, one stderr line is written. The total over a session has no limit.
5. The two sibling fix rows put a hard cap on the same kind of event line and cite AGENTS.md §3: cancel_refund.cpp:30-32,82 and stranded_wade.cpp:40-42,388 (`s_logged < kLogCap`, kLogCap = 16). foundation_piles has no such cap.
6. The line prints a heap pointer (%p), so the logs of two runs cannot be diffed.
7. The line is not in the ledger: grepping docs/history/review_20261103 for FoundationPiles or foundation_piles finds nothing.

Caveat: this fires once per relocation event, not once per tick or frame, so it is a cheap rule breach rather than a perf problem. It still breaks the AGENTS.md §3 rule that a shipped stderr line on a sim path needs a gate or a hard total cap, and the sibling rows read the rule that way.
verdict.minimal_fix: In foundation_piles.cpp, add file-scope `static int s_logged = 0; constexpr int kLogCap = 16;` with the comment "One stderr line per relocation, for the first few only (AGENTS.md §3)." Wrap the fprintf at :201-203 in `if (s_logged < kLogCap) { ++s_logged; std::fprintf(...); }`. This mirrors cancel_refund.cpp:30-32,82. Sim behaviour does not change.
