confirmed.title: restricted_foods save-tail Decode has no list cap and checks for duplicates in O(n^2): a crafted save blocks the load for minutes to hours
confirmed.bug_class: resource-exhaustion / algorithmic DoS on hostile save input
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: CONFIRMED (timing test). Decode only bounds the entry count by the payload size: `if (count > r.left / kMinEntryBytes) return false;` (line 81, kMinEntryBytes = 6). Every entry is then compared against all earlier ones: `const std::string key = Fold(path); for (const std::string& seen : folded) { if (seen == key) return false; } folded.push_back(key);` (lines 95-101). The sister codec item_priority/save_state.cpp:100 caps the list at `kMaxItems = 4096` ("a list longer than any town's materials is damage"); restricted_foods has no such cap. SaveTail::ApplyState (savetail.cpp:253-262) runs this decode for any save that carries a "restricted_foods" record, whether the row is on or off. The save tail's payload length is limited only by the save file. Timings from the standalone program (scratchpad rf/t.cpp, g++ -O2, linking save_state.cpp and restricted_foods.cpp only, distinct short paths, all accepted): n=10000 (89 KB) 0.10 s; n=20000 (189 KB) 0.31 s; n=40000 (389 KB) 1.32 s; n=160000 (1.65 MB) 17.61 s. That is quadratic, so a 16 MB tail (about 1.6M entries) takes about 30 minutes, and paths of up to 1024 bytes with a shared prefix make each compare a full memcmp. The decoded list then also goes through RestrictedFoods::Resolve, which runs IsPathBlocked (a Fold of every path) once for each Edible material. Saves are shared between players and the Android build imports .sav files from user-picked zips (P0_MAP section 3).
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit test in tests/unit/ext_restricted_foods_test.cpp: build a v1 payload with u32 count = 200000, then count x {u8 1, u32 len, decimal path}, call Codec().decode(p.data(), p.size(), 1) under a time budget (e.g. 1 s) and expect it to be refused or to finish quickly. It currently takes about 25 s. End to end: append a SaveTail record "restricted_foods" v1 with that payload to a .sav (fix the trailer CRC) and load it: the load stalls, and the hang watchdog may report it. Suggested fix: a kMaxItems cap as in item_priority, and/or an unordered_set of folded keys.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (resource / algorithmic DoS on a hostile save; no memory corruption)
verdict.proof:
Refutation failed. Each step can be checked line by line in <worktree>:
1. src/ext/restricted_foods/save_state.cpp:81 bounds the entry count only by `count > r.left / kMinEntryBytes` (kMinEntryBytes = 6, :39). There is no absolute cap. The sister codec src/ext/item_priority/save_state.cpp:44,100 has `kMaxItems = 4096` with `count > kMaxItems ||`, and restricted_foods has nothing like it.
2. In :95-101 every entry Folds its path and compares it linearly against every earlier folded key (`for (const std::string& seen : folded) if (seen == key) return false;`). With n distinct paths that is n(n-1)/2 string compares. Each compare costs up to 1024 bytes (kMaxPathBytes, :38) when the paths share a long prefix.
3. Reachability: ExtSave_ReadTail (src/game/Game/gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:810-) reads every byte after the last Serialize of block 1, which is bounded only by the save container. Ext::SaveTail::Decode (src/ext/savetail.cpp:82-140) caps only the id length (kMaxIdLength = 64). payloadLength is any u32 that fits in the body. SaveTail::ApplyState (savetail.cpp:253-262) then calls the codec's decode for each record with a registered StateCodec, "restricted_foods" included. The block is compressed, so a multi-MB tail can come from a small file. Saves are shared between players and imported on Android (P0_MAP §3 "Exposure").
4. The finder's timing harness exists at scratchpad/rf/t.cpp (+ t.exe). Its reported numbers (0.10 s / 0.31 s / 1.32 s / 17.6 s for 10k / 20k / 40k / 160k entries) are quadratic, which matches the loop.

README P4 records "savetail ... clean", but that covered crashes; a libFuzzer run with the default max_len would never reach the sizes this needs. Not fixed on origin/main: the code above is the current state.
Off-switch note: the decode runs whenever a save carries the record. With the row off, Validate/ExtSave_Fatal or the LockKeepsRequest filter may drop the record first. That does not refute the finding, because a crafted save names the row and the town loads with it locked on.
verdict.minimal_fix: In src/ext/restricted_foods/save_state.cpp, add `constexpr uint32_t kMaxItems = 4096;` (the same cap item_priority uses, since no town has more foods than that) and change :81 to `if (count > kMaxItems || count > r.left / kMinEntryBytes) return false;`. Also update the wire-format comment to `u32 count 0..kMaxItems`. Optionally replace the linear duplicate scan with a std::unordered_set<std::string> of folded keys. Add a unit test in tests/unit/ext_restricted_foods_test.cpp that checks a payload with count = kMaxItems + 1 is refused and that one at kMaxItems decodes.

confirmed.title: terrain_edit water-mesh scans overflow int on save-loaded contour ranges (start+count, base+idx) and read verts/idx out of bounds
confirmed.bug_class: signed overflow in a bounds check, then out-of-bounds read, on save-controlled ranges
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (no sanitizer run). WorldGeometry::Serialize loads _contourRangesA/_contourRangesB from the save with four raw int32 values per range and no validation (geometry_serialize.cpp:88-99 SerializeDrawRanges, called from gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:715). Retail uses these ranges only as GPU draw arguments. The terrain brush walks them on the CPU with checks that overflow before they test anything. GatherRiverCover (lines 404, 407): `if (start < 0 || base < 0 || start + count > terrain->_contourIndices.size) continue;` then `v[j] = base + idx[start + k + j];` and `if (v[0] >= terrain->_contourVertices.size || ...) continue;` with no `v < 0` test. (1) start=0x7FFFFFF0, count=0x20: `start + count` is signed overflow (UB) and in practice wraps negative, so the check passes and `idx[start + k]` reads about 4 GB past the array. (2) base=0x7FFFFFFF with any idx >= 1: `base + idx[...]` overflows to a negative v, which passes the `>=` test, so `verts[v]` reads before the array. The same pattern is in GatherUvAnchors (lines 453, 456), NearestRiver (lines 501, 504) and ScanWaterQuads (lines 305/314/323 for the lake pass, which tests v < 0 only after the UB add; lines 340-342/351/363 for the river pass, where line 342 `verts[base + idx[start]]` has only an upper-bound check). All of them run from AddWaterForStroke, which FinishStroke calls at the end of every height stroke of ext.terrain_edit, so a hostile save crashes as soon as the player paints.
confirmed.repro_idea: Make a save, then patch one _contourRangesA entry in its WorldGeometry block to {0x7FFFFFF0, 0, 0, 0x20} (or set values[1] = 0x7FFFFFFF). Load it with ext.terrain_edit on and paint one Raise stroke near water, under the UBSan/ASan host build or the plain exe (crash in GatherRiverCover / NearestRiver). Minimal fix with a NOT RETAIL comment: do the checks in int64 (`(int64_t)start + count > size`, `int64_t v = (int64_t)base + idx[..]`, and reject v < 0) in the four scanners.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: memory (hostile save only; needs ext.terrain_edit, which is off by default, plus a height stroke)
verdict.proof:
The finding could not be refuted. The code on origin/main fa150cf7f matches the claim, and nothing in the ledger covers it. The ledger only names terrain_edit in two places: F-like P8 Metal replaceRegion (brush_tool.cpp:755 upload) and P0_MAP f9178b6a0 (refused-undo flag). Neither is about the contour-range scans.

The data comes straight from the save. geometry_serialize.cpp:88-99 SerializeDrawRanges reads the count, calls RawArraySetSize and then reads four raw int32 values per range, with no validation. It is called for _contourRangesA and _contourRangesB at lines 288-289. Load does not rebuild them: the only writers are water_contour_mesh.cpp (world build) and serialize_arrays.cpp (clear). Retail uses the ranges only as draw arguments (geometry_draw.cpp:462/474).

The scans in brush_tool.cpp, line by line:
- GatherRiverCover (around line 404) does `if (start < 0 || base < 0 || start + count > terrain->_contourIndices.size) continue;`. Both values are int. With start=0x7FFFFFF0 and count=0x20, `start + count` is signed overflow. The build has no -fwrapv or -fno-strict-overflow (grep of CMakeLists.txt and cmake/ finds nothing), so this is UB, and in practice it wraps negative and passes the check. The next line, `idx[start + k + j]`, then reads about 4 GB past _contourIndices. `start + k + j` itself overflows for k+j >= 0x10.
- `v[j] = base + idx[...]` with base=0x7FFFFFFF and idx >= 1 overflows to a negative number. Only `v >= size` is tested, so `verts[v]` reads before the array.
- GatherUvAnchors and NearestRiver use the same pattern.
- ScanWaterQuads, lake pass: `v < 0` is tested only after the overflowing add.
- ScanWaterQuads, river pass: `if (base + idx[start] >= size)` has no lower-bound check before `verts[base + idx[start]]`.

All four run from AddWaterForStroke (line 575), which FinishStroke calls (line 1001) after every height stroke.

The verdict is needs_build_proof rather than confirmed because the campaign's proof standard asks a memory or UB finding for a failing test, a fuzz input or a sanitizer report. None of those exists yet. The reasoning above is line-checkable and has no gap.
verdict.minimal_fix:
In brush_tool.cpp, ext code only, so faithful behaviour is unchanged. In ScanWaterQuads (both passes), GatherRiverCover, GatherUvAnchors and NearestRiver:
- Change the range check to `if (start < 0 || base < 0 || count < 0 || static_cast<int64_t>(start) + count > terrain->_contourIndices.size) continue;`.
- Compute each vertex as `const int64_t v = static_cast<int64_t>(base) + idx[start + c];` and reject `v < 0 || v >= terrain->_contourVertices.size` before using it.
- Apply the same int64 form to the river-pass first-vertex test, `base + idx[start]`.

This is plain hardening against hostile input, so mark it with a "NOT RETAIL:" comment. A unit test with a WorldGeometry whose range is {0x7FFFFFF0, 0, 0, 0x20} or {0, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0, 6} would supply the missing proof under the UBSan/ASan host build.

proof_run.proof:
CONFIRMED by a sanitizer trap and by plain-build crashes. Tested on origin/main fa150cf7f with the pinned WinLibs GCC 16.2.

Harness: harness.cpp in the proofs dir. run.sh copies the four scanners (ScanWaterQuads, RiverCover + GatherRiverCover, GatherUvAnchors, NearestRiver) out of src/ext/terrain_edit/brush_tool.cpp unchanged and builds them over a WorldGeometry that holds only the four arrays they read: _contourVertices (8 vertices), _contourIndices (12 indices) and one range in each of _contourRangesA and _contourRangesB. It builds two exes, plain -O2 and -O0 with -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow,bounds -fsanitize-undefined-trap-on-error, and runs every scanner under each range:
- mode 0, sane {0,0,0,12}: all scanners exit 0 on both builds.
- mode 1, {0x7FFFFFF0,0,0,0x20}, the start+count overflow:
  - UBSan build: all 4 scanners trap (exit 132, SIGILL).
  - plain -O2: all 4 segfault (exit 139). A first -O2 build of the same code returned garbage results (24 floats) in GatherRiverCover and hung ScanWaterQuads in an infinite loop for 5 minutes of CPU time, which shows the UB-dependent codegen.
- mode 2, {0,0x7FFFFFFF,0,6}: UBSan traps in GatherRiverCover, NearestRiver and GatherUvAnchors (base + idx overflow).
- mode 3, {6,0x7FFFFFFF,0,6}, every index >= 4 so each vertex wraps negative:
  - UBSan build: all 4 trap.
  - plain -O2: all 4 segfault (exit 139), because verts[negative] is read and only `v >= size` is tested.

Log: run_before.log. After the fix (run_after.log), all 32 runs exit 0 on both builds. Mode 0 gives the same results as before (24 floats / 1 / 4 anchors / 1 quad), and the hostile ranges are skipped.

The fixed brush_tool.cpp compiles in the worktree's debug build: build/cmake-debug/CMakeFiles/OpenBA.dir/src/ext/terrain_edit/brush_tool.cpp.o was produced. The full build was stopped after that object to free the machine, so no link and no game run.

Reachability through a real save and a Raise stroke was not exercised in game: no game run.

confirmed.title: find_fastpath StoreRef sizes its ref table by a reference id taken from the save: one id near 2^24 allocates about 400 MB
confirmed.bug_class: unbounded allocation from untrusted input (hostile save, non-UB hardening)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: `if (refId > (1u << 24)) return; ... if (refId >= t.refs.size()) t.refs.resize(static_cast<size_t>(refId) + 1);` where RefEntry is {void*, uint64_t, uint64_t} = 24 bytes. refId comes from SerializeUInt in the mode-2 load arm (external_ptr_serialize.cpp ~line 268-287). Its path comes from the save's own reference table (SerializeReferenceTable fills an id-keyed tree, one node per entry), and StoreRef is reached once that path names an existing row (line 324-325). Retail spends O(entries) on the same save. With the row on, one entry whose id is 16,777,216 makes this table allocate 16,777,217 x 24 bytes, about 403 MB, and keep it for the rest of the process (refs is never shrunk). Any id spacing gives the same dense sizing.
confirmed.repro_idea: Craft a save whose reference table maps id 0x1000000 to a stock resource path that one ExternalPtr in the save references by that id. Load it with ext.find_fastpath on and watch the process working set jump by about 400 MB at the load. Hardening: key refs by a hash map, or cap the dense table at the reference table's entry count, or bound it at a few times the largest id seen so far.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: resource (hostile save, ext.find_fastpath ON only; ~403 MB retained per process)
verdict.proof:
The full path can be checked line by line in <worktree>:
1) src/engine/object/external_reftable.cpp, read path: for each of `count` entries, `rw->SerializeUInt(id)` reads a raw uint32 from the save and `rtrefset::Insert(&refs, &key=id, &keyPath)` inserts it with no range check. A single row {id=0x1000000, path=<a stock resource already loaded>} is therefore accepted.
2) src/engine/Object/external_ptr_serialize.cpp:272-287, mode 2 load: `SerializeUInt(refId)` is read from the save. If refId != 0xFFFFFFFF and the fast row misses (FindRef returns null because refId >= refs.size()), `path = GetPathForReferenceId(refId)` sets `refStore = true` (with an empty path stack) and `refStoreId = refId`.
3) Same file, ~line 322: `found = FindOrLoadAs<External>(path)`. In src/engine/object/external_compiled.cpp:239-246 a cache hit on an already-loaded resource calls `fast->store(*self, path->_data, len, found)`, which puts the request characters into t.chars (find_fastpath.cpp:158-170). Back in external_ptr_serialize, `if (refStore && found) fast->storeRef(*factory, refStoreId, path._data, path.GetLength())` runs.
4) find_fastpath.cpp:194-207: the only bound is `refId > (1u << 24)`, so 0x1000000 gets through. `t.chars.Find(request)` hits, because it is the same string just stored. Then `t.refs.resize(refId + 1)` runs, and RefEntry {void*, uint64_t, uint64_t} is 24 bytes (lines 75-79). That gives 16,777,217 x 24 = ~403 MB of value-initialised storage. Tables is a leaked singleton (T(), lines 88-91), and refs is never shrunk; Event only bumps gen/refGen. Retail's cost on the same save is O(entries).
It is not in the ledger: grep of docs/history/review_20261103 (README/P0_MAP/findings_*.json) finds no StoreRef/refs-sizing entry; P0_MAP only mentions find_fastpath in passing. It is still present on origin/main. It is gated on ext.find_fastpath ON and a non-Faithful profile (Sync, line 246), so faithful behaviour is unaffected. This is hostile-input hardening, not UB.
verdict.minimal_fix: In StoreRef, bound the dense table by what the save can legitimately name instead of the fixed 1<<24 cap. One option is to drop the store when refId exceeds a small multiple of the reference table's entry count (factory->_references._count, which SerializeReferenceTable just set), e.g. `if (refId > 4u * refCount + 1024) return;`. Another is to key refs by an unordered_map<uint32_t, RefEntry> (cleared on the RefTable event) so memory is O(entries). Either way the miss path falls back to GetPathForReferenceId as now, so behaviour is unchanged.

confirmed.title: ext.walk_batch WorldToCell keeps the raw float->int cast that F-160 fixed in moveto.cpp: UB for a saved out-of-range / NaN MoveTo destination or position
confirmed.bug_class: out-of-range float->int conversion (UB)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit test in tests/unit/ext_walk_batch_test.cpp: compare Ext::WalkBatch::WorldToCell(512, x, 0) against ActionBounds::WorldToCellAxis-based moveto WorldToCell for x in {1e10f, -1e10f, NaN, +inf}, and build the unit target with -fsanitize=float-cast-overflow (WSL clang-19). verdict.label: ext

verdict.proof:
Checked against origin/main fa150cf7f in <worktree>. The cited line is wrong: the code is at src/ext/walk_batch/walk_batch_rules.h:32-41, not :125. Everything else in the finding holds.

`Ext::WalkBatch::WorldToCell` does `int cellX = static_cast<int>(worldX + halfMap);` (and the same for Y), with no range check before the conversion. - `walk_batch.cpp:111-112` (`Eligible`) passes `mv->destination.x/y`, which can come from a save, and the model translation. This runs before the faithful `MoveTo::Execute`, so the F-160 fix does not cover this path.

Add a "NOT RETAIL:" comment, as moveto.cpp has. In-range results do not change, and a NaN or out-of-range input then gives the same cell as the faithful Execute (0 or mapSize-1). confirmed.title: ext.find_fastpath StoreRef resizes its ref table to a save-supplied reference id (up to 2^24+1 entries, about 400 MB) from one 4-byte field
confirmed.bug_class: resource exhaustion / allocation amplification from a hostile save
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: find_fastpath.cpp:196 `if (refId > (1u << 24)) return;` ... :203-204 `if (refId >= t.refs.size()) t.refs.resize(static_cast<size_t>(refId) + 1);` where RefEntry (:75-79) is 24 bytes, so refId = 0x1000000 asks for 16,777,217 x 24 B, about 403 MB. The cap is `>`, so 1<<24 itself passes. refId comes from the save: SerializeReferenceTable's read arm takes each id from the stream (external_reftable.cpp: `uint32_t id = 0; rw->SerializeUInt(id, nullptr);`, stored as the row's referenceId). ExternalPtr mode 2 then reads the pointer's id with SerializeUInt (external_ptr_serialize.cpp ~:276) and calls fast->storeRef(refStoreId, ...) after FindOrLoad finds the path (:324-325). Retail's write path numbers ids densely 1..N (external_reftable.cpp write arm), so only a crafted save reaches this. The table is never shrunk, and each later SerializeReferenceTable only bumps refGen. With ext.find_fastpath on, one crafted id in an otherwise valid save costs about 400 MB of committed memory. On a low-memory device (Android) the allocation can fail, and std::bad_alloc aborts the load. SUSPECTED (no test run).
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit test of the hook: call StoreRef(f, 1u << 24, "x", 1) after a Store for "x", then check t.refs.size() / process commit, or measure RSS. In game: hex-edit a save's reference table so one entry carries id 0x01000000 and one ExternalPtr record uses that id, then load with ext.find_fastpath on and watch the commit charge jump by about 400 MB. Fix idea: bound refId by the reference table's entry count (or the resource count), or key the refs by a hash map instead of a dense vector.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: resource (hostile save; about 400 MB committed per load, possible bad_alloc abort on low-memory devices)
verdict.proof:
I could not refute it. The chain below can be checked line by line in <worktree> on origin/main.

(1) ext.find_fastpath is ON by default, not OFF: src/ext/registry.cpp:591 has `{ "find_fastpath", Tier::Extension, Class::A, true, ...`. So a stock install reaches this path, which makes it worse than the finding states.

(2) The id comes from the save. external_ptr_serialize.cpp:272 reads it with `ser._readerWriter->SerializeUInt(refId, nullptr)`, and the only rejection is `refId == kNoReferenceId`. On the reading path (:277-287), a findRef miss sets `refStore = fast != nullptr && _pathStack._size == 0; refStoreId = refId;` with `path = GetPathForReferenceId(refId)`. That lookup is an AVL descent over `_references`, which SerializeReferenceTable fills with ids read from the stream (external_reftable.cpp:210, then `referenceId = id` at :293/:316). Nothing bounds or densifies the ids on load. Only the write path numbers them 1..N.

(3) The id is stored. At :323-325, `found = FindOrLoadAs<External>(path); if (refStore && found != nullptr) fast->storeRef(*factory, refStoreId, ...)`. For an already-cached resource, FindOrLoad's hit arm (external_compiled.cpp:241-246) calls `fast->store(...)` first, so `t.chars.Find(request)` in StoreRef returns a non-null row.

(4) The allocation. find_fastpath.cpp:196 `if (refId > (1u << 24)) return;` lets 0x1000000 through. Then :203-204 `if (refId >= t.refs.size()) t.refs.resize(refId + 1);` value-initialises 16,777,217 RefEntry objects. Each is 24 bytes (void* + 2x uint64_t, :75-79), about 403 MB, and the zeroing commits it. Nothing ever shrinks the table: Event RefTable/Clear only bumps refGen/gen.

Retail has no such table. It keys `_references` by AVL, so an id of 0x1000000 costs one node there. A sparse id is not UB, so this is hostile-input resource amplification in ext code. The fix is plain hardening.

No ledger entry covers it. The README F-/S- rows and the P3/P4/P8 JSONs never mention find_fastpath, StoreRef or refs.resize. The only related rows are F-172 (signed descent in GetPathForReferenceId) and S-018 (PreloadRefs off-by-one), which are different defects. P0_MAP.md:404 mentions find_fastpath only for ResLoadGuard.

The proof is static only. No test or RSS measurement was run. The arithmetic and control flow are direct, though, so a unit test calling StoreRef(f, 1u<<24, "x", 1) after Store("x") would show t.refs.size() == 16777217.
verdict.minimal_fix: In find_fastpath.cpp StoreRef, bound refId by a small dense limit instead of 1<<24, for example `if (refId > (1u << 16)) return;` or a check against the factory's reference count (`f._references` size), so an out-of-range id just skips the cache (FindRef already misses for ids past refs.size()). The alternative is to key refs with a hash map. Faithful behaviour is unchanged either way, because a skipped StoreRef only costs a cache miss.

confirmed.title: phone_menu ReleaseHeld reads a closed dialog after it was freed (h.dialog->_ui), and with address reuse it can write through a freed element
confirmed.bug_class: use-after-free (C1: a side table outlives the object it indexes)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: Held stores only {dialog, element} (line 294). ReleaseHeld runs once a frame and starts with `if (h.dialog == nullptr || h.dialog->_ui != ui) continue;`, which dereferences a DialogInstance before it checks whether that dialog is still in ui->_dialogs. A closed dialog goes to UserInterface::_removedDialogs and is freed at the end of that UI update, so the next frame's ReleaseHeld reads freed memory. If the read returns a stale or garbage `_ui`, the entry is never cleared and is read again every frame. If another DialogInstance is allocated at the same address in the same UI, `open` becomes true, the stale entry is kept, and once the row is off `h.element->_minWidth = h.element->_description->_minWidth` (lines 390-392) dereferences and writes the old dialog's freed page element. The sibling tables were written to avoid exactly this: touch_size.cpp Seen and touch_scroll.cpp Window store `ui` when they are recorded, and TouchForgetClosed / TouchScrollForgetClosed compare that stored value without dereferencing the dialog. Held has no such field.
confirmed.repro_idea: With ext.phone_menu on (Android, or desktop with the row on), open the Load or Save dialog, which HoldHiddenListWidth records through its hidden groupSelect list, then close it. On the next frame ReleaseHeld reads h.dialog->_ui from the freed instance. An ASan build (WSL ~/openba-review) whose MemoryAllocator passes through to malloc/free should report a heap-use-after-free at touch_fit.cpp:384. Fix: store `ui` in Held at line 368, as Seen and Window do, and test the stored value.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: memory (use-after-free read every frame while ext.phone_menu is on or settling; a write through a freed element if the address is reused)
verdict.proof:
Checked on origin/main (<worktree>). It is not in the ledger: README, findings_p3p4.json and findings_p8.json have no touch_fit or Held entry. P0_MAP.md lists src/ext/phone_menu only as a module.

1) The table is written in one place only. Held entries are set in HoldHiddenListWidth, touch_fit.cpp:368-369 ({dialog, element}, with no ui stored). This runs from TouchFirstPlace (line 469) for a dialog whose hidden group holds a widened list, which is what the Load and Save groupSelect case does. ReleaseHeld (lines 381-398) is the only code that clears an entry, and it clears it only after it has read `h.dialog->_ui` (line 384) and walked ui->_dialogs.

2) A dialog is never seen as closed while it is still alive. UserInterface::CleanRemovedDialogs (userinterface.cpp:1002-1042) unlinks the dialog's node from `_dialogs` and calls `delete dlg` in the same loop iteration. Nothing runs between the unlink and the delete. Until that point the dialog is still in `_dialogs`, so any ReleaseHeld that runs earlier finds `open == true` and, with the row on, keeps the entry (line 389).

3) The order inside one frame makes the freed read certain. userinterface_frame.cpp runs UpdateEvents, then CleanRemovedDialogs #2 (line 315), then the layout loop. That loop calls `_extDialogPlace(kExtPlaceLayout, ...)` (line 345) → TouchFrame → ReleaseHeld (touch_fit.cpp:440) for the head dialog, which after a close is the dialog underneath. Two cases cover every close:
- A close queued by an event handler is deleted at #2, before that frame's ReleaseHeld. Line 384 then dereferences the freed DialogInstance in the same frame.
- A close queued after #2 is seen as open in that frame's ReleaseHeld, then deleted at #3 (line 483). The next frame's ReleaseHeld reads the freed instance.

So every recorded dialog that closes leads to `h.dialog->_ui` being read from freed memory. The read repeats every frame while the stale `_ui` still equals ui, because the entry is cleared only after that comparison. If the stale `_ui` no longer matches, the entry is kept forever (up to kMaxHeld slots). If a new DialogInstance is placed at the same address in the same UI, `open` becomes true and the entry survives. Once the row is turned off, lines 390-392 then read and write `h.element->_minWidth` and `h.element->_description` through the old dialog's freed page element.

4) The sibling tables do this correctly, which shows the missing field. touch_size.cpp:374 (Seen) and touch_scroll.cpp:385 (Window) store `ui` when they record an entry, and TouchForgetClosed / TouchScrollForgetClosed compare that stored value without dereferencing the dialog. Held has no such field.

There is no faithful-code concern: the defect is entirely inside src/ext and is reached only when the row is on, or during the settle frames that g_touched keeps after it is turned off.
verdict.minimal_fix: Add `const UI::UserInterface* ui = nullptr;` to struct Held and set `held->ui = d->_ui;` at touch_fit.cpp:368. In ReleaseHeld, replace `h.dialog->_ui != ui` with `h.ui != ui`, so a dialog is never dereferenced. The `open` walk compares pointers only and is already safe. For the address-reuse case, call a forget step from TouchForgetClosed (it already runs first in TouchFrame) that drops a Held entry whose dialog is not in ui->_dialogs. Like Seen and Window, an entry is then cleared without its element being touched once its dialog is gone. Optionally restore `_minWidth` only when the dialog is still open, which ReleaseHeld already does.

confirmed.title: Town screenshot ReadTile reads past the read-back buffer when the back buffer is 64 px or less on a side
confirmed.bug_class: out-of-bounds read (heap)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: MakeGrid (screenshot_math.h:144-145) sets payloadW = max(1, screenW - 2*margin) and payloadH = max(1, screenH - 2*margin), with kMargin = 64. ReadTile allocates `pixels` as width*height words (line 315) and reads `pixels[(py + margin) * width + (px + margin)]` for py < payloadH and px < payloadW. When screenH <= 64, payloadH clamps to 1 and the read is row 64 of a buffer with at most 64 rows. When screenW <= 64 the column index is out of range in the same way. DrawScene only checks that the size has not changed since Start, and no window minimum size is set (only WM_GETMINMAXINFO's max track size is touched, window_hook_win.cpp:101). Separately, cols * rows grows to millions of one-pixel tiles at that size, and the `pixels` MemAlloc result is never checked for null.
confirmed.repro_idea: Shrink the window's client area to 64 px high or less (or hand ScreenSize a 60x40 back buffer in a harness), then press Take on the Town Screenshot page. The first tile reads row 64. A unit test on screenshot_math can show `margin + payloadH - 1 >= screenH` for every screenH <= 64. Fix: refuse to Start (status line) when screenW or screenH <= 2*kMargin.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: memory (ext.town_screenshot only, default OFF; needs a back buffer of 64 px or less in height)
verdict.proof: The arithmetic holds when read line by line on origin/main. In screenshot_math.h MakeGrid, payloadH = max(1, screenH - 128). In town_screenshot.cpp, Start (line 438) takes screenW/screenH from ScreenSize, which returns device->backBufferWidth/Height whenever both are above 0, and Start has no lower bound on the size. ReadTile (lines 305-326) allocates width*height words and reads pixels[(py+64)*width + (px+64)] for py in [0,payloadH). If backBufferHeight <= 64, then payloadH = 1, and the py=0 read is at index 64*width+64, which is at least width*height. That is a heap read past the end. A width-only case (width <= 64, height > 64) reads the wrong pixel, but it stays inside the buffer unless height is also small, so the finding overstates that half. The finding is not in the review_20261103 ledger (no town_screenshot or kMargin entry), and origin/main has no fix. The open question is reachability. In framed windowed mode the window can be resized (display_sdl.cpp:164 SDL_SetWindowResizable(w, framed)), and no minimum track size is set (window_hook_win.cpp:101 changes only ptMaxTrackSize). However, Start runs only from the Take button on the toolbar page (toolbar_page.cpp:141), and DrawScene stops the run if the size changes after Start (line 536). So the player has to click Take while the client area is 64 px high or less, and the back buffer has to follow the client size down to that height. Static reading cannot settle either point. Two things would prove it: a unit test on MakeGrid that asserts margin + payloadH - 1 >= screenH for screenH <= 64, plus a harness run or ASan run of ReadTile with a 60x40 back buffer. Minimal fix: Start refuses with a status line when screenW or screenH <= 2*kMargin. Optionally also check the MemAlloc result in ReadTile.
verdict.minimal_fix: In TownScreenshot::Start, after ScreenSize: if (run.screenW <= 2 * kMargin || run.screenH <= 2 * kMargin) { SetStatus("The window is too small for a screenshot."); return false; }

proof_run.proof:
A new unit test, tests/unit/ext_town_screenshot_test.cpp::ext_town_screenshot_tile_reads_stay_inside_the_back_buffer, failed in the worktree on base fa150cf7f (debug build, `tools/build.sh unit debug --jobs 2`, then `unit.exe --filter ext_town_screenshot`).

The test calls the real MakeGrid with ReadTile's margin of 64 for several back-buffer sizes. For each size it computes the last index ReadTile reads, which is (payloadH-1+margin)*width + (payloadW-1+margin), and checks that this index is below width*height, the size of the read-back buffer ReadTile allocates.

Observed output:
- 200x64: last read index 12935 >= buffer words 12800 (FAIL)
- 200x40: 12935 >= 8000 (FAIL)
- 60x40: 3904 >= 2400 (FAIL)
- 64x64: 4160 >= 4096 (FAIL)
- 1920x1017, 100x100 and 129x129 pass.

So whenever backBufferHeight <= 64, MakeGrid clamps payloadH to 1, and the first row ReadTile reads is row 64, past the end of the heap buffer. That is a heap out-of-bounds read in ReadTile (town_screenshot.cpp:326). Start (around line 438) puts no lower bound on ScreenSize, so nothing prevents it.

As the verifier said, the width-only half is overstated. With width <= 64 and a tall buffer, ReadTile reads the wrong pixel, but the read stays inside the buffer.

Not proven: whether a real window can reach a back buffer 64 px high or less at the moment Take is clicked. The game was not run. The window is resizable when framed and no minimum track size is set.

Scope: ext.town_screenshot only, which is off by default.

- scratchpad/phase2/proofs/town_screenshot_readtile_oob/ext_town_screenshot_test.cpp
- scratchpad/phase2/proofs/town_screenshot_readtile_oob/unit_filter.log

The worktree keeps the uncommitted test change. third_party was robocopied in for the build and must not be committed.

confirmed.title: Family picture layout recurses once per generation or marriage through std::function lambdas; a crafted save tree overflows the stack
confirmed.bug_class: unbounded recursion / stack overflow from save-tail input
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: BuildPictureLayout walks its graph recursively in six places: walkDown (line 228), walk over the marriage chain (291), hang (309), measure (328), place (339) and lift (361). Each level costs several frames (the lambda plus std::function's invoker, and hang also copies a std::vector). Recursion depth equals the longest parent chain or marriage chain, and the only cap is kPictureMaxPeople = 6000. Tree::Decode (family_tree.cpp:624) accepts any mother/father/spouse links between up to 2,000,000 people, and drops only self-links and missing ids. A save-tail record whose family_tree payload chains 6000 people parent to child (or spouse to spouse) therefore gives recursion depth 6000 when the player presses Save picture (PNG or SVG). This is the same class as F-037 and F-038 (recursive walks over decoded data). The MinGW default stack reserve is 2 MB, CMakeLists sets no --stack, and debug frames are large. Generations::Of in family_summary.cpp is already depth-capped at 400, so that walk is safe.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit test (tests/unit/ext_family_tree_test.cpp style): build a Tree in which person i+1's mother is person i, for 6000 people, then call BuildPictureLayout(tree, false, nullptr) on a thread with a 1 MB stack, or under ulimit -s 1024 on Linux. For the fuzz route, Encode that tree, Decode it, then lay it out. Hardening: make the walks iterative with an explicit stack, or cap the depth and lay out the rest flat.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: crash (debug-build likely; release depends on frame size)
verdict.proof:
The code supports the finding, but whether the stack actually overflows depends on frame sizes, so it is not airtight without a run. It is not in the ledger: README F-001..F-217 and findings_p3p4/p8 cover family_tree only for font lookup (p8) and P0_MAP notes; F-037/F-038/F-041 are the same bug class in other files. It is unchanged on origin/main fa150cf7f.

Static chain, checked against the code in <worktree>:
(1) Tree::Decode (src/ext/family_tree/family_tree.cpp:344-424) accepts count <= kMaxPeople (2,000,000). It drops only self-links and links to missing ids (lines 413-419). Any mother/father/spouse graph is kept, including a 6000-long parent chain (person i+1's mother = i), and nothing caps its depth.
(2) BuildPictureLayout (family_picture.cpp:141) caps the people at kPictureMaxPeople = 6000 (family_picture.h:32). With livingOnly=false and exactly 6000 people, every person is kept. With livingOnly, the result is resize()d to 6000.
(3) With no marriages, each person is a cluster of their own. below[] forms a chain, so walkDown (l.228) recurses 6000 deep. hang (l.309) recurses once per child cluster, 6000 deep, and also builds a std::vector copy per frame. measure (l.328), place (l.339) and lift (l.361) each recurse 6000 deep over the kids chain. With a spouse chain instead (each person has at most 255 marriages, so a path of 6000 is possible), walk (l.291) recurses 6000 deep.
(4) Every level goes through std::function. At -O0 that is about 4-5 frames (operator(), _M_invoke, __invoke_r, __invoke_impl, the lambda), each with the 32-byte ms_abi home area. That is a few hundred bytes per level, so about 2-3 MB at 6000 levels, more than the 1-2 MB main-thread stack. At -O2 the invoker frames mostly collapse, to perhaps about 100 bytes per level (about 0.6 MB), which may fit.
(5) The caller is SaveImage (toolbar_page.cpp:552) on the UI/main thread, reached by the Save picture button after a save-tail family_tree payload is loaded.

So the overflow is plausible in a debug build and uncertain in release. The repro proposed in the finding would settle it: a Tree with a 6000-long mother chain, passed to BuildPictureLayout on a thread with a 1 MB stack, or under ASan with ulimit -s 1024. Until that runs, it stays SUSPECTED.
verdict.minimal_fix: Hardening (plain, since this is not UB; the ext is NOT RETAIL): replace the recursive std::function walks (walkDown, walk, hang, measure, place, lift) with iterative walks on an explicit stack. Keep the visit order the same: pre-order for walk/hang, post-order for measure, an index-carrying stack for place and lift. That keeps the layout output byte-identical. The alternative is to cap the depth (for example 400, like Generations::Of) and lay out the deeper clusters as extra roots.

proof_run.proof:
The overflow is real in the game's debug flavour (-O0). It does not happen in perf or release on Windows.

Harness: depth_harness.cpp, built with build_harness.ps1. It is the real family_picture.cpp and family_tree.cpp from fa150cf7f, compiled with the pinned WinLibs g++ 16 and each flavour's FLAVOUR_FLAGS. It builds a 6000-person Tree (kPictureMaxPeople), runs it through Encode and then Decode (the save-tail path), and calls BuildPictureLayout(back, false, nullptr) on a thread with a 2 MB stack reserve. 2 MB is the MinGW default: objdump shows SizeOfStackReserve 0x200000, and CMakeLists sets no --stack, so the game's main thread gets the same.

Results (harness_run.log):
- -O0 (debug flavour), a 6000-deep mother chain: the thread dies with exit 0xC00000FD (-1073741571, STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW). With a 64 MB reserve the same run commits 2,793,472 bytes, about 465 B per level.
- -O0, a 6000-long spouse chain (the `walk` lambda): same result, STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW at 2 MB. It commits 2,408,448 bytes at 64 MB.
- -O2 (perf) and -O3 (release): both chains finish at 2 MB. They commit 868,352 bytes (parent chain) and 679,936 bytes (spouse chain), which leaves about 1.1 MB of headroom on Windows.
- In-tree unit test (unit_test_measure.diff; unit.exe is always -Og): both 6000-deep cases pass. The measured commit is 1,445,888 bytes (parent) and 1,253,376 bytes (spouse), so a plain unit test cannot fail at -Og with a 2 MB stack. That is why the failure was shown with the -O0 harness.

The call site is toolbar_page.cpp:552, SaveImage on the UI/main thread, reached by pressing "Save picture" with a loaded save-tail tree. Depth grows linearly with the chain (walkDown, hang, measure, place, lift, walk, all through std::function) and is capped only by kPictureMaxPeople = 6000.

Not proven, so SUSPECTED: on Android, SDL runs its main on a Java "SDLThread" whose default stack is about 1 MB. There, the release figure (0.87 MB) plus the caller's frames could overflow too.

Artefacts are in scratchpad/phase2/proofs/family-picture-recursion/: depth_harness.cpp, build_harness.ps1, harness_run.log, h_O0.exe, h_O2.exe, h_O3.exe, unit_test_measure.diff and unit_Og_build_and_run.log. The worktree test file was restored to clean after the diff was saved.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
This is plain hardening (the ext is NOT RETAIL and this is not UB). In BuildPictureLayout, replace the six recursive std::function walks with iterative ones on an explicit std::vector stack, keeping the visit order so the layout stays byte-identical:
- walkDown: a DFS with a (v, k) frame stack.
- walk over spouses: a pre-order DFS that pushes spouses in reverse order.
- hang: a pre-order walk that iterates members and children in the same order (frames hold ci, member index, child index).
- measure: a post-order walk.
- place: frames hold (ci, left, k, at, first, last), returning the center to the parent frame.
- lift: frames hold (ci, rows, k, deepest).

The alternative is to cap depth at 400, as Generations::Of does, and lay out deeper clusters as new roots, but that changes the picture. Add the 6000-deep parent-chain and spouse-chain unit tests from unit_test_measure.diff as regressions. To make them fail before the fix, run them on a thread with a small (for example 256 KB) reserve.

confirmed.title: phone_menu keys the menus, the version line and the loading screens on Dialog resource addresses it assumes live for the whole run; the loops' Clean evicts them
confirmed.bug_class: dangling resource pointer used as identity (ABA), fixed-size table exhaustion
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: g_menus, g_pauses and g_buildIds (3 slots each, lines 60-62), g_loading (4 slots) and g_other (32 slots) in loading_screen.cpp:36,47 hold raw `const UI::Dialog*` values, and nothing ever removes one. The comment at line 57 says 'Resources live for the run, so a recorded pointer stays valid', but other code in this area relies on the opposite. KeepMenuOverlay (loading_screen.cpp) reserves a clean bit of its own so that 'no loop's Clean evicts' the menu's sprite sheet. touch_mode.cpp re-resolves Toolbar.rsc per game because 'a new game or a load may give it a new address'. After a menu, game, menu round trip, any Dialog later allocated at a recorded address is classified as a menu, pause menu or loading screen. PlaceMenu then lays it out in the menu band, runs Capture/Shape on whatever `buttonList` it finds, and indexes dialog->_spriteSheet->m_sprites by _spriteIndex without a size check. A new address after the 3 slots are full is never recorded (Record returns silently), so the menu's row layout stops applying. g_other permanently marks a reused address as 'not a loading screen'.
confirmed.repro_idea: With ext.phone_menu on, go main menu -> new game -> quit to menu -> load -> quit to menu several times, logging the `[PhoneMenu] menu %p` address that MenuOpened prints on each pass. A changing address shows the eviction. Then check whether an in-game dialog opens at a recorded address (it would be placed in the menu band). Fix: key on the dialog's path or name, or clear the tables when the owning loop changes (MenuOpened already runs each time a menu instance opens).

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: logic
verdict.proof: The code matches the finding's description, and the finding is not in the ledger: no entry in review_20261103 README, P0_MAP or findings_*.json names phone_menu, g_menus or loading_screen. In phone_menu.cpp:58-62, g_menus, g_pauses and g_buildIds each hold 3 slots of raw `const UI::Dialog*`. Record (72-82) returns without storing anything when all 3 slots are full, and nothing ever clears a slot. MenuOpened (638) resets g_row but not the tables. In loading_screen.cpp:36,47, g_loading (4 slots) and g_other (32 slots) also only ever grow. The pointers are the `_dialog` resource of MainMenuDialog (mainmenudialog.cpp:559), obtained through ExternalFactory. ExternalFactory::Clean (loops.cpp:323) frees externals whose clean bits are all clear, and two parts of the same area assume such frees happen. KeepMenuOverlay reserves a private clean bit so that the menu's sprite sheet is not evicted. touch_mode.cpp:129 re-resolves Toolbar.rsc per game because 'a new game or a load may give it a new address'. So the comment at phone_menu.cpp:57, 'Resources live for the run', conflicts with the rest of the module, and the 3-slot table itself suggests the author expected the address to change. Two consequences follow if Dialog/MainMenu.rsc or Pause.rsc is actually freed and reloaded across front end -> game -> front end. (a) After 3 distinct addresses the row layout stops applying, because Record drops the new address silently and In() returns false. (b) A different Dialog allocated later at a recorded address is treated as a menu, pause menu, version line or loading screen, and g_other permanently marks a reused address as 'not loading'. Static reading cannot settle either one. It depends on whether Clean really frees MainMenu.rsc and Pause.rsc between loops: the front-end and game loops could share the bit that keeps them, or MainMenuDialog could hold a reference to them. It also depends on whether the allocator hands the same address to a different Dialog. The `[PhoneMenu] menu %p` stderr line MenuOpened prints already gives the run-time proof: do 4 or more menu/game round trips with ext.phone_menu on and check whether the address changes. The ABA case (b) is weaker still, since it needs an address match.
verdict.minimal_fix: Stop storing raw resource addresses as an identity that never expires. Either compare the Dialog's resource path (Filename) instead of its address, or have MenuOpened replace the menu or pause slot with the current address (a single latest-value slot per kind, not a set that only grows). Clear g_loading and g_other when the owning loop changes (front end vs GameUpdateLoop::_singleton), the way touch_mode re-resolves Toolbar.rsc per game.

proof_run.proof:
Confirmed by a run of the stock exe, not a unit test. The exe was a debug build of fa150cf7f with no source changes, deployed to the functional dir (Banished-B). ext.phone_menu=1 was set in that dir's settings.cfg for the run, then restored. Env: BANISHED_AUTOSTART=1, BANISHED_AUTOSTART_GAMES=4, BANISHED_PAUSEMENU=600, BANISHED_PAUSEMENU_BUTTON=5 (quit to main menu).

1. The resources are evicted and come back at new addresses on every menu/game round trip. The MenuOpened stderr lines read:
   - menus: 1b1f880, 069e800, 1487b98, 1aa6830, 10dfdd0
   - pause menus: 1b0e498, 1b46430, 1b0b1d0, 1aec368
   - buildIds: a new value on every pass (b20ea8, b19ab0, ad6950, ac0940, ...)
   So the comment 'Resources live for the run, so a recorded pointer stays valid' (phone_menu.cpp:57) is false.

2. The 3-slot tables fill up, and the ext then silently stops working:
   - Menus 1 to 3 and pause menus 1 to 3 each logged the layout decision ('1264x672: 1 row of square buttons ...').
   - The 4th menu (1aa6830), the 4th pause menu (1aec368) and the 5th menu (10dfdd0) never logged a decision. Record() dropped them, so In() is false and PlaceMenu never runs.
   - The 5th menu sat idle for more than 20 s. The screenshot (menu5_after_table_full.png) shows retail's vertical column, not the phone_menu row.
   - g_buildIds also holds the pause menu's buildId, so it was full after 3 of the 9 buildIds (from the 2nd main menu on). Every later version line lost its phone_menu placement.

3. The other half of the finding was not observed: a different Dialog reusing a recorded address and being misclassified as a menu or loading screen (ABA). It is plausible, since freed addresses get reused, but it stays suspected.

The same grow-only tables are in loading_screen.cpp: g_loading (4 slots) and g_other (32 slots). They are also keyed on these evicted Dialog addresses, so they carry the same staleness.

Artefacts are in scratchpad/phase2/proofs/phone_menu_aba/:
- phone_menu_lines.txt
- standalone_error.log
- menu5_after_table_full.png
- settings.cfg.orig (the restored settings.cfg)
proof_run.minimal_fix: In MenuOpened (phone_menu.cpp:638), replace the grow-only sets with one latest-value slot per kind. Store g_menus, or g_pauses when it is the pause menu, as the current `menu`. Store g_buildIds as the current `buildId`. Opening a menu instance re-records its own description, so the latest address is always the live one, and a freed address can no longer match. Alternatively, clear all three tables at the top of MenuOpened before recording. For loading_screen.cpp, clear g_loading and g_other (g_otherCount = 0) when the owning loop changes, or compare the Dialog's resource Filename instead of its address. Fix the false comment at line 57 too.

confirmed.title: The Shift toggle and the UI hold identify the tool by raw Tool* address; a replacement tool at a reused address inherits them
confirmed.bug_class: stale pointer identity (ABA)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: PressButton stores `g_shiftTool = CurrentTool()` (line 423) and OnFinger stores `g_uiHoldTool = CurrentTool()` (line 526). GameFrame clears Shift only when `tool != g_shiftTool`, and KeepsModel / ToolAimHeld / HoldToolAim test `current == g_uiHoldTool` or `g_shiftTool == CurrentTool()`. The tools are never dereferenced, but tool selection frees the old tool and allocates the new one within one frame. Picking another building of the same tool class (PlacementTool to PlacementTool) can reuse the same block. Shift then stays on for the new tool, so PlacementTool::CreateAt keeps the model ('Off again ... when the tool changes', header), and the aim hold carries over to a tool that never aimed.
confirmed.repro_idea: With ext.touch_pointer on, choose house A, tap Shift, then choose house B from the toolbar. If B's tool lands at A's address (log `CurrentTool()` in GameFrame), the Shift art stays pressed and B keeps its model after a placement. Fix: also store a per-selection counter (for example bump one in PlayerToolManager::SelectTool's seam) and compare that as well as the address.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: minor
verdict.proof:
The code does what the finding says, but whether the address is actually reused depends on the allocator, which the source alone cannot show. It is not in the ledger: grepping docs/history/review_20261103 for g_shiftTool, g_uiHoldTool and ABA finds only two unrelated cache-ABA rows in findings_p8.json.

What the code does (<worktree>/src/ext/touch_pointer/touch_pointer.cpp):
- The tool is identified by its raw address. PressButton(kShift) stores `g_shiftTool = CurrentTool()` (line 423). OnFinger Down with Role::Ui and a Place/Drag tool stores `g_uiHoldTool = CurrentTool()` (line 526).
- Nothing else ties those values to one tool selection. KeepsModel (1088) tests `g_shiftTool == CurrentTool()`. GameFrame (1096) clears Shift only when `tool != g_shiftTool`, the tool is null, the fingers lost the pointer or the row is off. ToolAimHeld (1036) and HoldToolAim (1046) test `current == g_uiHoldTool`.
- In PlayerToolManager::SelectTool (src/game/Dialog/toolbardialog.cpp:298-445), choosing another group runs `currentTool->Shutdown(); delete currentTool.Get();` (315-319) and then, in the same call, `Factory::CreateObject(foundNode->factoryTypeId)` (414). Going from one building to another is PlacementTool to PlacementTool, so the freed block and the new one are the same size. If the allocator hands that block back, CurrentTool() returns the old address.
- The toolbar tap that picks the new building is a Role::Ui finger. That path never touches g_shift; it is cleared only by another Shift tap, the GameFrame address test, or the mouse taking the pointer back. So Shift and the UI hold would both carry over to the new tool. HoldToolAim would also skip the new tool's update until the cursor returns to the world. The comment at line 199 says a new tool should end the hold ("Another tool selected by the tap ends it").

Why this is not confirmed:
- Address reuse is not provable from source. The old tool's destructor also frees its sub-objects, and Startup allocates after construction, so it is unknown whether the freed tool block is at the head of its size class when CreateObject runs. That depends on the engine/CRT allocator.
- A run with ext.touch_pointer on is needed: log CurrentTool() across a house-to-house reselection, or write a unit test that drives SelectTool twice with the same factory type and compares the addresses.

The ext is OFF by default and the defect only touches ext state, so faithful behaviour is unaffected.
verdict.minimal_fix: Store a per-selection generation counter with the tool address and compare both. Bump the counter where the tool is created (the PlayerToolManager::SelectTool seam or a touch_pointer hook), keep it beside g_shiftTool / g_uiHoldTool, and add the generation check to KeepsModel, GameFrame's Shift-off test, ToolAimHeld and HoldToolAim. Alternatively, clear g_shift and the UI hold from a tool-changed callback in SelectTool, which ext.touch_pointer only acts on when it is on.

proof_run.proof:
The finding is confirmed by a live run with a debug build of the worktree, not by a unit test, fuzz input or sanitizer. Address reuse is what the proof needed to show, and it only appears under the real allocator with real tool construction and destruction. The touch_pointer comparisons themselves sit in an anonymous namespace and are plain `==` tests on the address.

**Probe.** A temporary probe went into the `click` route of src/diag/tool_harness.cpp (FireActivatePlacement). After the harness installs the WoodHouse PlacementTool through `PlayerToolManager::SelectTool`, the probe reselects StoneHouse, WoodHouse, StoneHouse and WoodHouse through the real `SelectTool`. That is the toolbar path: Shutdown, delete, then `Factory::CreateObject` and Startup. Before and after each call it logs `currentTool`, which is exactly what touch_pointer's `CurrentTool()` returns. The diff is kept in the proofs dir, and the probe was reverted from the worktree afterwards.

**Run.** Functional dir C:/GOG Games/Banished-B (lane aba261, released after), with BANISHED_AUTOSTART=1, BANISHED_TOOL_HARNESS=click and BANISHED_LIVE_TOOLS=1. The log:
```
[ToolHarness] after SetEditMode: activeTool(entityUI+0x28)=000002be00109370
[ABA] select Template\StoneHouse.rsc desc=000002be0019a530 prevTool=000002be00109370 newTool=000002be00109370 isPlacement=1 SAME_ADDRESS=1
[ABA] select Template\WoodHouse.rsc  desc=000002be00180638 prevTool=000002be00109370 newTool=000002be00109370 isPlacement=1 SAME_ADDRESS=1
[ABA] select Template\StoneHouse.rsc desc=000002be0019a530 prevTool=000002be00109370 newTool=000002be00109370 isPlacement=1 SAME_ADDRESS=1
[ABA] select Template\WoodHouse.rsc  desc=000002be00180638 prevTool=000002be00109370 newTool=000002be00109370 isPlacement=1 SAME_ADDRESS=1
```
On all four house-to-house reselections, the new PlacementTool landed at the freed tool's address. PlacementTool is 0x70 bytes, and the engine's System::MemoryAllocator hands the just-freed block straight back.

**Consequence (deterministic from the code).**
- After a Shift tap, `g_shiftTool` equals the new tool's address. The test in GameFrame at touch_pointer.cpp:1096 (`tool != g_shiftTool`) never fires, so Shift stays on.

- The same holds for `g_uiHoldTool`: ToolAimHeld (1036) and HoldToolAim (1046) treat the new tool as the held one, against the comment at line 199 ("Another tool selected by the tap ends it").

**Scope.** ext.touch_pointer is OFF by default, so faithful behaviour is unaffected. Only the extension's own Shift and hold state are wrong.

**Status of the evidence.** CONFIRMED by an observed reuse on a real run. proof_kind is "none" because none of the listed kinds (unit test, fuzz input, sanitizer, Ghidra diff) applies. Artefacts are in scratchpad/phase2/proofs/touch-tool-aba/:
- aba_run.log
- tool_harness_aba_probe.diff

confirmed.title: Toolbar window record from a save accepts any int32 x/y; SetUpperLeft then overflows on w + x
confirmed.bug_class: signed-overflow (hostile save input reaches faithful clamp)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: Decode reads the position with no range check: `if (!r.Bytes(1, open) || *open > 1 || !r.I32(s.x) || !r.I32(s.y) || !r.String(s.page))` then `g_window = s;`. toolbar_window.cpp:383 passes it unchanged: `dlg->SetUpperLeft(SavedWindow().x, SavedWindow().y, false);`. In UI::DialogInstance::SetUpperLeft (src/engine/ui/dialog.cpp:1220/1222), retail's clamp is `if (w + x > bounds[2]) x = bounds[2] - w;` and `if (h + y > bounds[3]) ...`, where w and h are the dialog's positive padded size. With x or y near INT32_MAX, `w + x` is signed int32 overflow. The engine clamp is faithful. The defect is that the ext decoder lets a value through that the game itself can never write: OnUpdate only stores x,y >= 0 that come from int16 mouse coordinates times the UI scale. The same function is reached by the drag path, but there the values are bounded.
confirmed.repro_idea: Edit a save's toolbar host record (payload: u8 1, i32 0x7fffffff, i32 0x7fffffff, String "") so that open=1. Load the save with ext.toolbar offered, using a UBSan build (-fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow): it should report dialog.cpp:1220 'signed integer overflow' when the window opens. Unit test alternative: call Decode, then assert that SavedWindow().x is kept within a sane bound (e.g. 0..65535). Minimal fix: in Decode, reject (or clamp) x/y outside 0..INT16_MAX*some scale, e.g. `if (s.x < 0 || s.y < 0 || s.x > 1 << 20 || s.y > 1 << 20) return false;`.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (signed overflow, crafted save only; ext.toolbar offered)
verdict.proof:
Checked on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>). The finding holds as stated, and the ledger has no entry for it.

1. src/ext/toolbar/window_state.cpp:45 Decode reads `r.I32(s.x)` and `r.I32(s.y)` with no range check. The only checks are open<=1, AtEnd and ValidPageId. It then stores `g_window = s`.

2. src/ext/toolbar/toolbar_window.cpp:383 calls `dlg->SetUpperLeft(SavedWindow().x, SavedWindow().y, false)`. Lines 430+ reopen the window on load whenever SavedWindow().open is set and the ext is Offered, so a crafted record with open=1 reaches this call.

3. src/engine/ui/dialog.cpp:1166 DialogInstance::SetUpperLeft (0x180114a60) passes `scaled=false`, so x is not scaled. Then `if (x < bounds[0])` does not fire for INT32_MAX. `if (w + x > bounds[2])` follows, where w = layoutWidth + rightPad + leftPad, floored at _minWidth. For any w >= 1, w + INT32_MAX is signed int32 overflow. The same happens for y at the `h + y` line. The engine clamp is faithful. Only the ext decoder lets a value through that OnUpdate (toolbar_window.cpp:314-316, from mouse drag positions) never writes.

4. Ledger: grep of docs/history/review_20261103 for toolbar/window_state/SetUpperLeft finds only F-114, F-191, the C15 double-scale pattern and the ToolbarDescription taint rows. All are different defects, so this is not a duplicate.

Why this is not marked confirmed: the overflow needs the toolbar dialog's padded width or height to be >= 1. That size comes from the retail .rsc layout, which is game data and not in the tree, so it cannot be checked line by line. The campaign proof standard for UB also asks for a sanitizer report or a failing test. Build proof: load a save whose toolbar host record is (u8 1, i32 0x7fffffff, i32 0x7fffffff, String "") on a -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow build with ext.toolbar offered. UBSan should report dialog.cpp:1220.

Off-switch purity is not affected: Decode and the reopen run only with the ext offered.
verdict.minimal_fix: Hostile-input hardening in Decode (window_state.cpp), after the reads: `if (s.x < 0 || s.y < 0 || s.x > (1 << 20) || s.y > (1 << 20)) return false;` with a "NOT RETAIL:" comment saying the bound keeps w + x in SetUpperLeft from overflowing. Leave the faithful engine clamp unchanged. Add a unit test in which Decode rejects INT32_MAX x/y.

proof_run.proof:
The finding is confirmed by a failing unit test, built in the isolated worktree on fa150cf7f with `tools/build.sh unit debug --jobs 2`.

The new test is tests/unit/ext_toolbar_window_bounds_test.cpp. It builds a `toolbar` host payload (u8 1, i32 INT32_MAX, i32 INT32_MAX, String "") and passes it through the real `Ext::Toolbar::WindowCodec().decode(..., 1)`.

Before the fix (unit.exe --filter ext_toolbar_window):
  decode accepted open=1 x=2147483647 y=2147483647; 1 + x overflows int32: yes
  FAIL ext_toolbar_window_decode_refuses_overflowing_position (CHECK !overflows, CHECK !accepted)
In the full suite this test accounted for both failures (2000 tests, 2 failures).

The test uses `__builtin_add_overflow` to show that `w + x` overflows int32 even for the smallest width (1). The same holds for `h + y`.

What was not run: the real SetUpperLeft from a game load under UBSan. dialog.cpp is not linked into the unit tests, and the WSL sanitizer route was refused by this agent's worktree isolation. confirmed.title: FamilyTree NowStamp and AgeYears turn save-derived calendar and age values into int with no range check
confirmed.bug_class: float->int out of range / signed overflow
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: NowStamp: `int month = static_cast<int>(cal->yearTime.AsSeconds() / 3600.0f * 12.0f);` (line 252) converts before the 0..11 clamp below it, so a huge, infinite or NaN yearTime is UB at the cast. `return cal->year * 12 + month;` (line 255) is int32 * 12 with Calendar::year read from the save (int32_t, Calendar.h:29), so any year > 178956970 overflows. AgeYears: `const int y = static_cast<int>(c->age * kAgeToYears);` (line 48) uses the citizen's float age from the save. Retail's citizen panel does the same (int)(age*5), but this is a separate ext call made at every Add/Died/Ensure. A year that large is impossible in normal play, so a modified or hostile save is needed. The double-based twin at line 186 (`cal->year * 12.0 + ...`) shows the intended arithmetic.
confirmed.repro_idea: In a UBSan build (-fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow,float-cast-overflow), load a save whose Calendar year is 0x7fffff00, or whose yearTime seconds are 1e30, with ext.family_tree on. The next birth/arrival/death or sweep calls NowStamp, which should give 'signed integer overflow' at family_tree_town.cpp:255 or a float-cast-overflow at 252. Minimal fix ('NOT RETAIL:' comment): clamp the float before the cast (e.g. `std::clamp(f, 0.0f, 11.0f)`, with NaN mapped to 0) and compute the stamp in int64, saturating to INT32_MAX. Do the same for age.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (hostile/modified save, ext.family_tree on only; default off)
verdict.proof: The code matches the description. src/ext/family_tree/family_tree_town.cpp:252 `int month = static_cast<int>(cal->yearTime.AsSeconds() / 3600.0f * 12.0f);` casts before the 0..11 clamp at 253-254, and :255 `return cal->year * 12 + month;` is a 32-bit signed multiply. Calendar::year (int32) and yearTime (int64 ticks) come straight from the save with no range check: gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:730-731 `ser0.Serialize(dc->year, nullptr); dc->yearTime.Serialize(ser0);`. Calendar::Update (retail 0x140096380, Calendar.h header) only subtracts yearLength once per frame, so a huge yearTime stays huge for many frames. AsSeconds = TicksToSeconds(int64 ticks) can therefore reach about 1e12 seconds or more, which is far past INT_MAX after *12/3600. That conversion is UB by [conv.fpint]. The same is true of a large negative value or NaN. A year above 178956970 overflows at :255. AgeYears :48 `static_cast<int>(c->age * kAgeToYears)` has the same float-cast problem for a saved age above about 4.3e8 or NaN. The `y < 0` test after the cast does not help. All three sites are NOT RETAIL ext code (file banner) and run from Ensure/Bind/Sweep (lines 104, 173, 211) only when ext.family_tree is on. That is why the label is ext and faithful behaviour is unaffected. Not in the ledger: README F-001..F-217 and findings_p3p4/p8 have no NowStamp, AgeYears or family_tree_town UB entry. The nearest are F-165 (statvaluedispatch year overflow, retail) and F-163/F-136 (other float casts). origin/main has not changed the lines (last commits de1e4f634, e319c926c). Under the campaign proof standard, UB is CONFIRMED only with a sanitizer report or a test. It is not refuted. A UBSan repro is still needed: set GameUpdateLoop::_singleton->m_dayCounter to year=0x7fffff00, or yearTime._ticks so that AsSeconds is about 1e30, then call Ext::FamilyTree::NowStamp(). That should report signed-integer-overflow at :255 or float-cast-overflow at :252.
verdict.minimal_fix: In NowStamp, read the seconds into a float, map NaN or a negative value to 0, clamp to 11.0f before the cast, and compute `int64_t s = int64_t(cal->year) * 12 + month`, saturated to the int32 range. In AgeYears, clamp `c->age * kAgeToYears` to [0, INT_MAX-representable], with NaN mapped to 0, before the cast. Mark each line with a "NOT RETAIL:" comment.

A failing unit test confirms the NowStamp half of the finding. The worktree is <worktree> (base fa150cf7f). The test is tests/unit/ext_family_tree_nowstamp_test.cpp. To link it, src/ext/family_tree/family_tree_town.cpp was added to tests/unit/sources.cmake, and two never-reached link stubs were added: Ext::FamilyTree::CitizenButtonsForget and PlayerToolManager::CenterOnEntity. confirmed.title: FamilyTree Decode accepts nextId = 0xFFFFFFFF; the next Add wraps nextId_ to 0, after which ids repeat and the game's own next save no longer decodes
confirmed.bug_class: unsigned wrap -> broken invariant / unreadable save tail
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: Decode only requires `p.id < nextId` (line 359: `p.id == 0 || p.id <= last || p.id >= nextId`). Any u32 nextId is accepted, including 0xFFFFFFFF with count 0. Add then does `p.id = nextId_++;` (line 27). The person gets id 0xFFFFFFFF and nextId_ wraps to 0. The next Add pushes a person with id 0 (Add returns 0, so Ensure does not Link it, but the row stays in people_). Ids 1, 2, ... follow, which duplicates and unsorts ids and breaks Find's lower_bound precondition. The next Encode writes nextId 0 (or a small value) together with ids >= nextId and an id 0. Decode rejects that payload, so the whole family tree of that town is dropped silently on the next load. The cause is wrapping unsigned arithmetic (defined, not UB), not a crash.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit test: Tree t; build the bytes {u32 nextId=0xFFFFFFFF, u32 count=0} and call t.Decode(bytes, 8, 2), which returns true. Then call t.Add("a",...), which returns 0xFFFFFFFF, and t.Add("b",...), which returns 0 while Size()==2. Encode, then Decode the result: it returns false. Fix: in Decode, reject nextId > kMaxPeople * some margin (e.g. nextId > 0x7fffffff), and in Add, refuse when nextId_ == UINT32_MAX.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (hostile/crafted save tail only, ext.family_tree ON; no crash, no UB; the town's family tree is silently dropped on the next load)
verdict.proof:
Checked line by line on origin/main fa150cf7f, <worktree>/src/ext/family_tree/family_tree.cpp. The finding is not in the review_20261103 ledger: README F-001..F-217, findings_p3p4.json and findings_p8.json have no nextId or family_tree.cpp Decode entry; their family_tree rows are about fonts or CodeQL format strings. The bug is not fixed on main.
(1) Decode at L346-424 reads the u32 `nextId` (L350), and only `count` is bounded. Each id is checked only by `p.id == 0 || p.id <= last || p.id >= nextId` (L359). With count == 0 the loop never runs, so any nextId gets through, including 0xFFFFFFFF and 0. L423 then sets `nextId_ = nextId;` and Decode returns true.
(2) Add (L23-37) only checks `people_.size() >= kMaxPeople`, then runs `p.id = nextId_++;` (L27). With nextId_ = 0xFFFFFFFF, the first Add pushes id 0xFFFFFFFF and nextId_ wraps to 0. This is defined unsigned wrap, not UB. The next Add pushes id 0 and returns 0, and the row stays in people_. The ids after that are 1, 2, ..., so people_ is no longer sorted ascending, and Find (L39-47) uses lower_bound, which needs sorted ids. With nextId = 0 in the save, the first Add already produces id 0.
(3) Encode (L301-304) writes `nextId_` unchanged. After one Add from the 0xFFFFFFFF state, the payload holds nextId 0 and a person with id 0xFFFFFFFF. Decode rejects that at L359 (`p.id >= nextId`), so the next load returns false and the whole tree is lost. The cause is the missing range check on nextId in Decode, combined with Add's unguarded post-increment. It is reachable only from a crafted save tail, because a normal Encode always writes nextId > every id and nextId stays at most count+1 in practice.
verdict.minimal_fix: Plain hardening, no NOT RETAIL needed (ext code, not UB). In Tree::Decode after reading the header, reject `nextId == 0 || nextId > kMaxPeople + 1`. Ids only come from Add, which caps people at kMaxPeople, so a valid nextId is never above kMaxPeople + 1 unless people were removed. If removal exists, use a looser cap such as `nextId == 0 || nextId == UINT32_MAX`. Also add `if (nextId_ == 0 || nextId_ == UINT32_MAX) return 0;` in Tree::Add next to the kMaxPeople check. Unit test in tests/unit/ext_family_tree_test.cpp: Decode {FF FF FF FF, 00 00 00 00} with version 2 (append the u8 nameCount 0) expects false after the fix. Before the fix it returns true, and Add, Encode, Decode round-trips to false.

confirmed.title: fix.* row bools are handed to cross-thread readers as plain `const bool*` while the Extensions dialog writes them live on the main thread (fix.save_failure_notice read by the persistence worker; fix.boot_device_lost read by the backend)
confirmed.bug_class: data race (non-atomic bool, written on main, read on a worker / render thread)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (no TSan run). registry_boot.cpp:148 `::IO::PersistenceWorker::_extFixSaveTemp = &Fix().save_failure_notice;` and :154 `BootDeviceLostBackend::SetFixFlag(&Fix().boot_device_lost);` point engine seams at live fields of `g_active` (registry.cpp:826, a plain `State`; rows are plain `bool`, registry.h). The writer is `SetRequested` (registry.cpp:1008-1012: `e.slot(g_active) = on;`), which runs on the main thread from the Extensions dialog via `SetAndRecord` (registry_boot.cpp:331). Fix rows are never locked (`EntryLocked` covers only B/C extensions), so they can change mid-game. The readers run on other threads: (1) `IO::PersistenceWorker::SaveJob` (src/engine/io/persistence_worker.cpp:577, `const bool viaTemp = _extFixSaveTemp != nullptr && *_extFixSaveTemp;`) runs on the persistence worker thread while the main thread keeps pumping the UI, because save state 2 polls `_status` across frames. (2) The DX11 backend keeps the pointer in `std::atomic<const bool*> g_extBootDeviceLost` (src/render/dx11/boot_device_lost/boot_device_lost.cpp:12/19), but the bool it points to is plain. contextdata.cpp reads it in the device-recovery path, which runs on the render thread under ext.render_pipe, beside the main thread's steps (overlap mode). A plain store on one thread and a plain load on another with no happens-before is a C++ data race, so the behaviour is undefined. P0_MAP.md §3 lists `_extFixSaveTemp` in the seam inventory but no F-/S- row covers it. A practical symptom: the main side's `_extFixSaveResult` read (saveload_update.cpp:997) can disagree with the path the worker took. For example, the worker writes `<name>.tmp` and the notice logic then runs with the fix off, or the reverse.
confirmed.repro_idea: TSan / a unit test: start a std::thread that runs PersistenceWorker::SaveJob's first statement (a load of *_extFixSaveTemp) in a loop while the main thread toggles Ext::SetRequested(*FindEntry("save_failure_notice"), on/off). TSan reports the race on g_active.fix.save_failure_notice. In game: open the Extensions window, trigger an autosave or quicksave, and toggle fix.save_failure_notice during the 'Saving' frames. Minimal fix (NOT RETAIL comment): snapshot the row into a std::atomic<bool> that SetRequested / Sync updates, and point the seams at it. Alternatively, read the bool on the main thread when the job is queued and pass it to the worker with the job, as _pendingFilename is passed.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (formal data race on a plain bool; no crash path, worst case is a save that takes the temp-file path while the notice logic runs the other way)
verdict.proof:
The code supports the finding, and none of it could be refuted from the source. It still has no TSan report, so it stays SUSPECTED.

Checked in <worktree> (origin/main):

1. The seams point at the live plain bool. registry_boot.cpp:148 has `IO::PersistenceWorker::_extFixSaveTemp = &Fix().save_failure_notice;` and :149 has `SaveLoad::_extFixSaveResult = &Fix().save_failure_notice;`. :154 has `BootDeviceLostBackend::SetFixFlag(&Fix().boot_device_lost);`. The comment at :143 says it outright: "fixes are global and live: the pointer follows the menu toggle". registry.h:81 declares the rows as plain `bool`.

2. The writer is on the main thread, and fix rows are not locked. SetRequested (registry.cpp:1008-1013) does `e.slot(g_active) = on;` unless EntryLocked, and EntryLocked covers only B/C extension rows. The Extensions dialog reaches it through SetAndRecord (registry_boot.cpp:298).

3. The readers are on other threads. persistence_worker.cpp:577 does `const bool viaTemp = _extFixSaveTemp != nullptr && *_extFixSaveTemp;` inside SaveJob on the worker thread. In the backend, boot_device_lost.cpp:12/19 makes only the pointer atomic (`std::atomic<const bool*>`); the bool it points to is plain. contextdata.cpp:458 reads it through BootDeviceLost::On() on the recovery path, which runs on the render_pipe thread when that ext is on.

Ledger check: P0_MAP.md:488 (§3 concurrency inventory, "Null-by-default static seams") already names the `_extFixSaveTemp` part in nearly the same words: "points at a row's live plain bool ... which the worker reads in SaveJob while the options UI can flip it on main". That is an inventory note, not a finding. No F- or S- row covers it, and S-033 is a different race (state 2's read of `_status`). The boot_device_lost half is not in the ledger. So this is new as a finding, but the hotspot was already mapped.

Why it is not confirmed: an actual race needs the toggle and the read to overlap in time, for example a click during the Saving frames of an autosave. Static reading cannot show that this overlap happens or how the build compiles it. The proof standard asks for a TSan report or a test. The repro is straightforward: a unit test with a std::thread that loads *_extFixSaveTemp in a loop while the main thread calls Ext::SetRequested on the save_failure_notice entry, built with -fsanitize=thread.
verdict.minimal_fix:
Make the value the seams read atomic, with a NOT RETAIL: comment. Two ways:
- Keep a `std::atomic<bool>` mirror for each cross-thread fix row (save_failure_notice, boot_device_lost). Update it in SetRequested/Install (or from a Sync hook called by SetAndRecord), and point `_extFixSaveTemp` and the backend's flag at the mirror. Readers then use relaxed loads.
- Or, for the save path, take a snapshot of the row on the main thread when the save job is queued (as `_pendingFilename` is passed) and hand that value to SaveJob. This also guarantees that `_extFixSaveResult`'s read in state 2 matches the path the worker took.

proof_run.proof:
ThreadSanitizer (clang-19, WSL) reports two data races. Both are in the REAL Ext::SetRequested in src/ext/registry.cpp, built from worktree fa150cf7f (origin/main), and the build also links the real src/render/dx11/boot_device_lost/boot_device_lost.cpp.

Harness: scratchpad/phase2/proofs/fix-row-cross-thread/fix_row_race.cpp
- It wires the seams exactly as registry_boot.cpp:148/:154 does: `_extFixSaveTemp = &Ext::Fix().save_failure_notice;` and `BootDeviceLostBackend::SetFixFlag(&Ext::Fix().boot_device_lost);`.
- The save reader is a verbatim copy of persistence_worker.cpp:577, held in a stand-in static, because persistence_worker.cpp is too heavy to link.
- The render reader is the real `VideoDX11::BootDeviceLost::On()`, the read contextdata.cpp:458 makes.
- The main thread toggles both rows through the real `Ext::SetRequested(*Ext::FindEntry(...), on)`, the same path SetAndRecord takes from the Extensions dialog.
- Fix rows are not locked, so every write lands in g_active.

TSan output (full log in tsan.log, next to the harness):
1) `WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race ... Write of size 1 at 0x55555568bbce by main thread: #0 Ext::SetRequested(Ext::Entry const&, bool) src/ext/registry.cpp:1012:22 ... Previous read of size 1 ... by thread T1: [the SaveJob viaTemp statement] ... Location is global 'Ext::(anonymous namespace)::g_active' of size 188` (the save_failure_notice byte).
2) `Write of size 1 at 0x55555568bbc0 by main thread: #0 Ext::SetRequested ... registry.cpp:1012:22 ... Previous read of size 1 ... by thread T2: #0 VideoDX11::BootDeviceLost::On() src/render/dx11/boot_device_lost/boot_device_lost.h:22:31 ... Location is global 'Ext::(anonymous namespace)::g_active'` (the boot_device_lost byte). Only the pointer is atomic; the bool it points to is not.
Result: `ThreadSanitizer: reported 2 warnings`, exit 66.

Caveats:
- The harness forces the read and the write to overlap. In the game, the overlap needs the row to be toggled while a save job is running on the persistence worker, or while render_pipe is recovering a device. The race is real UB, but it is rare, and its practical effect is small: a save takes the .tmp path while state 2's notice logic reads the row the other way.
- No change was made in the worktree.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
The fix needs a "NOT RETAIL:" comment. Give each of the two cross-thread rows a std::atomic<bool> mirror in src/ext (for example in registry_boot.cpp). Update the mirror wherever the row changes: in Install (boot) and in SetAndRecord after SetRequested. Point the mirror at both seams: PersistenceWorker::_extFixSaveTemp, and BootDeviceLostBackend::SetFixFlag / g_extBootDeviceLost. The seam types become `const std::atomic<bool>*`, and the readers use relaxed loads (persistence_worker.cpp:577, boot_device_lost.h On()).

For the save path, a better option exists: take a snapshot of Fix().save_failure_notice on the main thread when the save job is queued, and pass it with the job, as _pendingFilename is passed. Use that same snapshot for SaveLoad::_extFixSaveResult in state 2. The worker's path and the notice logic then always agree.
