confirmed.bug_class: off-switch purity: state from an ext switched off leaks into faithful drawing
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.repro_idea: Per-entry profile with ext.town_screenshot on: start a game, start a Maximum-quality town screenshot (many tiles, or the up to 600-frame Waiting phase while render_pipe drains), open the pause menu and quit to the main menu while it runs. Turn ext.town_screenshot off in Extensions and start a new game: no status icons and no weather are drawn, and [Ext] shows render_pipe requested=0. A unit check: call Start() with stub singletons, destroy the loop, then construct DrawOptions and assert g_gameSettings->statusIconEnable was left alone. The fix is to reset the run when the game ends (UnlockForGame or GameUpdateLoop::Load), or to make DrawOptions test the row and Stale().

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: off-switch
verdict.proof:
Line-by-line in origin/main (<worktree>):
1. Start() (town_screenshot.cpp ~424-486) sets g_run.phase=Waiting, copies g_choices.ignoreWeather (default true, town_screenshot.h:35) and, if render_pipe was on, calls PipeOff() -> Ext::SetRequested(render_pipe,false), which writes g_requested (registry.cpp:1008-1014).
2. g_run goes back to Idle only through Restore(): from Active() when Stale() (line 412-419), Cancel() (only the page's Cancel button), finish (line 370), and the screen-size and 600-frame paths inside DrawScene. DrawScene is reached only through Active(). PageClose (toolbar_page.cpp:168) does not cancel. UnlockForGame (registry.cpp:1051) calls only SaveTail::ResetAllState and copies requested->active. Nothing on game teardown or GameUpdateLoop::Load touches g_run.
3. Active()'s one caller is gameupdateloop.cpp:1592 `if (Ext::Ext().town_screenshot && Ext::TownScreenshot::Active())`, so with the row off Stale() is never checked.
4. GameUpdateLoop::Draw builds `Ext::TownScreenshot::DrawOptions` every frame with no row test (gameupdateloop.cpp:1423). Its constructor (line 512) tests only `g_run.phase == Phase::Idle || g_gameSettings == nullptr`, then sets statusIconEnable=false and, with ignoreWeather true by default, showWeather=false for the frame.
So when a run is left unfinished by leaving the game (the pause lock covers only the pause hotkey, not the Escape menu) and the next game runs with the class B row off (toggled at the menu, where UnlockForGame makes active=requested, or a loaded save whose B/C set leaves it out via LockForGameWithSet), every frame of that faithful game is drawn without status icons and weather. Also, render_pipe's g_requested stays false for the session because only Restore() calls PipeOn(). The ext-off faithful frame is therefore not byte-identical. No town_screenshot entry in docs/history/review_20261103 (grep empty). The secondary claim (same-address reuse making Stale() false) is speculative and is not part of this confirmation.
verdict.minimal_fix: Reset the run when the game ends: for example, call TownScreenshot::Cancel() (Restore(false) when Stale()) from the GameUpdateLoop teardown / Ext::UnlockForGame path, or make DrawOptions::DrawOptions return early unless Ext::Ext().town_screenshot is set and run the Stale() check there (Restore(false) puts render_pipe back).

confirmed.title: ext.family_tree: g_on is latched per frame, so the next game's load (StartTown citizens) runs OnCreatedSlow with the row already off
confirmed.bug_class: off-switch purity: seam body runs while the row is off (stale per-frame latch across a game boundary)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: The seams test `g_on` (family_tree.h inline OnCreated / OnMarried / OnLifeEvent / OnRemoved: `if (g_on) ...Slow(...)`), and only BeginFrame refreshes it from the row: `g_on = ::Ext::Ext().family_tree;`, which runs in GameUpdateLoop::Update (gameupdateloop.cpp:674). GameUpdateLoop::Load takes the new game's lock (gameupdateloop_load.cpp:740) and then spawns the start town (StartTown_SpawnEntities, gameupdateloop_load.cpp:1239 -> CitizenComponent::Initialize -> citizencomponent_lifecycle.cpp:272 Ext::FamilyTree::OnCreated) before the new loop's first Update. When the previous game had the row on and the new one has it off, g_on is still true. OnCreatedSlow / Ensure then add each new citizen to Town() (std::vector and std::string allocations) and to the s_idOf / s_citizen maps for a game in which the extension is off. The first BeginFrame clears the maps (ForgetAll) but not Town(). No sim or save bytes change, since the codec writes only while the row is active, but extension code runs and allocates while the row is off. The reverse case (row off before, on now) misses the founders' creation, and the sweep later records them as arrivals dated 'now'.
confirmed.repro_idea: Play a new game with ext.family_tree on, quit to the menu, switch the row off and start a new game. A breakpoint or a one-off stderr counter in OnCreatedSlow fires once per StartTown citizen. The fix is to refresh g_on in the load path (next to Ext::SaveTail::ResetAllState) or to test Ext::Ext().family_tree in the seams.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: minor
verdict.proof:
Checked line by line on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>).
1. Only one place writes g_on: Ext::FamilyTree::BeginFrame (family_tree_town.cpp:258-260, `g_on = ::Ext::Ext().family_tree;`). The only caller of BeginFrame is GameUpdateLoop::Update (gameupdateloop.cpp:674). Neither UnlockForGame (registry.cpp:1051-1062) nor the codec's ResetState (family_tree.cpp:472-475) resets g_on.
2. The seams OnCreated, OnMarried, OnLifeEvent and OnRemoved (family_tree.h:213-221) test only g_on. They do not read the row.
3. When a game ends, ~GameUpdateLoop calls UnlockForGame (gameupdateloop.cpp:2427). That runs ResetAllState and sets active = requested, but g_on keeps the value from the last frame (true if the old game had the row on). At the menu, BeginFrame does not run, because nothing calls GameUpdateLoop::Update there.
4. In the next game's Load (gameupdateloop_load.cpp:695), LockForGame runs at line 740 and ResetAllState at 743. Then StartTown_SpawnEntities runs at line 1239 -> CitizenComponent::Initialize -> citizencomponent_lifecycle.cpp:272 Ext::FamilyTree::OnCreated. Update cannot run first: it returns early while m_game == nullptr (gameupdateloop.cpp:637-645), which is before BeginFrame.
5. So with the row now off and g_on still true, OnCreatedSlow runs once for each StartTown citizen. It calls Town().Add (allocating vector and string memory) and Link (inserting into the s_idOf / s_citizen maps) for a game with the extension off. The first BeginFrame sees was=true and now=false, so it calls ForgetAll and CitizenButtonsForget, but Town() is not cleared. The stale people stay in it until the next UnlockForGame / ResetAllState.
6. Save bytes do not change: savetail.cpp:165 ActiveRecords skips rows that are not Active, so the stale tree is never encoded. The sim does not change either: nothing in the sim reads Town().
7. The reverse case (row off before, on now) also holds. g_on is false while the founders spawn, so they are only picked up by the Bind/Sweep on the first BeginFrame, and are recorded as arrivals dated "now" through Ensure.
This breaks the purity rule for a row that is off (extension code runs and allocates), with no effect on the sim or the save. It is not in the ledger: the review_20261103 README, P0_MAP.md and the findings JSONs mention family_tree only for the citizen-button pointers (e319c926c) and the font lookup.
verdict.minimal_fix: Re-read the row when the game is locked, not only once per frame. Split the was/now transition at the top of BeginFrame (set g_on from Ext().family_tree; if it went off, call ForgetAll + CitizenButtonsForget; if it went on, install g_liveHint / g_onTreeReplaced and set s_needBind) into Ext::FamilyTree::SelectForGame(). Call it in GameUpdateLoop::Load right after Ext::SaveTail::ResetAllState() (gameupdateloop_load.cpp:743), next to the FastPaths/PathWorkers SelectForGame calls, and keep calling it from BeginFrame. Simpler alternative: clear g_on (ForgetAll, CitizenButtonsForget, g_on = false) in the family_tree codec's reset path at unlock, then set it again after LockForGame.

confirmed.title: FamilyTree::Decode accepts nextId = 0xFFFFFFFF from a save, so Tree::Add later wraps and hands out id 0 and then duplicates of ids already in use
confirmed.bug_class: hostile save input / unchecked counter wrap / id collision
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: CONFIRMED (failing test). Decode only checks `if (!r.U32(p.id) || p.id == 0 || p.id <= last || p.id >= nextId) return false;` and keeps any nextId above the largest id. Tree::Add (line 27) does `p.id = nextId_++;` with no wrap check, while Find (line 39) assumes ids are unique and ascending (lower_bound). Repro scratchpad/extui/ft_nextid.cpp: decode a v2 payload with nextId=0xFFFFFFFF and one person (id 1), then call Add three times. Output: `decode=1 add1=4294967295 add2=0 add3=1 Find(1)->name=A` / `BUG: ids wrap; duplicate/zero ids handed out` (rc=1). After that the person table holds id 0, which Find never resolves and which Add also returns to mean 'table full'. It also holds a second id 1, so births and marriages attach to the wrong person. The next Encode writes ids out of order, so the next load's Decode refuses the whole record (`p.id <= last`) and the town's tree is lost.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit test (tests/unit/ext_family_tree_test.cpp): Decode a v2 payload {nextId=0xFFFFFFFF, count=1, person id 1, jobs 0, names 0}, then Add twice and expect a non-zero id that is not a duplicate. Minimal fix: in Decode, refuse `nextId == 0xFFFFFFFF` (or nextId > kMaxPeople-scale bound); in Add, return 0 when nextId_ == UINT32_MAX.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (logic; reachable only from a hand-edited or hostile save tail with ext.family_tree on)
verdict.proof: Read on origin/main fa150cf7f, <worktree>/src/ext/family_tree/family_tree.cpp. There is no upper bound on nextId anywhere in Tree::Decode (lines ~345-424). It reads `r.U32(nextId)`, and the only later use is the per-person check `p.id >= nextId -> return false` (line 359), which cannot reject 0xFFFFFFFF. At the end it does `nextId_ = nextId;` (line 423). Even count=0 with nextId=0xFFFFFFFF decodes successfully. Tree::Add (lines 23-37) checks only `people_.size() >= kMaxPeople` (2,000,000) and then does `p.id = nextId_++;` with no wrap check. Starting from 0xFFFFFFFF, the first Add returns 0xFFFFFFFF, the second returns 0 (the same value Add uses to mean "table full", and Find(0) returns nullptr), and the third returns 1, which duplicates the decoded person 1. Find (lines 39-46) assumes the ids are unique and ascending: it tries the fast path id==index+1, then lower_bound. Once 0 and a second 1 are appended, the vector is no longer sorted, so lookups resolve to the wrong person or to none. Encode writes the people in vector order. On the next load, Decode's `p.id <= last` check rejects the whole record, so the tree is lost. The ledger has no entry for this: README F-001..F-217, findings_p3p4.json and findings_p8.json only mention family_tree for font fallback, CodeQL format arguments and C1 table clearing. It is not fixed on origin/main. The proof is static and can be checked line by line. No test or sanitizer run is needed to show the wrap, but the repro the sweep cites (scratchpad/extui/ft_nextid.cpp) agrees with it.
verdict.minimal_fix: In Tree::Decode, after reading nextId, reject `nextId == 0` and `nextId > UINT32_MAX - kMaxPeople`, or another bound that leaves room for kMaxPeople more ids. Alternatively, in Tree::Add, return 0 when `nextId_ == UINT32_MAX` (or 0) before the increment. Add a unit test in tests/unit/ that decodes {nextId=0xFFFFFFFF, count=1, id 1}, calls Add twice and expects no zero or duplicate id. Mark the guard as hostile-save hardening. It is NOT RETAIL-relevant because the code is ext-only.

confirmed.title: BuildPictureLayout recurses once per generation or spouse link through std::function lambdas; a deep chain from a save overflows the main-thread stack
confirmed.bug_class: unbounded recursion on save-controlled graph depth / stack exhaustion
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: CONFIRMED (crash repro). `walkDown` (line 228, recursing at 234) descends the parent-to-child cluster graph, and `walk` (line 291) follows the spouse chain. Both recurse once per link, bounded only by kPictureMaxPeople = 6000. The later hang/measure/place/lift lambdas (309-361) recurse in the same way. Decode accepts any mother/father/marriage links between existing ids, so a class C tail record can hold a 6000-long parent chain or spouse chain. Repro scratchpad/extui/ft_deep.cpp, built with g++ -O0 -static (2 MB stack reserve, the MinGW default): a parent chain of 5000 or 6000 people exits with 0xC00000FD (STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW). A spouse chain of 6000 also exits 0xC00000FD. Chains of 4000 or fewer pass. The caller is toolbar_page.cpp:552 on the UI thread (Make picture button), so the game dies when the player asks for the picture.
confirmed.repro_idea: Load a save whose family_tree tail holds a 6000-person parent chain (each person's mother = the previous id), open the family tree page and press the picture button. Unit test: Tree with 6000 Add(..., mother=prev) then BuildPictureLayout under a 1 MB thread. Fix: make walkDown/walk iterative (explicit stack), as DescendantIds already is.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: crash (crafted save, ext.family_tree on, player presses Make picture); proven in the -O0 debug flavour, not proven for the -O2 release build
verdict.proof:
Not in the ledger: a grep of docs/history/review_20261103 (README, P0_MAP, findings_p3p4/p8 json) finds no family_picture / BuildPictureLayout / walkDown entry. It is also not fixed on origin/main fa150cf7f.

Code (<worktree>/src/ext/family_tree/family_picture.cpp): the std::function lambdas walkDown (228-237, self-call at 234), walk (291-296), hang, measure, place and lift (309-361) each recurse once per parent-to-child cluster link or per spouse link. The only depth bound is kPictureMaxPeople = 6000 (family_picture.h:32, applied at 146-153).

Input reachability: Tree::Decode (family_tree.cpp:344-420) accepts up to kMaxPeople people. A mother/father may be any existing id other than the person's own, and each person may have up to 255 marriages to any other existing id. Only self-links and dangling links are dropped. So a class C save tail can hold a 6000-long mother chain, or a spouse chain in which each person has 2 spouses.

Caller: toolbar_page.cpp:552 calls BuildPictureLayout(Town(), ...) synchronously from the Make-picture handler on the game thread. The CMakeLists sets no larger stack reserve (no --stack), so the MinGW default of 2 MB applies.

Run: the existing repro (scratchpad/extui/ft_deep.cpp, which links the real family_tree and family_picture sources) was run again during this check. `ft_deep.exe 4000` printed "layout people=4000" and exited 0. `ft_deep.exe 6000` (parent chain) and `ft_deep.exe 6000 s` (spouse chain) both printed "built 6000" and then died silently before "layout" (exit 127 under bash, the stack-overflow crash the finding reports as 0xC00000FD).

The repro was built with -O0, which is what the debug flavour uses (CMakeLists.txt:134), so the debug exe is affected. In the -O2 perf and release builds the frames are smaller, and 6000 levels may fit in 2 MB; that part is unproven. Only a crafted or hostile save reaches this. A natural town never builds a chain thousands of generations deep, and ext.family_tree is off by default.
verdict.minimal_fix: Make walkDown, walk, hang, measure, place and lift iterative with an explicit std::vector stack, as DescendantIds and the marriage-component DFS at lines 263-276 already are. walkDown needs a (v, k) frame stack to keep the state==1 back-edge rule. walk can become a pre-order DFS that pushes spouses in reverse order. Measure is a post-order pass and place a pre-order pass carrying left. A cheaper option is a depth guard that trims the picture past a few hundred generations. Add a unit test: a 6000-person mother chain and a 6000-person spouse chain run through BuildPictureLayout on a 1 MB thread.

confirmed.title: Town screenshot ReadTile reads past the frame copy when the back buffer is 64 px tall or less (tile margin larger than the screen)
confirmed.bug_class: OOB read from unchecked platform input (window size)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (static). MakeGrid clamps the payload with `g.payloadW = std::max(1, screenW - 2 * margin)` (screenshot_math.h:144) but keeps margin = kMargin = 64. ReadTile then indexes `pixels[(py + r.grid.margin) * width + (px + r.grid.margin)]` into a width*height buffer. When backBufferHeight <= 64 the first row read (row 64) does not exist, so the read is past the end of the MemAlloc'd copy (for example 100x40: index 6464 in a 4000-word buffer). When the width is 64 px or less, column 64 wraps into the next row. For widths up to 128 px the tile is mostly the discarded margin, so the picture is garbage. Windowed mode allows such sizes: Video::Device::SizeWindow publishes any client rect as backBufferWidth/Height. ScreenSize only replaces a zero size. Start and DrawScene never check that the screen is larger than 2*kMargin. The MemAlloc result at line 314 is also used without a null check.
confirmed.repro_idea: Windowed mode with ext.town_screenshot on: drag the window to a client area of about 300x40, start a town screenshot, and run under ASan or the allocator's guard (or read a sentinel past the buffer). Fix: refuse Start (status line) when screenW or screenH <= 2*kMargin, and stop the run in DrawScene on the same test.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: memory (OOB heap read, ext.town_screenshot only, off by default; needs a windowed client area 64 px tall or less)
verdict.proof:
Static reasoning, checked line by line in <worktree> (origin/main). Not in the ledger: the only screenshot hit in docs/history/review_20261103 is the Vulkan SubmitFrameSoFar null-cb item in findings_p8.json and a P0_MAP.md line about BMP writing. Neither covers this.
(1) Where the size comes from: Video::Device::SizeWindow (src/engine/video/device_window.cpp:69-79) and AdjustDisplay (device_adjustdisplay.cpp:206-211) copy GetClientRect into backBufferWidth/Height with no lower bound. No WM_GETMINMAXINFO minimum is set (window_hook_win.cpp:101 only raises the maximum track size, behind windowAnySize). Windows' default minimum track size covers the whole frame, so the client height can drop well below 64 px. ScreenSize (town_screenshot.cpp:122-129) replaces only a zero or negative size.
(2) Start (town_screenshot.cpp:438, 461) calls MakeGrid(..., screenW, screenH, kMargin=64). In screenshot_math.h:141-149, payloadH = max(1, screenH - 128) = 1 while margin stays 64. Neither Start nor DrawScene (lines 535-541, which only checks that the size has not changed) tests screenW/screenH > 2*kMargin.
(3) ReadTile (lines 303-338) allocates pixels as width*height words (line 314) and reads pixels[(py+margin)*width + (px+margin)]. On the first iteration (py=0, px=0, iy=row*1 < foot.height) the index is 64*width + 64. When height <= 64 this is >= width*height, so the read runs past the MemAlloc'd copy. Example: 300x40 gives index 19264 in a 12000-word buffer.
The arithmetic is deterministic, so no runtime assumption is needed beyond a windowed client height <= 64, which the window code allows. Mostly-margin garbage for heights up to 128 is a correctness side effect, not memory. A missing null check on the MemAlloc result at line 314 is a separate, weaker point: the engine allocator's failure behaviour decides it, so it is not proven here.
A sanitizer run would raise this to the campaign's CONFIRMED proof standard, but the static proof is airtight.
verdict.minimal_fix: In Start, right after ScreenSize(run.screenW, run.screenH): if (run.screenW <= 2 * kMargin || run.screenH <= 2 * kMargin) { SetStatus("The window is too small for a town screenshot."); return false; }. DrawScene already stops the run when the size changes, so the check in Start covers the whole run. Plain hardening (ext code, not retail), no flag.

confirmed.title: Town screenshot allocates its picture (up to 256 MB) with vector::assign and does not catch std::bad_alloc; low memory terminates the game
confirmed.bug_class: resource exhaustion / unhandled allocation failure
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (static). `run.rgba.assign(static_cast<size_t>(run.foot.width) * static_cast<size_t>(run.foot.height) * 4u, 0);` can ask for kMaxPixels * 4 = 256 MB in one block. Nothing in the file catches the exception, so on a phone or 32-bit-constrained heap a bad_alloc reaches std::terminate in the middle of a game. The family tree's PNG path guards the same kind of whole-picture buffer with `catch (const std::bad_alloc&)` (family_tree/toolbar_page.cpp:567, 581) and reports 'memory' instead. WritePng then makes another full-size copy inside SDL_IOFromDynamicMem, which doubles the peak.
confirmed.repro_idea: On Android (or under a capped allocator / ulimit -v in the Linux build), start a Maximum-quality town screenshot of a large map. Fix: wrap the assign in try/catch(std::bad_alloc), SetStatus("Not enough memory for the picture.") and leave Idle without taking the pause or the render_pipe toggle.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (resource; ext.town_screenshot is off by default, the action is player-started, and the size is capped by design)
verdict.proof: The code matches the narrow claim. In <worktree>/src/ext/town_screenshot/town_screenshot.cpp:463, Start() calls `run.rgba.assign(w*h*4, 0)`. ChoosePixelsPerCell(..., kMaxPixels) caps w*h at kMaxPixels = 64,000,000 (line 65, whose comment says the picture is held whole in memory), so one block can be up to 256 MB. The town_screenshot directory has no try/catch, so a std::bad_alloc thrown there reaches std::terminate. It is thrown before the pause lock, the paused flag and PipeOff (lines 476-479), so a fix would leave no half-applied state to undo. This is not a duplicate: the ledger (README F-/S- rows, findings_p3p4.json, P0_MAP.md) lists town_screenshot nowhere, and its bad_alloc rows (F-039, S- signature reserve) are about uncapped counts read from files. The finding is not confirmed for three reasons. (1) No test, fuzz input or sanitizer report backs it, so under the campaign's proof standard it stays SUSPECTED. (2) The impact is overstated on the platforms the finding names. On Linux and Android, overcommit means a 256 MB `new` almost never throws. The zero-fill in assign then touches the pages, and on real memory pressure the OOM killer ends the process, which a catch cannot stop. Only Windows commit-limit exhaustion would raise bad_alloc in a form the proposed catch can handle. (3) The claim that WritePng doubles the peak does not lead to termination. SDL_IOFromDynamicMem and SDL_SavePNG allocate with C malloc and return NULL or false when that fails; they do not throw. They also run later, in a separate phase. A build proof would be a unit or harness run with a capped allocator (Windows job-object commit limit, or `ulimit -v` / ASan `allocator_may_return_null=0` plus `-malloc_limit_mb=200` in the Linux build) driving Start() on a large map, showing terminate rather than a status message. Plain hardening would be acceptable if the ruling wants it, because this is not UB and faithful behaviour does not change while the ext is off.
verdict.minimal_fix: In Start(), wrap line 463 in `try { run.rgba.assign(...); } catch (const std::bad_alloc&) { SetStatus("Not enough memory for the picture."); return false; }`, placed before the pause lock and PipeOff so the early return leaves Idle untouched (mirrors family_tree/toolbar_page.cpp:567). Add #include <new>.

proof_run.proof:
I confirmed the finding on Windows with a standalone harness built with the pinned WinLibs GCC 16.2.0 r3 and `-static`, as the exe is. The harness sizes the picture with the real `src/ext/town_screenshot/screenshot_math.h` (a copy is kept in the proofs dir under `inc/`), using the constants from town_screenshot.cpp: kMaxPixels = 64,000,000, Maximum quality and the +40 height. It then runs the exact expression from line 463, `rgba.assign(w*h*4, 0)`, after capping the process commit with a Windows job object (JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PROCESS_MEMORY).

Results, logged in run.log:
- **512-cell map, Maximum quality:** ppc 14.44, 10456 x 6104, so the assign asks for 255,293,696 bytes (243.5 MB).
  - With a 200 MB cap the harness prints "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'" and exits with 0xC0000409 (-1073740791, the abort/terminate fail-fast).
  - With the proposed catch the same run prints the status line and exits 0.
  - With a 2048 MB cap it allocates fine.
- **1024-cell map:** 238.2 MB, and it also terminates under the 200 MB cap.
- **256-cell map:** 85.5 MB, which allocates fine.

There is no handler anywhere on the call chain. `Start()` is called straight from `PageChanged` (toolbar_page.cpp:141), and there is no `catch (` anywhere in src/app, src/engine, src/game or src/ext/town_screenshot. A bad_alloc therefore reaches std::terminate in the middle of a game.

Limits:
- The harness runs the exact line-463 expression with the real sizing code. It does not drive `Start()` itself, which needs a running GameUpdateLoop and is not linked into `unit`.
- The bad_alloc can be caught only on Windows, when the commit limit is reached. Under Linux/Android overcommit the zero-fill touches the pages instead, and the OOM killer ends the process, which a catch cannot prevent.
- The WritePng copy uses C malloc and SDL returns an error rather than throwing, so it adds to peak memory but does not cause a terminate.
- The throw happens before the pause lock, the paused flag and PipeOff, so an early return has no state to undo.

Severity is low: the ext is off by default, the action is player-started, and the size is capped by design. This is not UB, so the fix is plain hardening.

confirmed.title: pinpanel probe reads the EntityUI controller after the drain has closed and freed its dialog
confirmed.bug_class: use-after-free (dangling pointer across frames)
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: FirePinPanel stores `s_pin_ctrl = entCtrl;` (line 1257), a raw UI::DialogController* owned by the house's info dialog. It then marks the house for removal. Each frame for 14 frames, ToolHarness_Tick does `UI::DialogController* ctrl = s_pin_ctrl; void* rawDS = ctrl->_dataSource; void* checkedDS = ctrl->_dataSource;`. The harness's own comment (lines 3490-3496) says that EntityList_CloseDialogsForDyingEntities (entitylist.cpp:1007) now closes every dialog whose data source carries 0x400 at the drain, and that function calls dlgUI->CloseDialog on it. The pinned dialog and its controllers are therefore released on the next UI clean, and from then on every `ctrl->_dataSource` read is a read of freed memory. It is the exact UAF this probe was written to observe, now performed by the probe itself.
confirmed.repro_idea: Linux ASan build. BANISHED_TOOL_HARNESS=pinpanel with BANISHED_LIVE_TOOLS=1 on an autostart run. ASan should report heap-use-after-free in ToolHarness_Tick at the rawDS read within 1-3 frames of the '[EntityList] closed info dialog' line. Fix: drop s_pin_ctrl once IsDialogOpen(dialog) is false, or re-fetch the controller through the UI list each frame.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: low (diagnostic harness only, BANISHED_TOOL_HARNESS=pinpanel; never reached in a normal run)
verdict.proof:
The chain holds line by line on origin/main (<worktree>), and the bug is not in the ledger: no pinpanel or s_pin_ctrl entry in docs/history/review_20261103/.

1. Nothing keeps the controller alive. GetControllerByType (src/diag/tool_harness.cpp:1195) returns a raw DialogController* through an InternalPtr. InternalBasePtr is trivially copyable and trivially destructible, and Copy is a plain qword move (src/engine/object/Internal.h). There is no refcount, so leaking the placement-new'd InternalPtr pins nothing. FirePinPanel stores s_pin_ctrl = entCtrl (tool_harness.cpp:1257).

2. The house gets flagged. FirePinPanel calls local->MarkForRemoval(), which sets _entityFlags |= 0x400 (src/game/Action/action_base_hunt.cpp:75), and pushes the house onto removalList.

3. The drain closes the dialog. EntityList::DrainRemovals (src/game/Entity/entitylist.cpp:1185) sees removalCount > 0 and calls EntityList_CloseDialogsForDyingEntities first. That function finds each dialog whose EntityUI controller's _dataSource has bit 0x400 set, which matches the pinned house panel; the pin flag on ToolUI does not affect this path. It then calls dlgUI->CloseDialog. UserInterface::CloseDialog (src/engine/ui/userinterface_close.cpp:253) runs OnClosed and pushes the dialog onto _removedDialogs.

4. The dialog and its controllers are freed. UserInterface::CleanRemovedDialogs (src/engine/ui/userinterface.cpp:1002) runs every UI frame (userinterface_frame.cpp:214/315/483) and does `delete dlg` unless dialog flag bit 5 is set, which an ordinary info dialog does not have. ~DialogInstance runs ReleaseFields (src/engine/ui/dialog.cpp:~818), which does `delete c` on every controller in _controllers, including the EntityUI controller that s_pin_ctrl points at.

5. The harness keeps reading. ToolHarness_Tick (tool_harness.cpp:3479-3500) guards only on `s_pin_fired && s_pin_ctrl`. For every frame with rel in 0..14 it does `ctrl = s_pin_ctrl; rawDS = ctrl->_dataSource; checkedDS = ctrl->_dataSource;`. Nothing checks whether the dialog is still open, and nothing clears s_pin_ctrl. The drain happens within a frame or two of the mark, so for the remaining frames of the 14-frame window these are reads of a deleted controller. That is a heap use-after-free; whether ASan sees it depends on MemoryAllocator routing the delete to the system heap. The harness's own comment (lines 3490-3496) says the drain now closes the panel, which confirms that the dialog it probes is destroyed during the window. The "(datasource cleared — dialog closed)" branch reads that same freed memory.

Remaining assumption: dialog flag bit 5 is clear on the EditTool info dialog. That is the normal case; bit 5 marks a dialog owned by a nested ShowDialog UI. A Linux ASan run of the pinpanel route would turn this into sanitizer proof.
verdict.minimal_fix: In FirePinPanel, keep the DialogInstance* as well (s_pin_dialog = dialog). In ToolHarness_Tick, before any ctrl-> read, walk ui->_dialogs; if s_pin_dialog is no longer in the list or is in _removedDialogs, log "dialog closed", set s_pin_ctrl = nullptr and stop. Alternative: re-fetch the controller each frame with GetControllerByType(s_pin_dialog, EntityUI::TypeId()), but only after confirming the dialog is still in ui->_dialogs.

confirmed.title: MouseInject PostUpdate dereferences a target element and dialog that the UI Update in between may have freed
confirmed.bug_class: use-after-free (pointer held across UserInterface::Update)
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: PreUpdate stores raw `g_lastTarget = t.elem; g_lastDlg = t.dlg;` (lines 773-774). Then the real UI::UserInterface::Update runs, with the injected press/release/drop edge on that element. PostUpdate then reads `const uint32_t f = g_lastTarget->_flags;` and `g_lastDlg->_hovering` (lines 847-850) with no liveness check. When the click closes the dialog (a close/OK button, or any DeleteOnClose dialog), Update's CleanRemovedDialogs frees the dialog and its element tree in that same call. PostUpdate then reads freed memory, and with BANISHED_MOUSE_TRACE also reads d->_hoverMouseX/_hoverTime and so on.
confirmed.repro_idea: ASan build, BANISHED_MOUSE_INJECT=hover,press,release and BANISHED_MOUSE_TARGET=#buttonClose (any element whose click closes its dialog), with a panel open (BANISHED_PANEL_HOLD). Expect heap-use-after-free in MouseInject::PostUpdate on the release frame. Fix: before reading, re-resolve g_lastDlg in ui->_dialogs (IsDialogOpen) and skip if it is gone.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: memory (harness-only, armed only by BANISHED_MOUSE_INJECT; diag code, not game/engine)
verdict.proof:
No entry for mouse_inject in docs/history/review_20261103/, so this is not a duplicate. The finding is plausible, but the free does not happen on the frame the finding names. PreUpdate clears g_lastTarget and g_lastDlg every frame (mouse_inject.cpp:737-738), so the pointers never carry over from one frame to the next. The click edge on the release frame only queues an event during the dialog pump in UserInterface::Update (userinterface_frame.cpp ~405-440). The handler runs in the NEXT frame's UpdateEvents (line ~314). A CloseDialog there pushes the dialog onto _removedDialogs, and CleanRemovedDialogs #2 (line 315) then runs `delete dlg` (userinterface.cpp ~1028).

The default hold is 20 frames (mouse_inject.cpp:188), so a release step lasts more than one frame. On release frame 1, PreUpdate runs FindTarget again while the dialog is still listed and sets g_lastTarget and g_lastDlg (773-774). Update then dispatches the queued click and frees the dialog at #2. PostUpdate then reads g_lastTarget->_flags and g_lastDlg->_hovering (847-850), and the trace fields (863-878). That is a use after free if the delete really frees the dialog and its element tree.

Three things are not established statically:
(a) whether the chosen close button's handler calls CloseDialog synchronously inside UpdateEvents, or only sets state that a dialog loop acts on later;
(b) whether the flag-bit-5 owner exemption applies to the dialog;
(c) whether the Element is kept alive by another InternalPtr reference.

An ASan run with BANISHED_MOUSE_INJECT=hover,press,release on a close button, using the default hold or any hold of 2 or more, would settle it. With BANISHED_MOUSE_HOLD=1 the script finishes (g_done) before the dispatch frame, so no read happens.
verdict.minimal_fix: In PostUpdate, before any read, check that g_lastDlg is still in ui->_dialogs (walk the linked list, or use the existing IsDialogOpen-style helper), and that it was not just freed. If it is gone, clear g_lastTarget and g_lastDlg and return. Alternatively, hold Object::InternalPtr references to the element and dialog from PreUpdate to PostUpdate, provided this does not change refcount-driven teardown in a run with the harness armed.

proof_run.proof:
Confirmed with an ASan game run: a private clang-19 ASan debug build of this worktree (base fa150cf7f), run under WSL with lavapipe in a private game dir.

Route: newgame with BANISHED_PAUSEMENU=600 and BANISHED_PAUSEMENU_QUIT=100000. The quit value keeps the pause harness from ever touching the closed dialog. The injector ran BANISHED_MOUSE_INJECT=hover,press,release,w with BANISHED_MOUSE_TARGET=#buttonResume, START=760, HOLD=20 and TRACE=1. An earlier probe run with the prior ASan exe listed the pause menu's elements and gave the name buttonResume.

READ of size 4" at MouseInject::PostUpdate, mouse_inject.cpp:847:38 (`g_lastTarget->_flags`), called from GameUpdateLoop::Update gameupdateloop.cpp:1164. CleanRemovedDialogs #2 then deletes the dialog, and PostUpdate reads the freed element.

confirmed.title: Pause-menu harness probes liveness by reading the vtable word of a possibly freed dialog, then calls a virtual on it
confirmed.bug_class: use-after-free (liveness probe through freed memory)
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: `s_dialog` is the raw DialogInstance* from OpenPauseMenu, held for s_quitDelay frames (120 by default). Line 283 is `void* nowVtable = *reinterpret_cast<void**>(s_dialog);`, and line 275 (open-only mode) does the same every 120 frames. If the menu was closed meanwhile (Escape, Resume, or a world change), this read is of freed memory. If the block was reused by another MainMenuDialog (same class, same vptr, e.g. a fresh Pause.rsc menu), the compare passes and `s_dialog->OnElementEvent(...)` (line 299) dispatches on an object that is not the one that was opened. The comparison cannot detect what it claims to detect.
confirmed.repro_idea: ASan build, BANISHED_PAUSEMENU=600 BANISHED_PAUSEMENU_QUIT=300, and close the menu with Escape (or BANISHED_PAUSEMENU_BUTTON=1 from another route) before the delay expires. Expect a heap-use-after-free read at line 283. Fix: check `ui->IsDialogOpen(&InternalPtr(s_dialog))` instead of reading the vptr.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: memory (diag-only, latent; needs the menu to close inside the probe window)
verdict.proof:
The finding holds up in the code, but it has no sanitizer report yet, so it stays at needs_build_proof.

What the code shows (origin/main, <worktree>):
- `src/diag/pausemenu_harness.cpp:246`: `s_dialog = eui->OpenPauseMenu()` keeps a raw `UI::DialogInstance*`. It holds no `InternalPtr` or reference, so the harness does not keep the dialog alive.
- `src/game/Dialog/toolbardialog.cpp:716` and onward: `OpenPauseMenu` uses MemAlloc to get 0xC8 bytes and adds a MainMenuDialog to the UI. Only the UI owns it.
- The UserInterface close and drain path is quoted in `src/engine/ui/UserInterface.cpp:~800` (0x180120b90). For each dialog in `_removedDialogs`, it unlinks the node and runs the dialog's deleting destructor unless flag bit 5 is set. So a closed pause menu (Resume, Escape, Quit to menu) is freed.
- Lines 257, 275 and 283 use the first word of `s_dialog` as a "liveness probe", and the comments at 255-256 and 289-290 say so outright. The compare can only matter when the object was destroyed, and in that case the read is of freed memory. That is UB by design. The compare also cannot detect what it claims: the allocator may leave the old vptr in place, or the block may be reused by another MainMenuDialog with the same vptr. Either way line 288 passes and line 299 calls `s_dialog->OnElementEvent` on a stale or foreign object.

Why it is not confirmed:
- Every `s_dialog` read is a real use-after-free only if the menu closes between the open and the probe. That is up to `s_quitDelay` frames in click mode, or any 120-frame tick in open-only mode at line 275.
- An unattended route has no closer in that window. It needs someone pressing Resume or Escape, or another driver acting. The proof standard asks for an ASan report: an ASan build with `BANISHED_PAUSEMENU=<n> BANISHED_PAUSEMENU_QUIT=<large>`, then close the menu inside the window. A heap-use-after-free read is expected at line 283, or at line 275 in open-only mode.

Not a duplicate: nothing in `docs/history/review_20261103/` (README F-001..F-217, P0_MAP, findings_p3p4.json, findings_p8.json) mentions pausemenu_harness or this probe. It is not fixed on origin/main.
verdict.minimal_fix: Stop reading through `s_dialog` to check liveness. At lines 257, 275 and 283, replace the vptr probe with `ui->IsDialogOpen(...)` (UserInterface.h:362, retail 0x180120410). It walks `_dialogs` and compares pointers only, never dereferencing the dialog. Wrap the pointer in an `Object::InternalPtr<UI::DialogInstance>` holder or equivalent. Dispatch `OnElementEvent` only when the dialog is open. Delete `s_vtable` and the "vtableIntact" log field. Fallback: check `_addDialogs` too, because a just-opened dialog may still be pending. Comment says the probe is NOT RETAIL harness code.

proof_run.proof:
Observed in a real game run, not with a sanitizer. MinGW GCC on Windows has no ASan, and this worktree-isolated agent was refused access to WSL, so the observed dangling read is the evidence.

Setup: a debug build of the worktree (base fa150cf7f) plus a proof-only patch to src/diag/pausemenu_harness.cpp, saved as proof_instrument.patch and reverted in the worktree afterwards. The patch does two things:
1. Half way through the delay (open + quitDelay/2) it calls ui->CloseDialog on the pause menu. This is exactly what a player's Escape or Resume does.
2. At the probe frame it logs ui->IsDialogOpen(s_dialog) next to the harness's own vptr compare.

Run: functional dir with BANISHED_AUTOSTART=1, BANISHED_PAUSEMENU=600, BANISHED_PAUSEMENU_QUIT=300 and /profile:faithful. From standalone_error.log:
  [PauseMenu] pause dialog=0000024c20e3ca78 vtable=00007ff6476bdcc0 (UI array index=1 of 2)
  [PauseMenuProof] frame 751 - closed the menu (as Escape would)
  [PauseMenuProof] frame 901 - IsDialogOpen=0 vptrProbeSaysLive=0
  [PauseMenu] frame 901 - dialog=0000024c20e3ca78 vtable=00007ff6476bd1d0 (was 00007ff6476bdcc0) UI array index=-1 of 0
  [PauseMenu] click aborted - the dialog's vtable changed, so the object was destroyed under us

Symbols from nm on the same exe:
- vtable for MainMenuDialog = 0x140e5dcb0, so the vptr is +0x10 = ...dcc0.
- vtable for PlayAnimation = 0x140e5d1c0, so the vptr is ...d1d0.

What this shows: by frame 901 the UI's drain had freed the 0xC8-byte MainMenuDialog. Its block was reused by a live PlayAnimation component. Lines 283 and 286 (and line 275 in open-only mode) then dereferenced s_dialog, which pointed into another object's storage, and read that object's vptr. That is a read through a freed pointer.

In this run the reused block happened to hold a different class, so the compare caught it. If the block is reused by another MainMenuDialog, the compare passes and line 299 dispatches OnElementEvent on the wrong object. If the block is left untouched, the compare passes and line 299 dispatches on freed memory. So the probe cannot tell a live dialog from a freed one; it only avoided harm by luck here.

Proof kind is set to none because a run log fits none of the schema's kinds (unit_test, fuzz_input, sanitizer, ghidra_diff). An ASan report would still need the WSL bed.

Unattended trigger: no unattended route closes the menu inside the window. It takes a human (Escape or Resume during the delay) or another driver, so this is a latent bug in harness-only code.

Artefacts are in scratchpad/phase2/proofs/pausemenu-vptr-probe/: proof_instrument.patch, standalone_error.log, vtable_symbols.txt.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
In src/diag/pausemenu_harness.cpp, stop dereferencing s_dialog to check liveness:
- Delete s_vtable and the reads at lines 257, 275 and 283.
- At the click (line 283) and in the open-only report (line 275), wrap the pointer: `Object::InternalPtr<UI::DialogInstance> h(s_dialog);`.
- Treat the dialog as live when `ui->IsDialogOpen(&h)` is true (UserInterface.h, retail 0x180120410, compares pointers only), or when it is still pending in `_addDialogs` (the existing DialogListIndex already finds it there).
- If it is not live, log that the click was aborted because the menu was closed, and return.
- Only otherwise call `s_dialog->OnElementEvent(...)`.
- Replace the log field "vtableIntact" with "open".
- Add a comment that the check is harness code, NOT RETAIL.

confirmed.title: panelclose route calls FindElement on the held dialog without checking that it is still open
confirmed.bug_class: use-after-free (raw dialog/tool pointers held 120 frames)
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: FirePanelClose stores raw `s_pc_dialog = tool->entityRef; s_pc_tool = tool;` (lines 3396-3397). 120 frames later PanelCloseTick computes `openBefore = ui->IsDialogOpen(&dialogRef)` but does not act on it. It goes straight on to `dialog->FindElement(closeName)` (line 3416), `s_pc_tool->lastEntityRef` (line 3420) and `dialog->OnElementEvent(...)`. If the panel was closed in the meantime (the entity's drain close, another tool replacing the EditTool, a modal), these are virtual calls and reads on freed objects.
confirmed.repro_idea: ASan: BANISHED_TOOL_HARNESS=panelclose together with BANISHED_KILL_FAMILY or a demolish route that removes the founding house within 120 frames, or any route that selects another tool. Fix: return when !openBefore, and resolve the EditTool from toolManager->currentTool instead of keeping s_pc_tool.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: low (diagnostic harness only, reached only with BANISHED_TOOL_HARNESS=panelclose; not in shipped gameplay paths)
verdict.proof:
The code matches the description. In <worktree>/src/diag/tool_harness.cpp, FirePanelClose (3386-3406) stores raw pointers `s_pc_dialog = tool->entityRef` and `s_pc_tool = tool`. 120 frames later, PanelCloseTick (3408-3437) computes `openBefore = ui->IsDialogOpen(&dialogRef)` (3414) but only logs it. It then calls `dialog->FindElement(...)` (3416), reads `s_pc_tool->lastEntityRef` (3420) and calls `dialog->OnElementEvent(...)` (3425) without checking either pointer. The block comment at 3376-3377 says the dialog and tool are "never dereferenced" after the click. They are dereferenced before it, with no check.

Neither pointer keeps its object alive. `EditTool::entityRef` is a raw `UI::DialogInstance*` (src/game/Player/EditTool.h:68). EditTool::CloseInfoDialog (src/game/Player/edittool.cpp:186+) goes through UserInterface::CloseDialog, and its comment says that call "releases the DialogInstance and runs every controller's dtor slot". So if the panel is closed during the 120-frame window, line 3416 makes a virtual call on a freed DialogInstance. Retail's own triggers would close it: EditTool::Update (0x1400fcda0) closes the dialog when the entity is dead or has no screen rect. A tool switch would also free s_pc_tool.

Against the finding: in the unattended panelclose route nothing obviously closes the panel within 120 frames. The founding house stays alive, the camera does not move and no input arrives. The suggested repro also looks wrong. BANISHED_KILL_FAMILY kills occupants, not the house (see the "housepanel" note at tool_harness.cpp:1262-1275: "the house entity itself stays alive"). The defect is real at the code level, but no route in the tree has been shown to trigger it.

Not in the ledger: no match for panelclose / PanelClose / s_pc_ under docs/history/review_20261103/. Not fixed on origin/main. The finding needs an ASan run, or a route that closes the panel or swaps the tool within the window, to move from SUSPECTED to CONFIRMED.
verdict.minimal_fix: In PanelCloseTick, after computing openBefore: `if (!openBefore) { fprintf(stderr, "[ToolHarness][panelclose] FAILED: panel closed before the click\n"); return; }`. Read the tool from `toolManager->currentTool` and check it with EditTool_IsEditTool, rather than dereferencing s_pc_tool. Keep s_pc_tool for pointer comparison only.

proof_run.proof:
ASan confirms it. I built the game with ASan (clang-19, debug) under WSL from worktree wf_4a641053-fa7-264 at fa150cf7f. tool_harness.cpp there is identical to origin/main and to ~/openba-review. I ran the panelclose route with one extra existing harness flag that moves the camera away from the town: BANISHED_TOOL_HARNESS=panelclose BANISHED_CAMERA_PIN=-110,-110,20 (Vulkan on lavapipe, /profile:faithful, via ~/linux_run_review.sh newgame).

The house is then off screen, so the retail close path fires. EditTool::Update gets no screen rect (retail 0x1400fcebc) and calls CloseInfoDialog -> UserInterface::CloseDialog, which frees the DialogInstance. At frame 180 the harness still dereferences the stale pointer.

Log sequence:
  [ToolHarness][panelclose] OPEN house[0]=0x508000066d20 dialog=0x5110001e89c0 EditTool=0x50700057e0d0; close scheduled for frame 180
  [EditTool] deselect -> closed info dialog 0x5110001e89c0
  ==21795==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address 0x5110001e8a10 ... READ of size 8
    #3 UI::DialogInstance::FindElement(System::String const&) src/engine/ui/dialog.cpp:871
    #4 (anonymous namespace)::PanelCloseTick(PlayerToolManager*, int) src/diag/tool_harness.cpp:3416
    #5 ToolHarness_Tick src/diag/tool_harness.cpp:3567
  0x5110001e8a10 is located 80 bytes inside of 256-byte region [0x5110001e89c0,0x5110001e8ac0)

That region starts exactly at the dialog pointer the harness kept. ASan's "freed by" stack shows the most recent free of that memory, a lavapipe realloc, so the dialog's memory had already been freed and handed to another allocation before the harness read it. The process ended with exit 3.

confirmed.title: SpouseOrganic dereferences raw CitizenComponent pointers held for up to 3600 frames
confirmed.bug_class: dangling pointer across frames
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: `CitizenComponent* s_widower` and `s_widow` (lines 732-733) are taken in stage 0 and then dereferenced every 60 frames through stages 1 and 2: `s_widower->spouse`, `->age`, `->description->_f4c`, `s_widow->age = ...`, for 1800 + 1800 frames. They are never re-validated against the town list. A citizen who dies in that window frees the component: old age at speed, starvation, disease, or the same harness's BANISHED_KILL_CITIZENS / KILL_FAMILY / FORCE_SICK arms. The harness then reads and writes freed memory, including the write `s_widow->age = ...`. The nomad arm has the same problem: `ImmigrationComponent* s_hall` (line 818, used at line 889) is cached once for the process and never reset. A burnt or demolished hall, or a second world (BANISHED_AUTOSTART_GAMES / quit-to-menu), leaves it dangling.
confirmed.repro_idea: ASan: BANISHED_SPOUSE_PROBE with BANISHED_KILL_CITIZENS=<all> at a frame between probe+600 and probe+4200, or BANISHED_FORCE_FIRE on the hall with BANISHED_NOMAD_HARNESS. verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: low (diag harness only, opt-in flags BANISHED_SPOUSE_PROBE / BANISHED_NOMAD_HARNESS; never in a normal game)
verdict.proof:
Not in the ledger: no hit for SpouseOrganic / s_widower / s_hall / death_harness under docs/history/review_20261103/. The code on origin/main (<worktree>/src/diag/death_harness.cpp) matches the description. s_widower and s_widow (lines 732-733) are raw CitizenComponent* taken in stage 0 (lines 741-753). CitizenDeathHarness_Tick (lines 935-936) calls SpouseOrganic every 60 frames from probe+600. Stages 1 and 2 read s_widower->spouse, ->age and ->description->_f4c, and write s_widow->age at line 784, with no check against townMgr->citizens. The 1800-frame timeouts allow up to about 3600 frames. s_hall (line 818) is cached once, never reset, and used without a check at lines 889-891 (imm->_description, imm->_entity->FindComponent). Nothing re-validates it after the hall is destroyed or a second world loads.
Why it is not confirmed: the static case is missing two links.
(a) That a citizen's death or entity removal actually frees the CitizenComponent storage inside the window. The InternalPtr/Object lifetime and the deferred entity destroy were not traced to a free.
(b) That a death can happen in the window on a real route. tools/harness_route.sh marry runs at FORCE_SPEED=10 without KILL_CITIZENS / FORCE_SICK, for roughly two game months. A founding adult dying there (accident, starvation, disease) is possible but rare. The immigration route builds one world and does not burn the hall.
The repro combinations the finding proposes (KILL_CITIZENS with SPOUSE_PROBE, FORCE_FIRE on the hall, AUTOSTART_GAMES>1 with NOMAD_HARNESS) are opt-in harness configurations no route uses.
Proof needed: an ASan/debug run of SPOUSE_PROBE with BANISHED_KILL_CITIZENS set to fire between probe+600 and probe+4200. It should show a heap-use-after-free in SpouseOrganic, or at least the component pointer leaving townMgr->citizens while it is still being dereferenced.
verdict.minimal_fix: In SpouseOrganic stages 1 and 2, start each poll by scanning townMgr->citizens (list[0..n)) for s_widower and s_widow. If either is missing, print a "[SpouseOrganic] FAIL ... citizen gone" line, set s_organicStage = 3 and return. In NomadHarness, call FindTownHall(gw) on every poll instead of caching s_hall (or re-check the cached pointer against FindTownHall's result), and clear s_hall when the world changes.

The run used the harness_route marry route plus BANISHED_KILL_CITIZENS=6 and BANISHED_KILL_AT_FRAME=2400. - Frame 3000: the stage reads reused heap: "[SpouseOrganic] FAIL frame 3000: married beyond the window (spouses 0000000000000000 / 0000025f0000006a, ages -30067277958511329280.00 / 0.00)". That is a garbage spouse pointer and a garbage age read from freed CitizenComponent storage. Had stage 2 been reached, the write s_widow->age = ... would have gone into the freed block.

No crash this time (crash log empty, exit 0), only silent garbage reads.

The nomad s_hall half (a stale ImmigrationComponent* after the hall burns, or after a second world) was not run. It has the same raw-pointer-cached-forever shape but stays SUSPECTED. The instrumentation was reverted in the worktree. No commit, no PR.
proof_run.minimal_fix: In src/diag/death_harness.cpp SpouseOrganic, start stages 1 and 2 by scanning townMgr->citizens (list[0..n)) for s_widower and s_widow. If either is missing, print "[SpouseOrganic] FAIL frame %d: citizen gone" and set s_organicStage = 3 before any dereference. Also handle TownList returning false (town empty) in stages 1 and 2 by ending the stage. In NomadHarness, call FindTownHall(gw) on every poll instead of caching s_hall, or re-check the cached pointer against it, and reset s_hall when the world changes.

confirmed.title: Sampler exit flush runs concurrently with a still-running sampler thread when the 2 s join times out
confirmed.bug_class: race / use-after-free at shutdown
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: AtExitFlush: `if (g_thread) { WaitForSingleObject(g_thread, 2000); } Sampler_Flush(); if (g_out) { std::fclose(g_out); ...}`. The wait result is ignored. The sampler thread calls Sampler_Flush itself every 10 s (line 249). Sampler_Flush swaps g_flushBuf under g_lock but then runs `WriteSamples(g_flushBuf); g_flushBuf.clear();` outside the lock. A periodic flush of 10 s of samples at 2000 Hz across N threads (20 frames each, with GetModuleHandleExA per frame) can take longer than 2 s. In that case main and sampler iterate, swap and clear the same std::vector at once, and main then fcloses g_out while the sampler is still writing to it. After atexit returns, the static vectors (g_samples, g_tracked) are destroyed under a live thread.
confirmed.repro_idea: BANISHED_SAMPLE=4000 on a stress run that quits right after a periodic flush begins (or add a Sleep in WriteSamples). Expect a crash or garbled standalone_samples.txt. Fix: if the wait times out, skip the flush and fclose (or hold one mutex across the whole of Sampler_Flush).

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: low (harness-only: BANISHED_SAMPLE; exit-time race, needs a periodic flush longer than 2 s)
verdict.proof:
The code supports the shape of the finding, and the finding is not in the ledger. The only sampler entry in findings_p8.json is the different "DiagThreads busy pointer UAF" (Tracked::busy read after Thread object freed). F-068 is the D3D sampler-state table, unrelated. The finding is not fixed on origin/main either: sampler.cpp was last touched by 53403ad45.

Static facts (<worktree>/src/diag/win/sampler.cpp):
- l.257: `if (g_thread) { WaitForSingleObject(g_thread, 2000); }`. The return value is ignored, so on WAIT_TIMEOUT execution goes straight on to l.258 `Sampler_Flush()` and l.259 `fclose(g_out); g_out = nullptr`.
- l.266-271: Sampler_Flush holds g_lock only around `g_flushBuf.swap(g_samples)`. `WriteSamples(g_flushBuf); g_flushBuf.clear();` run unlocked. WriteSamples also lazily fopens g_out (l.130), which is an unsynchronised global.
- l.249: the sampler thread calls Sampler_Flush itself every 10 s. That is the only other caller; main.cpp calls only Sampler_Init. g_stop is checked only at loop boundaries, so a flush in progress runs to completion after g_stop is set.
- main.cpp returns normally (l.1133/1243), so the atexit handler runs while the sampler thread is still alive. After the handler returns, the static vectors and g_lock users are torn down under that thread.

So if a periodic flush is still running 2 s after AtExitFlush sets g_stop, the two threads use g_flushBuf concurrently: main swaps it, and both threads iterate and clear it. Main can also fclose g_out while the sampler is still writing to it. That is a data race / UAF.

The unproven part is whether a flush ever lasts more than 2 s. If the flush finishes within 2 s, WaitForSingleObject returns WAIT_OBJECT_0 and there is no race. One 10 s window at 2000 Hz is about 20k main-thread samples, plus samples from busy workers. Each sample has up to 20 frames and one fprintf per frame. Frames in system DLLs go through GetModuleHandleExA + GetModuleFileNameA, because only the exe is registered via AddMod and the comment saying "engine DLLs are added at the first flush" no longer holds. That is plausibly 0.5-3 s, but it is a timing claim with no measurement. Promoting this to confirmed needs a run that triggers the race: either a Sleep(3000) injected in WriteSamples on a test build with BANISHED_SAMPLE=2000 and a quit just after a periodic flush starts, showing a crash or garbled output, or a timing log showing a real flush longer than 2 s.
verdict.minimal_fix: In AtExitFlush, keep the wait result. If it is not WAIT_OBJECT_0, skip Sampler_Flush and the fclose: leak the buffer and let the process end. The alternative is to hold g_lock across the whole of Sampler_Flush (swap, write and clear) and to do the fclose under g_lock as well. The sampler thread then blocks on g_lock instead of racing.

proof_run.proof:
Confirmed: the exit race crashes the process. The proof is a standalone harness that compiles the unmodified src/diag/win/sampler.cpp (byte-identical to origin/main in <worktree>) with stub headers for diag_threads.h, hw_watch.h, load_time.h and options.h (Opt().sample = 2000). It was built with the pinned WinLibs g++ 16.2.0 r3 at -O1.

How the harness forces the race: the stub LoadTime::CounterToMs is called once per sample inside WriteSamples, and it does Sleep(1). That is the injected delay the verifier asked for, and it makes one periodic flush last much longer than 2 s. main() waits until the sampler thread enters its 10 s periodic Sampler_Flush, sleeps 200 ms and returns, so atexit runs AtExitFlush. A second atexit handler, registered before Sampler_Init so that it runs after AtExitFlush, checks GetExitCodeThread on the sampler thread.

Unfixed result, two runs (run_unfixed.log, run_unfixed_2.log): WaitForSingleObject(g_thread, 2000) times out, and AtExitFlush goes on to Sampler_Flush and fclose(g_out). It prints "[Sampler] done: 13591 samples", and the process then dies with a segmentation fault (exit 139) after about 12 s. The sampler thread was still in WriteSamples, writing to the g_out that had just been closed and nulled. standalone_samples.txt is cut off at about 15 KB of the 13-15k sample lines.

Fixed result (sampler_fixed.cpp, which only changes the wait to INFINITE; run_fixed.log): "[repro] after AtExitFlush: sampler thread exited ... PASS", exit 0, and a full 1.5 MB standalone_samples.txt.

Limit of the proof: the length of the flush is forced by the stub. Whether a real stress-run flush exceeds 2 s without help was not measured. The race and the crash once it does are proven.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
In AtExitFlush (src/diag/win/sampler.cpp l.257), wait for the sampler thread with no timeout: `if (g_thread) { WaitForSingleObject(g_thread, INFINITE); }`. Add a comment that a periodic flush in progress always finishes and the loop then exits on g_stop.

Skipping the flush and the fclose when the wait times out (the verifier's other option) is not enough. After atexit returns, the static destructors of g_flushBuf, g_samples and g_tracked still run under the live thread. The flush is bounded (no sampling once g_stop is set, and the timer wait is at most 50 ms), so INFINITE cannot hang.
proof_run.repro_path: scratchpad/phase2/proofs/sampler-exit-race/ (build_and_run.sh [fixed], repro_main.cpp, stubs/, sampler_fixed.cpp, fix.diff, run_unfixed.log, run_unfixed_2.log, run_fixed.log)

confirmed.title: Windows hang dump and the redzone thread dump call loader-lock APIs while the target thread is suspended
confirmed.bug_class: deadlock (lock held by a suspended thread)
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: WriteHangDump runs SuspendThread(th), then `StandaloneWalkStack(&ctx, &HangStackSink, nullptr)`, then ResumeThread. StandaloneWalkStack (crash_handler_win.cpp:61-65) calls GetModuleHandleExA(FROM_ADDRESS) and GetModuleFileNameA for every frame. Both take the loader lock. RtlLookupFunctionEntry can also take the dynamic function-table lock. redzone_alloc.cpp DumpOneThreadStack (line ~535) and sampler.cpp TakeSample do the same. If the suspended thread holds the loader lock (a hang inside LoadLibrary/DllMain, thread creation/exit, or simply suspended mid-GetModuleHandleEx), the watchdog blocks forever: no standalone_hang.log, and no TerminateProcess(4) on an unattended run. The Darwin twin documents and avoids exactly this (boot_state_watchdog_darwin.cpp lines 133-137: 'Nothing here may ... call dladdr ... while the thread is suspended'). It captures raw PCs first and symbolizes after resuming. Windows does not.
confirmed.repro_idea: Make a worker hold the loader lock (e.g. a test thread that calls LoadLibrary on a DLL whose DllMain sleeps 60 s) while the main loop stalls for 20 s. The watchdog then never writes END HANG and the process never exits 4. Fix: copy the Darwin two-phase scheme (capture RIP/RSP and walk with RtlVirtualUnwind into a raw array while suspended, resume, then resolve modules).

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: low (diagnostic-only, Windows; a rare hang during a hang dump loses standalone_hang.log and the exit-4 path)
verdict.proof: The code is as the finding describes. In src/diag/win/boot_state_watchdog.cpp WriteHangDump, the watchdog calls SuspendThread(th) and GetThreadContext, then StandaloneWalkStack(&ctx, &HangStackSink, nullptr), and only after that ResumeThread(th). StandaloneWalkStack (src/diag/win/crash_handler_win.cpp, about lines 55-90) calls GetModuleHandleExA(FROM_ADDRESS|UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT), GetModuleFileNameA and RtlLookupFunctionEntry on every frame while the target is still suspended. The walker's own comment shows that only the CRT FILE lock was considered ("a suspended thread can be holding the CRT's file lock"). The loader lock and the inverted/dynamic function-table locks were not. The Darwin twin (src/diag/darwin/boot_state_watchdog_darwin.cpp:135, 219-232) captures the raw PCs while the thread is suspended and calls dladdr only after resuming it, which is the scheme the finding proposes. Nothing matching is in the ledger: grep of docs/history/review_20261103 for loader lock, GetModuleHandleEx, SuspendThread and hang dump finds only unrelated POSIX thread and UseGate items, and P0_MAP lists the watchdog only as an Interlocked flag inventory. origin/main has no fix. It is not confirmed because the deadlock depends on ntdll/kernelbase internals: whether GetModuleFileNameA takes LdrpLoaderLock and whether the RtlPcToFileHeader / RtlLookupFunctionEntry SRW locks are held exclusively by the suspended thread. A reader cannot check that line by line in this tree. A repro still has to run: a worker sits in a DllMain that sleeps (or holds LdrLockLoaderLock) while the main loop stalls past the budget, and the result should be no END HANG and no exit 4.
verdict.minimal_fix: Use the Darwin two-phase scheme in WriteHangDump, and the same in redzone_alloc.cpp DumpOneThreadStack and sampler.cpp TakeSample. While the thread is suspended, unwind into a fixed local array of RIP/RSP. Use RtlLookupFunctionEntry/RtlVirtualUnwind only if a test shows they are safe; otherwise copy the context only. Call ResumeThread, then resolve modules with GetModuleHandleExA/GetModuleFileNameA and write the lines.

proof_run.proof:
CONFIRMED as a deadlock: a lock is held by the suspended thread, and the hang dump then blocks forever. The finding names the wrong lock and proposes a fix that is not enough. Tested on Windows 10 22H2 (19045.7807) with the pinned WinLibs GCC 16.2.

The harnesses are standalone programs, not part of the tree. The unit target does not link src/diag/win, and a test that deadlocks would hang the suite. Each harness holds a verbatim copy of StandaloneWalkStack (crash_handler_win.cpp:55) and runs WriteHangDump's sequence: SuspendThread, GetThreadContext, walk, ResumeThread.

1) The loader lock itself is NOT the trigger (probe.cpp, probe_output.log). Worker threads are created before the lock is taken, as the real watchdog is, and each signals completion with a done event: thread exit also takes the loader lock, which confounded the first two attempts (kept as *_confounded.log). In scenario 1 a thread holds LdrLockLoaderLock and is suspended. In scenario 2 a thread hangs inside DllMain during LoadLibrary and is suspended. In both, GetModuleHandleExA(FROM_ADDRESS), GetModuleFileNameA, RtlLookupFunctionEntry and the full walk return. The specific repro in the finding (a DllMain that sleeps) therefore does NOT deadlock.

2) A thread suspended inside the loader's map/unmap path DOES deadlock the walker (stress.cpp, stress_output.log). A victim loops LoadLibrary/FreeLibrary. A pre-created watchdog suspends it, walks it with the verbatim walker, then resumes it. All 7 of 7 runs printed "DEADLOCK: walk stuck after 0..36 walks". The walker was stuck in GetModuleFileNameA (phase 2) in 6 runs and in GetModuleHandleExA (phase 1) in 1 run. The victim was suspended at ntdll+2DA2D, 2E06D, 9D8F4, 2DE63, 2D6A6, 2E2FA, 9DFF4 and 290B6. These are ntdll's module-table and function-table SRW locks, not LdrpLoaderLock. Any thread caught inside LoadLibrary/FreeLibrary or thread start/exit when the hang dump suspends it therefore stops the dump: no END HANG, no TerminateProcess(4).

3) The proposed fix, unwinding with RtlLookupFunctionEntry + RtlVirtualUnwind while suspended and resolving modules after resume, ALSO deadlocks. With "stress.exe 30 twophase" all 3 of 3 runs stuck in RtlLookupFunctionEntry (phase 3), victim at ntdll+9DFF4: the inverted function table lock. sampler.cpp TakeSample calls RtlLookupFunctionEntry while suspended (line 161), so it is exposed too. This likely explains the memory note that the sampler at 4000 Hz can hang boot. redzone_alloc.cpp DumpOneThreadStack (lines 535-572) calls all three APIs while suspended.

4) A lock-free variant passes: 3 of 3 runs, about 1.0M suspended walks each over about 38k load/free loops, no deadlock ("stress.exe 45 snapshot"). It snapshots the module list (EnumProcessModules) BEFORE SuspendThread. While suspended it finds the RUNTIME_FUNCTION by a binary search of the module's own exception directory, reading through ReadProcessMemory(GetCurrentProcess()) so an unloaded module fails cleanly instead of faulting, and calls only RtlVirtualUnwind. It resumes, then resolves names with GetModuleHandleExA/GetModuleFileNameA.

Severity stays low: diagnostics only, and the window is narrow (a thread must be inside the loader's locked region at the moment it is suspended).
proof_run.minimal_fix:
Nothing between SuspendThread and ResumeThread may call GetModuleHandleExA, GetModuleFileNameA or RtlLookupFunctionEntry. All three were observed to deadlock here; RtlVirtualUnwind was not.

In StandaloneWalkStack's hang path (boot_state_watchdog.cpp WriteHangDump), redzone_alloc.cpp DumpOneThreadStack and sampler.cpp TakeSample:
(a) take a module table (EnumProcessModules, plus each image's base, SizeOfImage and exception directory) before suspending;
(b) while suspended, look up the function entry with a binary search of that module's .pdata, reading through ReadProcessMemory(GetCurrentProcess()) into a local RUNTIME_FUNCTION, and record raw RIP/RSP with RtlVirtualUnwind into a fixed local array;
(c) call ResumeThread, then resolve module names and write the lines.

The crash-handler path (the faulting thread walking itself) can keep the current walker. The reference implementation is the "snapshot" mode in stress.cpp.

Artefacts in scratchpad/phase2/proofs/hang-dump-loader-lock/: probe.cpp, sleepdll.cpp, stress.cpp, probe_output.log, stress_output.log, and the per-run logs (stress_run*, twophase_run*, snapshot_run*, verbatim_recheck). No changes in the worktree.

confirmed.title: POSIX/Android hang dump closes the log fd while a slow signal handler may still be writing to it
confirmed.bug_class: race (late signal handler after fd close / fd reuse)
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: For each thread the watchdog sends kDumpSignal and waits `sem_timedwait(&g_dumpDone, &deadline)` for 1 s, then moves on. At the end it runs `close(g_hangLog); g_hangLog = -1;` (line 209). A handler that took longer than 1 s keeps writing through the old fd number: backtrace + dladdr + snprintf, none of them async-signal-safe, and blocked by a lock the hung thread holds. That number is reused at once by the next fopen("standalone_boot_state.txt") in WriteStateFile, so stack lines can land in the state file that tools/boot_state.sh parses. Late sem_posts also satisfy the next thread's wait, so stacks get attributed to the wrong thread, and handlers can interleave in the log. The same code is in android/boot_state_watchdog_android.cpp (lines 219 and 227).
confirmed.repro_idea: Linux: block one worker in a dl_iterate_phdr callback (so dladdr in its handler waits) and stall the main loop for 20 s on an attended run. Then check standalone_boot_state.txt / standalone_hang.log for interleaved frames. Fix: dup the fd per dump and never close it while a post is outstanding (count the outstanding signals), or capture the raw PC in the handler and symbolize on the watchdog.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: low (diagnostic-only, attended POSIX/Android hang dump; needs a signal handler stalled more than 1 s that later resumes)
verdict.proof:
The code matches the description (<worktree>/src/diag/posix/boot_state_watchdog_posix.cpp). WriteHangDump sends kDumpSignal with tgkill (l.194) and waits sem_timedwait for 1 s (l.199-202). On a timeout it moves on to the next thread. At the end it runs close(g_hangLog); g_hangLog = -1 (l.209-210). DumpSignalHandler (l.144-149) calls backtrace, dladdr and snprintf, none of which are async-signal-safe. It then calls sem_post on the same shared semaphore.

Both effects are possible but not proven:

(a) A late sem_post satisfies the next thread's wait, so stacks are attributed to the wrong thread.

(b) A handler that resumes after the close can write to a reused fd number. On an attended run the watchdog loop next calls fopen("standalone_boot_state.txt") (l.84), which takes the lowest free fd.

Two things narrow (b):

- HangLogRaw re-reads g_hangLog before every line (l.100). Once -1 is stored, later lines are dropped, so only a line whose check ran before the close and whose write ran after it can land. That is a single-line window, and the plain-int read/write is itself a data race.
- A handler blocked on a lock held by the thread it interrupted never resumes. Only a lock held by a different thread that is later released leads to a late write.

Unattended runs exit with code 4 right after the dump, so the reuse needs an attended run. The finding is not in the ledger: P0_MAP.md:438 lists the watchdog only for its Interlocked flags, and nothing in docs/history/review_20261103 mentions g_dumpDone or the hang-dump handler. It is not fixed on origin/main. The defect depends on timing, so a build or test is needed to show a late write or a stack under the wrong thread; it stays SUSPECTED until then.
verdict.minimal_fix: Use a generation counter. Each tgkill carries or records an expected sequence number, and the handler posts only if the sequence still matches. Also never close the fd while a signal is outstanding: count the outstanding signals and skip the close (leak the fd) if any are pending. A simpler alternative is for the handler to store only the raw backtrace PCs into a per-dump buffer, with the watchdog symbolizing them and writing them out. Apply the same change to src/diag/android/boot_state_watchdog_android.cpp.

proof_run.proof:
A standalone Linux test fails against the real code. It #includes the real src/diag/posix/boot_state_watchdog_posix.cpp from the worktree at origin/main fa150cf7f; options.h and topology.h are stubbed. It then calls the real BootState::Start() and BootState::{anon}::WriteHangDump(). It was built and run in WSL Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39, g++ 13.3) and exits 1.

Setup: a "loader" thread dlopens libslow.so, whose constructor runs for 1.5 s. glibc runs dlopen constructors with GL(dl_load_lock) held, and dladdr() takes the same lock. So every other thread's DumpSignalHandler stalls in dladdr until the constructor returns. This is a stand-in for any lock held by a thread other than the interrupted one, which the verifier named as the case that leads to a late write. Three parked threads (victim1, victim2, victim3) sit in VictimOneParked, VictimTwoParked and VictimThreeParked.

Observed in standalone_hang.log (run1.log):
- The BootState thread timed out with "(no answer within 1s ...)". Its handler then resumed late and wrote its stack (clock_nanosleep / nanosleep / usleep) under the "--- thread 642 (victim1) ---" header, line-interleaved with victim1's own frames (#0 #0 #1 #1 ...).
- The "--- thread 643 (victim2) ---" section is empty. A stale sem_post satisfied the wait for victim2 before its handler wrote anything.
- victim2's stack (VictimTwoParked+0xD) appears under "--- thread 644 (victim3) ---", interleaved with victim3's.
- After the dump and a 2.5 s settle, sem_getvalue(&g_dumpDone) is 1. That stale post will satisfy the first wait of the next dump, which an attended run can trigger.

Test output: "MISATTRIBUTED: #4 ... (VictimTwoParked+0xD) under header [--- thread 644 (victim3) ---]", "stale semaphore posts left for the next dump: 1", "FAIL".

Part (a) of the finding (late posts satisfy the next wait, stacks land under the wrong thread, handlers interleave) is confirmed.

Part (b) was NOT observed: no write through a closed or reused fd, and standalone_boot_state.txt was clean. As the verifier noted, HangLogRaw re-reads g_hangLog before each line, so only a single-line window between that check and the write remains. That window is also an unsynchronised plain-int race.

The Android twin (src/diag/android/boot_state_watchdog_android.cpp) has the same structure but was not built or run.

Rerun with: wsl.exe -e bash <proofs>/hangdump-late-handler/run.sh
proof_run.minimal_fix:
Do not let a late handler's output or post count toward a later thread:
1. Before each tgkill, store the target tid in a std::atomic<pid_t> g_dumpTarget. In the handler, write and sem_post only if CurrentTid() == g_dumpTarget. On timeout, set g_dumpTarget to 0 before moving on, so a late handler drops its lines and its post.
2. Drain stale posts with sem_trywait in a loop before each tgkill and at the start of WriteHangDump.
3. Make g_hangLog a std::atomic<int>. Count handlers in flight with an atomic incremented on entry and decremented on exit, and skip close() (leak the fd) while the count is non-zero, so a late write can never hit a reused fd number.

A simpler alternative: the handler only copies backtrace() PCs into a per-target buffer and posts. The watchdog thread does the dladdr, the snprintf and the writing, which also removes the non-async-signal-safe calls from the handler.

Apply the same change to src/diag/android/boot_state_watchdog_android.cpp. This is harness code (diagnostic only), so it needs no NOT RETAIL comment.

confirmed.title: Linux crash handler installs the alternate signal stack on the main thread only
confirmed.bug_class: missing per-thread resource (stack overflow on worker loses the crash log)
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: CrashHandler_Install calls `sigaltstack(&ss, nullptr)` once, from the main thread. sigaltstack is per thread and glibc does not give new pthreads one. SA_ONSTACK therefore has no effect on the loader, render, pathfinder and pool threads. A stack overflow there re-faults while the kernel delivers SIGSEGV onto the exhausted stack, and the process dies with no standalone_crash.log (exit 139 instead of 3). Triage relies on the crash log being written ('read standalone_crash.log first'). On Android, bionic gives each pthread its own alternate stack, so this is a Linux gap.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit-level: start a std::thread that recurses without bound after CrashHandler_Install. On Linux no crash log is written and the exit is SIGSEGV, not 3. Fix: install a per-thread sigaltstack from the thread-start seam (Platform thread entry), or at least in System::Thread's entry.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: minor
verdict.proof:
The finding holds. In <worktree>/src/diag/posix/crash_handler_posix.cpp:299-318, CrashHandler_Install sets up one static 64 KiB altStack with `sigaltstack(&ss, nullptr)` and registers SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGFPE/SIGILL/SIGABRT with SA_ONSTACK. It is called once, from main (src/app/main.cpp:787). Nothing else in src/ calls sigaltstack. The engine thread seam does not either: src/platform/posix/thread_posix.cpp Trampoline (latch, then t->entry(t->arg)) and ThreadCreateSuspended's pthread_create have no sigaltstack. The ext/render workers start through std::thread (async_save_compress, background_save, derived_cache, sharp_ui, bc4_chain, async_create, lazy_table…) and the watchdog through pthread_create. None of those install one.

POSIX/Linux semantics, from man pthread_create: "The new thread does not inherit the creating thread's alternate signal stack". Linux clears the altstack on a clone with CLONE_VM. So on every non-main thread SA_ONSTACK has no effect. When such a thread overflows its stack, the kernel cannot push the SIGSEGV frame onto that stack and forces a default-action SIGSEGV. The handler never runs, standalone_crash.log is not written, and the exit is by signal (139), not 3.

Not in the ledger: no grep hit for sigaltstack, altstack or "alternate stack" in docs/history/review_20261103/. It is not fixed on origin/main.

Correction to the scope: src/diag/darwin/crash_handler_darwin.cpp:246-262 has the identical main-thread-only install, so macOS has the same gap. The Android twin is covered by bionic's per-thread signal stacks. This is a diagnostics/harness gap with no retail or sim effect.

A unit test (std::thread with unbounded recursion after CrashHandler_Install, expecting exit 3 plus a log) would show it at run time, but the static chain above is complete.
verdict.minimal_fix: Add CrashHandler_InstallThreadAltStack() to src/diag/crash_handler.h. On posix/darwin it allocates (malloc or mmap) a SIGSTKSZ-or-64 KiB stack and calls sigaltstack. It is a no-op on Windows and Android. Call it at the top of Trampoline in src/platform/posix/thread_posix.cpp, which covers the engine threads. Optionally call it at the start of the std::thread worker entries and the watchdog. Free the stack (sigaltstack SS_DISABLE, then free) before the thread returns. Apply the same to the darwin twin.

confirmed.title: ALLOCSTATS block table deletes by clearing the slot, which breaks linear-probe chains and inflates live bytes
confirmed.bug_class: hash-table deletion bug (stale records, wrong accounting)
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: Insert takes the first empty slot within 32 probes. Lookup (StatsRecordFree, AllocStats_Lookup) stops at the first empty slot (`if (!b.ptr) break;`). Free erases with `b.ptr = nullptr;` and leaves no tombstone. Once an entry earlier in a chain is freed, every later entry in that chain becomes unreachable. Its free is then counted as g_freeUnknown, g_liveBytes and the caller's liveBytes are never decremented, and the stale record keeps the slot for ever, so the table fills and tableFull grows. The report then overstates live bytes and per-caller live totals, which are the figures it exists to give for heap exhaustion.
