confirmed.title: Screen keyboard: a keyboard-hidden event raised by a previous box's SDL_StopTextInput can arrive after the next box's TextEntryChanged(true) and inject a Return that ends the new box's edit; the g_textEntry check and the push are also not atomic
confirmed.bug_class: race (TOCTOU between the UI-thread event watch and the game thread)
confirmed.label: port
confirmed.evidence: WatchScreenKeyboard runs on Android's UI thread: `} else if (e->type == SDL_EVENT_SCREEN_KEYBOARD_HIDDEN) { if (!g_textEntry.load()) return true; std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_mutex); PushScreenKey(SDL_SCANCODE_RETURN, false); }`. g_textEntry is read before the lock, while TextEntryChanged(false) stores false (:139) and only then clears the queue under the lock (:141-144). SDL raises the hidden event asynchronously on the UI thread in two places: SDLActivity's COMMAND_TEXTEDIT_HIDE handler, posted by SDL_StopTextInput, calls onNativeScreenKeyboardHidden(); and SDLSurface.onApplyWindowInsets (API 30+) calls it again when the IME insets become invisible (third_party/SDL/android-project/.../SDLActivity.java:955-965, SDLSurface.java:216-224). Sequence: box A loses the keyboard (store false, SDL_StopTextInput posts the hide), then box B takes it before the IME's insets callback has run (store true, SDL_StartTextInputWithProperties). The late hidden event for A then sees g_textEntry == true and queues a Return. AddScreenKeys delivers it to B, which ends its edit at once, as if Enter had been pressed. A second, smaller window exists: the watch reads true, the game thread clears the queue, then the watch pushes the Return after the clear. The Return then reaches a game binding while no box is active, which contradicts the banner's 'Losing the box clears the queue, so no key typed into the box reaches a game binding' (:38-39). This is NOT RETAIL code (issue #100 screen keyboard); retail had no screen keyboard.
confirmed.repro_idea: On the emulator or an S25: open a dialog with two edit boxes, or end one box's edit and tap a second box within about 300 ms (the IME hide-animation window). Observe in the [Input] trace or by behaviour that the second box ends its edit immediately with no key pressed. Deterministic unit test with a fake SDL event source: call TextEntryChanged(true), TextEntryChanged(false), TextEntryChanged(true), then deliver SDL_EVENT_SCREEN_KEYBOARD_HIDDEN to WatchScreenKeyboard; AddScreenKeys then presses DIK_RETURN. Possible fix: give each start a generation number, and have the watch ignore a hidden event that arrives within one generation of a stop, or count Return only after a hidden event that follows a shown event of the current generation. Also read g_textEntry under g_mutex.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: low (race; a stray Return ends a text edit or reaches a game binding)
verdict.proof:
The code supports a race, but it is narrower than the finding says, and nothing proves it yet. No ledger match: there are no hits for input_android, WatchScreenKeyboard or KEYBOARD_HIDDEN in docs/history/review_20261103. The code is unchanged on origin/main.

Facts from the code:
1. TextEntryChanged is only reached through SetTextEntryActive (src/platform/sdl/input_sdl.cpp:185-190). That function runs once per input update (src/engine/input/input_device_update.cpp:617) on `_suspendCount > 0` and fires only when the value changes. A switch from box A to box B inside one update keeps `_suspendCount > 0`, so false then true never happens. The race needs A's end and B's start in different input updates, at least one frame apart.
2. SDL_StopTextInput (SDL_video.c:5859-5877) calls Android_JNI_HideScreenKeyboard, which posts COMMAND_TEXTEDIT_HIDE to the UI-thread handler. B's start posts ShowTextInputTask to the same commandHandler (SDLActivity.java:1454), so they run in FIFO order. The HIDE handler calls onNativeScreenKeyboardHidden, which calls SDL_SendScreenKeyboardHidden, which calls SDL_PushEvent. The watch runs inside that push, on the UI thread. If the UI thread has not handled HIDE before the game thread's next-frame store(true), the watch sees g_textEntry == true and queues a Return. This needs the UI looper to fall at least one frame behind (16 ms or more), which is possible but not normal.
3. The insets path (SDLSurface.java:216-224) is gated by SDL_SendScreenKeyboardHidden's `screen_keyboard_shown` flag (SDL_video.c:5958-5960). The HIDE handler has already cleared that flag. A late hidden event from the insets path needs B's ShowTextInputTask to set it again (only when imm.isAcceptingText()), and it also needs the IME insets to go invisible after B's show. Whether an interrupted hide animation still reports ime-invisible depends on the device and IME, and has not been shown.
4. The second window is real: line 116 reads g_textEntry outside g_mutex, while TextEntryChanged(false) stores false (:139) and clears the queue under the lock (:141-144). The order watch reads true, game clears, watch pushes would leave a Return queued with no box active. That requires a user-caused hide (Return or Back) at the same moment the game thread lets go of the box. The window is a few instructions wide.

Every interleaving needs either specific UI-thread timing or IME inset behaviour. The described unit test needs a fake event source that does not exist, and the real effect needs an emulator or S25 run. The finding is plausible but not proven.
verdict.minimal_fix: Read g_textEntry under g_mutex in the SCREEN_KEYBOARD_HIDDEN arm, and store g_textEntry while holding g_mutex in TextEntryChanged(false), before the clear. That closes the TOCTOU. For a stale hide: add a generation counter (under g_mutex) that TextEntryChanged(true) increments. Record the generation at each SDL_EVENT_SCREEN_KEYBOARD_SHOWN in the watch, and queue Return on HIDDEN only when a SHOWN of the current generation came before it.

proof_run.proof:
Both halves are confirmed by unit tests that fail on fa150cf7f (Windows, `tools/build.sh unit debug --jobs 2`, then `unit.exe --filter screen_keyboard`).

How the test works: tests/unit/screen_keyboard_race_test.cpp compiles the real src/platform/android/input_android.cpp into the test. It renames its namespace with `#define Platform ScreenKeyboardUnderTest` so it does not clash with the host's input twin. It stubs the ten SDL calls the file makes, because `unit` links no SDL, and supplies a fake non-null GameWindow. The only CMake change is a per-source INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES entry for third_party/SDL/include on that one test.

1. Stale hide (`screen_keyboard_stale_hide_does_not_end_next_box`): the test calls TextEntryChanged(true), then (false), then (true), then delivers SDL_EVENT_SCREEN_KEYBOARD_HIDDEN to WatchScreenKeyboard. AddScreenKeys then presses DIK_RETURN into box B. Output: "stale hidden event pressed Return in box B" and "FAIL ...:128: !pressed". This is deterministic. The control test, a hidden event while the box is active, queues Return as it should and passes.

2. TOCTOU (`screen_keyboard_hide_racing_release_leaves_no_return`): a helper thread holds g_mutex. The watch thread reads g_textEntry == true at line 116 and blocks on the mutex. TextEntryChanged(false) stores false, and the helper lets the mutex go from inside the stubbed SDL_StopTextInput (which runs between the store at :139 and the lock at :141). The game thread usually wins the lock, clears the queue, and the watch then pushes its Return. Output: "199 of 200 rounds left a Return queued with no box active" and, on a second run, "197 of 200 rounds". So with no box active, a Return reaches the poller, which contradicts the banner at :38-39.

Moving the g_textEntry load inside g_mutex in the HIDDEN arm, and the store(false) inside the lock in TextEntryChanged, makes test 2 pass (0 stray rounds). Test 1 still fails, as expected: the stale hide needs the generation fix.

What the test does not show: whether the UI thread really falls a frame or more behind on a device, or whether the IME insets path re-raises a hidden event after the next box's show. No emulator or S25 run was made, so how likely this is on a device is unmeasured. The code has no defence against a hidden event that arrives late, and the TOCTOU interleaving is reachable.
proof_run.minimal_fix: TOCTOU, tested here (toctou_fix.diff): in WatchScreenKeyboard's SDL_EVENT_SCREEN_KEYBOARD_HIDDEN arm, take g_mutex before reading g_textEntry. In TextEntryChanged(false), call g_textEntry.store(false) inside the g_mutex lock, right before the queue clear. Stale hide, not tested: add a generation counter under g_mutex and bump it in TextEntryChanged(true). Record the generation at each SDL_EVENT_SCREEN_KEYBOARD_SHOWN in the watch, and queue Return on HIDDEN only when a SHOWN of the current generation came before it. Before relying on SHOWN, check that Android's ShowTextInputTask always raises it (the verifier notes it only does so when imm.isAcceptingText()). Otherwise use a per-start token that drops the first HIDDEN after a stop/start pair. Both changes need a "NOT RETAIL:" note in the banner (this is issue #100 code).

confirmed.title: Android crash handler's re-entry guard is process-wide: a second thread that faults while the first is still dumping calls _exit(3), cutting off the dump and the debuggerd tombstone
confirmed.bug_class: cross-thread re-entry guard / exit ordering with worker threads
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: `static volatile sig_atomic_t inHandler = 0; if (inHandler) _exit(3); inHandler = 1;` (lines 294-296). The flag is one per process, not one per thread. It cannot tell a fault inside the dump on the same thread (the case the comment means) from an unrelated fault on another thread. While thread A is in CrashHandler (register dump, then RedzoneAlloc_HeapDump, which can be long, then the frame-pointer walk with a pipe() probe per frame), a SIGSEGV, SIGBUS or SIGABRT on thread B runs CrashHandler on B and ends the whole process with _exit(3). The results: standalone_crash.log is cut mid-dump (no 'Stack trace:', no '=== END CRASH'); the sigaction(g_previous) re-delivery at :334-335 never runs, so debuggerd writes no tombstone, which the banner (:18-21) promises; the exit is code 3 instead of death by signal. Two threads faulting together is a common shape with ext.render_pipe: the render thread and the main thread touch the same freed object. The same pattern is in crash_handler_posix.cpp:182 and crash_handler_darwin.cpp:180. A per-thread guard (thread_local, or the gettid of the dumping thread stored in an atomic) keeps the re-entry exit for same-thread re-entry; another thread then blocks (pause / sleep loop) until the first dump finishes. SUSPECTED: no repro has run.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit harness that links crash_handler_posix.cpp (same body): install the handler, start two threads that both write through nullptr after a barrier. With RedzoneAlloc_HeapDump stubbed to sleep(1), standalone_crash.log ends before 'Stack trace:' and the exit status is 3, not SIGSEGV. On device, run two threads with a null write each from a debug key and compare the tombstone and log against a single-thread crash.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: low (diagnostics only; a crash still ends the process, but the crash log can be cut short and the Android tombstone lost)
verdict.proof:
Checked against origin/main in <worktree>. The finding is not in the ledger: no README F-row, P0_MAP entry or S-row mentions the crash handler re-entry guard.

The code supports the claim. Each step can be checked against the source:
1. crash_handler_android.cpp:294-296: `static volatile sig_atomic_t inHandler = 0; if (inHandler) _exit(3); inHandler = 1;`. This is one flag for the whole process, set at entry and never cleared.
2. Installation is at :387-390: `sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO | SA_ONSTACK` with no SA_NODEFER, and the handler is installed for each fatal signal. POSIX blocks the delivered signal only in the mask of the thread that is running the handler. Another thread B keeps its own mask, so a synchronous SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGABRT on B runs CrashHandler on B at the same time.
3. On B, inHandler is already 1 (thread A set it), so B calls `_exit(3)`. `_exit` ends every thread in the process at once. A is stopped wherever it is: in LogRegisters, RedzoneAlloc_HeapDump (:324) or PrintSignalStack (:327). It never writes '=== END CRASH' (:329), never calls FlushLogsToDisk (:330), and never runs the re-delivery `sigaction(sig, &g_previous[sig])` (:334). debuggerd therefore never sees a fatal signal, so no tombstone is written, and the exit status is 3 instead of death by signal.
4. The missing SA_NODEFER also means the guard rarely does what its comment says. If the same signal faults again on the same thread, that signal is blocked there, so the kernel kills the process with the default action and the handler never re-enters. The guard is only reached by a different fatal signal on the same thread, or, as in this finding, by a fault on another thread. Most of what it catches is the cross-thread case.

The same pattern is in crash_handler_posix.cpp:182-184 and crash_handler_darwin.cpp:180-182 (sa_flags at :314 and :261, also without SA_NODEFER).

Not established: how often two threads actually fault together (the "common with ext.render_pipe" remark is speculation). That changes the severity, not whether the defect exists. This is port-only diagnostic code with no retail counterpart, so it involves no faithfulness question.
verdict.minimal_fix: Record which thread owns the dump instead of a process-wide 0/1 flag. Use a lock-free std::atomic<pid_t> owner, set with compare_exchange from 0 to gettid() (pthread_self on darwin). If the CAS fails and owner == the current thread, keep `_exit(3)`: that is genuine same-thread re-entry. If it fails and owner is another thread, wait in a pause()/nanosleep loop (both async-signal-safe) so the first thread can finish its dump and re-deliver the signal. Apply the same change to crash_handler_posix.cpp:182 and crash_handler_darwin.cpp:180.

confirmed.title: Hang dump's 1-second sem_timedwait loses step with late answers: a stale sem_post makes later threads' stacks print under the wrong thread header, and the handler reads g_hangLog (a plain int) while the watchdog closes it
confirmed.bug_class: wait/wakeup mismatch (counting semaphore with timeout) + data race on fd global
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: WriteHangDump sends kDumpSignal to each thread, then `if (sem_timedwait(&g_dumpDone, &deadline) != 0) HangLogRaw("  (no answer within 1s ...)");` (:216-220). DumpSignalHandler always ends with `sem_post(&g_dumpDone)` (:165). A thread that answers after its 1-second deadline (signal masked for a while, or slow to be scheduled: the hung case this tool exists for) still posts later. g_dumpDone is a counting semaphore, so the NEXT thread's sem_timedwait returns at once on that stale count, before the next thread's handler has written anything. From then on every thread's frames land under the following thread's '--- thread N ---' header, or after the end. Two handlers can also write to the fd at the same time, so lines interleave. The stale count also survives into a second HUNG dump later in an attended run (hungReported resets when frames move). Separately, g_hangLog is a plain `int` (:89). The handler reads it on the target thread (HangLogRaw :94, HangLogf :104) while the watchdog thread writes it (:171, then `close(g_hangLog); g_hangLog = -1;` :227-228). That is a C++ data race. A late handler that loaded the fd before the close writes into whatever file next gets that descriptor number (for example a save .tmp the Persistence worker opens). Fix: a per-dump sequence number (atomic) that the handler checks and echoes, with stale posts drained, and the fd held in a std::atomic<int> that is never closed while a request is outstanding. The POSIX twin has the same loop. SUSPECTED: no repro has run.
confirmed.repro_idea: Test (Linux, same loop in boot_state_watchdog_posix.cpp): start two worker threads, block kDumpSignal in the first for 1.5 s and then unblock it, and trigger WriteHangDump directly. The second thread's section of standalone_hang.log is empty or holds the first thread's frames. Run under TSan to get the g_hangLog read/write race report.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: low (diagnostic-only output corruption; the fd-reuse write needs an attended run plus a late handler)
verdict.proof:
The code matches the description, and the finding is not in the ledger: P0_MAP.md:438 only lists the watchdog's Interlocked flags, and README F-/S- rows and findings_p3p4/p8 have no row on the hang-dump semaphore or g_hangLog. origin/main has not fixed it.

What the code does, in src/diag/android/boot_state_watchdog_android.cpp:
- g_dumpDone is a counting semaphore, sem_init(...,0,0) at :330.
- DumpSignalHandler (:161-167) always ends with sem_post.
- WriteHangDump (:212-220) sends tgkill to each tid in turn and waits once per thread with a 1 s sem_timedwait. It never drains the semaphore and never matches a post to a request.
- So a handler that finishes after its 1 s deadline leaves a count behind. The next thread's sem_timedwait takes that count at once, and from then on each section is filled by the previous request. Its own handler can also run while the watchdog is already writing the next header, so lines interleave on the shared fd.

A late answer is realistic, not hypothetical. The handler writes every frame line through an fd opened O_SYNC (:171): up to 40 synchronous flash writes, each with a pipe()/write/close probe (Readable) and a dladdr. On a loaded Android device that can take more than 1 s. A thread that is runnable but starved under the hang also qualifies. If dladdr deadlocks on the loader lock, there is never a post, so that case only causes a timeout, not a stale count.

g_hangLog is a plain int (:89):
- The watchdog writes it (:171, :227-228).
- The signal handler reads it on another thread (:94, :104). This is a formal data race; a TSan report would show it.
- The fd-reuse write needs a late handler to load the fd before close(:227) and write after it. In an unattended run, _exit(4) at :281 follows straight away, so only an attended run continues long enough to hit a reused descriptor.
- The second-dump carryover also needs an attended run. hungReported resets when frames move (:245-248), and the stale count survives into the next dump.

The POSIX twin has the same loop: boot_state_watchdog_posix.cpp:144/153/201/209.

No test, fuzz input or sanitizer report exists yet. A Linux test on the POSIX twin is needed to confirm. The test blocks the dump signal in worker A for 1.5 s, then calls WriteHangDump. Worker B's section should then hold A's frames or nothing. The same test under TSan should report the race on g_hangLog.
verdict.minimal_fix: The fix applies to the Android and POSIX twins. Each request carries a std::atomic<uint32_t> sequence number. The handler copies it on entry and posts only if it still matches; alternatively the watchdog loops sem_trywait to drain the semaphore after each timeout and before each tgkill. g_hangLog becomes std::atomic<int>. After any timeout, close the fd only once the outstanding handlers have answered (or after a final bounded wait); otherwise leave it open, because this is diagnostic-only code. Harness code, so no NOT RETAIL comment is needed.

proof_run.proof:
The finding is confirmed on the POSIX twin, src/diag/posix/boot_state_watchdog_posix.cpp at worktree HEAD fa150cf7f, which is the same as origin/main. The Android file runs the same loop: the per-thread sem_timedwait and the handler's unconditional sem_post.

**Test harness.** The proof is a Linux test that #includes the watchdog .cpp, so the anonymous-namespace WriteHangDump and DumpSignalHandler can be called directly. It was built under WSL with g++ 13.3 and -rdynamic. It installs the handler exactly as Start() does, then starts three threads in tid order:
- A blocks kDumpSignal and unblocks it 1.5 s after the dump starts.
- B blocks it and unblocks it at 3.0 s.
- C answers at once.

**1) Stale post: frames printed under the wrong thread (plain build, failure observed).** In standalone_hang.log:
- "--- thread 664 (thrA) ---" holds only "(no answer within 1s ...)".
- "--- thread 665 (thrB) ---" holds A's stack, "#4 plain_bin + 0x5E8C (ThreadA_Park+0x134)" under pthread_sigmask, and no timeout line. B's section therefore claims an answer B never gave, and B's own frames appear nowhere.
- After the dump returned and the late answers arrived, sem_getvalue(g_dumpDone) was 1. That stale count carries into the next dump.
- The test printed "RESULT: FAIL (4)" and exited 1.

**2) Data race on g_hangLog (TSan build).** The same test built with -fsanitize=thread reports "WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race". The read is in HangLogRaw at boot_state_watchdog_posix.cpp:100 (the g_hangLog check), reached from DumpSignalHandler:146 on thread thrA. The previous write is in WriteHangDump:153 (g_hangLog = open(...)) on the watchdog thread. TSan names the location "global BootState::(anonymous namespace)::g_hangLog". A second report covers the fd itself: write() at :101 in the handler against open() at :153.

In the TSan run, TSan's extra internal thread took the late slot, so that run's section order came out clean. The plain run is the evidence for the misattribution; the TSan run is the evidence for the race.

**Not reproduced.** The descriptor-reuse write after close(:209) (on Android, :227) needs a handler that loads the fd just before the close. Nothing deterministic was built for it. It follows from the reported race but has not been observed.

No source file was changed in the worktree.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
Apply the fix to both boot_state_watchdog_posix.cpp and boot_state_watchdog_android.cpp. This is harness code, so it needs no NOT RETAIL comment.

1. **Sequence number.** Add `std::atomic<uint32_t> g_dumpSeq` and `std::atomic<uint32_t> g_dumpAck`. Before each tgkill, the watchdog increments g_dumpSeq and drains the semaphore with `while (sem_trywait(&g_dumpDone) == 0) {}`. The handler copies the sequence on entry (`const uint32_t s = g_dumpSeq.load();`), writes its frames, then stores `g_dumpAck = s` and calls sem_post. The watchdog repeats sem_timedwait until `g_dumpAck == its own seq` or the deadline passes. A post from an earlier request is consumed and ignored, so it can no longer satisfy the next thread's wait.
2. **Atomic fd.** Make g_hangLog a `std::atomic<int>`. HangLogRaw and HangLogf load it once per call.
3. **Close only after the last answer.** When any request has timed out, do not close the fd until a last bounded wait has collected every outstanding answer. If some are still missing, leave the fd open: it is one descriptor in a diagnostic path that ends in _exit(4) on unattended runs. This rules out a late handler writing into a reused descriptor such as a save .tmp.
proof_run.repro_path: scratchpad/phase2/proofs/hang-dump-sem/ (hang_dump_stale_post_test.cpp, run.sh which builds plain + TSan under WSL against the worktree source, run.log with the full output of both runs)

confirmed.title: Game-files copy can replace WinData packages while the game is starting and reading them: the 'game is running' lock is checked only when the screen refreshes, never at install time
confirmed.bug_class: check-then-act across threads / activities (TOCTOU)
confirmed.label: port
confirmed.evidence: GameFilesScreen.refresh() computes `dataLocked = mMode == Mode.MANAGE && gameRunning()` and only enables or disables the Folder / Archive buttons (GameFilesScreen.java:379-381). Once a COPY_FOLDER or COPY_ARCHIVE job has started, nothing checks again. The worker thread runs for many seconds over ~300 MB and then calls installStaged, which does `if (target.exists() && !target.delete()) ...; if (!f.renameTo(target)) ...` for each package straight into WinData (:248-255). GameFilesActivity has its own taskAffinity (AndroidManifest.xml:65), so the player can start a copy from the launcher shortcut and, while it runs, tap the OpenBA icon. OpenBAActivity.onCreate sees the old data0.pkg (GameFiles.hasGameData), so it does not show the first-run screen and the native main starts reading WinData. Then installStaged deletes and renames packages under the running game. An open fd keeps the old inode, but a package opened later (patch*.pkg, the *.pkm mods list, a re-open) comes from the new set. The game then runs on a mix of two installs. A package opened between the delete and the rename is missing, which gives NO_GAME_DATA or a load failure. OpenBAActivity.startGameAfterFirstRun is safe only because FIRST_RUN starts the game after onFinished. Fix: check OpenBAActivity.gameRunning() in installStaged (or in GameFilesJob.start for copy kinds, plus a flag OpenBAActivity checks before handing off to SDL) and fail the job with 'the game is running'. Not retail: Android glue only (issue #96). SUSPECTED: no device repro has run.
confirmed.repro_idea: On a device or the emulator, from the launcher long-press 'Game files', choose a large WinData folder. While the bar runs, tap the OpenBA icon. Logcat shows the game booting while 'game files: COPY_FOLDER done' lands. Use a second WinData whose patch1.pkg differs, or add a SystemClock.sleep before installStaged, to widen the window. Then check standalone_error.log for package-load failures or mismatched resources.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: race (Android only, needs a deliberate user sequence)
verdict.proof:
Checked against origin/main in <worktree>. The ledger has no entry for it: P0_MAP.md mentions GameFilesJob only for the save-import surface (:275, :353), and there is no F-/S- row on installStaged or the game-running lock.

The code matches the description:
- GameFilesScreen.refresh() (GameFilesScreen.java:379-381) is the only place that reads OpenBAActivity.gameRunning(), and it only enables or disables the Folder and Archive buttons.
- GameFilesJob.start() checks only isRunning() of another job.
- run() -> copyFromFolder/copyFromArchive -> installStaged() (GameFilesJob.java:240-256) deletes and renames into WinData with no further gameRunning() check.
- OpenBAActivity.onCreate (:91) checks only GameFiles.hasGameData() and never GameFilesJob.isRunning(). If old data0.pkg is present it goes straight to SDL, and SDL starts main.
- GameFilesActivity has its own taskAffinity (AndroidManifest.xml:65) and OpenBAActivity is singleInstance. The launcher icon can therefore start the game while a MANAGE copy from the shortcut is still running. Both run in the same process, and the job's static sCurrent and thread survive.

Not refuted: nothing in the code closes the check-then-act window. The FIRST_RUN path is safe because the game starts only from onFinished. If WinData has no data0.pkg, onCreate shows the FIRST_RUN screen, which attaches to the running job, so that case is also safe. The hole is MANAGE with existing data.

Not confirmed: the harm depends on when the native engine opens packages. If every .pkg/.pkm is opened once at boot and held, an unlinked inode stays valid and the only failure is the short window between delete and rename at boot. If it opens or re-opens them later, mixed installs are possible. No device, emulator or instrumented run (for example a sleep before installStaged) has shown a load failure or mixed resources. The finding's own text says no repro has run, so it needs a device or emulator test.
verdict.minimal_fix: In GameFilesJob.installStaged (or at the top of copyFromFolder/copyFromArchive and again just before the install), throw IOException("the game is running; close it first") when OpenBAActivity.gameRunning() is true. In OpenBAActivity.onCreate, when a COPY_FOLDER or COPY_ARCHIVE job is running (GameFilesJob.isRunning() with a copy kind), show the FIRST_RUN-style screen attached to the job and start the game from onFinished, instead of handing off to SDL straight away.

proof_run.proof:
Confirmed by a failing JVM test. The test runs the real, unmodified GameFiles.java and GameFilesJob.java from origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>), compiled with javac 24 against small android.* stubs. Uri is a file path. Handler.post runs inline under a lock. OpenBAActivity is a stand-in with a settable gameRunning().

Scenario (InstallLockTest):
1. A MANAGE COPY_ARCHIVE starts while gameRunning() is false, so the screen's Archive button would be enabled. The archive is a 3-package WinData of about 450 MB, tagged NEW.
2. GameFiles.hasGameData() is still true from the old data0.pkg, as OpenBAActivity.onCreate would see it, so the test sets gameRunning() true. This is the launcher-icon tap.
3. A "game" thread keeps opening patch1.pkg until the job ends.

Result on origin/main (run_origin_main.log, exit 1):
"game booted on: data0=OLD patch1=OLD (gameRunning=true)" ... "WinData after the job, game still running: data0=NEW patch1=OLD data1=NEW" -> FAIL.
installStaged replaced data0.pkg and added data1.pkg while gameRunning() was true. Nothing at install time checks the lock: GameFilesScreen.refresh() is the only reader, and it only greys the buttons.

On Windows the game thread's open handle made the delete of patch1.pkg fail ("cannot replace patch1.pkg"). The job reported failure but left a mixed install on disk: data0 and data1 NEW, patch1 OLD. That breaks the file's own promise that "a failure leaves WinData as it was", because installStaged's delete+rename loop is not atomic across files.

On Android (POSIX), unlink of an open file succeeds, so the whole set is swapped under the running game instead. Any later open, such as modification_refresh.cpp re-scanning *.pkm in the Mods menu, reads the new set. This was not run on a device.

With the minimal fix (a gameRunning() check at the top of installStaged), the same test passes (run_fixed.log, exit 0): the job fails with "the game is running" and WinData stays data0=OLD patch1=OLD.

Artefacts are in scratchpad/phase2/proofs/gamefiles-install-lock/: test/org/openba/game/InstallLockTest.java, stubs/, src/ (origin/main copy), src_fixed/, fix.diff, run_origin_main.log, run_fixed.log.

Rebuild and run: javac -d classes (stubs, src, test *.java), then java -cp classes org.openba.game.InstallLockTest.

Not in tests/unit: the repo has no JVM test target for the Android glue.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
In GameFilesJob.installStaged, before the first delete or rename, add:
`if (OpenBAActivity.gameRunning()) { throw new IOException("the game is running; close it, then copy the game files again"); }`
The staging folder is then removed by the existing finally, and WinData stays untouched (fix.diff in the proofs dir).

Optional follow-up, so the icon tap waits instead of the copy failing: in OpenBAActivity.onCreate, when GameFilesJob.isRunning() and the job is a COPY_FOLDER or COPY_ARCHIVE, show the FIRST_RUN-style screen attached to the job and start SDL from onFinished.

Separate hardening seen in the test: the per-file delete+rename loop can leave a partial install when one replace fails. It could move the old packages aside first and roll them back on error. This is not needed for the race fix.

confirmed.title: Screen-keyboard watch can queue a stale Return after the edit box has let go (or into the next box): it tests g_textEntry outside g_mutex, and a keyboard-hidden event from an earlier StopTextInput arrives on the UI thread late
confirmed.bug_class: TOCTOU on atomic flag outside the queue lock; late cross-thread event
confirmed.label: port
confirmed.evidence: `} else if (e->type == SDL_EVENT_SCREEN_KEYBOARD_HIDDEN) { if (!g_textEntry.load()) return true; std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_mutex); PushScreenKey(SDL_SCANCODE_RETURN, false); }` (:115-119). This runs on the Java UI thread. TextEntryChanged(false) runs on the game thread and does `g_textEntry.store(false); SDL_StopTextInput(w); lock; g_head = g_count = 0;` (:139-144). (1) If the UI thread's load sees true before the store, and the game thread's clear finishes before the UI thread takes the lock, the Return is pushed AFTER the clear. That breaks the banner's promise that 'Losing the box clears the queue, so no key typed into the box reaches a game binding'. The next AddScreenKeys hands that Return to the game. (2) SDL_StopTextInput only posts COMMAND_TEXTEDIT_HIDE. SDL's screen_keyboard_shown stays true until the UI thread runs onNativeScreenKeyboardHidden (SDLActivity.java:965, SDL_video.c:5954-5966). A box that takes the keyboard again in that gap (TextEntryChanged(true) sets g_textEntry = true) gets the earlier hide's HIDDEN event: a Return is queued and the new edit ends at once. Also, SDL_StartTextInput skips the show because the flag is still set, so the keyboard does not come back. Fix: check g_textEntry under g_mutex, and in TextEntryChanged store false under the same lock. Tag each hide with an entry generation, so that a HIDDEN event raised by the game's own Stop is dropped. Not retail (issue #100 glue). SUSPECTED: no device repro has run.
confirmed.repro_idea: Emulator with Gboard: finish a save-name edit with the IME's Return, then tap the same box again within the same frame or the next one (scripted with adb input tap back to back). The new edit closes at once, the keyboard does not reappear, and an extra Return reaches the dialog. For (1), add a usleep between the load and the lock in a debug build and toggle text entry off from the game thread while pressing Back.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: low (theoretical window; a stray Return or an edit that ends early, no memory-safety issue)
verdict.proof:
The finding is not in the ledger: a grep of docs/history/review_20261103 for input_android, KEYBOARD_HIDDEN and g_textEntry returns nothing. It is not fixed on origin/main either: src/platform/android/input_android.cpp:115-119 and :139-144 read as the finding quotes them.

(1) The TOCTOU is real when the code is read line by line. WatchScreenKeyboard reads g_textEntry at :116 before it takes g_mutex at :117. TextEntryChanged(false) stores false at :139, calls SDL_StopTextInput, then locks and clears the queue at :141-144. So this order is possible: the UI thread reads true, the game thread runs the store and the clear, then the UI thread locks and pushes a Return. That Return is left behind after the clear, against the banner's promise at :38-39. To hit it, the user must press Back or Return on the IME, which raises HIDDEN through SDLSurface/SDLActivity, while the game ends the edit for some other reason. The window is only a few instructions wide. The effect is one Return in the game's DIK state on the next AddScreenKeys, and no code shows that a game binding acts on it. This is plausible and unproven.

(2) The stale hide is partly supported by SDL's code. SDL_StopTextInput (third_party/SDL/src/video/SDL_video.c:5860-5877) only calls HideScreenKeyboard, which posts COMMAND_TEXTEDIT_HIDE. screen_keyboard_shown is cleared only when the UI thread runs onNativeScreenKeyboardHidden (SDL_video.c:5954-5966). Until then, SDL_StartTextInputWithProperties skips the show (:5834). The finding's 'tap again within the same frame' case is not reachable, though. SetTextEntryActive (src/platform/sdl/input_sdl.cpp:185-190) is sampled once per input update from _suspendCount>0 (input_device_update.cpp:617), so moving from one box to another inside a frame never produces a false followed by a true. The true has to come at least one input update later, and the Android Handler usually runs the HIDE message within a few ms. The finding's own repro case, ending the edit with the IME Return, does not leave a stale hide at all. In that case SDL hides the keyboard and raises HIDDEN on the UI thread first, so screen_keyboard_shown is already false when the game's TextEntryChanged(false) calls SDL_StopTextInput, and no HIDE is posted. Only an edit the game ends while the keyboard is still up, followed by a new box within the Handler's latency, can lose the next edit. Whether that happens on a device depends on timing.

Both parts are plausible races in issue #100 glue that is not retail code. Neither has a device repro, a test or a TSan report, and the effects are minor. No Ghidra check applies because this is platform code.
verdict.minimal_fix: In WatchScreenKeyboard, take g_mutex first and then read g_textEntry, in the HIDDEN branch as the key branch already does. In TextEntryChanged(false), do g_textEntry.store(false) and the queue clear inside the same lock_guard (call SDL_StopTextInput outside it). For (2), only if a device repro shows it: count Stops made by the game (or SDL_ScreenKeyboardShown before Stop) and drop one HIDDEN per Stop that had a keyboard shown, so that a hide the game started never queues a Return. Add a NOT RETAIL comment, since this is issue #100 glue.

proof_run.proof: Part (1), the TOCTOU, is CONFIRMED by an observed failure. A standalone harness compiles the unchanged origin/main src/platform/android/input_android.cpp (fa150cf7f) into its own translation unit, with SDL stubbed, so it runs the real WatchScreenKeyboard, TextEntryChanged and AddScreenKeys. Case 1b runs the two sides on real threads: the UI thread calls WatchScreenKeyboard(SCREEN_KEYBOARD_HIDDEN) while the game thread calls TextEntryChanged(false), after TextEntryChanged(true), with CPU-hog threads to provoke preemption. On origin/main, 9668 of 300000 runs (2431 of 300000 in an earlier run) ended with g_textEntry == false and a Return still queued after the clear. In every one of those runs the next AddScreenKeys set DIK_RETURN = 0x80 in the game's DIK state, which breaks the banner's promise that "Losing the box clears the queue". With the minimal fix applied to the worktree, the same harness reports 0 of 300000. Case 1 forced the interleaving by holding g_mutex and found nothing in 400 iterations, because the winpthreads mutex hands the lock to the waiters in order (FIFO). Part (2), the late HIDDEN from the game's own Stop, is only shown by a model. The harness injects the late event in sequence: TextEntryChanged(true), then false, then true, then HIDDEN, and box B's edit gets a Return (case2 ENDS). The code has no guard against such an event, but whether SDL/Android actually delivers it inside that window on a device was not reproduced. The verifier showed that within a single frame the false-then-true pair cannot happen, so part (2) stays SUSPECTED. No Ghidra check applies: this is platform glue for issue #100, not retail code.
