confirmed.title: Exported launcher activity turns any caller's BANISHED_* intent extras into harness flags (autoload, kill, save-test, user dir), and a hostile Bundle crashes onCreate
confirmed.bug_class: untrusted input / IPC trust (hostile platform input)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: AndroidManifest.xml:52 `android:exported="true"` on OpenBAActivity (the MAIN/LAUNCHER filter). onCreate:81 `final boolean harness = applyLaunchEnvironment(getIntent());` and :262-276 `for (String key : extras.keySet()) { if (!key.startsWith(FLAG_PREFIX)) continue; final Object value = extras.get(key); ... Os.setenv(key, String.valueOf(value), true);`. options.cpp then reads every flag, so any app on the device can cold-start the game with e.g. BANISHED_AUTOLOAD=Auto (diag/autostart.cpp:155 loads the player's save), BANISHED_KILL_CITIZENS / BANISHED_FORCE_FIRE / BANISHED_SAVE_TEST (writes saves), BANISHED_USER_DIR (re-points settings and saves inside the app's storage) or BANISHED_AUTOQUIT. A harness launch also skips the first-run screen (:91). The ONLY catch is ErrnoException: `extras.keySet()` / `extras.get(key)` unparcel the Bundle, and a Serializable/Parcelable extra of a class the app lacks throws BadParcelableException/RuntimeException out of onCreate, so the app crashes at launch. P0_MAP §11 noted the exposure as a lead; it has no F/S row.
confirmed.repro_idea: From a second app or `adb shell am start -n <pkg>/org.openba.game.OpenBAActivity -e BANISHED_AUTOLOAD Auto -e BANISHED_KILL_CITIZENS 50` with the game process not running: the player's Auto save loads and is mutated with no user action. Crash: send an intent with a custom Serializable extra keyed BANISHED_X. Fix idea: honour the extras only on a debuggable build (ApplicationInfo.FLAG_DEBUGGABLE) or from the shell uid (getReferrer/getCallingPackage == null with adb), and wrap the Bundle walk in catch (RuntimeException).

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: logic / IPC trust (low-moderate: needs a hostile app on the device or adb; it reaches the player's saves)
verdict.proof:
The trust defect can be checked line by line on origin/main (<worktree>):
1) android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:44-57: OpenBAActivity has android:exported="true" and the MAIN/LAUNCHER filter. No android:permission attribute is set. The sibling GameFilesActivity is deliberately exported="false", so the authors knew about the exposure there but not here. Any app can therefore call startActivity on the explicit component with arbitrary extras.
2) OpenBAActivity.java:81: onCreate calls applyLaunchEnvironment(getIntent()) unconditionally, before super.onCreate. It does not check FLAG_DEBUGGABLE, getCallingPackage() or getReferrer().
3) OpenBAActivity.java:259-276: every extra key that starts with "BANISHED_" is passed to Os.setenv(key, String.valueOf(value)), and the method returns true. At :91 that skips the first-run screen.
4) src/app/options.cpp reads these flags with no build-type gating (the file has no #if at all): userDir = BANISHED_USER_DIR at :103, autoload at :112-114, saveTest at :150, killCitizens at :306 (consumed by src/diag/death_harness.cpp:77). Harness flags meant for tools/android.sh are therefore live in the shipped release apk, and any caller on the device can set them on a cold start.
The scope is a cold start only. With launchMode=singleInstance a warm launch goes to onNewIntent and does not reach this path, because the native side has already read Options at boot.
Ledger: P0_MAP.md:350 records this only as a review lead ("Android IPC ... worth a review"). It has no F-/S- row in README.md, findings_p3p4.json or findings_p8.json, so it is not a duplicate.
The second part, the crash on a hostile Bundle, is plausible but not proven here. Only ErrnoException is caught, so a BadParcelableException or RuntimeException thrown while unparcelling a custom Serializable/Parcelable extra would leave onCreate. On API 33+ Bundles unparcel lazily, so only extras.get() on a BANISHED_* key would throw. Proving it needs an on-device intent test. The main finding does not depend on it.
verdict.minimal_fix: In applyLaunchEnvironment, honour BANISHED_* extras only when (getApplicationInfo().flags & ApplicationInfo.FLAG_DEBUGGABLE) != 0. Otherwise ignore them and return false, so the first-run screen is not skipped. This keeps tools/android.sh working on debug apks. Also wrap the keySet()/get() walk in catch (RuntimeException e), log it once and treat the intent as having no harness extras. The env-clearing loop stays as it is.

confirmed.title: Zip import has no bound on the bytes it writes: the free-space check uses the compressed archive size (packages), and the saves import has no check at all
confirmed.bug_class: resource exhaustion (decompression bomb)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: copyFromArchive :431-433 `final long archiveSize = documentSize(mUri); checkFreeSpace(archiveSize); bytesTotal = archiveSize;` then :476-488 writes every *.pkg/*.pkm entry of EVERY folder (not only the winning one) to staging until `zip.read` returns 0, with no running total checked against free space or any cap. importSaves :561-594 calls no checkFreeSpace and pumps each *.sav entry unbounded (`pump(zip, out)`). A deflate entry expands up to ~1000:1, so a few-MB zip fills the shared external storage until ENOSPC. The staging is then deleted, but in the meantime other apps and the game's own saves/settings writes on the same volume fail (WriteFileAtomic, the autosave).
confirmed.repro_idea: Make a zip holding WinData/data0.pkg plus a 20 GB entry of zeros named big.pkg (or x.sav for Import saves), ~20 MB compressed; pick it in the first-run screen or Import saves on a device with less free space than 20 GB; watch df fill to 0 before the IOException. Fix: count bytesDone against usable space minus a margin (or a fixed cap such as 4 GiB per entry / 2x a known retail total) and abort with a message.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (resource exhaustion, transient; it needs the player to pick a hostile zip on their own device, and the staging folder is deleted on failure)
verdict.proof:
I could not refute this. Each step can be checked against <worktree>/android/app/src/main/java/org/openba/game/GameFilesJob.java on origin/main.

1. copyFromArchive (:431-433) calls `checkFreeSpace(documentSize(mUri))`. That is the compressed size of the picked document, or 0 when the provider gives no SIZE. checkFreeSpace (:228-235) skips the check entirely when needed == 0 (`needed > 0 && ...`).
2. The per-entry loop (:476-488) runs `while ((n = zip.read(buffer)) > 0) { out.write; bytesDone += n; }`. bytesDone is only used for progress. Nothing compares it with getUsableSpace(), with archiveSize, or with any cap, and nothing checks entry.getSize().
3. Every *.pkg / *.pkm entry is staged as it streams in. The `depthOf(folder) > depthOf(best)` skip (:462) only applies once data0.pkg has been seen, so a large entry placed before data0.pkg, or at the same depth, is always written. GameFiles.isPackageName gates only the file name.
4. importSaves (:561-605) never calls checkFreeSpace. It runs `pump(zip, out)` (:593). pump (:203-213) is the same unbounded read/write loop with only checkCancel.

So inflated output is bounded only by ENOSPC. A deflate stream reaches about 1000:1, so a zip of tens of MB can write tens of GB to the app's data volume. The IOException then unwinds and `GameFiles.deleteTree(staged)` in the finally block (:505-507 and :613-616) removes the staging. While the copy runs, other writers on the same volume fail, including the game's own settings and save writes if it is running. Android's reserved space (getUsableSpace already excludes it) keeps the OS itself working, which is why I rate this low.

Ledger: this is not a duplicate. P0_MAP.md:353 covers only zip-slip and name filtering, and :275 only notes the exposure. No F- or S- row covers the decompression size, and origin/main has no fix.

Proof kind: this is a missing-bound logic defect that can be verified line by line. Byte-for-byte retail faithfulness does not apply, because this is Android launcher code with no retail counterpart.
verdict.minimal_fix: Plain hardening, no NOT RETAIL comment needed because this is not game code. Read the free space once at the start: `final long budget = usable - (64L << 20)`, using the same margin as checkFreeSpace. Inside the copy loops of copyFromArchive (:480) and pump (used by importSaves), throw `IOException("not enough free space ...")` as soon as the running total of written bytes (bytesDone, or a local counter in pump) exceeds budget. Optionally add a fixed per-entry cap (e.g. 4 GiB for a .pkg, 256 MiB for a .sav) and reject any entry whose getSize() is larger than the cap. Also call checkFreeSpace (or set the budget) at the start of importSaves. The existing finally blocks already delete the staging folder when the exception is thrown.

confirmed.title: installStaged deletes each WinData package before renaming its replacement in; a failure mid-loop leaves WinData with mixed or missing packages and the finally block then deletes the staged copies
confirmed.bug_class: error path continues with partial state
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: `for (File f : files) { final File target = new File(winData, f.getName()); if (target.exists() && !target.delete()) throw ...; if (!f.renameTo(target)) throw new IOException("cannot move " ...); }` and the callers wrap it in `try { ... installStaged(staged); } finally { GameFiles.deleteTree(staged); }` (:347-365, :434-507). If renameTo fails for the k-th file (EIO, the FUSE layer refusing, or the process killed: OpenBAActivity.onDestroy:162 calls System.exit(0) when the first-run activity is finishing, e.g. swiped from recents during the copy), packages 1..k-1 are new, package k is DELETED, and k+1..n are old, while the staged new copies are removed. The file comment promises 'nothing is half-written in WinData' and 'a failure ... leaves WinData as it was'.
confirmed.repro_idea: Inject a renameTo failure for the 2nd staged file (make WinData/patch0.pkg a directory with a file in it so delete() fails, or a read-only replacement target) while replacing an existing install via Game files > Choose the folder: data0.pkg is replaced, patch0.pkg stays/old or is gone, staging deleted. Fix: rename the old packages aside (WinData.old) first, move all new ones in, and roll back on any failure; delete the old set only at the end.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (logic / broken atomicity contract; recoverable by re-running the copy, the source data is untouched)
verdict.minimal_fix: In installStaged, first rename each existing WinData target that the stage will replace to a backup name (e.g. WinData/.old/<name>, or <name>.old). Then rename all staged files in. On any failure, delete the files already moved in and rename the backups back, then rethrow. Delete the backups only after every move has succeeded. Alternatively, correct the comments at :18-19 and :237-238 so they no longer promise atomicity.

confirmed.title: The game can start while a Game files package copy is still installing: the 'game is running' lock is checked only when the screen refreshes, and OpenBAActivity never checks for a running job
confirmed.bug_class: race between a background file job and the game loader
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: refresh():379 `final boolean dataLocked = mMode == Mode.MANAGE && gameRunning();` only greys the buttons. onActivityResult:472-503 starts COPY_FOLDER / COPY_ARCHIVE with `GameFilesJob.start(mActivity, kind, uri)` without re-checking gameRunning(). GameFilesActivity is its own task (manifest taskAffinity org.openba.game.files), so while a long copy runs the player can go Home and tap the icon: OpenBAActivity.onCreate:91 checks only `GameFiles.hasGameData(this)` (true: the old data0.pkg) and starts main, never `GameFilesJob.isRunning()`. installStaged then deletes and renames WinData packages while the engine's package loader opens them: packages opened before the swap are old, ones opened after are new (data0 new + patch1 old), or one is briefly absent between delete() and renameTo().
confirmed.repro_idea: Long-press icon > Game files (game not running) > Choose the folder with a full retail WinData on slow storage; during the copy press Home and start OpenBA from the icon; observe the loader opening a mix (log the package sizes/mtimes at open) or a missing-package error. Fix: OpenBAActivity refuses to start main (or waits) while GameFilesJob.isRunning() is true for a package kind, and onActivityResult re-checks gameRunning() for MANAGE copies.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (race, narrow window)
verdict.proof:
The gap in the lock is real, and a reader can check it line by line in <worktree>/android/app/src/main. (1) GameFilesScreen.refresh():379 computes `dataLocked = mMode == Mode.MANAGE && gameRunning()`. It is used only to enable or disable the Folder and Archive buttons. (2) onActivityResult:472-503 calls `GameFilesJob.start(mActivity, kind, uri)` for COPY_FOLDER / COPY_ARCHIVE and does not check gameRunning() again. GameFilesJob.start:122 checks only isRunning() of the job itself. (3) AndroidManifest.xml gives GameFilesActivity `taskAffinity="org.openba.game.files"`, and OpenBAActivity is singleInstance with the LAUNCHER filter. Both run in the same process, because there is no android:process attribute, so the statics are shared. (4) OpenBAActivity.onCreate:91 checks only `GameFiles.hasGameData(this)` and never `GameFilesJob.isRunning()`. So a game can start while a copy runs (from the icon during the copy, or while the picker is open), and installStaged (GameFilesJob.java:239-256) then runs the delete() + renameTo() loop over WinData while the game is up. That breaks the MANAGE-mode invariant 'the game is running: quit it to replace the game files'.

The stated consequence (the loader opens a mix of old and new packages, or finds one missing) is weaker than the finding says. The staging copy writes outside WinData. Only installStaged touches WinData, and it is a short loop of same-filesystem renames. The engine mounts WinData/*.pkg at boot (src/engine/io/filesystem_find.cpp, the *.pkg enumeration in the pack directory) and keeps the package handles. On Android (Linux), unlinking or replacing a file that is already open leaves the open handle reading the old inode. A game that mounted before the install therefore keeps reading consistent old data; the new data only applies on the next launch. A mixed or missing package needs the boot mount to overlap that loop of a few milliseconds, so it is timing-dependent and has not been demonstrated.

Not in the ledger: README F-001..F-217 / S-001..S-055 have no GameFilesJob, installStaged or Game files entry; S-012/S-023/S-041 are unrelated Android items. It is not fixed on origin/main. A device run or an instrumented test that forces a mount during installStaged is needed to confirm the mixed-load symptom. The broken lock invariant itself is evident from the code.
verdict.minimal_fix: In GameFilesScreen.onActivityResult, refuse COPY_FOLDER / COPY_ARCHIVE when mMode == MANAGE && gameRunning(), with the same status text as refresh(). In OpenBAActivity.onCreate, if GameFilesJob.isRunning() and the job is a package copy, do not start main yet. Either show the first-run screen or a 'game files are being installed' screen that waits for the job, or check gameRunning() again inside GameFilesJob just before installStaged and leave the files staged or fail if the game started.

proof_run.proof:
The race is confirmed by a JVM test that fails. No Android device was attached (`adb devices` listed none), and this is Java code that the C++ `tests/unit` cannot reach.

**How the test is built**
- It runs `GameFiles.java` and `GameFilesJob.java` copied unmodified from the worktree at `fa150cf7f`. They are compiled with `javac 24` against small stand-ins for the `android.*` classes they use: `Context`, `ContentResolver`, `Cursor`, `Uri`, `Handler`, `Looper`, `SystemClock`, `OpenableColumns`, `DocumentsContract` and `Log`.
- The test fills WinData with old packages, then starts a real `COPY_ARCHIVE` job through `GameFilesJob.start`. This is the call `GameFilesScreen.onActivityResult` makes at line 496 without checking `gameRunning()` again.
- The archive stream holds its first read, which stands in for a slow copy.

**Check 1: the launcher gate lets the game start during the copy.** While the job runs, the test evaluates the launcher's gate from `OpenBAActivity.onCreate:91` with `harness = false`, `!harness && !GameFiles.hasGameData(this)`, using the real `hasGameData`. Output:
`copy running: GameFilesJob.isRunning() = true` / `OpenBAActivity.onCreate gate: first-run screen shown = false, SDL main starts = true` -> FAIL.
The gate itself is the expression copied from that line; `OpenBAActivity` was not run, because SDLActivity cannot load on a JVM.

**Check 2: the running game sees a mixed or missing package set.** A "game-loader" thread stands in for the engine's boot enumeration of `WinData/*.pkg`. It takes snapshots of the package set while the job's real `installStaged()` runs its `delete()` + `renameTo()` loop.
- With 400 packages: `mount snapshot 17: 382 old, 18 new, 0 missing of 400 packages`.
- With 12 packages, the race was hit in 5 of 5 runs, for example `11 old, 1 new` and `11 old, 0 new, 1 missing of 12 packages`.

So a mount that overlaps the install loop sees `data0` new while the patch packages are still old, or finds a package missing.

**Check 3: WinData is replaced while the game runs.** The job reports `succeeded=true, Copied 400 packages`. `installStaged` replaced WinData with the game "running", because it has no `gameRunning()` check.

**Limits**
- The test ran on Windows (NTFS) through `File.length()` snapshots, not on Android ext4/f2fs. `delete()` followed by `renameTo()` is just as non-atomic there, so the same gap applies.
- The verifier's caveat still holds: a game that mounted *before* the install keeps its open handles to the old files, so the harm needs the mount to overlap the install loop.

**Evidence and how to re-run**
- Proof directory: `scratchpad/phase2/proofs/gamefiles-lock-race/`
  - test: `src/org/openba/game/GameFilesRaceTest.java`
  - stand-ins: `stubs/android/**`
  - logs: `run_400.log`, `run_12x5.log`
- Re-run: `javac -d out <stubs + src .java>`, then `java [-Dpackages=12] -cp out org.openba.game.GameFilesRaceTest` (exit 1 means it failed).

Nothing in the worktree was changed.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
1. `OpenBAActivity.onCreate`: when `GameFilesJob.isRunning()` and the job kind is `COPY_FOLDER` or `COPY_ARCHIVE`, do not start SDL main. Show the `GameFilesScreen` (FIRST_RUN-style "game files are being installed"), and start the game from its finished callback.
2. `GameFilesScreen.onActivityResult`: for `REQUEST_FOLDER` / `REQUEST_ARCHIVE`, refuse when `mMode == MANAGE && gameRunning()`, with the same status text `refresh()` uses.
3. As a backstop, `GameFilesJob.installStaged` checks `OpenBAActivity.gameRunning()` first and fails ("the game is running: quit it to replace the game files") instead of touching WinData. Optionally, the job and the game's start could be serialized on one lock.

confirmed.title: Folder copy writes to new File(staged, displayName) with a provider-supplied COLUMN_DISPLAY_NAME: '../' escapes the staging folder (e.g. straight into WinData, bypassing staging)
confirmed.bug_class: path traversal from hostile platform input
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: children():292 `out.add(new Doc(c.getString(0), c.getString(1), folder, size));` (display name from the DocumentsProvider), filtered only by suffix (`GameFiles.isPackageName(d.name)` :341), then `OutputStream out = new FileOutputStream(new File(staged, d.name))`. java.io.File does not normalise, so a name '../WinData/data0.pkg' or '../../x.pkm' is written outside WinData.incoming; installStaged never sees it (it lists `staged` only) and deleteTree(staged) leaves it. A name containing '/' without '..' simply fails the job. The system's ExternalStorageProvider cannot produce such names, so the attacker is a third-party documents provider the player picks. P0_MAP §12 lists this as an unverified lead (no F/S row).
confirmed.repro_idea: A test DocumentsProvider app returning a child with display name '../WinData/evil.pkm' (mime application/octet-stream) beside a data0.pkg; pick its root in Choose the folder; evil.pkm appears in WinData without the staging/rollback path. Fix: reject names containing '/', '\\', or equal to '.'/'..' (or take new File(name).getName() and require it to equal name), as the archive path already does by numbering folders.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: minor
verdict.proof:
Checked against origin/main fa150cf7f in <worktree>. The finding holds; each step below can be checked line by line.

1. GameFilesJob.java:292 `children()` stores `c.getString(1)` (COLUMN_DISPLAY_NAME, which the DocumentsProvider supplies) as Doc.name unchanged.
2. :341 `GameFiles.isPackageName(d.name)` (GameFiles.java:51-57) is the only filter. It is a suffix test only: `lower.endsWith(PACKAGE_SUFFIX) || lower.endsWith(MOD_SUFFIX)`. It does not reject '/', '\\' or '..', so a name like '../WinData/evil.pkm' passes.
3. :347 `stagingDir("WinData.incoming")` (:215-226) gives `<dataDir>/WinData.incoming`. GameFiles.winDataDir (GameFiles.java:32-40) is `<dataDir>/WinData`, a sibling folder. So `new File(staged, "../WinData/evil.pkm")` resolves to `<dataDir>/WinData/evil.pkm`. java.io.File does not normalise the path, and FileOutputStream passes it to open(2), which follows '..'.
4. :355 `new FileOutputStream(new File(staged, d.name))` therefore writes the provider's bytes outside the staging folder. `installStaged` (:239-257) only lists `staged`, and `deleteTree(staged)` in the finally block (:364) only removes the staging folder. The escaped file stays in place even when the job fails or is cancelled, so it bypasses the staging and rollback path.
5. The holdsBasePackage gate (:298-305) only needs one sibling child named exactly data0.pkg, which a hostile provider can supply.

Ledger: the only mention is P0_MAP.md:354, which says "Not verified." There is no F- or S- row in README.md or the findings JSON, so this is not a duplicate. Nothing on origin/main fixes it.

Exposure: only a third-party DocumentsProvider that the player picks in Choose the folder can produce such a name; the system ExternalStorageProvider cannot. This is hostile non-UB input, so under the campaign ruling it gets plain hardening and is not a retail matter.
verdict.minimal_fix: In copyFromFolder's package filter (GameFilesJob.java:341), only accept a child whose name is a plain file name: `d.name.equals(new File(d.name).getName()) && !d.name.contains("\\") && !d.name.equals(".") && !d.name.equals("..")`. Skip any other child, the same way a non-package child is skipped. No retail comment is needed because this is Android launcher hardening.

confirmed.title: Phone-seed key matching differs from the settings parser: a key written with blanks, after a BOM or indented is 'missing', so the seed appends a line that overrides the player's value (last wins)
confirmed.bug_class: inconsistent parser for the same input (settings.cfg)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: phone_seed.h:216-218 `const size_t eq = line.find('='); return eq == npos ? std::string() : line.substr(0, eq);` compares the raw text before '=' (only a trailing '\r' dropped, :226). IO::SettingsFile::Parse (src/engine/io/settings_file.cpp:100-138) skips a leading UTF-8 BOM, trims blanks around key and value, and unescapes; and `entries[it->second].value = ...; // last wins`. So a hand-edited `VideoRenderScale = 75` (or ` GameEdgeScroll=true`) is a key the engine has, but MissingSeedLines reports it missing and SeedPhoneSettings (app_android.cpp:206-211) appends `VideoRenderScale=50`, which Parse then takes over the player's 75. The header contract is 'A key the file has keeps its value, whatever it is'. The engine rewrites the file canonically after a run, so only a hand edit between runs reaches it.
confirmed.repro_idea:
Unit test in tests/unit/phone_seed_test.cpp: MissingSeedLines("VideoRenderScale = 75
", "VideoRenderScale=50
") returns "VideoRenderScale=50
" (expected empty); feed existing+result to IO::SettingsFile::Parse and observe 50. Fix: take the keys of `existing` from IO::SettingsFile::Parse instead of a raw split.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: minor (Android only; needs a hand edit of settings.cfg between runs, since the engine writes the file back as canonical key=value)
verdict.proof:
The logic defect can be checked line by line. The finding cites the wrong lines: on origin/main, phone_seed.h has 97 lines, and the code is at :20-36, not :216. In <worktree>/src/platform/android/phone_seed.h:21-23, MissingSeedLines' keyOf is `line.find('=')` followed by `line.substr(0, eq)`. hasKey (:25-36) compares that raw prefix with `==`, after dropping only a trailing '\r' (:31). It skips no BOM, trims no blanks and unescapes nothing. IO::SettingsFile Parse (src/engine/io/settings_file.cpp, the block at ~:100-140) does differ: it skips a leading EF BB BF, skips leading blanks, splits at the first unescaped '=', runs TrimRaw on the key and the value, unescapes both, and does `entries[it->second].value = std::move(value); // last wins` for a repeated key.

Trace with existing = "VideoRenderScale = 75\n":
1. keyOf(existing line) = "VideoRenderScale " (trailing blank kept).
2. The seed key "VideoRenderScale" therefore does not match, so hasKey returns false and MissingSeedLines returns "VideoRenderScale=50\n".
3. In app_android.cpp:196-215 (SeedPhoneSettings), a non-empty `missing` is appended to settings.cfg with fopen(path, "a").
4. Parse then finds the key "VideoRenderScale" twice, and last wins, so the value becomes 50. The player's 75 is lost.

A first line behind a UTF-8 BOM or an indented line fails the same way. This breaks the header contract at :7-8: "A key the file has keeps its value, whatever it is."

The ledger has no entry for it: a grep of docs/history/review_20261103 for phone_seed/MissingSeed found nothing. It is not fixed on origin/main. No retail angle applies, because the file is marked NOT RETAIL.
verdict.minimal_fix: In MissingSeedLines, take the key set of `existing` from IO::SettingsFile::Parse(existing.data(), existing.size()) instead of the raw split. If phone_seed.h must stay engine-free, mirror Parse's key rules in keyOf: skip a leading BOM on the first line, skip comment lines starting with '#', split at the first unescaped '=', and trim blanks around the key. Add the repro case to tests/unit/phone_seed_test.cpp: MissingSeedLines("VideoRenderScale = 75\n", "VideoRenderScale=50\n") must return "".

confirmed.title: Hang dump: a thread that answers the dump signal after the 1 s timeout posts a stale semaphore, writes concurrently with later threads, and can write after close() into a reused fd; dladdr runs inside the signal handler
confirmed.bug_class: signal-handler race / fd reuse / non-async-signal-safe call
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.evidence: WriteHangDump :212-220 `syscall(SYS_tgkill, pid, tid, kDumpSignal)` then `if (sem_timedwait(&g_dumpDone, &deadline) != 0) HangLogRaw("  (no answer within 1s ...)")` and moves on; DumpSignalHandler :161-166 always ends with `sem_post(&g_dumpDone)`. A thread stuck in the kernel (the usual hang: a driver ioctl, fsync) takes the signal later: its post satisfies the NEXT thread's wait before that thread's handler ran, so two handlers write g_hangLog at once and the watchdog reaches :226-228 `fsync(g_hangLog); close(g_hangLog); g_hangLog = -1;` while a handler may still read the plain int g_hangLog and write(2) to it. Between close() and the -1 store the fd number can be reused by another thread's open (the Persistence worker's FileCreateWrite, the next WriteStateFile), so stack text lands in that file. DumpFrame :125 calls dladdr in the handler, which takes the linker lock: a thread interrupted while another holds it blocks in the handler for good, and an attended run (an icon launch: unattendedBoot false, no _exit) then never recovers from a transient stall. Same pattern in src/diag/posix/boot_state_watchdog_posix.cpp:201-209.
confirmed.repro_idea: Harness test: block the dump signal on one worker thread (pthread_sigmask) for 1.5 s, force a HUNG (BANISHED_ hang injection or a 21 s sleep on the main loop); the dump shows the next thread's stack under the wrong header / interleaved lines, and a late handler's write after close. Fix: carry the target tid in the handler (sigqueue value or a global the handler compares with gettid()) and ignore late answers; keep g_hangLog open (or atomic) until every handler has answered; resolve symbols in the watchdog thread from saved pcs instead of calling dladdr in the handler.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: low (diagnostic-only path, runs once per detected HUNG; wrong attribution in standalone_hang.log, rare stray write into a reused fd)
verdict.proof:
Not in the ledger: the README F-/S- table, P0_MAP.md (only :438, the Windows Interlocked flags) and findings_p3p4.json / findings_p8.json have no entry for the Android or POSIX hang dump. Not fixed on origin/main (openba-review).

The core defect can be checked line by line in src/diag/android/boot_state_watchdog_android.cpp:
1. :212 tgkill queues kDumpSignal for the target. :216-220 waits on g_dumpDone for at most 1 s. On timeout it only logs and continues the readdir loop. Nothing cancels the pending signal and nothing records which tid it was meant for.
2. :161-166 DumpSignalHandler always runs DumpInterruptedStack and then calls sem_post(&g_dumpDone) without condition, with no tid check.
3. The kernel delivers a pending signal when the thread next returns to user space. A thread in uninterruptible sleep longer than 1 s (driver ioctl, fsync) therefore runs the handler late. Its sem_post then completes the next thread's sem_timedwait before that thread's handler has run. From then on the semaphore is one ahead: the next thread's frames appear under a later header, two handlers write g_hangLog at once with interleaved lines, and the last waits can return early.
4. :226-228 fsync, then close(g_hangLog), then g_hangLog = -1. A handler that is still running, or arrives late, reads the plain int g_hangLog with no synchronisation. That is a C++ data race with the watchdog's store. In the window after close(), the handler can write(2) into whatever file has reused that fd number.
src/diag/posix/boot_state_watchdog_posix.cpp:194-209 has the same pattern.

Overstated parts:
- dladdr is not async-signal-safe under POSIX, which is true. But bionic's g_dl_mutex is a recursive mutex, so a thread interrupted while it holds the lock does not deadlock itself. A handler only blocks while another thread holds the lock. If that holder is permanently stuck, the process is already hung. If not, the handler continues once the lock is released. The claim that an attended run "never recovers from a transient stall" is not supported.
- The fd-reuse write needs a narrow timing window. It is plausible but not demonstrated.

Whether a late answer happens depends on the environment (a thread in D-state longer than 1 s). Given that precondition, the miscount follows deterministically from the code.
verdict.minimal_fix: Write the target tid into a std::atomic<pid_t> g_dumpTarget before tgkill. In the handler, compare it with gettid() and return without dumping or posting when they differ. On timeout, set g_dumpTarget = 0 so a late answer is ignored. Make g_hangLog a std::atomic<int> and read it once per handler. Only store -1 and close after the loop, and use one compare (or a done counter) so that no handler is between its load and its write when close() runs. Optionally keep the raw pcs in the handler and resolve them with dladdr in the watchdog thread. Apply the same change to src/diag/posix/boot_state_watchdog_posix.cpp.

confirmed.title: A render pipeline that fails to compile is never remembered: every draw with that state recompiles it synchronously on the render thread and prints an uncapped stderr line
confirmed.bug_class: error path not cached -> per-draw synchronous recompile plus hot-path log (resource)
confirmed.label: ext
confirmed.evidence: Pipeline() inserts into the fast cache only on success: `auto state = CachedPipeline(desc, bound.vs, bound.ps, true); if (state) { pipelines.Insert(...); }` (backend.mm:397-401). CachedPipeline's required path keeps a nil result: warm-up compiles never start for required keys, so `entry->started` is false and `if (entry->state) return entry->state;` falls through. Every call then runs `auto state = [gpu newRenderPipelineStateWithDescriptor:d error:&error]; ... if (error) { fprintf(stderr, "[Metal] pipeline: %s\n", ...); } ... entry->state = state;` (pipeline_cache.h:343-353), which stores nil again. Each draw with that state therefore costs a Find miss, a DescribePipeline + NSJSONSerialization of the full descriptor, AddPipelineRecord, a synchronous Metal compile and one stderr line. The line has no count cap, no _DEBUG guard and no Opt() gate, which AGENTS.md section 3 forbids on a hot path. The failing descriptor is also written to pipelines.txt and replayed asynchronously at every later launch. A descriptor fails when, for example, the vertex shader reads an attribute the layout never declared. That happens when VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate skips an element (`e.format >= 9 || e.stream >= 23`, backend.mm:2080) or reads only the first 31 elements. S-055 is a different site (the command-buffer completion handler).
confirmed.repro_idea: Make one VertexLayout element invalid (a mod resource with element format 9, or temporarily drop one attribute in PlatformCreate) for a mesh drawn every frame. Expect '[Metal] pipeline: Vertex attribute ... is not defined' once per draw in standalone_error.log and a frame-time spike in standalone_metal_frames.csv (pipeline_ms, new_pipelines growing every frame). Minimal fix: remember the failure, for example a `failed` flag on PipelineEntry checked before the compile, or a nil sentinel in the fast cache, and log once per key.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: resource
verdict.proof: Verified line by line in <worktree> (origin/main). backend.mm:361 Pipeline() returns early only on a fast-cache hit; backend.mm:397-401 calls CachedPipeline(desc, vs, ps, true) and runs pipelines.Insert only `if (state)`, so a nil result is never cached. In pipeline_cache.h CachedPipeline: 311-322 run on every call (LoadPipelineRecords, DescribePipeline, NSJSONSerialization with sorted keys, AddPipelineRecord, which writes the failing descriptor into pipelineRecords, so it is persisted to pipelines.txt and replayed by RegisterPipelineShader/StartPipeline at later launches). 326-335: for a required key with no warm-up running, `entry->state` is nil, so the function falls through; for a key whose replayed async compile failed (started=true, done=true, state=nil) it also falls through. 343-352: a synchronous `newRenderPipelineStateWithDescriptor:error:` runs, `fprintf(stderr, "[Metal] pipeline: %s\n", ...)` prints with no _DEBUG guard, no Opt() gate and no count cap, and `entry->state = state` stores nil again. PipelineEntry has no failed flag (only started/done/state), so nothing remembers the failure. Every draw that binds that state repeats the whole path: a synchronous Metal compile on the render thread plus one stderr line, which AGENTS.md section 3 forbids on a hot path. Trigger: any descriptor Metal rejects. One example is a vertex shader attribute missing from the layout, which happens when VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate (backend.mm:2078-2080) skips an element with format >= 9 or stream >= 23, or drops elements past 31 (mod or hostile resource data). The per-draw no-negative-cache defect holds for any such failure. Not in the ledger: S-054 covers address-reuse eviction and S-055 covers the command-buffer error handler log at backend.mm:784. Neither covers pipeline compile failure. Not fixed on origin/main. Metal-only code (no retail counterpart), so the label is ext. Reaching it needs a failing descriptor; stock game data has not been shown to produce one.
verdict.minimal_fix: Add a `failed` flag to PipelineEntry. In CachedPipeline, once the entry lock is held, return nil when `entry->failed` is set (or when `entry->done && !entry->state` after a warm-up). After the synchronous compile, set `entry->failed = (state == nil)` and print the stderr line only on that first failure. Skip AddPipelineRecord, or remove the record, for a failed key so it is not replayed at the next launch. If a missing draw is preferable to repeated work, Pipeline() can also insert a nil sentinel into the fast cache.

confirmed.title: RenderStateData::Bind converts the serialized depth bias to int with no range check (float-cast-overflow UB)
confirmed.bug_class: out-of-range float->int conversion
confirmed.label: retail
confirmed.evidence: CONFIRMED (UBSan on a verbatim transcription). Code: `bound.bias = float(int(_owner->_depth.bias * 16777215.0f));`. RenderState::Depth::bias is a float read straight from the resource/stream by Depth::Serialize (renderstate.cpp:159) with no bound; any |bias| >= ~128 (or NaN/inf) puts bias*2^24 outside int range, which is UB in C++. Retail VideoDX11 does the same multiply + CVTTSS2SI (0x180003827-0x18000384b; mirrored at src/render/dx11/renderstatedata.cpp:369 and src/render/vulkan/companions.cpp:900), which yields INT_MIN on x86 rather than UB. Repro scratchpad/metal_ub/repro.cpp (g++ -fsanitize=undefined,float-cast-overflow, WSL): 'repro.cpp:35:48: runtime error: 1.67772e+10 is outside the range of representable values of type int' for bias=1000. Not in the ledger (S-042 covers only the DX11 table indexes; F-136/F-160/F-163 are other sites). Minimal fix: clamp to [INT_MIN, INT_MAX] (and NaN -> INT_MIN) before the cast to reproduce CVTTSS2SI's result, with a NOT RETAIL: comment; the DX11 and Vulkan siblings carry the same pattern.
confirmed.repro_idea: A RenderState resource (or mod .rsc) whose Depth bias float is 1000.0 (or NaN); bind it on the Metal backend under UBSan, or run the transcription repro above.

verdict.label: retail
verdict.severity: UB (low impact: hostile/modded RenderState resource only)
verdict.proof:
The attempt to refute it failed. Checked on origin/main fa150cf7f in <worktree>.

1. The code is there as described. src/render/metal/backend.mm:2206 reads `bound.bias = float(int(_owner->_depth.bias * 16777215.0f));`. Line 2202 clamps `_cullMode`, but nothing clamps bias.

2. The value comes straight from the data with no bound. src/engine/video/renderstate.cpp:159, in RenderState::Depth::Serialize (0x1800f4a00), does `ser.Serialize(bias, nullptr);`, a raw float with no range check after it. A RenderState resource from a mod or a crafted .rsc therefore controls bias completely, including NaN and inf.

3. Standard: C++ [conv.fpint] says a float-to-int conversion is undefined when the truncated value cannot be represented. Any |bias| >= about 128.0 gives bias*16777215 outside the int range, and NaN or inf is always out of range. So the cast at 2206 is UB for such input. The finder's UBSan output for bias=1000 (1.67772e+10 outside the int range) is what the standard predicts.

4. The same pattern is at src/render/dx11/renderstatedata.cpp:369 (`static_cast<INT>(rs->_depth.bias * kDepthBiasScale)`, mirroring retail CVTTSS2SI at 0x180003827-0x18000384b) and at src/render/vulkan/companions.cpp:900. On x86, retail's CVTTSS2SI gives the integer-indefinite value 0x80000000. That is defined at the hardware level but UB in the C++ port. The label is "retail" because the pattern comes from VideoDX11; Metal copies it.

5. It is not in the ledger. A case-insensitive grep for "bias" over docs/history/review_20261103 (README.md, P0_MAP.md, findings_p3p4.json, findings_p8.json) finds no depth-bias entry. The float-cast entries that do exist (F-136 audio _maxLength, the PlayPlatform duration, the RasterizeFile font metrics) are other sites, and S-042 covers only the DX11 table indexes. It is not fixed on main.
verdict.minimal_fix: Add one small helper shared by the three sites: Metal backend.mm:2206, DX11 renderstatedata.cpp:369 and Vulkan companions.cpp:900. For a product p = bias * 16777215.0f it returns INT_MIN if p is NaN or p is not inside (-2147483648.0f, 2147483648.0f), and int(p) otherwise. This gives the same result as retail's CVTTSS2SI (integer-indefinite 0x80000000), so the behaviour on x86 does not change. Mark it with a `// NOT RETAIL: CVTTSS2SI yields INT_MIN for an out-of-range or NaN product; the C++ cast is UB there.` comment. Add a unit test with bias = 1000.0f, -1000.0f, NaN and inf.

confirmed.title: ApplyInitialWindowGeometry overflows int on a saved VideoWindowX/Y near INT_MAX (signed overflow UB) on a 1x display
confirmed.bug_class: signed integer overflow from unbounded settings input
confirmed.label: port
confirmed.evidence: CONFIRMED (UBSan on a verbatim transcription linked against the real display_geometry.cpp). Code (lines 140-151): `px = PixelsToPointsRound(savedX, d); py = PixelsToPointsRound(savedY, d); ... const Platform::Rect win{ px, py - top, px + cw, py + ch }; ... placed = RectTouchesAnyDisplay(win, &disp, 1) && py - top >= b.y;`. savedX/savedY are Configuration::windowX/windowY, read from settings.cfg by Configuration::Startup through strtol with no range check (device.cpp kSaveFields) and passed raw by the Metal CreateDevice (backend.mm:928) for any windowed start. On a density-1 display (non-Retina external monitor) PixelsToPointsRound returns the value unchanged, so VideoWindowY=2147483000 gives py=2147483008 and `py + ch` overflows. Unlike the AdjustDisplay path (which re-centres an off-display origin before FitToUsableScreen sees it), this opening-geometry path has no such filter. Repro scratchpad/metal_ub/repro.cpp: 'repro.cpp:17:61: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 2147483008 + 720 cannot be represented in type int'. NOT RETAIL code (Darwin twin only). Hardening: do the rect arithmetic in int64 or reject saved origins outside, say, +/-1e6 points before use.
confirmed.repro_idea: macOS, windowed, primary/target display at 1x scale: set Video WindowY=2147483000 (WindowWidth/Height > 0) in ~/Documents/Banished/Save/settings.cfg and start the Metal build compiled with -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow; or run the transcription repro.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: UB (low impact: needs a hand-edited settings.cfg; Darwin/Metal only, non-retail code)
verdict.proof:
Could not refute. The finding holds on origin/main fa150cf7f, and it is not in the review_20261103 ledger (no F-/S- row names window_darwin / ApplyInitialWindowGeometry / WindowX/Y). Line-by-line proof:
1) Input: device.cpp:400-401 kSaveFields maps settings.cfg "WindowX"/"WindowY" to Configuration::windowX/windowY. They are read through IO::Persistence::Get(int&) (strtol base 10, no range check), so any int value is reachable. backend.mm:928 passes cfg->windowX/windowY/windowWidth/windowHeight raw to Platform::Window::ApplyInitialWindowGeometry.
2) Guard: window_darwin.cpp:139 requires only savedPxW>0 && savedPxH>0 && !(x==-1&&y==-1). A saved WindowWidth/Height (e.g. 1280x720) meets it.
3) display_geometry.cpp:56: PixelsToPointsRound = (int32_t)lround((float)pixels / d). For d=1 (non-Retina display) and savedY=2147483000, float rounds to 2147483008 (ulp 128 above 2^30). lround gives 2147483008, which fits int32, so py=2147483008.
4) InitialWindowPoints (display_geometry.cpp:85-88) clamps ch to at least kMinWindowPointsH (360) and at most the usable height, so ch>=360.
5) window_darwin.cpp:149 `py + ch` = 2147483008 + 360..720 > INT_MAX: signed int overflow, which is UB. `px + cw` is the same with WindowX. Nothing between lines 140 and 149 filters an off-display origin. The existing transcription repro (scratchpad/metal_ub/repro.cpp, verbatim lines 139-151 linked to the real display_geometry.cpp) reports 'signed integer overflow: 2147483008 + 720'.
The function is Darwin-only and not retail, so this is a hardening fix and not a drift fix.
verdict.minimal_fix: In window_darwin.cpp ApplyInitialWindowGeometry, do the placement arithmetic in int64_t (e.g. `const int64_t px64 = px, py64 = py;` and compare against the display bounds in int64), or skip the saved-origin arm (placed=false, falls back to centring) when px/py are outside a sane range such as |v| > 1'000'000 points. Add a "NOT RETAIL:" comment, since the campaign ruling covers UB found in port code.

confirmed.title: Int4 vertex widening reads the source buffer at an unchecked layout offset (host out-of-bounds read)
confirmed.bug_class: out-of-bounds read from unvalidated resource offset/stride
confirmed.label: port
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (no run). Code: `size_t n = (source.length - begin) / stride; ... auto src = static_cast<const uint8_t*>(source.contents) + begin; for (v < n) for (k < 4) dst[v * 4 + k] = src[v * stride + a.offset + k];`. Only `begin < source.length` is checked. `a.offset` is VertexLayout::Element::offset, an int32 from the layout resource that PlatformCreate copies unchecked (`a.offset = e.offset;` line 2084; only format and stream are range-checked), and `stride` is the bind stride from the vertex buffer. The read stays inside the buffer only when a.offset + 4 <= stride; a larger offset reads up to offset+4-stride bytes past the end, and a negative offset converts to a huge NSUInteger and reads before the buffer. Metal never validates this offset: Pipeline() (lines 369-376) rewrites every widened attribute to buffer 7, offset 0, stride 16, so the original offset is not in any pipeline descriptor. Retail D3D11 never reads vertex data on the CPU (CreateInputLayout validates AlignedByteOffset; the IA is bounds-checked), so this is a Metal-only divergence. Not in the ledger (S-021 is the nil NewBuffer on the same path). Fix: skip the expansion (or the draw) when a.offset + 4 > stride, as the begin >= length case already does.
confirmed.repro_idea: A mod VertexLayout for a skinned (int4 BLENDINDICES) shader with the UChar4 element at offset 0x7ffffff0 (or -64), or bound with a vertex stride of 4 and offset 8; draw it on the Metal backend under ASan / guard malloc.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: memory (host OOB read from hostile/malformed mod VertexLayout data; Metal backend only)
verdict.proof:
I could not refute it. The defect holds up when read line by line in <worktree>/src/render/metal/backend.mm, but it is a Metal-only path and nobody has run it. The campaign standard for a memory finding asks for a sanitizer or test report, and no such run exists.

Facts, read line by line:
(1) Element offset is not checked. vertexlayout.cpp:132 serialises `e->offset` as a raw int from the resource. VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate (backend.mm ~2080-2088) checks only format and stream, then does `a.offset = e.offset;`. A negative int becomes a huge NSUInteger.
(2) The widening loop (backend.mm ~530-583) reads `a = bound.layout.attributes[...]`. That is the stored descriptor, not the pipeline copy that Pipeline() (lines 369-376) rewrites to buffer 7 / offset 0. So the original offset reaches the CPU loop. `stride = bound.strides[slot]` is the bind stride (line 1983). The only guards are `!source || !stride` and `begin >= source.length`.
(3) Bound arithmetic. Let n = floor((L-b)/stride), so n*stride <= L-b. The last read is at byte b + (n-1)*stride + offset + 3.
- For offset >= 2*stride this is >= b + (n+1)*stride + 3 > L, so it is out of bounds for every n >= 1.
- For stride <= offset < 2*stride it is out of bounds whenever the remainder (L-b) - n*stride <= offset + 3 - stride.
- A negative offset, after conversion to NSUInteger, wraps the pointer to before or far outside the buffer.
- Example: stride 4, UChar4 at offset 8, so a.offset + 4 = 12 > stride. Nothing in the path rejects it, and the Metal validation layer never sees this offset because the pipeline uses offset 0.

Retail has no CPU read of vertex data: in D3D11 the input assembler is bounds-checked. So this is a divergence in the port, not retail behaviour.

Ledger: the ledger has S-021 (findings_p8.json ~2774, README.md:294) for the nil-NewBuffer write on the same expansion path. Nothing there covers the source over-read at a.offset or stride. It is not a duplicate, and origin/main does not fix it.

Not fully confirmed because:
- There is no ASan or guard-malloc run on macOS. The backend does not build on Windows or Linux.
- Reaching it needs a crafted mod layout plus a mesh, and nobody has exercised that.
verdict.minimal_fix: In the widening loop, after computing stride, add `if (a.offset > stride || a.offset + 4 > stride) continue;` (do the check in size_t / NSUInteger so a negative offset that became a huge value also skips), with a "NOT RETAIL:" comment saying D3D11 bounds-checks the input assembler. Optionally also reject e.offset < 0 in VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate as plain hardening.

proof_run.proof:
I reproduced the fault with a guard-page harness, which works the way macOS guard malloc does. It was not a real Metal run: the Metal backend does not build on Windows, and WSL ASan was blocked by the worktree isolation guard.

How the harness works:
- It #includes the widening code verbatim, cut out with sed from src/render/metal/backend.mm at fa150cf7f (origin/main = this worktree HEAD). Line 546 is `size_t n = (source.length - begin) / stride;` and lines 579-584 are the `src[v * stride + a.offset + k]` loop.
- Plain structs stand in for the Metal objects. They keep the same member names and types: MTLBuffer length / contents, and the attribute offset as a 64-bit NSUInteger, filled from an int32 as `a.offset = e.offset` does in PlatformCreate.
- The 64-byte source buffer ends exactly at a PAGE_NOACCESS page, and there is another guard page before it.
- It applies the same guards backend.mm has (stride != 0, begin < length).

Results, from run.log (stride / offset):
- 4 / 0: no fault (control).
- 16 / 12: no fault (control).
- 4 / 8: n=16, the last byte read is at index 71 of 64. ACCESS VIOLATION at the first byte after the buffer.
- 16 / 16: the last byte read is at index 67. ACCESS VIOLATION past the end.
- 16 / -5000: the negative int32 becomes a huge NSUInteger, and the pointer wraps to before the buffer. ACCESS VIOLATION in the leading guard page.

So the read leaves the buffer whenever a.offset + 4 > stride (as the remainder allows), or when the offset is negative. Nothing on the path rejects this:
- PlatformCreate range-checks only format and stream.
- Pipeline() rewrites the widened attribute to buffer 7 / offset 0, so Metal validation never sees the original offset.

Caveat: the harness exercises the loop's own code, not the full path from a mod VertexLayout to a Metal draw. I reasoned through that path statically, as the verifier did.

Files are in scratchpad/phase2/proofs/metal-int4-widen-oob/: harness.cpp, n_line.inc, loop.inc, run.log, harness.exe.
proof_run.minimal_fix: In the Int4 widening loop in src/render/metal/backend.mm, right after the `begin >= source.length` guard, add `if (a.offset > stride || a.offset + 4 > stride) { continue; }` and keep the comparison in NSUInteger / size_t, so an offset that started as a negative int32 and became huge also skips. Add a "NOT RETAIL:" comment saying that D3D11's input assembler bounds-checks vertex fetches and retail never reads vertex data on the CPU. As optional plain hardening, VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate could also skip elements with e.offset < 0.

confirmed.title: Indexed-draw bounds check is defeated by a negative start index or index offset (unsigned wrap)
confirmed.bug_class: bounds check bypassed by signed->unsigned wraparound
confirmed.label: port
confirmed.evidence: SUSPECTED (no run). Code: `NSUInteger offset = NSUInteger(ctx->_indexOffset) + NSUInteger(start) * 2; if (indexBuffer && offset + NSUInteger(count) * 2 <= indexBuffer.length) [enc drawIndexedPrimitives:... indexBufferOffset:offset ...]`. start (DrawIndexed's startIndex, from mesh subset data) and _indexOffset are int; a negative value wraps to near 2^64, and `offset + count*2` wraps back below indexBuffer.length, so the check passes and Metal is handed indexBufferOffset ~2^64-2. The unsigned arithmetic itself is defined, but the guard this code adds is ineffective exactly for the out-of-range inputs it is meant to stop: the GPU reads at a wild offset (command-buffer fault, then the per-frame error spam of S-055). Retail D3D11 takes StartIndexLocation as UINT with robust buffer access (out-of-range index fetches return 0). Fix: reject start < 0 or _indexOffset < 0 before the conversion, or compare in a form that cannot wrap (offset <= length && count*2 <= length - offset).
confirmed.repro_idea: A mesh resource with a subset start index of -1 (count 3) drawn on the Metal backend: the check passes and the command buffer reports a GPU fault.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: minor
verdict.proof: Static logic proof, checked line by line on origin/main in <worktree>. src/render/metal/backend.mm:450 declares `static void Draw(..., int count, ..., bool indexed, int start, int baseVertex)`. Lines 601-602 compute `NSUInteger offset = NSUInteger(ctx->_indexOffset) + NSUInteger(start) * 2; if (indexBuffer && offset + NSUInteger(count) * 2 <= indexBuffer.length)`. When start = -1 and count = 3, offset = _indexOffset + 2^64 - 2. Adding 6 wraps the sum to _indexOffset + 4, so the guard passes, and drawIndexedPrimitives receives indexBufferOffset = 2^64 - 2 + _indexOffset. A negative count wraps the same way: count*2 = 2^64 - 2 makes the sum offset - 2, and indexCount then reaches Metal as a huge NSUInteger. The arithmetic is defined behaviour; the defect is that the guard fails for exactly the inputs it should reject. The values are reachable. ContextData::DrawIndexed (backend.mm:1340-1342) passes startIndex and indexCount straight to Draw. Its callers IssueDraw (src/engine/graphics/meshinstance_draw.cpp:215, rec._f08 / rec._f0c) and geometry_draw.cpp:450 take them from mesh TriangleList records. Those records are read as raw ints by `SerializeInt(e->_f08)` / `SerializeInt(e->_f0c)` (closure_batch2b.cpp:292-293) with no range check, so a crafted or modded mesh resource controls them. _indexOffset comes from BindIndexBuffer's int `first`, which has the same origin. Nothing on origin/main fixes this; the last change to backend.mm is 044dcd83f, which did not touch these lines. It is not in the ledger: no F-/S- row covers backend.mm:601. S-055 (backend.mm:784) is the per-frame stderr spam that a resulting GPU fault would set off, a downstream symptom and not the same defect. The GPU-fault consequence is not shown here (no macOS/Metal machine), but the bypass itself needs no run. Class: hardening of hostile input, not UB, so no NOT RETAIL comment is needed.
verdict.minimal_fix: In Draw's indexed branch, reject negative values before converting them, and compare in a form that cannot wrap: `if (indexBuffer && ctx->_indexOffset >= 0 && start >= 0 && count >= 0) { NSUInteger offset = NSUInteger(ctx->_indexOffset) + NSUInteger(start) * 2; NSUInteger bytes = NSUInteger(count) * 2; if (offset <= indexBuffer.length && bytes <= indexBuffer.length - offset) { [enc drawIndexedPrimitives:...]; } }` (one statement per line, format only the touched lines).

confirmed.title: Metal Int4 vertex expansion reads the source vertex buffer at a layout offset that is never checked against the stride or the buffer length (CPU heap out-of-bounds read)
confirmed.bug_class: unchecked file input -> out-of-bounds read
confirmed.label: port
confirmed.evidence: VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate (backend.mm:2080-2084) checks only format and stream, then stores the serialized int32 offset unchanged: `if (e.format < 0 || e.format >= 9 || e.stream < 0 || e.stream >= 23) continue; ... a.offset = e.offset;`. A negative offset becomes a huge NSUInteger. Draw (backend.mm:536-584) widens every UChar4 attribute that feeds a DXBC int4 input (the skinned-mesh bone-index path, run every frame), using the stride from VertexBufferData::Bind: `size_t n = (source.length - begin) / stride; ... auto src = static_cast<const uint8_t*>(source.contents) + begin; for (v < n) for (k < 4) dst[v * 4 + k] = src[v * stride + a.offset + k];`. Only `begin` is checked against source.length. When a.offset + 4 > stride, the last vertex reads past the MTLBuffer contents; a negative offset wraps and reads before them. Pipeline() (backend.mm:371-375) rewrites this attribute to offset 0 / buffer 7 / stride 16, so the pipeline still compiles and the hostile offset reaches the CPU loop. DX11 never runs this loop on the CPU (the input assembler bounds-checks fetches, and CreateInputLayout rejects a bad AlignedByteOffset), so this is a Metal-only divergence. Suggested fix: skip the expansion (or leave the attribute zeroed) when a.offset > stride - 4 or the offset was negative.
confirmed.repro_idea: Unit-level: build a VertexLayout whose element has format 7 (UChar4) and offset -4096 (or offset = stride), bind a vertex buffer of stride 8 and a VS with an int4 input, and Draw under ASan on macOS; the expected report is a heap-buffer-overflow read in VideoMetal::Draw. In game: a mod MeshLayout .rsc with a skinned layout whose BLENDINDICES offset is 0x7ffffff0.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: memory (OOB read on the render thread, crash with a hostile mod MeshLayout; Metal only)
verdict.proof:
Checked on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>/src/render/metal/backend.mm). This is not a duplicate. The ledger's only Metal Int4-expansion entry is S-021 (backend.mm:575, the NewBuffer result is not checked for nil). That is a different defect, and nothing in README.md, P0_MAP.md or findings_p3p4.json/findings_p8.json covers the offset.

How a file value reaches the read:
(1) VertexLayout::Serialize (src/engine/video/vertexlayout.cpp:239-244) reads _elements straight from the resource and does not validate the offset.
(2) VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate (backend.mm, about line 2080) skips an element only for format or stream: `if (e.format < 0 || e.format >= 9 || e.stream < 0 || e.stream >= 23) continue;`. It then stores `a.offset = e.offset;` unchanged into an NSUInteger, so a negative value wraps to a huge one.
(3) Pipeline() (about line 369) rewrites any UChar4 attribute that feeds an Int4 VS input to `offset = 0; bufferIndex = 7; stride 16`. The pipeline therefore never sees the bad offset, and nothing upstream rejects it.
(4) Draw (lines 531-584) reads `a = bound.layout.attributes[...]`, the original descriptor that still holds the file offset. The stride comes from VertexBufferData::Bind (`bound.strides[slot] = strideBytes`, line 1983) and is independent of the layout. The only bounds check is `begin >= source.length`. It then computes `n = (source.length - begin) / stride` and runs `dst[v*4+k] = src[v*stride + a.offset + k]` with src = contents + begin.

Concrete case: element format 7 (UChar4) with offset 0x7ffffff0, any stride, and a buffer shorter than 2 GB. At v=0 the loop reads contents + begin + 0x7ffffff0, past the end of the MTLBuffer. Two smaller cases fail the same way:
- offset == stride: the last vertex reads (n-1)*stride + stride + 3 >= length - begin.
- negative offset: the index wraps and the read lands before contents.

This runs on every cache miss of a skinned draw (dynamic streams every draw). The D3D11 input assembler does not fetch out of bounds, so this is a Metal-only port divergence.

Caveat on the suggested repro: MTLBuffer storage is not malloc heap. ASan would likely not report a small overrun, but the 0x7ffffff0 case faults outright.
verdict.minimal_fix:
In Draw's Int4 expansion, before computing n:
`if (a.offset > stride || stride - a.offset < 4) continue;`
This covers a wrapped negative offset too, because it becomes huge and fails the first test. Alternatively, at PlatformCreate, skip an element with a negative offset. Plain hardening of hostile input, Metal backend only.

confirmed.title: ApplyInitialWindowGeometry adds the window size and title-bar height to the settings.cfg WindowX/WindowY values without overflow checks (signed overflow UB at density 1)
confirmed.bug_class: signed overflow from settings.cfg (UB)
confirmed.label: port
confirmed.evidence: Configuration::Startup reads WindowX/WindowY/WindowWidth/WindowHeight from settings.cfg with strtol into int32 and no range check (engine/video/device.cpp:400). The Metal CreateDevice passes them unchanged (backend.mm:928). window_darwin.cpp:140-149: `px = PixelsToPointsRound(savedX, d); py = PixelsToPointsRound(savedY, d); ... const Platform::Rect win{ px, py - top, px + cw, py + ch }; ... placed = RectTouchesAnyDisplay(win, &disp, 1) && py - top >= b.y;`. At PixelDensity 1.0 (a non-Retina display), WindowX=2147483000 with any saved size makes px + cw (cw >= 640 from InitialWindowPoints) overflow int32. WindowY=-2147483648 (or 2147483647, which float rounding turns into INT_MIN) makes py - top (top >= 28) overflow. FitToUsableScreen (lines 92-98: `*clientY - frame.top`, `*clientY + *clientH + frame.bottom`, `*clientX + *clientW + frame.right`) has the same arithmetic on the outer rect that AdjustDisplay builds from the same cfg->windowX/Y. This body exists only on Darwin, not in retail. Suggested fix: compute in int64, or reject saved positions outside +/-2^30, before the rect math.
confirmed.repro_idea: Pure test with -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow: call the geometry arithmetic (extract it, or drive ApplyInitialWindowGeometry with a stub SDL window of density 1) with savedX=2147483000, savedY=0, savedPxW=800, savedPxH=600; UBSan should report 'signed integer overflow' at window_darwin.cpp:149. In game: settings.cfg with VideoWindowX=2147483000, VideoWindowWidth=800, VideoWindowHeight=600, VideoFullscreen=0, launched on a 1x display.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: UB (low impact: macOS-only, needs a hand-edited settings.cfg and a 1x display)
verdict.proof:
The finding could not be refuted. The code supports it line by line, but no UBSan run has been done, and the campaign standard needs a sanitizer or test before UB counts as CONFIRMED.

Path (read from <worktree>):
1. backend.mm:926-929: for a windowed config, `cfg->windowX/windowY/windowWidth/windowHeight` reach `ApplyInitialWindowGeometry` unchanged. These are the WindowX/Y/Width/Height keys from settings.cfg (device.cpp:396-401 field table, strtol load), with no range check.
2. window_darwin.cpp:139: the guard only needs savedPxW>0, savedPxH>0 and not (-1,-1). savedX=2147483000, savedY=0, W=800, H=600 passes it.
3. display_geometry.cpp:56-57: `PixelsToPointsRound` is `(int32_t)lround((float)pixels / d)`. At d=1.0, (float)2147483000 rounds to 2147483008 (float spacing near 2^31 is 128). That is below INT32_MAX, so px = 2147483008 = 2^31 - 640.
4. display_geometry.cpp:85-88: `InitialWindowPoints` clamps cw to at least kMinWindowPointsW (640), then to maxW = usable.w - left - right, which is at least 640 on any real Mac display. So cw >= 640.
5. window_darwin.cpp:149: `px + cw` >= 2^31, which is signed int overflow (UB). `py - top` overflows the same way for savedY = INT_MIN (top >= 28, line 123). savedY = 2147483647 also gets there: the float rounds to 2^31, lround gives 2147483648 as a 64-bit long, and the narrowing to int32 yields INT_MIN.
6. At density 2 (Retina) the values halve and nothing overflows. So it is reachable only when SDL reports PixelDensity 1.0, for example on an external non-Retina display.

FitToUsableScreen (lines 92-98) has the same unguarded int sums (`*clientY - frame.top`, `*clientX + *clientW + frame.right`), but whether hostile values reach it was not traced.

Ledger: docs/history/review_20261103 has no entry for ApplyInitialWindowGeometry, window_darwin geometry, WindowX overflow or InitialWindowPoints. That covers README F-001..F-217 and S-001, P0_MAP, findings_p3p4.json and findings_p8.json. P0_MAP.md:568 only mentions window_darwin.cpp:56 (HIGH_PIXEL_DENSITY). It is not fixed on origin/main.

Retail has no counterpart: this is a NOT-RETAIL Darwin body, so the label is port and there is no Ghidra question. To close it: a pure test built with -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow that runs PixelsToPointsRound(2147483000, 1.0f) and InitialWindowPoints(800, 600, 0, 0, 1.0f, 1920, 1050), then evaluates px + cw as on line 149. UBSan should report the overflow.
verdict.minimal_fix: In window_darwin.cpp, before the rect math at lines 140-151 (and in FitToUsableScreen), do the sums in int64_t. Alternatively, treat a saved origin outside +/-(1<<30) as unplaced, like (-1,-1), so the window centres on the usable area. Comment it as "NOT RETAIL: hostile settings.cfg origin" (plain hardening of a port-only body).

proof_run.proof:
The overflow is confirmed by a UBSan trap-mode run. MinGW has no libubsan runtime, so the build used -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow -fsanitize-undefined-trap-on-error with the WinLibs GCC 16.2.0 compiler. Running under WSL was blocked by the worktree isolation guard.

repro.cpp links the real src/platform/common/display_geometry.cpp from worktree fa150cf7f (the origin/main tip). It copies these lines verbatim:
- window_darwin.cpp:139-151 (ApplyInitialWindowGeometry placement).
- window_darwin.cpp:88-98 (FitToUsableScreen).

SDL is replaced by fixed values: PixelDensity 1.0, one usable display at (0,25) 1920x1050, title bar top=28.

Results (run.log):
- sane (savedX=100, savedY=100, 800x600): placed=1, exit 0.
- x (savedX=2147483000, savedY=0, 800x600): px=2147483008, cw=800. `px + cw` overflows and the process traps with 0xC000001D (STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION, the sanitizer ud2) at window_darwin.cpp:149.
- ymin (savedY=INT_MIN): `py - top` overflows and traps.
- ymax (savedY=2147483647): PixelsToPointsRound turns it into py=INT_MIN, then `py - top` overflows and traps.
- fitx (FitToUsableScreen with cx=2147483000, cw=800): `*clientX + *clientW + frame.right` overflows and traps.
- fity (FitToUsableScreen with cy=INT_MIN): `*clientY - frame.top` overflows and traps.

Reachability: WindowX/WindowY/WindowWidth/WindowHeight come from settings.cfg, read with strtol and no range check (device.cpp:396-401). backend.mm:928 passes them unchanged to ApplyInitialWindowGeometry for a windowed config. FitToUsableScreen is reached through display_sdl.cpp:194 SetWindowPos (after PixelsToPointsRound + OuterToClient); only its arithmetic was exercised, not that call route.

This is a Darwin-only port body with no retail counterpart (label port, no Ghidra question). At density 2 the values halve and nothing overflows, so it is reachable only when the display reports density 1.0.
proof_run.minimal_fix: In src/platform/darwin/window_darwin.cpp ApplyInitialWindowGeometry, treat a saved origin outside +/-(1<<30) as unplaced, the same way as (-1,-1), so the window centres on the usable area: add `&& savedX > -(1 << 30) && savedX < (1 << 30) && savedY > -(1 << 30) && savedY < (1 << 30)` to the line-139 condition, with a "NOT RETAIL: hostile settings.cfg origin" comment. In FitToUsableScreen, do the edge sums in int64_t: `(int64_t)*clientY - frame.top`, `(int64_t)*clientY + *clientH + frame.bottom`, `(int64_t)*clientX - frame.left`, `(int64_t)*clientX + *clientW + frame.right`. This is plain hardening of a port-only body.
proof_run.repro_path: scratchpad\phase2\proofs\darwin-window-origin-overflow\repro.cpp (with run.log and repro.exe in the same directory)

confirmed.title: PathfinderThread::Run reads queueCount outside the pathfinder lock while enqueuers write it under the lock (data race, UB; retail-shaped)
confirmed.label: retail
confirmed.severity: low (UB data race; benign on x86-64 in practice: a stale value only under-counts since only the worker decrements)
confirmed.proof_kind: clang diagnostic + precise interleaving + Ghidra quote
confirmed.proof: clang-19 -Wthread-safety: `pathfinder_seed.cpp:63:17: error: reading variable 'queueCount' requires holding mutex 'lock'` and `:82:17` (same). Racing pair: the worker in PathfinderThread::Run executes `count = queueCount` (before the loop and after each ApplyCommand) with no lock, while the main thread's enqueuers write `queueCount = queueCount + 1` under `lock` (keystone_a_zone.cpp:61 SetCellTerrain, action_pf_astar.cpp:786 RequestPath, path_query_first.cpp:43). The enqueuers append while the worker is running: that is how the queue works. So the write and the read of the same int have no happens-before, which is a data race under [intro.races]. Retail 0x1400a6360 does the same: `0x1400a6366 CMP dword ptr [RCX+0x70],0` and `0x1400a6400 CMP dword ptr [RBX+0x70],ESI` are both outside the critical section (EnterCriticalSection at 0x1400a6388, LeaveCriticalSection at 0x1400a63ed). No TSan repro: the proof is the interleaving argument.
confirmed.minimal_fix: Every access to queueCount goes through LoadQueueCount / StoreQueueCount (src/game/Game/pathfinder_queue_count.h): each read is an acquire load and each write a release store, with a NOT RETAIL (UB fix) comment quoting the retail addresses; the field stays a plain int32_t. On x86-64 they are the plain MOV / CMP retail runs. Fixed in PR #161.

confirmed.title: S-001 refuted: VS cb slot 3 (tc_ TransformConstants) bound at the 64-byte rung against a 3328-byte declaration is retail behaviour
confirmed.label: retail
confirmed.proof: VideoDX11-x64.dll 0x180001460 (Bind): EAX = [rsp+0x70] / [R11+0x20] - 1 when [R11+0x19] (banked); if [RCX+0x10] != EAX then store it and CALL [R10+0x38] (VSSetConstantBuffers) with startSlot [R11+0x14], else skip; then CALL [R10+0x180] (UpdateSubresource). 0x180001300 (Create): banked loop ByteWidth = [R8+0x20]*(i+1) (IMUL ECX,ESI). 0x180001c40 (BindTransforms): size = [ctx+0x20] SHL 6, src ctx+0x10d8, buffer ctx+0x2050. The port's buffers.cpp:851-876, the Create ladder and contextdata.cpp:852 match instruction for instruction. tc_ is AddConstant(transform[52], float4x4, 208 regs) = 3328 B with bankStride 0x40 (constant_buffer.cpp:737-745). Runs log rungs of 64/192/512/640/1216 B under DrawIndexed/DrawIndexedInstanced (id 351 x8.9M in a 4-min run). Vulkan: companions.cpp:651 copies only the rung bytes into the ring while the descriptor range is always kConstantBufferRange=16384 (pipelines.h:96, draw.cpp:923). Reads past the rung are defined but return stale ring bytes, not D3D11's zeros. There are 0 validation errors.
confirmed.minimal_fix: None (retail). Optional note in docs/retail_bugs.md or known_port_issues.md that the Vulkan ring does not zero-pad past the rung.

confirmed.title: Fullscreen minimise+restore leaves a 4960x2852 client on a 2560x1440 display (SDL seam takes a negative frame measured mid-restore)
confirmed.label: port
confirmed.proof: DX11 debug, faithful, VideoFullscreen=true; SW_MINIMIZE on the foreground game window, then restore. The window client was 4960x2852 after restore (reproduced 3 times). Trace before the fix: '[ResizeTrace #1] entry win=(-32000,-32000 160x28) client=2560x1440 dev=2560x1440' then 'post-AdjustDisplay win=(0,0 4960x2852) client=4960x2852 dev=2560x1440'; WndMsg 'WM_SIZE type=0 4960x2852'. SDL_GetWindowBordersSize measured each side pair as -(2560-160) / -(1440-28) while Windows still reported the iconic rect, and CurrentFrame accepted any borderless measurement. OuterToClient(2560x1440 outer) then gave 4960x2852. Retail AdjustDisplay (0x1800f7e20) passes the outer rect straight to Win32 SetWindowPos. After the fix: 'post-AdjustDisplay win=(0,0 2560x1440) client=2560x1440' and the Alt+Tab round trip is unchanged. New unit test display_geometry_frame_measured_mid_restore_is_refused passes (2000 tests, 0 failures).
confirmed.minimal_fix: PR #163: UsableFrameMeasurement() in display_geometry refuses a frame with a negative side; CurrentFrame keeps the last good one.

confirmed.title: BANISHED_D3D_DEBUG: D3dDebug::Attach on the re-created device leaks the old ID3D11InfoQueue (and with it the old device) and registers atexit twice
confirmed.label: harness
confirmed.proof: dx11_devlost run (BANISHED_D3D_DEBUG=1, BANISHED_FORCE_DEVICE_LOST=8000): '[D3D11] BANISHED_D3D_DEBUG: debug layer on, info queue attached' appears twice, and the exit prints '[D3D11] debug layer totals: corruption=0 error=0 warning=5056076' twice.
