suspected.title: AUTOSTART_GAMES rearm compares the new main menu with the freed old one by address and can wait for ever
suspected.label: harness
suspected.evidence: `void* s_lastMenu` keeps the address of the MainMenuDialog that New Game was clicked on. On a rearm, WaitMenuSettle refuses `if (mainMenu == s_lastMenu) { s_phaseFrame = 0; return; }`. After quit-to-menu the old dialog is freed and the new MainMenuDialog is allocated with the same size through the same MemAlloc. The engine's boundary-tag allocator can return the same block, and in that case the fresh menu is never accepted. The run then sits at the main menu until the external timeout, with no error line.
suspected.repro_idea: BANISHED_AUTOSTART_GAMES=3 with BANISHED_PAUSEMENU_BUTTON=5 over many runs, or force reuse by freeing and reallocating the same size before the menu rebuild. The log stops after 'rearmed' and the boot state stays RUNNING on the menu. Fix: compare a generation (e.g. a counter bumped in the MainMenuDialog ctor) or menuDLT's dialog-change event instead of the pointer.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: low (harness-only; BANISHED_AUTOSTART_GAMES > 1 runs only)
verdict.proof: The code matches the description. In <worktree>/src/diag/autostart.cpp, line 260 stores `s_lastMenu = mainMenu` when the New Game click fires. On a rearm (lines 279-285), s_lastMenu is not cleared; only the AUTOTUTORIAL path at line 518 clears it. WaitMenuSettle (lines 252-255) then refuses any menu whose address equals s_lastMenu and resets s_phaseFrame each frame, with no timeout and no log line. Between the Start click and the quit-to-menu, the old dialog instance is released: src/engine/engine/loops.cpp lines 351/356 null `_dialogInstance` at shutdown, and a fresh dialog is assigned at lines 478/551. Nothing prevents the allocator from returning the same block for the new MainMenuDialog. If that happens, the predicate is true for ever and the harness stalls at the menu until the external timeout. So the identity-by-address defect can be checked line by line. What is not proven is that the reuse actually happens: a whole world load, game run and teardown sit between the free and the new allocation, and same-size reuse depends on the allocator's state. That needs a run (many AUTOSTART_GAMES=3 cycles that log the mainMenu addresses) or a unit test that forces reuse. No matching entry turned up in docs/history/review_20261103/ or docs/known_port_issues.md (grep for s_lastMenu / AUTOSTART_GAMES / rearm).
verdict.minimal_fix: Do not use the address as identity. For example, on rearm set a flag that requires menuDLT->_dialogInstance to be observed null (or the menu loop to be torn down or re-entered) before a non-null menu is accepted, then clear s_lastMenu. Alternatively, compare a generation counter bumped when the menu loop assigns _dialogInstance.

proof_run.proof:
The code does what the finding says. src/diag/autostart.cpp:252 refuses any menu whose address equals s_lastMenu. It does so with no timeout and no log line, and the rearm at lines 279-285 never clears s_lastMenu. So if the allocator returned the old MainMenuDialog's block for the new menu, the run would stall at the menu with nothing in the log.

That reuse was not observed in the real path. A debug build of fa150cf7f was made in the isolated worktree with one temporary probe in WaitMenuSettle, which logs the refusal at 1, 600 and 3000 frames (probe_instrument.diff, since reverted; the worktree is clean). It ran on the functional game dir with BANISHED_AUTOSTART=1, BANISHED_AUTOSTART_GAMES=3 and then 8, BANISHED_PAUSEMENU=600, BANISHED_PAUSEMENU_QUIT=60, BANISHED_PAUSEMENU_BUTTON=5 and /profile:faithful.
- Both runs completed every game with no stall.
- Run 1 menus: 0x...97500, 0x...7d8300, 0x...6866408.
- Run 2 menus: 0x...1a7500, a09f9e08, a0794888, a0050c40, a09eb080, a09a65f0, a0237510, a0ab73f8.
- That is 11 quit-to-menu rebuilds in total, and every new MainMenuDialog got a different address from the one before.
- The refusal fired only for 1 frame, on the old menu just after the Start click (the case it was written for). It never reached 600 frames.

A whole world load and teardown sit between the free and the new allocation, so getting the same block back did not happen in practice. A unit test that forces the reuse would only restate the predicate, so none was written. The defect is real but not reproduced, and harness-only (BANISHED_AUTOSTART_GAMES > 1). Status is SUSPECTED, not refuted.
proof_run.minimal_fix: Stop using the menu's address to tell the old menu from the new one. On rearm, set a flag (for example s_awaitMenuGone) that WaitMenuSettle clears only after it has seen menuDLT->_dialogInstance == nullptr or a different menuDLT. Accept a non-null menu only once that flag is clear, then reset s_lastMenu. Optionally log once if the refusal lasts more than N frames, so a stall leaves a line in the log.
proof_run.repro_path: scratchpad/phase2/proofs/autostart-aba/ (run.sh, probe_instrument.diff, run1_*/run2_* error logs and autostart lines)

suspected.title: A package copy started from the Game files screen while the game is not running keeps going after the player starts the game from the icon; installStaged then deletes and renames WinData packages underneath the booting or running game
suspected.bug_class: resource lifetime: game data replaced under a live consumer (missing lock between GameFilesJob and the game start)
suspected.label: port
suspected.evidence: SUSPECTED (static only). The Game files screen only blocks the copy when the game is already running: `final boolean dataLocked = mMode == Mode.MANAGE && gameRunning(); mFolderButton.setEnabled(!busy && !dataLocked);` (GameFilesScreen.java:379-381). The reverse case has no check. GameFilesActivity can run in a fresh process (the launcher long-press shortcut) and start a COPY_FOLDER/COPY_ARCHIVE job, which runs on its own thread and outlives the activity (the static sCurrent). Its Back button is disabled, but Home is not. OpenBAActivity.onCreate then only checks `if (!harness && !GameFiles.hasGameData(this))` (OpenBAActivity.java:91). It never checks `GameFilesJob.isRunning()`, so with an earlier data0.pkg present SDL starts the game's main at once. The job's installStaged then does `if (target.exists() && !target.delete()) ... if (!f.renameTo(target)) ...` for each package (GameFilesJob.java:248-256). The engine's LoadPackages (FindFiles over WinData, then PlatformOpenFile per .pkg, src/engine/io/filesystem_openfile.cpp:243-290) can therefore see data0.pkg missing between the delete and the rename, or a mix of old and new packages. The native check (game_data_check.h: data0.pkg present) then stops the boot with NO_GAME_DATA, or the boot mounts mismatched packages. A remount later (a mod toggle reopens the packages) picks up the half-replaced set. The file header promises that 'a cancel, a failure or a wrong folder leaves WinData as it was'; the staging covers that, but nothing guards the install step against a concurrent game start.
suspected.repro_idea: On a device or the emulator with packages already installed: long-press the icon, open Game files, and choose the WinData folder again (about 300 MB, so the copy takes several seconds). Press Home and tap the OpenBA icon while the bar is still running. Watch logcat for the game's package mount racing '[GameFiles] ... done'. Add a sleep between the delete and the rename in installStaged to widen the window, and show the boot fail with NO_GAME_DATA, or the game mounting a package that is renamed afterwards. Fix idea: OpenBAActivity shows the screen (or waits) while GameFilesJob.isRunning() and the job is a COPY_*.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: low (logic race; needs a deliberate Home + icon tap during a package copy, and the harmful window is only the rename loop)
verdict.proof: Not in the ledger (no GameFilesJob/installStaged entry in README F-rows, P0_MAP or findings_p3p4/p8 S-rows; P0_MAP mentions GameFilesJob only for zip-slip/save import), and not fixed on origin/main. The missing interlock checks out line by line: GameFilesScreen.java:379 locks the folder/archive buttons only for `mMode == Mode.MANAGE && gameRunning()`. GameFilesActivity (manifest: own taskAffinity "org.openba.game.files", same process) runs a COPY_* job on GameFilesJob's own thread, held in the static sCurrent. OpenBAActivity.onCreate (lines 81-96) checks only `!harness && !GameFiles.hasGameData(this)` and never GameFilesJob.isRunning(), so with an earlier data0.pkg present SDL's layout stays and the game's main starts. installStaged (GameFilesJob.java:239-257) then does delete+renameTo for each staged file into WinData while that happens. A reader can confirm that no guard exists. The harm is not proven, though. (1) Most of the copy is staging into a folder beside WinData, which the game never reads. Only the short rename loop touches WinData, so the race needs the boot's data0.pkg check or LoadPackages' FindFiles/open to land in a window of a few milliseconds. (2) On Android, unlinking a package the game already holds open leaves its inode readable, so a mounted package is not corrupted. The remaining risks are a NO_GAME_DATA exit, if the check lands between the delete and the rename of data0.pkg, or a mixed old/new set mounted mid-loop. Both depend on timing and are not shown. A remount after the loop sees a complete new set, which is consistent. Confirming it needs a run on a device or emulator with a sleep injected between the delete and the rename, as the repro idea says.

suspected.title: A vertex stream that the pipeline's vertex descriptor fetches can be left unbound: a nil bound.vertex slot or a skipped int4 expansion still draws, and Metal has no D3D11-style zero read for an unbound slot
suspected.bug_class: out-of-bounds GPU read: vertex fetch from an unbound buffer index (port divergence from D3D11's defined zero read)
suspected.label: ext
suspected.evidence: Draw binds only the non-nil snapshots: `for (unsigned i = 0; i < 23; ++i) { if (vertexBuffers[i]) { [enc setVertexBuffer:vertexBuffers[i] offset:bound.vertexOffsets[i] atIndex:i + 8]; } }` (backend.mm:525-529). The pipeline's vertex descriptor is `[bound.layout copy]` (Pipeline, :366) and still declares every layout stream (VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate sets layouts[e.stream + 8] for each element, :2083-2088), so a stream whose buffer is nil is fetched from an unbound index. The int4 widening has the same gap: Pipeline() rewrites the attribute to `a.bufferIndex = 7; desc.vertexDescriptor.layouts[7].stride = 16` (:371-376) unconditionally. Draw then `continue`s without binding index 7 when `!source || !stride` (:539-541) or when `begin >= source.length` (:543-545). D3D11 defines a fetch from an unbound vertex-buffer slot to return 0, so the DX11 backend draws (wrong but bounded). Metal gives no such guarantee: without API validation the GPU reads whatever is at that buffer index, and the command buffer can fault (a GPU page fault). The nil cases are reachable in this backend: VertexBufferData::Create when MakeBuffer returns nil (:1917-1924), an ext.create_on_demand Ensure that ends Failed (a re-decode failure in lazy_create.mm:71-77 leaves `buffer` nil, and Bind stores nil at :1980), a dynamic stream whose Lock failed, and a Bind with strideBytes 0.
suspected.repro_idea: With MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1, force one static vertex buffer to stay nil: make lazy_create.mm's Redecode fail for one record (fault injection), or return nil from NewBuffer once for kind "vertex". Then draw the mesh that uses it. The validation layer reports a missing vertex buffer binding at index N+8. Without the layer, watch for '[Metal] command error' (GPU fault) in that frame. Minimal fix: in Draw, skip the draw when a stream the layout references has no buffer (or when the int4 expansion did not bind index 7), or bind a zeroed dummy buffer there, with a NOT RETAIL comment.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (reachable only after an allocation or re-decode failure; the result is a GPU fault or garbage geometry, not CPU memory corruption)
verdict.proof:
Checked against origin/main fa150cf7f in <worktree>. The finding is not in the ledger: README F-001..F-217, P0_MAP and findings_p3p4/p8 have no unbound-vertex-slot entry. The nearest entry is the p8 item "Int4 vertex expansion writes through an unchecked NewBuffer result", which is a different defect (a nil.contents write on the CPU).

The code matches the description:
- Draw (backend.mm:525-529) binds only the non-nil snapshots `vertexBuffers[i]`.
- Pipeline() (:366) copies `bound.layout`. VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate (:2083-2088) declares `layouts[e.stream+8]` for every element.
- Pipeline() also always rewrites int4/UChar4 attributes to bufferIndex 7 (:371-377).
- The int4 expansion `continue`s without binding index 7 when `!source || !stride` (:539-541) or when `begin >= source.length` (:543-545).
- Draw never checks that every stream the descriptor references was bound, and nothing returns early.
- VertexBufferData::Bind (:1975-1985) stores `buffer` even when it is nil (Create failed, or a create_on_demand Ensure failed).
So the missing guard is real.

Why this is not CONFIRMED:
1. The fault is not provable statically. Draw does not end the encoder between draws, and Metal keeps an encoder's earlier setVertexBuffer bindings, so a later draw usually reads a stale but valid buffer. Only the first draw on a fresh encoder reads a slot that was never set. Whether that faults or reads zero depends on the GPU and the driver (Apple Silicon behaves differently from Intel/AMD Macs). It needs a run under MTL_DEBUG_LAYER / Metal API validation, or a GPU fault seen in a run.
2. Every trigger is a failure path: MakeBuffer returning nil (OOM), a failed ext.create_on_demand re-decode, or a stride/offset the engine does not normally pass.
3. The "Lock failed" case is weak, because a caller whose Lock returns null normally skips the draw.
4. The "Bind with strideBytes 0" case does not leave a slot unbound for ordinary streams: the buffer is still set, and the descriptor keeps the stride from PlatformCreate. Stride 0 only skips the int4 expansion at :539.

The divergence from DX11 is real: an IASetVertexBuffers null slot returns a zero fetch. But this is a Metal-only backend detail with no retail counterpart (label ext/port-backend). It does not affect faithful sim or save bytes.

Proof needed: a fault-injection run (NewBuffer returns nil once for kind "vertex", or Redecode fails once) with Metal API validation on. The run should report a missing buffer binding at index N+8 or 7, or log '[Metal] command error'.
verdict.minimal_fix: In Draw (src/render/metal/backend.mm, after the snapshot), skip the draw when a layout stream the pipeline's vertex descriptor references (any layouts[i+8] with stride != 0 that an attribute uses) has a nil vertexBuffers[i]. Do the same when the int4 expansion `continue`s without binding index 7. Alternatively, bind a small zeroed dummy MTLBuffer at those indices to match D3D11's zero fetch. Add a "NOT RETAIL:" comment either way.

proof_run.proof:
The finding is not proven on this host. The code at origin/main fa150cf7f matches the description, but no failure was observed.

Code checked in <worktree>/src/render/metal/backend.mm:
- Draw (:525-529) binds only the non-nil vertexBuffers[i].
- Pipeline() (:366-377) copies bound.layout, which declares every stream. It also always redirects int4/UChar4 attributes to buffer index 7 with stride 16.
- The int4 expansion loop `continue`s without binding index 7 when `!source || !stride` (:539-541) or when `begin >= source.length` (:543-545).
- No path skips the draw.

The proof cannot be built here. The host is Windows 10 (MINGW64) with no macOS, Xcode or Metal device, so backend.mm cannot be compiled or run, and MTL_DEBUG_LAYER is not available. A tests/unit case cannot observe a GPU fetch from an unbound buffer index: that behaviour belongs to the Metal driver and validation layer, and macOS CI runs only unit, with no GPU draw.

Every trigger is a failure path: MakeBuffer returning nil, a failed create_on_demand re-decode, or stride 0 on an int4 stream. A stale binding from an earlier draw on the same encoder also usually hides the gap.

To confirm it needs a Mac run with Metal API validation and fault injection: NewBuffer returns nil once for kind "vertex", or Redecode fails once. The expected result is a "missing vertex buffer binding" report at index N+8 or 7, or "[Metal] command error".
proof_run.minimal_fix:
In Draw in src/render/metal/backend.mm, after the vertexBuffers snapshot:
- Return without drawing when a stream the pipeline's vertex descriptor uses is unbound. That is any attribute's bufferIndex in 8..30 with vertexBuffers[bufferIndex-8] == nil.
- Also return without drawing when an int4/UChar4 attribute was redirected to index 7 but the expansion loop `continue`d without binding 7.
- Add a "NOT RETAIL:" comment. D3D11 returns 0 for an unbound slot; Metal has no defined read for one.
- Alternative: bind a small zeroed dummy MTLBuffer at those indices instead of skipping the draw.

suspected.title: AttachColorBuffer / AttachDepthBuffer write the frame thread's mainColor / mainDepth / msaaSamples statics and the alias's strong `texture` field from the loader thread without the device lock, racing RebuildMainTargets / ApplyEngineSettingsChange
suspected.bug_class: data race on ARC strong statics and fields (state documented as 'render thread only' written from a second thread); ownership across threads
suspected.label: port
suspected.repro_idea: macOS TSan build (or Xcode Thread Sanitizer). Start loading a saved town and, while the loading screen shows, drag-resize the window continuously, or move it between a Retina and a non-Retina display (OnWindowEvent raises settingsChanged). Repeat over many loads. Expect TSan reports on `mainColor` (backend.mm:1423 vs 1145/1148/687) and on `ImageBufferData::texture` (1433 vs 694). A deterministic unit form: call AttachColorBuffer on one thread and RebuildMainTargets on another against a stub device, with a barrier between `colorAliases.insert` and `texture = mainColor`.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: race (suspected, unproven reach)
verdict.proof:
The code shape is accurate. In src/render/metal/backend.mm:69, mainColor, mainDepth, targetColor and targetDepth are documented "render thread only". AttachColorBuffer (1412-1434) and AttachDepthBuffer (1435-1457) read and write mainColor, mainDepth and msaaSamples with no device lock. They also do `texture = mainColor` after `colorAliases.insert(this)` and outside stateMutex. ApplyEngineSettingsChange (1143-1150, under dev->Lock in BeginCommands 1160-1166) and RebuildMainTargets (682-697, alias writes under stateMutex) write the same statics and the alias `texture` fields. The ledger (docs/history/review_20261103: README, P0_MAP, findings_p3p4.json, findings_p8.json) has no entry for AttachColorBuffer, FrameCopy, colorAliases or RebuildMainTargets. The nearest is the p8 entry on the settingsChanged flag race, which is a different defect. This is therefore not a duplicate.

The finding's cross-thread path does not hold as cited, though. The comment it quotes at splash_loop_stubs.cpp:361-369 says the opposite of what the finding claims. Retail ran the menu-scene load on the loader thread, but the port moved LoadSceneA1 (the caller that constructs the menu scene's FrameCopyImageBuffer) onto the MAIN thread's splash update. It also gates the load on `!EngineLoader::IsBusy() && !resetPending` (line 370). So that FrameCopy ctor runs on the same thread as BeginCommands/ApplyEngineSettingsChange, which is the main thread unless ext.render_pipe is on, and it never runs while a settings reset is pending. The other two FrameCopy constructors in the tree are also main-thread work: the screenshot in w2_takescreenshot.cpp:120 and the save thumbnail in saveload_draw.cpp:403.

A real race would need either of two things, and the source alone does not show either:
(a) A FrameCopyImageBuffer created on the Engine::Loader thread through FindOrLoad -> FrameCopyImageBuffer::CreateNewObject (imagebuffer_derived.cpp:267) during a game load, such as a water/refraction resource that the menu scene did not already put in the resource cache. No such resource load was found in src/game.
(b) ext.render_pipe (default OFF), where BeginCommands runs on the render thread while the main thread builds the screenshot or thumbnail FrameCopy.

If either happens, the unlocked `texture = mainColor` and the strong-store race on mainColor are real UB: concurrent objc_storeStrong on the same field leads to a double release or use-after-free. A macOS TSan run (game load with a resize during the loading screen, plus a render_pipe-on screenshot under resize) is needed to show it is reachable.
verdict.minimal_fix: In AttachColorBuffer and AttachDepthBuffer, take the device lock (or stateMutex) around the whole body: the mainColor/mainDepth/msaaSamples creation, the alias insert and the `texture = mainColor/mainDepth` store, so the alias can never be published before its texture is set. Do the RebuildMainTargets static stores under the same lock. Mark the change NOT RETAIL: a Metal-backend-only locking addition.

proof_run.proof:
The race itself was not observed. The Metal backend (backend.mm) cannot be built or run on this Windows bed or under WSL, so no TSan report exists, and the status stays SUSPECTED under the proof standard. The reach that the verifier doubted was confirmed on a real run.

Method: temporary stderr instrumentation in the shared engine code, reverted afterwards. The FrameCopyImageBuffer ctor (wave23_lane_gfxbody.cpp:243), which calls image->_data->AttachColorBuffer() unguarded, printed the current thread id and Video::Device::lockOwnerThreadId (+0x88). The DX11 ContextData::BeginCommands printed its thread id. The exe was a debug build at fa150cf7f, run with tools/build.sh run (autostart new game, profile faithful) in functional dir Banished-B.

Observed (run_threads.log):
- BeginCommands tid=22800 (main).
- FrameCopy ctor n=1 tid=22800 deviceLockOwner=4294967295. This is the menu scene, LoadSceneA1 on the main thread, as the verifier said.
- FrameCopy ctor n=2 tid=23408 deviceLockOwner=4294967295. It runs right after "loader.run thread=loader GameUpdateLoop / loader.resources thread=loader", and "loop.started thread=main GameLoadDialogLoopT" shows the main thread drawing the loading screen at the same time.

So the game load builds a second FrameCopyImageBuffer on the Engine loader thread, with the device lock not held (owner = none). On macOS this means Metal ImageBufferData::AttachColorBuffer runs on the loader thread while the main thread runs BeginCommands. That is the verifier's path (a).

The writes then go unsynchronised:
- the loader reads mainColor;
- the loader does colorAliases.insert(this) under stateMutex, then `texture = mainColor` outside it, which is objc_storeStrong / retain of mainColor;
- on the main thread, ApplyEngineSettingsChange (under dev->Lock only, when settingsChanged is set by a resize or a display change during loading) does `mainColor = nil` and a release, then RebuildMainTargets stores mainColor and every alias `texture` under stateMutex.

Because the loader holds neither the device lock nor stateMutex around its reads and stores, a resize in that window gives a concurrent retain/release of the same object and a concurrent strong store to the alias's `texture`. That is a use-after-free or double release, or an alias left on a stale texture.

Without a settings change in the window, main-thread Present only reads mainColor, and the read-read is benign. The race therefore needs a resize or a Retina/non-Retina display move during the game-load resources phase. Confirming it needs a macOS TSan run (load a game, drag-resize during the loading screen); it is expected to report backend.mm:1421/1433 against 1145/1148/687/694.

The verifier's other scenario, (b) render_pipe screenshot, was not tested.
proof_run.minimal_fix: In src/render/metal/backend.mm, ImageBufferData::AttachColorBuffer and AttachDepthBuffer: take Video::Device::_singleton->Lock() (recursive; ApplyEngineSettingsChange runs under the same lock in BeginCommands) around the whole body: the mainColor/mainDepth/msaaSamples creation, the alias insert and the `texture = mainColor/mainDepth` store, and Unlock at the end. The alias is then published together with its texture, and the loader can no longer interleave with ApplyEngineSettingsChange/RebuildMainTargets. Comment it as "NOT RETAIL: Metal backend only; the game load builds a FrameCopyImageBuffer on the loader thread without the device lock". Optionally move `texture = mainColor` inside the stateMutex block as well. The ext.share_gpu_data DropTexture must stay inside the locked region. No change to engine/shared code.
proof_run.repro_path: scratchpad/phase2/proofs/metal-attach-race/run_threads.log (also instrumentation.diff, instrument.py in the same dir)

suspected.title: pipelines.txt warm-up trusts every numeric field of a cached record and never checks the record against its key: a malformed cache can abort pipeline creation at boot or bind a pipeline built from a different descriptor
suspected.bug_class: unchecked cache-file input / error path continues with garbage
suspected.label: port
suspected.evidence: PipelineRecordValid (pipeline_cache.h:42-75) checks only the types (NSNumber, array counts 31/31/8), never the values. RestorePipeline (165-203) copies them straight into a descriptor: `v.format = (MTLVertexFormat)[a[0] unsignedIntegerValue]; v.offset = ...; v.bufferIndex = [a[2] unsignedIntegerValue]; ... b.stride = ...; c.pixelFormat = (MTLPixelFormat)[r[@"color"] ...]; d.rasterSampleCount = [r[@"samples"] unsignedIntegerValue]; ... c.writeMask = ...`. RegisterPipelineShader then compiles each record asynchronously with newRenderPipelineStateWithDescriptor (207-227) as soon as its vs/ps identities load. Metal's descriptor checks (out-of-range bufferIndex, no pixel format, unsupported sample count, invalid enum) report through MTLReportFailure, which can abort the process even without the debug layer. That would happen at every launch until the user deletes ~/Library/Caches/OpenBA/pipelines.txt. Separately, LoadPipelineRecords (99-105) stores records[key] under the file's key without recomputing the key from the record. CachedPipeline (311-335) returns warmPipelines[key].state for any live descriptor whose JSON equals that key, so a record whose contents differ from its key (corrupt or edited file) puts a pipeline with other formats, blend or vertex layout on live draws. Suggested hardening: range-check the values (bufferIndex < 31, sampleCount in {1,2,4,8}, known pixel formats), and drop any record whose recomputed DescribePipeline JSON, minus 'seen', is not equal to its key.
suspected.repro_idea: Write a version-2 pipelines.txt plist whose one record has valid vs/ps identities from a previous run but color=0, depth=0 (no attachment formats), or attrs[0]=[29,0,40] (bufferIndex 40). Launch with the Metal backend and check standalone_crash.log for a Metal 'failed assertion' / abort during RegisterPipelineShader. For the key mismatch: copy one record's key onto a record with a different blend array and compare the rendering of that draw against a run without the cache.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: crash (unproven); wrong-pipeline binding only with a hand-edited or forged cache file
verdict.proof:
The ledger does not have it. findings_p8.json has only the FastPipelineCache evict/insert race (fast_pipeline_cache.h), and P0_MAP.md:306-308 lists the Vulkan pipeline cache and the Metal tests. Nothing covers pipelines.txt validation. It is not fixed on origin/main: <worktree>/src/render/metal/pipeline_cache.h is as the finding describes.

What the code shows, line by line:
(1) PipelineRecordValid (42-75) checks types and array lengths only. It never checks values.
(2) RestorePipeline (165-203) puts those values straight into an MTLRenderPipelineDescriptor: format, offset and bufferIndex (178-180), stride, stepFunction and stepRate (183-185), color, depth and stencil formats (188-190), rasterSampleCount (191), and the blend enums and writeMask (194-201).
(3) RegisterPipelineShader (237-245) starts StartPipeline, which calls the async newRenderPipelineStateWithDescriptor, for every record whose vs/ps functions resolve.
(4) LoadPipelineRecords (99-105) stores records[key] under the key read from the file. It never recomputes the key with DescribePipeline. CachedPipeline (312-335) recomputes the key from the live descriptor, looks it up in warmPipelines, and returns entry->state, which was compiled from the record's own contents. So when a record's contents do not match its key, a pipeline built from a different descriptor is bound to live draws. That part follows from the code. It needs a file that is both a valid plist and inconsistent with itself. The game only writes this file through writeToFile:atomically: from DescribePipeline output, so in practice that means a hand-edited or hostile file, not ordinary corruption. Under the campaign rules that is plain hardening, not UB.

The crash claim, that Metal aborts through MTLReportFailure at every boot without API validation, is not proven statically. With validation off (the default outside Xcode), Metal often rejects a bad descriptor by returning an NSError in the completion handler, which line 224 logs, rather than asserting. Whether out-of-range bufferIndex values, an invalid pixel format enum, or rasterSampleCount values such as 3 hard-abort on the shipping driver needs a macOS run with a crafted pipelines.txt. No test, sanitizer report or crash log exists.

There is no retail counterpart, since this is a Metal-backend cache, so this is not port drift. The crash severity needs build proof; the key-mismatch half is a hardening item.
verdict.minimal_fix:
In LoadPipelineRecords, after PipelineRecordValid passes, also range-check the values:
- bufferIndex < 31
- stepFunction <= 4
- rasterSampleCount in {1,2,4,8}
- blend factor and operation enums within their known ranges
- writeMask <= 0xF

Then drop any record whose key does not match. Recompute the key the way CachedPipeline does: take the record minus "seen", serialise it with NSJSONSerialization using NSJSONWritingSortedKeys, and require it to equal the file key.

proof_run.proof:
Not proven, and not refuted. This bed cannot build or run src/render/metal/pipeline_cache.h. It is Objective-C++ against Metal.framework, and CMake builds the metal backend only on APPLE. No macOS host is reachable: the ssh config lists only 192.168.1.208 and 192.168.1.216, neither of them a mac. WSL has no Metal. The existing tests/unit/metal_*_test.cpp files cover only pure C++ headers such as fast_pipeline_cache.h, and this file cannot be unit-tested without Metal.

Reading origin/main confirms the static facts:
- PipelineRecordValid (42-75) checks types and array counts only.
- RestorePipeline (165-203) copies the unchecked values into the MTLRenderPipelineDescriptor: format, offset and bufferIndex, stride, stepFunction and stepRate, the color, depth and stencil formats, samples, the blend enums and writeMask.
- RegisterPipelineShader starts the async compile for every record whose functions resolve.
- LoadPipelineRecords (99-105) stores records[key] under the file's key without recomputing it.
- CachedPipeline returns warmPipelines[key].state, compiled from the record's own contents.

So a record whose contents differ from its key binds a mismatched pipeline. By code inspection that half is certain. It needs a hand-edited or forged plist, though, because the game writes the file only from DescribePipeline output. That makes it hardening, not UB.

The crash half is the open question. When API validation is off, does Metal hard-assert (MTLReportFailure) on bufferIndex >= 31, rasterSampleCount 3 or an invalid pixel format? Or does it return an NSError, which line 224 already logs? That needs a macOS run with a crafted pipelines.txt. The repro recipe is in the proofs dir.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
Two changes, both in LoadPipelineRecords after PipelineRecordValid passes:
- Range-check the values: bufferIndex < 31, stepFunction <= 4, samples in {1,2,4,8}, blend factor and operation enums within the known MTLBlendFactor / MTLBlendOperation ranges, and writeMask <= 0xF.
- Drop any record whose key does not match. Recompute the key the way CachedPipeline does: take the record minus "seen", serialise it with NSJSONSerialization using NSJSONWritingSortedKeys, and require it to equal the file key.

This is plain hardening, with no NOT RETAIL comment, because Metal has no retail counterpart.

verdict.proof:
I traced it line by line on origin/main fa150cf7f; main.cpp is unchanged there. The only merged PR that matches the search terms is #106, and it is about something else.

1. The step loop calls the pump with no lock. In src/engine/engine/mainloop_frame.cpp, line 364 calls _extFrame(kExtBeforeSteps). Then the loop `while (_accumulator >= _deltaTime._ticks)` at line 371 calls Platform::Pump(&Application::WindowProc) at line 420. The pump calls the observer that main.cpp:731 installs (WndMsgObserver) before WindowProc, on the main thread.

2. The observer runs a reset without a lock. In main.cpp:694-696, a WM_ACTIVATE with LOWORD(wParam)!=0 calls ForceVideoContextReset. At main.cpp:647-662 that function checks g_bootedExclusiveFullscreen, ml->_context and !ctx, then writes `ml->_contextDirty = 0; ctx->Reset();`. It takes no device lock and no handoff lock. In src/engine/video/context.cpp:480+, Context::Reset assigns _dirty. It memsets the pixel staging at +0x208 and +0x248, _viewProjection (0xd0 bytes), _boneAndProjectionStaging, _transforms and _lightStaging. It nulls every _imageBuffers[i], every _vertexBuffers/_vertexOffsets/_vertexStrides entry, _indexBuffer, _renderBuffer and _vertexLayout, and ORs into _imageBufferDirty and _vertexBufferDirty. None of these fields is atomic.

3. With render_pipe on, the steps run while the render thread is still drawing. In src/ext/render_pipe/pipe_driver.h:133-156, BeforeSteps on a held packet with overlap=true calls _handoff->ClaimSteps(). When that succeeds it sets _overlapping=true and returns, so the fence is not taken. handoff.h:51-58 says ClaimSteps waits only until the job's BeginCommands has returned (NoteBegun). From then until the job's Gate, the render thread keeps running. The render_pipe.cpp banner says an overlapped packet's "pass 2 runs beside the next Frame's steps", and the Gate is EngineOps::Gate at line 421, after Pass2. EngineOps::Pass2 at render_pipe.cpp:405-418 runs Ext::RenderPipe::Pass2(*p.renderer, *ctx, ...) on the render thread. ctx is loop->_context, the same Context* the observer resets (render_pipe.cpp:581). Pass 2 sets and reads the same _imageBuffers, _vertexBuffers, _dirty, _transforms and staging fields through Context's Set* and draw calls. Nothing orders the two threads: the render thread holds the device lock, Reset never takes it, and the handoff mutex is taken only at the claim and the gate.

4. Nothing turns either side off in this setup. The overlap governor in overlap_governor.h has no platform gate. Line 566 sets next.overlap=true whenever the governor is on, and it switches on for any frame that does not idle and has a removable fence wait of at least 1 ms, such as a heavy town or high game speed. Nothing in src/ext/render_pipe mentions fullscreen. g_bootedExclusiveFullscreen comes from Render::BootedExclusiveFullscreen(), which is the DX11 swap chain's Windowed=0.

So within one Frame's steps, the main thread's Reset writes and nulls non-atomic Context fields that the render thread is writing and reading in pass 2 at the same moment. That is a C++ data race (UB). In practice a draw can bind a half-cleared Context: _dirty bits get lost, buffers arrive null, transforms get zeroed partway. Retail has no render thread, and the observer is NOT RETAIL focus code, so the label is ext.

A related point outside S-002: the engine's own WM_ACTIVATE handler in the same pump (DeviceData_OnActivate, the swap-chain rebuild) also runs beside the overlapped pass 2. The F-158 note in handoff.h covers only pump writes that BeginCommands reads.
verdict.minimal_fix: Do not touch the Context from the pump. ForceVideoContextReset should only latch a static flag (g_pendingFseReset = true). Then do the `ml->_contextDirty = 0; ctx->Reset();` from the main thread at a point where no emit is running: in the faithful path at the Frame tail before Draw, and with render_pipe after its join (Host::AfterJoin, or the tail once Overlapping() has settled). A smaller alternative is to skip the reset while MainLoop::_extFrame is installed, and have render_pipe force a full join (WaitIdle) before Platform::Pump whenever a refocus is pending. Either way, comment the change as NOT RETAIL. With the ext off, behaviour stays byte-identical, because the reset still happens before the next Draw.

(2) BuildParameters (wave27_lane_gfxbig.cpp:634 and :675) stores that result in v.sourceIndex without a check. It then takes v.shaderSlot from PixelProgram::_textures/_constants[i].dest (:651, :678). verdict.label: retail
verdict.severity: memory-corruption (use-after-free on the Persistence worker thread, timing-dependent)
verdict.proof:
Still open on origin/main fa150cf7f, and the static chain holds. The campaign's proof bar (a test, fuzz input or sanitizer report for a finding that is not port drift) is not met yet, so the verdict is needs_build_proof.

Retail (Ghidra, Runtime-x64.dll ??1SaveLoad 0x1800c3c90) has no wait in the destructor. In order it does:
1. `MOV [0x1801fc6f0],0`
2. releases the String at +0x70
3. `LEA RCX,[RBX+0x50] / CALL 0x1800329c0` (~Array<SaveInfo>)
4. `MOV RCX,[RBX+0x30] / TEST / JZ / CALL 0x180006a10` (MemFree of _embeddedState._data)
5. releases the String at +0x20, then RET.

It never reads Persistence or _worker. RtSave_SaveLoad_Dtor (src/engine/save/saveload.cpp:400-418) copies this exactly, so the port is faithful and the bug is retail's.

Retail MainMenuDialog::ReturnToMenu (Application-x64.exe 0x1400b4790) also has no wait. It loads the SaveLoad pointer from +0xb8 -> +0x140 or +0xc0 -> +0xb70, then does `CALL [0x140151f88]` (??1SaveLoad) and `CALL [0x140152b68]` (MemFree), with no wait or status check first. The port (src/game/Dialog/mainmenudialog.cpp:204/212) does the same.

How the buffer gets lent:
- UpdateSaveTail (src/engine/save/saveload_update.cpp:1060-1076) sets `blocks[0].data = _embeddedState._data` and `blocks[1].data = _saveState->_data`, and calls RtIo_PersistenceWorker_EnqueueSave.
- On the worker thread, SaveJob (src/engine/io/persistence_worker.cpp:610-630) reads `blockPtrs[i]` twice: once for Crc32Chunked and once for the Platform::FileWrite loop.
- Nothing ties the job to the SaveLoad that lent the buffer. The only gate is SaveLoad::Update's IsWorking check, which drives the state machine and never runs in the destructor.

Not fixed by a merged PR. PR #148's F-101 added WaitForFinish to ~PersistenceWorker only. That does not cover S-004, for two reasons:
- (a) On ReturnToMenu, Persistence is never destroyed, so the worker keeps running against the freed buffer.
- (b) On quit, GameUpdateLoop::Shutdown (gameupdateloop.cpp:2279-2283) destroys SaveLoad before Persistence goes away, so the free happens before that wait.

Not a duplicate of F-101: F-101 is the worker freeing its own arrays, while here the owner frees a borrowed buffer.

Missing piece: a dynamic repro showing ReturnToMenu or Shutdown running inside one SaveJob window. Suggested shape, like PR #148's persist_dtor ASan repro: enqueue a save with blocks from a real SaveLoad, make the job slow (a large block 1 or a slow FileWrite stand-in), call RtSave_SaveLoad_Dtor + MemFree on the main thread, and expect heap-use-after-free in SaveJob on the blocks[0] read. Alternatively, a gate run that triggers an autosave and calls ReturnToMenu on the same frame.

Side note: the destructor also never frees the heap _saveState (+0x40). That leak is retail's too.
verdict.minimal_fix: At the top of RtSave_SaveLoad_Dtor, before anything is freed: if IO::Persistence's singleton exists and `_worker.IsWorking()`, call `_worker.WaitForFinish()`. Mark it with a "NOT RETAIL:" comment: retail frees _embeddedState._data (+0x30) while a SaveJob (blocks[0]) or a list LoadJob may still use it. hFinished is a manual-reset event that every enqueue resets, so the wait returns at once when no job is running. Valid runs produce the same bytes.

proof_run.proof:
ASan reports heap-use-after-free, and the run is reproducible (3 of 3). The repro was built with clang-19 ASan+UBSan in WSL against a private copy of worktree fa150cf7f (~/openba-s004, synced by a private copy of lx_san.sh, third_party taken from openba-review). It links fuzz_tree plus these real files: src/engine/io/persistence_worker.cpp (RtIo_PersistenceWorker_EnqueueSave, Run, SaveJob), src/engine/save/saveload.cpp (RtSave_SaveLoad_Dtor), src/engine/system/thread.cpp with the posix thread and sync layer, file_posix.cpp, and allocator.cpp (the engine heap under ASan is malloc/free).

2. Builds UpdateSaveTail's blocks[] verbatim and enqueues the save on a real worker.
3. 5 ms later, on the main thread, runs ReturnToMenu's sequence: RtSave_SaveLoad_Dtor(sl) then MemFree(sl), with no wait.

Result:
- ASan report: `heap-use-after-free on address 0x531000014800 ... READ of size 65536 ... thread T1`.
- Stack: `#0 write`, `#1 Platform::WriteAll file_posix.cpp:98`, `#2 IO::PersistenceWorker::SaveJob() persistence_worker.cpp:636` (the FileWrite of blockPtrs[0]), `#3 System::Thread::ThreadFunc thread.cpp:208`.

- The other four job arms trap, and the usual archive link stubs are present (same pattern as save_meta_fuzz.cpp / F-101).

At the top of RtSave_SaveLoad_Dtor (src/engine/save/saveload.cpp:400), before anything is freed, add: `if (::IO::Persistence* p = PersistenceSingleton(); p != nullptr && p->_worker.IsWorking()) p->_worker.WaitForFinish();`. verdict.label: retail
verdict.severity: low (the stated route cannot happen; at most a one-frame race)
verdict.proof:
Not fixed on origin/main fa150cf7f. statusbarui.cpp:392-438 still has the retail shape the finding quotes: the index wraps to 0 and _data[0] is read before any test of `citizens._size`. Retail 0x14007a120 has the same shape, so this is retail behaviour, not port drift. No merged PR touches it ("statusbar" and "S-006" searches find nothing related, and src/ext has no row for it).

The reproduction route the finding gives does not work. Opening the status bar in an empty town and clicking an icon cannot reach the handler:
- StatusBarUI::OnUpdateLayout (retail 0x1400798d0, statusbarui.cpp:177-270) runs every frame. It ORs every citizen's StatusIconComponent activeMask into statusBitfield, then for each icon k calls `statusIcons[k]->SetFlagsOnOff(hasStatus ? 0 : 1, hasStatus ? 1 : 0)`.
- Flag 0x1 is kElementFlagHidden (Element.h:119). With citizens._size == 0, statusBitfield is 0, so all six icons (ids 100..105) are hidden.
- A hidden element is never hit (element_vtable.cpp:269: `if ((_flags & (kElementFlagHidden | kElementFlagNoHitTest)) != 0) return false;`), so no click event with eventType 2 and id 100..105 is ever produced for them.
- More generally, an icon is visible only when the last layout pass saw at least one live citizen with that status bit.

Only one route is left: a same-frame race. A layout pass runs with _size >= 1 (icon shown), the mouse event for that icon is pushed by DialogInstance::Update (dialog.cpp:1038, which hit-tests the current flags), and the last citizen is removed from town->citizens (ArrayRemove8 leaves a stale slot) before StatusBarUI::OnElementEvent (0x14007a3a0) dispatches it. Whether the main loop ever runs the sim tick between the layout or hit-test and the event dispatch decides it, and the static reading here does not settle that order. Proving it takes a build: a harness or unit route that removes the last citizen between the layout pass and the queued click, run under ASan, or a trace of the frame order (UI update / event dispatch / sim tick / layout). Without that, the finding stays SUSPECTED and its stated reproduction is refuted.
verdict.minimal_fix: Apply this only if a build proves the race: a fix.* row under src/ext that returns from StatusBarUI_StatusIconHandler_Impl when town->citizens._size <= 0, before the index increment, with the faithful arm kept and a NOT RETAIL comment. Otherwise make no code change, and correct the finding's reproduction note: in an empty town every icon is hidden (flag 0x1 set by OnUpdateLayout) and cannot be hit.

proof_run.proof:
S-006 is CONFIRMED by a failing unit test. Its corrected route is a one-frame race: a click queued in frame N is dispatched in frame N+1, after that frame's sim tick has removed the last citizen. The empty-town route in the finding is refuted, as triage said: OnUpdateLayout hides every icon (flag 0x1), and a hidden icon cannot be hit.

Frame order in retail, read from the call sequence in Ghidra:
- Runtime UserInterface::Update (0x1801213e0) calls, in this order:
  - UpdateEvents 0x18011fc60 at 0x1801215e1, which dispatches the events queued earlier;
  - DialogInstance::ComputeLayout 0x180113d90 at 0x180121610, which runs StatusBarUI::OnUpdateLayout and sets the icon flags;
  - DialogInstance::Update 0x180113980 at 0x18012176a, which hit-tests against those flags and pushes the click into _events.
- So a click pushed in frame N is only dispatched by frame N+1's UpdateEvents, and that happens before frame N+1's layout pass.
- Exe GameUpdateLoop::Update (0x140096380) runs EntityList::Update 0x1400c4090 (at 0x14009642b) and CitizenBehavior::Update 0x14008c2b0 (at 0x140096467) before the UI update import at 0x140096593 / ToolManager::Update 0x1401026a0.
- CitizenComponent::OnRemove calls citizens.Remove (ArrayRemove8): _size goes 1 -> 0 and slot 0 keeps the removed pointer.
- Result: when the last citizen leaves the town in the tick right after the click, StatusBarUI::OnElementEvent runs with _size == 0. The port reproduces this order: userinterface_frame.cpp UpdateEvents -> layout -> pump, and gameupdateloop.cpp sim -> UI.

Test: tests/unit/statusbar_icon_race_test.cpp, built with tools/build.sh unit debug --jobs 2 on Windows, in worktree wf_4a641053-fa7-228 based on fa150cf7f.
- It links the real src/game/Dialog/statusbarui.cpp, plus abort stubs for the element bodies that only OnOpened / OnUpdateLayout name.
- Setup: one citizen whose StatusIconComponent has bit 1 set. The real Array::Remove (ArrayRemove8) then removes it, and the test checks _size == 0 and that _data[0] still holds the removed citizen.
- It then dispatches eventType 2 / id 101 through the real StatusBarUI::OnElementEvent.
- Expected: no navigation in an empty town.
- Observed: `FAIL statusbar_icon_race_test.cpp:146: g_centerCalls == 0`, `FAIL ...:147: g_centerEntity == nullptr`, and "S-006: the click centred on the removed citizen's entity (_data[0] read with _size == 0)".
- The control test statusbar_icon_click_finds_live_citizen passes.
- Unit totals: "2001 tests, 2 failures, 1 skipped". Both failures are the two CHECKs in statusbar_icon_click_after_last_citizen_removed, which is the only failing test.

In the port, the dying entity is still alive at that point (the EntityList drain is deferred one frame), so the defect shows as CenterOnEntity on an entity the town has already removed. In retail, the drain at the end of the same EntityList::Update has freed it, so the read of _data[0]->_entity is a use-after-free (static reasoning from the drain order; no ASan run, because MinGW GCC has no ASan and the WSL route was not available to this agent).

In StatusBarUI_StatusIconHandler_Impl (statusbarui.cpp:391), after the game-flags test, read `town->citizens._size`. When the row is on and the count is <= 0, return before the statusCitizenIndex++ and add a "NOT RETAIL:" comment: retail 0x14007a120 wraps to 0 and reads _data[0] with no size test. verdict.label: retail
verdict.severity: memory-corruption (hostile save only; faithful to retail)
verdict.proof:
Still present on origin/main fa150cf7f. No merged PR touches it: #134 (F-109), #135 (F-131/F-182..186) and #141 (F-143 etc.) fix other EntityList paths. Not a duplicate. F-131 is the save-supplied bucket *cursor* in Update, and S-038 is the time delta. Neither covers the per-entity master index, bucket index or bucket id.

Line-by-line proof on origin/main, <worktree>/src/game/Entity/entitylist.cpp:
(1) EntityList::Serialize Step 8, lines ~1604-1630, on load: `serializer.Serialize(masterIdxField)`, `serializer.Serialize(bucketIdxField)` and `serializer.Serialize(bucketId)` read three ints straight from the stream. They are stored back with no range test: `_entityId = masterIdxField`, the low 24 bits of `_handle = bucketIdxField`, and `_handleBytes[3] = (int8_t)bucketId`.
(2) EntityList.h:108 declares `UpdateBucket buckets[5];` at +0x18.
(3) RemoveEntity, line ~1393, reads `int8_t bucketIdx = _handle >> 24`. The only test is `if (bucketIdx != 6)`, so any value in -128..127 other than 6 reaches `&buckets[bucketIdx]` at line 1416. That is an out-of-bounds pointer for 5, 7..127 and for negative values. The code then calls `bucket->_size` and `bucket->SetSize()` on a fake Array made from EntityList bytes or memory past them. The UB is there and it writes memory.
(4) `entityBucketIdx` holds 24 bits from the save. `bucketData[entityBucketIdx] = bucketData[lastIdx]` writes out of bounds when it is >= _size.
(5) `entityMasterIdx = entity->_entityId` comes from the save. `masterData[entityMasterIdx] = masterData[lastMasterIdx]` and the following `->_entityId = ...` write out of bounds when it is >= masterArray._size or negative.
The trigger is any removal of that entity after a crafted save is loaded: demolition, death, or FlushForSerialize on the next save.

The finding's Ghidra quote (Serialize 0x1400c44a0 stores at 0x1400c46b9-0x1400c46dd with no test; RemoveEntity 0x1400c38e0 does `MOVSX RCX,byte [RAX+0x1f]; CMP ECX,6; JZ`, then indexes `[RDI+R8*8+0x18]` and writes `[RDX+RCX*8]`) shows the port matches retail. This is retail behaviour, not port drift. It is still UB driven by a save from outside, so the campaign ruling calls for a minimal NOT RETAIL fix.

The finding's extra claim, a null master slot dereferenced at line 1608 after the IsDerivedFrom filter nulls it, is part of the same Step 8 loop. It falls under the same fix.
verdict.minimal_fix:
In EntityList::Serialize Step 8, on load only, validate each entity before writing the fields back. Add a "NOT RETAIL:" comment, or use a fix.* row if the maintainer rules it is behaviour.

The checks: the master slot is non-null; masterIdxField == entityIdx; bucketId is in 0..4 or == 6; when bucketId != 6, bucketIdxField < buckets[bucketId]._size and buckets[bucketId]._data[bucketIdxField] == the entity.

When a check fails, either fail the load (serializer error) or rebuild the fields from the actual positions: _entityId = entityIdx, and the bucket id and index from a scan of buckets[0..4]. The scan only runs on an inconsistent save, so a valid save gives byte-identical results.
