verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: UB (latent; harmless today only because ~Array re-zeroes the header and -fno-lifetime-dse is passed)
verdict.proof:
Still present on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>). No merged PR touches it: a search for "S-030" or "DestroyAndFree" finds nothing relevant. The pattern appears at five sites:
- src/engine/io/persistence_worker.cpp:335 `w->_blockPtrs.~Array();` is followed at :336 by `w->_blockPtrs.SetSize(w->_blockDescs._size);` and :338-339 reads `_data` / `_size`.
- persistence_worker.cpp:420-421 `w->_blockDescs.~Array(); w->_blockPtrs.~Array();` is followed at :435-436 by `SetSize(blockCount)` on both.
- src/engine/io/persistence_begin_saveinfo.cpp:82-83 makes the same two explicit destructor calls, and the jobs then use the arrays.
Collection.h:562-565 defines `Array::~Array()` as a user-provided (non-trivial) destructor whose body is `DestroyAndFree()`. Under [basic.life]/1 an explicit call to it ends the member's lifetime. Nothing placement-news a new Array into that storage, so the following SetSize and the `_data` / `_size` reads use an object outside its lifetime, which [basic.life]/6-7 makes undefined. ~PersistenceWorker then destroys the member a second time, which [class.dtor] also makes undefined.
The port, not retail, introduced this: retail calls 0x180024aa0 / 0x18002a930 as plain clear-and-free routines on a live member. The repo already has a non-destructor member with the identical body: `Array::DestroyAndFree()` (Collection.h:558, `ClearCallback(hdr)`), the same routine ~Array calls. Swapping to it gives the same calls, frees and stores, so machine behaviour stays byte-identical.
No sanitizer detects this class of bug. The proof rests on the language rules applied line by line.
verdict.minimal_fix: Replace `X.~Array()` with `X.DestroyAndFree()` at src/engine/io/persistence_worker.cpp:335, 420, 421 and src/engine/io/persistence_begin_saveinfo.cpp:82, 83. Keep the retail-address comments. Add a "NOT RETAIL:" note saying the C++ spelling changed but the bytes did not: the same ClearCallback body runs as in retail 0x180024aa0 / 0x18002a930.

verdict.label: retail
verdict.severity: UB (low): indeterminate-value read on a truncated/hostile resource; outcome of the magic/version test depends on stack contents
verdict.proof:
Not fixed on origin/main fa150cf7f; PR #141/#144 (the External::Load review fixes) touched only the type-id arms (F-122/123/143/144/145/172). No F-* or other S-* covers these locals (README uninitialised rows are F-049/054/111/146/152/159/168, all other sites), so not a duplicate.

Line-by-line chain on origin/main:
1. src/engine/object/external_load.cpp:292-294 `int32_t magic; SerInt(rw, &magic); if (magic != kCompiledMagic)` and :372-376 `int32_t version; SerInt(rw, &version); ... if (version != objVersion)`. Neither local is initialised (the comment at :289-291 says so on purpose, mirroring retail 0x1800bc6da/0x1800bc772 where [RSP+0x34]/[RSP+0x30] are never stored before the SerializeInt call).
2. SerInt -> BinaryReader::SerializeInt (serialize_family.cpp RT_RW_READER_BODY): `stream->Read((int32_t)sizeof(T), &v);`, result discarded.
3. CompressedStream::Read (compressed_stream_read.cpp ~443-480) returns false without writing (or after writing only a prefix) in two ways: (a) SetWindow(_position) fails -> on a read miss it returns DecompressFromSource(pos>>15), which returns false for blk >= _headerSize (line 253), i.e. an empty stream or a read starting past the last block: nothing is written to magic/version; (b) the last block is short: the first iteration copies chunk = w->end - pos bytes (< 4), the next iteration takes the SetWindow fast path, chunk == 0, and the F-074 hardening returns false: the remaining bytes of the int stay indeterminate.
So a resource whose decompressed payload is 0..3 bytes (magic) or 8..11 bytes (version, after magic+typeId) leaves the compared int fully or partly indeterminate, and the `!=` reads it: undefined behaviour ([basic.indet]; erroneous behaviour under C++26). Reachable from mod packages / corrupt .pkg data the loader opens. Retail has the same uninitialised slots (faithful = label retail), so per campaign ruling it gets a minimal NOT RETAIL fix. A sanitizer/fuzz repro would be MSan on a 2-byte resource, but the static chain is complete without it.
verdict.minimal_fix: In src/engine/object/external_load.cpp initialise both locals with a NOT RETAIL (review S-031, UB) comment: `int32_t magic = 0;` (0 != kCompiledMagic 0x5412a91f, so a short read deterministically takes the bad-magic exit) and `int32_t version = -1;` (no type's GetFileVersion returns -1, so a short read takes the bad-version exit). Valid files are unaffected because a successful read overwrites both. Optionally a unit test feeding a 2-byte and a 9-byte compressed resource asserting Load returns null with g_lc.badMagic / badVersion bumped.

verdict.label: retail
verdict.severity: low (formal UB: memmove with a null source and n == 0; no memory is touched. Side effect: the row gets metadata read from an empty stream instead of the 'no metadata' arm, which is retail behaviour)
verdict.proof:
Still present on origin/main fa150cf7f. No merged or open PR touches it (open review PRs: #159 docs, #160 F-087). Not a duplicate: F-035 and F-061 are the mod-count and thumbnail-size input bugs in the same function, not this path.

Line-by-line chain, all in <worktree>:
1. State 2 (saveload_update.cpp ~1597) calls BeginGetSaveGameInfo(row.name, 2), which sets _worker._status = 0, sets the start event and returns (persistence_begin_saveinfo.cpp:70-100). The info job runs on the worker thread: open, header, then a CRC over the whole file. It sets _status = 1 when it succeeds (persistence_saveinfo_job.cpp:300).
2. State 3 (saveload_update.cpp:1603-1616) is the next tick. Its guard `!IsWorking() && _status == 1` fails while the info job is still running (bit 0 is set, or _status is still 0 because the thread has not woken yet). In that case SetupLoad and BeginLoad are skipped, but `_progress = 4` is still written. The port banner (point 2, ~1263) says this matches retail 0x1800c2251.
3. State 4 (:1621-1636) is the tick after that. Only BeginGetSaveGameInfo, EnqueueLoad and the other Begin* calls reset _status (persistence_worker.cpp:294/333/417). So if the info job has finished in between, the same guard now passes on the INFO job's status 1, and LoadMetaData runs even though no load was issued.
4. _embeddedState at that point is {nullptr, 0}. The previous LoadMetaData ended with the unconditional stores `_data = nullptr; _size = 0;` (saveload_loadmeta.cpp ~398-399, retail 0x1800c1d98..db5). Nothing has called SetupLoad since.
5. saveload_loadmeta.cpp:268-271 then runs `Open((int)0)` and `std::memmove(dst, _embeddedState._data /*nullptr*/, 0)`. Under C17 7.24.1p2 and 7.1.4, which C++ incorporates, a null pointer argument is UB even when n == 0. CompressedStream::Open then fails, and its result is discarded as in retail. The serializer reads fail, so the row is filled from those failed reads instead of taking the black-thumbnail arm.

Reachability: in the Load or Save dialog, any save whose info job (a whole-file CRC) takes longer than one frame and finishes within the next. This depends on timing but happens in normal play. Retail has the same control flow (transcribed from 0x1800c2251 and 0x1800c1b30), so the label is retail.

Why no sanitizer report: GCC 15+/16 declares the memmove builtin nonnull_if_nonzero, so UBSan will not fire for n == 0. A sanitizer report is therefore not available as proof. The static chain above is complete and depends on no unknowns, which is why the proof is static.
verdict.minimal_fix: In saveload_loadmeta.cpp:269, wrap the copy as `if (_embeddedState._size != 0) std::memmove(cmsObj->_memoryStream._data, _embeddedState._data, _embeddedState._size);`. Keep retail's second read of _size. Add the comment: "NOT RETAIL: memmove with a null source is UB even for n == 0. UpdateList state 3 can skip SetupLoad/BeginLoad while state 4 still calls here, leaving _embeddedState {nullptr, 0}." This leaves every byte and the state machine unchanged. Do not touch the UpdateList state 3/4 transition: it is faithful, and the 'no metadata' degradation depends on it.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (already fixed on main)
verdict.proof:
S-033 describes the same race as F-147: the persistence worker's `_status` hand-off was read with no acquire. F-147 is confirmed by TSan (README.md:198), and it was fixed by PR #148, merged as 4646b1bfe ("thread hand-offs are defined ... review F-101 ... F-147 ..."). Current origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>):

- Reader, src/engine/save/saveload_update.cpp:1001, in the fix.save_failure_notice seam: `const int32_t status = __atomic_load_n(&persistence->_worker._status, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);`. The comment there cites review F-147. The volatile cast that S-033 quotes is gone.
- Writer, src/engine/io/persistence_worker.cpp:658/660, in SaveJob: `__atomic_store_n(&_status, wroteAll ? 1 : 2, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);` and `__atomic_store_n(&_status, 2, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);`.

The release/acquire pair now orders the worker's writes and its file move before state 2 frees the SavedState. That is exactly the minimal fix S-033 proposes.

The finding's remaining sub-point is the plain `_status = 0` store at saveload_update.cpp:1464, called "EnqueueSave" in the finding. That store is in the list-saves request path and is written before `Platform::EventSet(_hStart)`. The worker only reads `_status` after waking on that event, and the event set/wait is the synchronising edge, so no race is left there.
verdict.minimal_fix: None needed. The fix is already on main through PR #148 (4646b1bfe): an acquire load at saveload_update.cpp:1001 and release stores at persistence_worker.cpp:658/660.

verdict.label: harness
verdict.severity: UB, low impact: a heap read after free on the sampler thread, only with BANISHED_SAMPLE on, in a narrow window
verdict.proof:
Checked on origin/main fa150cf7f. The bug is not fixed. PR #148 (fix/review-thread-sync) made _runFlags atomic but left the registry lifetime alone, and no merged PR touches DiagThreads or sampler.cpp for this. It is not a duplicate: the other _runFlags findings (F-101/F-103/F-150 and the persist, audio and pathfinder races) are about memory ordering of the flag, not about the object's lifetime.

Line by line:
(1) thread.cpp:204 `DiagThreads::RegisterNamed(typeid(*self).name(), &self->_runFlags)` stores a pointer into heap Thread storage (Engine::Loader, Audio::Stream, IO::PersistenceWorker or PathfinderThread).
(2) diag_threads.cpp keeps it in g_slots[i].busy. There is no Unregister or Forget. Register only overwrites the slot when a new thread reuses the same tid.
(3) sampler.cpp RefreshTracked copies it into Tracked::busy once.
(4) sampler.cpp WantSample runs `WaitForSingleObject(t.h,0) != WAIT_TIMEOUT` (liveness check, at time T0), then `QueryThreadCycleTime` (T1), then `return ran || (t.busy && (*t.busy & 1u) != 0)` (dereference, at T2).
(5) Thread::ReleaseFields (thread.cpp:158) does EventSet(_hStop), ThreadJoin and closes the handles. The owning subclass then frees the object.
(6) Nothing orders the sampler's T0..T2 against the owner's join and free.

The finding's own proof misses the `ran ||` short-circuit, which narrows the window but does not close it. The dereference needs `ran == false`, meaning the worker used no cycles between the previous tick's query and T1. That holds for a worker parked in EventWaitAny (an idle loader, audio stream or persistence worker at shutdown or at the end of a world build). This interleaving reaches it: the worker is parked, the sampler passes T0 and T1 with no cycle change, the sampler thread is preempted (TIME_CRITICAL lowers the chance but does not prevent it), the owner sets hStop, the worker returns and exits, the join returns, the subclass is freed, and the sampler reads *t.busy at T2. That read is freed heap, which is UB.

Reachability: diag only. The sampler starts only with BANISHED_SAMPLE (perf and stress runs). The faithful game path is unaffected, so the label is harness rather than retail or port. No sanitizer repro was built; forcing the interleaving would need an injected delay between QueryThreadCycleTime and the dereference.
verdict.minimal_fix: Simplest: stop handing out object storage. In ThreadFunc, call `DiagThreads::RegisterNamed(typeid(*self).name(), nullptr)`. The sampler's cycle-count test already catches any thread that ran since the last tick, so the busy bit only adds a worker that is blocked mid-job, and the cost of dropping it is small. If that bit is wanted, the registry should own the word instead: add an atomic busy word to each DiagThreads::Slot. ThreadFunc mirrors bit 0 into it (once per job, no hot-path cost) and the sampler reads the slot's word, so nothing ever points into a Thread object. A Forget() in ReleaseFields does not fix it on its own, because the sampler caches the pointer and would still race between its load and its dereference.

verdict.label: retail
verdict.severity: UB (heap use-after-free read in the UI teardown; benign-looking on the arena, an ASan report under BANISHED_SANITIZE=asan). Reachable only when code closes a dialog that hosts a ComboElement while its drop-down is open, for example EntityList_CloseDialogsForDyingEntities after a tornado or fire removes the building.
verdict.proof:
Not fixed on origin/main fa150cf7f. None of the merged review PRs (#103-#157) touches combodialog/comboelement, and docs/retail_bugs.md has no entry for it.

Retail and the port are identical, so the defect is retail's own:

- ~ComboElement 0x180112490 (checked in Ghidra): `MOV RCX,[RCX+0x120]; TEST RCX,RCX; JZ; MOV [RSP+0x48],RCX; LEA RDX,[RSP+0x48]; MOV RCX,[RCX+0x10]; CALL 0x180120f20`. This matches comboelement.cpp:204-208.

Line-by-line chain on origin/main:
1. ComboElement::Update (comboelement.cpp:166-172) builds the ComboDialog with parent = *dialog, the dialog that owns the combo, and stores `_openDialog = made2`. The ComboDialog ctor (combodialog_ctor.cpp:400-420) links it into parentDlg->_children.
2. Code calls CloseDialog(parent) while the drop-down is open. Block A (userinterface_close.cpp:261) loops `while (dlg->_children._count > 0)` and runs CloseDialog on the ComboDialog first. That runs OnClosed (the inherited 0x180115330, controllers only), UnlinkFromParent and PushRemovedUnlessPresent, so _removedDialogs[0] = the ComboDialog. The parent is then pushed as [1].
3. _openDialog is never cleared on this route. It is cleared only at combodialog.cpp:206/232 (OnUpdate / OnElementEvent), combodescription.cpp:191 and widgets_input.cpp:617.
4. CleanRemovedDialogs (userinterface.cpp:1002) runs `delete dlg` on i=0, which frees the ComboDialog (flags |= 2, so bit 5 is clear). On i=1 it deletes the parent. Its ReleaseFields (dialog.cpp:~820) runs `delete _root`, the element-tree teardown reaches ~ComboElement, and that reads `open->_ui` at +0x10 of the freed ComboDialog. CloseDialog then reads the freed `dlg->_children._count` (+0x48) in Block A. That is a heap use-after-free read.

On the retail arena, Block C/D then find nothing (slot [0] was nulled and the dialog was unlinked from _dialogs), so it goes unnoticed. The behaviour is still UB.
verdict.minimal_fix: Under the campaign ruling (every UB gets a minimal fix with a NOT RETAIL: comment), clear the back-pointer when the drop-down is destroyed. In src/engine/ui/combodialog.cpp, change `ComboDialog::~ComboDialog() {}` to `ComboDialog::~ComboDialog() { // NOT RETAIL: retail 0x180111cd0 leaves _combo->_openDialog dangling when the parent's CloseDialog closes the drop-down; ~ComboElement then reads the freed dialog. if (_combo != nullptr && _combo->_openDialog == this) _combo->_openDialog = nullptr; }`, written on separate lines. The fix assumes _combo still points at a live ComboElement at that point. That holds: the parent's root (and so the combo) is deleted after the ComboDialog, at index [1] after [0]. Also add an entry to docs/retail_bugs.md. Verify with a unit test or an ASan run that closes a combo-hosting dialog while its drop-down is open.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: UB (use-after-free read) plus count drift. Latent: the stock game never inserts a duplicate Profession*.
verdict.proof:
Checked on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>/src/game/Dialog/professionui.cpp:384-430). No merged PR touches it. The code is unchanged.

Port, non-empty-root arm:
- `MemAlloc(0x30, 8)` runs before the walk.
- On an equal key it calls `MemFree(newNode); inserted = true;`.
- It then runs `if (newNode->parent != nullptr)` (line 424), which reads the freed block. That is a UAF read.
- It finishes with `professionIndexCount = professionIndexCount + 1;` (line 430), which runs on the duplicate path too.

Retail Application-x64.exe 0x140076ca0, from Ghidra disassembly in this session:
- The walk runs before any allocation: `140077070 MOV RAX,[RDI]; 140077073 CMP RBX,RAX; JC 0x140077094` (less goes to the child at +0x18), then `140077078 CMP RAX,RBX; 14007707b JNC 0x140077131` (equal).
- The allocation `CALL [0x140152b60]` happens only at a null child (0x1400770af and 0x1400770ec). Those arms store the child and fall into `14007711f LEA RDX,[RSP+0x38]; LEA RCX,[R14+0x60]; 140077128 CALL 0x140013480` (rebalance), then `14007712d INC dword ptr [R14+0x68]` (count).
- The empty-root arm also ends with `JMP 0x14007712d`, so it counts and skips the rebalance.
- The duplicate target 0x140077131 is `LEA R8,[RBX+0x30]`, the SetText setup. It comes after both the rebalance and the INC, so retail neither allocates, rebalances nor counts on a duplicate.

The port differs from retail in two ways: allocate-then-free order, and the count is bumped on a duplicate. The UAF read is a direct consequence of the port's order, line by line.

Reachability: only a duplicate Profession* in the profession list hits this. ProfessionList::Startup produces distinct entries, so it is latent, which the finding already states.

A second drift was noticed but not part of S-036. Retail passes &[RSP+0x38] to the rebalance, which holds RDI, the parent node walked to. The port passes &nodePtr = newNode. This is worth a separate check against BSTRebalance_Impl's expectation.
verdict.minimal_fix:
Restructure the professionui.cpp non-empty-root insert to follow retail's order:
1. Walk the tree first.
2. On an equal key, break out with no allocation, no rebalance and no professionIndexCount increment.
3. Allocate and link only at a null child, then rebalance and increment.

Move `professionIndexCount + 1` into the insert and root arms only, so it is skipped on a duplicate.

The smallest alternative keeps the current order: on the duplicate arm, free the node, set a `duplicate` flag, skip the `newNode->parent` test and skip the increment.

Separately, verify the rebalance argument (parent vs new node) against retail's `LEA RDX,[RSP+0x38]`.

verdict.label: retail
verdict.severity: UB (save-reachable signed int64 overflow; low practical impact)
verdict.proof:
Still present on origin/main fa150cf7f. None of the merged review PRs touches it: #134 and #135, the EntityList ones, fix F-109 and F-131/F-182..186, not S-038. Line-by-line proof from <worktree>/src/game/Entity/entitylist.cpp:
(1) Line 1548: `accumulatedTime.Serialize(serializer);`. System::Time::Serialize (src/engine/system/value_types.cpp:277) is `s.Serialize(_ticks, nullptr);`, a raw int64 read from the save with no bound.
(2) Line 1615: `masterArray._data[entityIdx]->_lastUpdateTime.Serialize(serializer);` is the same raw int64 read per entity, also unbounded.
(3) Line 824 in Update: `accumulatedTime._ticks += time->_ticks;` is a signed int64 add.
(4) Line 889: `int64_t currentTime = accumulatedTime._ticks;`. Line 910: `int64_t delta = currentTime - entIBP->_lastUpdateTime._ticks;` is a signed int64 subtract, followed by `if (delta > 0)`.
A save with accumulatedTime = INT64_MAX - k (k small) and a live entity (bit 10 clear) whose _lastUpdateTime is negative (e.g. -1) makes line 910 overflow on the first Update. That is signed overflow, which is undefined behaviour in C++. Line 824 overflows the same way once accumulatedTime is near INT64_MAX. A grep of CMakeLists.txt and cmake/ finds no -fwrapv or -fno-strict-overflow, so GCC is free to assume no overflow at the `delta > 0` test. Retail 0x1400c4090 does the same subtraction as a wrapping SUB (`local_58[0] = *param_1 - *(longlong*)(ent+0x20); if (0 < local_58[0])`). So the arithmetic is faithful, and the UB comes only from writing it as signed C++.
No sanitizer run or fuzz input was produced. The verdict rests on this static proof: the operands are unconstrained, save-supplied int64 values and the operations are plain signed arithmetic.
verdict.minimal_fix: In src/game/Entity/entitylist.cpp, line 910: `int64_t delta = (int64_t)((uint64_t)currentTime - (uint64_t)entIBP->_lastUpdateTime._ticks);`. Line 824: `accumulatedTime._ticks = (int64_t)((uint64_t)accumulatedTime._ticks + (uint64_t)time->_ticks);`. Each gets a "NOT RETAIL: retail wraps (two's-complement SUB/ADD); unsigned arithmetic keeps the wrap without signed-overflow UB" comment. Both keep retail's results bit-for-bit and do not change the save format.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: none (UB claim refuted); residual non-UB nit: address-equality cache, unproven
verdict.proof:
Re-read on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>); the code is unchanged (window_android.cpp:113-149, device.cpp:545 call at the end of CreateSwapchain, reached from BeginCommands:1417 on the render thread under render_pipe).

(1) The claim that SDL_GetWindowProperties off the main thread is a data race is wrong for the vendored SDL. third_party/SDL/src/video/SDL_video.c:2915-2923: the function checks the window magic, then returns window->props, creating it only if it is 0. On Android, window->props is created on the main thread in Android_CreateWindow (SDL_androidwindow.c:78 sets SDL_PROP_WINDOW_ANDROID_WINDOW_POINTER on it). That happens before the device and the render thread exist. After that the call is a plain read of fields that never change. SDL_GetPointerProperty takes properties->lock (SDL_properties.c, SDL_LockMutex). The Java thread's clear (SDL_android.c:1338, SDL_SetPointerProperty) takes the same lock, so the property read and that write are serialised. The "main thread only" note in the header is an API contract, not UB in this build.

(2) The use-after-release claim does not hold on the reachable path. CreateSwapchain runs only while `surface` is live. `surface` is made in the same BeginCommands (device.cpp:1405, SDL_Vulkan_CreateSurface on data->native_window), or earlier, and only LifecycleWatch destroys it. Android's libvulkan CreateAndroidSurfaceKHR keeps a strong reference (sp<ANativeWindow>) to the window the surface was made from. So when the Java thread's ANativeWindow_release (SDL_android.c:1339) drops SDL's reference, the window the property names is still held by the VkSurface and is not freed. Rotation and resize do not replace the ANativeWindow: surfaceChanged keeps the same Surface. The only way to get a different, unreferenced pointer is two full surface destroy/create cycles on the Java thread inside one CreateSwapchain call, and each cycle needs WILL_ENTER_BACKGROUND, which the main thread handles through LifecycleWatch. That is not a reachable sequence, and in any case it would be dwarfed by the existing surface teardown and rebuild handshake.

Residual (not UB, not proven): the `native == g_frameRateWindow` short-circuit at line 130 compares raw addresses. If a new ANativeWindow after a trip to the background were allocated at the freed one's address, the preferred rate would not be applied to it again. Whether that happens depends on the allocator and needs a device run. It is at most a P12 pacing nit, not the UB filed here.
verdict.minimal_fix: None for the UB. Optional hardening for the residual: clear g_frameRateWindow (set it to nullptr under g_frameRateLock) on SDL_EVENT_WILL_ENTER_BACKGROUND, or drop the address cache, so the next native window is always told the rate.

The fields are uint32_t or enum (RenderState.h:147-149, 217, 314-315). Nothing checks their range. When reading, Serialize calls PlatformCreate() right away and always returns true ("there is no failure path").
(2) Where they are used: RenderStateData::Create (src/render/dx11/renderstatedata.cpp:345-410) uses each field directly as an index into the fixed static tables kBlendFactor[10] (line 159), kBlendOp[3] (174), kCompareFunc[8] (182), kStencilOp[8] (197), kCullMode[3] (212) and kFillMode[2] (220). There is no clamp between (1) and (2). For example, a RenderState resource with blendOp=3 reads kBlendOp[3], and one with _fillMode=2 reads kFillMode[2]. Both are past the end of the array, which is UB.
(3) Retail: the port's own comments give the retail addresses for each load (0x180003914 / 0x18000392a / 0x1800037d3 / 0x180003801 / 0x180003977). The finding's label_evidence quotes those as movslq plus a scaled load into stack tables, with no compare before them. So retail has the same unchecked index, and this is a retail bug the port reproduces faithfully, not port drift.
Not a duplicate. F-068 (imagebufferdata.cpp:375, the sampler address and filter tables) is the same kind of bug in a different function with different fields. No other S-* or F-* entry covers renderstatedata.cpp; the only other renderstate match is about Metal pipeline-cache eviction, which is unrelated.
The campaign rule says a UB gets a minimal fix with a NOT RETAIL comment.
verdict.minimal_fix: In RenderStateData::Create (src/render/dx11/renderstatedata.cpp), check each index against the size of its table before the lookup. One helper is enough, e.g. `template<size_t N> static unsigned Clamp(uint32_t v, unsigned def) { return v < N ? v : def; }`. Out-of-range values fall back to the RenderState constructor defaults: srcBlend 1, dstBlend 0, blendOp 0, depth func 4, stencil func and ops per the constructor, cullMode 1, fillMode 0. Mark it with a `// NOT RETAIL: retail 0x1800037c0.. indexes these tables unchecked; a corrupt/mod .rsc value reads past the table (UB)` comment. In-range values are unchanged, so faithful behaviour stays byte-identical. A unit test that feeds an out-of-range RenderState (or the table lookup helper) would also move this to sanitizer-proven. The Vulkan and Metal backends should be checked for the same table lookups, which would mean separate findings.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (logic bug, not UB: the UB/race half is closed by F-158)
verdict.proof:
Re-read on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>). The finding has two shapes.

Shape 2, the render_pipe data race: REFUTED as stated. It is the F-158 shape, and F-158 is fixed on main. Every writer of Device::settingsChanged runs on the main thread inside the fixed-step loop:
- SizeWindow and OnWindowEvent run from Platform::Pump at mainloop_frame.cpp ~400, inside `while (_accumulator >= _deltaTime._ticks)`. SDL event watches fire during SDL_PumpEvents.
- Options Apply (ApplyChangedSettings, optionsdialog.cpp:1007-1012) and the registry toggles (registry_boot.cpp:311/326, render_scale_entry.cpp:94, video_rows.cpp:45) are UI input handlers that run in a step.
On a frame that steps, the kExtBeforeSteps fence (mainloop_frame.cpp:363-364 -> pipe_driver.h BeforeSteps) either joins the pending emit or calls Handoff::ClaimSteps. Since F-158, ClaimSteps waits until the job's BeginCommands has returned (NoteBegun; handoff.h comment "Review F-158 ... no step runs before it returned"). On a frame that does not step, no pump and no UI step runs. So no write can land between the read at backend.mm:1160 and the clear at backend.mm:1178. The cross-thread UB half of S-044 is therefore a duplicate of F-158 and is already fixed.

Shape 1, minimised (single-threaded): the defect is real in the code, but it has not been shown to happen.
- ApplyEngineSettingsChange (backend.mm:1118-1120) returns at once when SDL_WINDOW_MINIMIZED is set.
- BeginCommands then reads SDL_GetWindowSizeInPixels. On Cocoa this stays > 0 for a miniaturised window: SDL3's Cocoa GetWindowSizeInPixels uses the content view's backing bounds.
- So the code reaches the unconditional `dev->settingsChanged = 0;` at 1178 without rebuilding anything. A pending request is dropped.
- For a resize, SizeWindow has already moved backBufferWidth/Height while mainColor/mainDepth keep the old size, and nothing raises the flag again after restore, because the pixel size does not change on deminiaturise.
- By contrast, the w<=0 early return keeps the flag, and the Vulkan backend clears it only in the branch that applied it.

Reachability is narrow. While the window is minimised it has no focus and receives no clicks, so the Options Apply, ext-row and fullscreen-chord triggers cannot fire then. What remains:
(a) SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_DISPLAY_SCALE_CHANGED delivered to a minimised window, for example when a display is unplugged or its scale changes.
(b) A resize event and a minimise event drained in the same pump, so that frame's tail draws minimised.
Whether macOS delivers (a) to a miniaturised window, and whether the result is the black-frame / viewport-past-attachment failure described, needs a macOS Metal run. No such run exists, and none is possible from this Windows bed. The proof standard (failing test, sanitizer or Ghidra diff) is not met. There is no retail counterpart: src/render/metal is macOS-only.
verdict.minimal_fix: In ContextData::BeginCommands (src/render/metal/backend.mm), make ApplyEngineSettingsChange return bool: false on the minimised / null-window early return and when mainColor is nil, true after the rebuild. Clear dev->settingsChanged only when it returns true, inside the `if (dev->settingsChanged)` branch under dev->Lock(). Delete the unconditional `dev->settingsChanged = 0;` at line 1178. This is the same as the Vulkan backend's consume-where-applied pattern. No atomic is needed, since F-158's ClaimSteps already orders every writer against BeginCommands. Verify on macOS with a drag-resize, then minimise in the same frame, then restore.

proof_run.proof:
S-044 stays SUSPECTED. The code reasoning is now tighter, but no failure has been seen in the real backend. Two things block that here. src/render/metal/backend.mm is Objective-C++ built against Metal and QuartzCore, so it cannot be compiled or unit-tested on Windows or WSL. And there is no macOS Metal run available.

Shape 2 (the render_pipe data race) is not re-tested. Triage already ruled it a duplicate of F-158, which is fixed on main (ClaimSteps waits on BeginCommands).

Shape 1 (minimised, single-threaded):

1. SDL source, checked on origin/main fa150cf7f. This closes the "pixel size stays > 0 while minimised" premise that triage left open.
   - Cocoa_GetWindowSizeInPixels (third_party/SDL/src/video/cocoa/SDL_cocoawindow.m:2734-2741) returns windata.viewport.size.
   - viewport is written only at :1246 (resize) and :2302 (backing change).
   - windowDidMiniaturize (:1291-1300) only sends SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_MINIMIZED and leaves viewport alone.
   - So a minimised window reports its old non-zero pixel size. BeginCommands passes the w<=0 check at backend.mm:1169 and reaches the unconditional `dev->settingsChanged = 0;` at :1178. ApplyEngineSettingsChange had already returned early at :1120 on SDL_WINDOW_MINIMIZED, so nothing was rebuilt.
   - Deminiaturise sends no pixel-size event, so nothing raises the flag again.

2. Model test. I copied the flag control flow of backend.mm:1118-1178 line for line, plus SizeWindow (device_window.cpp:76) and OnWindowEvent (backend.mm:894), against a fake window that behaves like SDL Cocoa. Built with WinLibs g++ 16.2 -std=c++20 -Wall. It exits 1 with:
   [S-044 b] after restore: flag=0 backBuffer=1600x900 attachment=1280x720 -> FAIL (request lost)
   [S-044 a] after restore: flag=0 window=2560x1440 px attachment=1280x720 -> FAIL (request lost)
   - Case b: a resize and a minimise in the same pump.
   - Case a: DISPLAY_SCALE_CHANGED while minimised.
   - In both, the flag is cleared without a rebuild and stays at 0 after restore. The attachment keeps the old size while the back buffer and window have moved on.

What is still unproven:
- The model checks the transcribed logic, not the shipped file.
- It is not known whether macOS actually delivers either event order to a miniaturised window.
- The visible symptom (black frames, viewport larger than the attachment) has not been seen.

To confirm, run on macOS Metal: drag-resize, minimise in the same frame, restore. Then check for the `[Metal] back buffer rebuilt` line and look for a black window. Or unplug or rescale a display while the window is minimised.

No change was made in the worktree.
proof_run.minimal_fix:
In src/render/metal/backend.mm, make ApplyEngineSettingsChange return bool:
- false on the null-window / SDL_WINDOW_MINIMIZED early return (:1120) and when mainColor is nil;
- true after RebuildMainTargets.

In ContextData::BeginCommands, inside `if (dev->settingsChanged)` under dev->Lock(), clear the flag only when the call returns true. Delete the unconditional `dev->settingsChanged = 0;` at :1178. This is the same consume-where-applied pattern the Vulkan backend uses. No atomic is needed, because F-158's ClaimSteps already orders every writer against BeginCommands. With this fix, the model test above passes both cases: the flag survives the minimised frame and the rebuild runs on the first frame after restore.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (spec-level lifetime hazard; no observed failure, typical drivers tolerate it)
verdict.proof: The code on origin/main fa150cf7f matches the finding. No merged PR touches it (gh pr list --state merged with "semaphore"/"review" turns up nothing relevant). Line numbers have moved slightly. In src/render/vulkan/device.cpp, renderFinished is one semaphore per swap-chain image (:113). Each frame it is the signal of the frame submit and the only wait semaphore of vkQueuePresentKHR (:1534-1539). A present that returns OUT_OF_DATE, SUBOPTIMAL or SURFACE_LOST sets swapchainDirty (:1544-1545), and so does an acquire that returns SUBOPTIMAL (:1443-1444). The next BeginCommands then runs vkDeviceWaitIdle (:1415) and CreateSwapchain. CreateSwapchain calls DestroySwapchainObjects (:502), which runs vkDestroySemaphore on every renderFinished (:374) before the old swapchain is destroyed. The background lifecycle path does the same: vkDeviceWaitIdle, then DestroySwapchainObjects (:181-182). The extension is not used anywhere: grep finds no swapchain_maintenance1 in src/render/vulkan, so no present fence proves the present engine has finished waiting. Whether vkDeviceWaitIdle covers present-semaphore waits is exactly the grey area that the Khronos swapchain-semaphore-reuse guidance flags, so the hazard is real at spec level. It is still not proven. There is no failing test, no validation-layer report and no observed crash, and the reading rests on an interpretation of the spec, not on a line-by-line contradiction. A Vulkan validation-layer run (with sync validation) that resizes the window or forces OUT_OF_DATE, then shows VUID-vkDestroySemaphore-semaphore-05149 (or 01137) at :374, would confirm it. Retail has no Vulkan backend, so this is not port drift.
verdict.minimal_fix: Do not destroy renderFinished in DestroySwapchainObjects on a rebuild. Keep the per-image semaphores across swapchains: grow the vector when the new image count is larger, and destroy only at device shutdown. The other option is to retire each old semaphore until its image index has been acquired again, or until a VK_EXT_swapchain_maintenance1 present fence has signalled where that extension is available. Add a "NOT RETAIL:" comment is not needed (Vulkan backend has no retail counterpart); a short comment citing the present-semaphore lifetime suffices.

proof_run.proof:
S-045 is refuted. The check the triage named, a Vulkan validation run that should show VUID-vkDestroySemaphore-semaphore-05149 or 01137 at device.cpp:374, does not fire on the shipped code, and a positive control shows the layer would catch the real hazard.

Setup: origin/main fa150cf7f, Windows Vulkan debug build (GCC 16.2). In _DEBUG the backend loads VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation; the run used Vulkan SDK 1.4.363 with VK_KHRONOS_VALIDATION_VALIDATE_SYNC=true. The GPU was an RTX 5080. A local-only harness (harness.diff, not committed) sets swapchainDirty = true every 120 presents. That drives the exact path in the finding: present to renderFinished[i], then the next BeginCommands runs vkDeviceWaitIdle, then CreateSwapchain, DestroySwapchainObjects and vkDestroySemaphore on every renderFinished. The runs used AUTOSTART, AUTOQUIT=2400 and /profile:faithful on the functional dir Banished-B.

Run 1 (shipped order, wait idle kept): 56 swap-chain builds plus the shutdown teardown. There were 0 validation ERRORs and no VUID-vkDestroySemaphore-* message. The only messages were the unrelated "SV_Target written with no colour attachment" warnings. Exit 0.

Run 2 (positive control, harness_with_control.diff): the first forced rebuild skips vkDeviceWaitIdle and the other 55 keep it. The layer reports the hazard at once:
"[Vulkan] validation ERROR: vkDestroySemaphore(): can't be called on VkSemaphore 0x100000000010 that is currently in use by VkQueue ... VUID-vkDestroySemaphore-semaphore-05149"
It reports this twice, for two in-flight renderFinished semaphores, plus VUID-vkDestroySwapchainKHR-swapchain-01282. There are no other errors.

Conclusion: the layer does track the present waits on renderFinished. It counts them as finished after vkDeviceWaitIdle, which the spec defines as vkQueueWaitIdle on every queue, and that covers queue operations including the present's semaphore wait. The background path (:181-182) and the shutdown path (:1221 then :1237) use the same order: wait idle, then destroy. The finding's spec-level reading is not backed by the tool its own triage named, so no failure was observed. A VK_EXT_swapchain_maintenance1 present fence would only be a belt-and-braces measure, not a fix for an observed defect.
proof_run.minimal_fix: None needed. On every path the shipped code runs vkDeviceWaitIdle before DestroySwapchainObjects, and the validation layer treats that as retiring the present-semaphore waits. A short comment at DestroySwapchainObjects saying that callers must wait idle first is optional.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (Vulkan valid-usage violation). Only reached after a vkCreateSwapchainKHR failure on a rebuild, then on every retry. Low frequency; no retail counterpart, since the Vulkan backend is port-only.
verdict.proof:
Checked line by line against origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>/src/render/vulkan/device.cpp). No merged PR touches it: `gh pr list --search swapchain` shows only the open docs PR #159.

1. In CreateSwapchain (L494-500), `ci.oldSwapchain = swapchain;` is followed by `r = vkCreateSwapchainKHR(device, &ci, nullptr, &created);`. If `r != VK_SUCCESS`, the function sets *why and returns false. The global `swapchain` still holds the old handle. DestroySwapchainObjects and vkDestroySwapchainKHR(swapchain) only run on the success path (L502-504).
2. The Vulkan spec for vkCreateSwapchainKHR says: "Upon calling vkCreateSwapchainKHR with an oldSwapchain that is not VK_NULL_HANDLE, oldSwapchain is retired -- even if creation of the new swapchain fails." So after a failed call, `swapchain` holds a retired handle.
3. Both rebuild callers retry and keep that handle:
   - ApplyEngineSettingsChange (L592-595) sets `swapchainDirty = true` on failure.
   - BeginCommands (L1414-1425) calls CreateSwapchain again on the next frame. On failure it returns false with swapchainDirty still set ("retried every frame"). The one exception is a DEVICE_LOST failure with fix.boot_device_lost on, which goes to BeginLostFrame.
4. The retry runs L494 again with `ci.oldSwapchain = swapchain`, which is the retired handle. That breaks VUID-VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR-oldSwapchain-01933 ("If oldSwapchain is not VK_NULL_HANDLE, oldSwapchain must be a non-retired swapchain"). Breaking a valid-usage rule is undefined behaviour. With the row off or the faithful profile, the same violation repeats on every frame while the failure lasts.
5. The early returns in CreateSwapchain before L494 (relative lines 20 and 75 of the 365-440 window) return before vkCreateSwapchainKHR is called, so they do not retire anything. Only the post-call failure path is affected.
6. The other teardown paths (LifecycleWatch L181-184 and device shutdown L1237-1239) null `swapchain` after destroying it, which shows the intended invariant. The failure path is the only one that breaks it.

No other S-*/F-* in findings_p8 covers this.
verdict.minimal_fix:
In CreateSwapchain, on `r != VK_SUCCESS` and only when `ci.oldSwapchain != VK_NULL_HANDLE`:
1. Call DestroySwapchainObjects().
2. Call vkDestroySwapchainKHR(device, swapchain, nullptr). The callers have already waited for idle.
3. Set `swapchain = VK_NULL_HANDLE`.
4. Then return false.

Add a "NOT RETAIL:" style comment citing that the spec retires oldSwapchain even on failure (VUID-01933). The next retry then creates from VK_NULL_HANDLE, and nothing can acquire or present on the retired chain, because swapchainDirty stays set and BeginCommands rebuilds before it acquires.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: UB (latent; Vulkan backend only, not observed in play)
verdict.proof:
Not fixed on origin/main fa150cf7f: no merged review PR (#113, #114, #117, #122, #149, #150 and others) changes this. The code claim holds line by line. src/render/vulkan/draw.cpp:1446-1453: `VkBuffer buffer = ib ? ib->store.Buffer() : VK_NULL_HANDLE; if (!buffer) buffer = ZeroBuffer().buffer;` then `vkCmdBindIndexBuffer(cb, buffer, 0, VK_INDEX_TYPE_UINT16); vkCmdDrawIndexed(cb, count, instances, first, baseVertex, 0);`, with no check of first+count against the buffer size. ZeroBuffer is kZeroBufferBytes = 64ull << 10 (resources.cpp:26, 391), which holds 32768 uint16 indices. device.cpp:1141-1153 builds want2.features field by field and never sets robustBufferAccess, so an index fetch past the bound range is undefined in Vulkan, while D3D11 defines it as 0.

The fallback is reached by more than a null IB. BufferStore::Buffer() (VideoVulkanData.h:134) returns VK_NULL_HANDLE for a dynamic buffer that has never been written (current == -1), and also for a static buffer whose Create failed, for example on device memory exhaustion. In those cases the draw keeps its real index count, so a large mesh would read past 32768. CreateOnDemand's DrawScope::Touch makes a lazy buffer synchronously before the draw (lazy_create.h:119-123), so ext.create_on_demand does not open this path.

What is missing is a trigger. The finding names no engine call that issues DrawIndexed with first+count > 32768 while the IB is null, unwritten or failed. The P6 GPU-AV run and the DX11 debug layer saw no such draw, and no test, fuzz input or validation report exists. Under the campaign standard this stays unproven: it needs a build proof, for example a unit or validation-layer test that binds a null or unwritten dynamic IB and draws 40000 indices under GPU-AV.
verdict.minimal_fix: In IssueDraw (draw.cpp:1447), when the zero buffer stands in for the index buffer and first + count > kZeroBufferBytes / 2, count the draw as failed (++g_frame.failedDraws; return) with a NOT RETAIL comment. ZeroBuffer's byte size needs exposing in resources.h for this. A more general option is to enable robustBufferAccess when have2.features.robustBufferAccess is set, which also covers vertex streams read past the end of the zero buffer (draw.cpp:1217).

proof_run.minimal_fix: In IssueDraw (src/render/vulkan/draw.cpp:1447), when the zero buffer stands in for the index buffer and uint64_t(first) + count > ZeroBufferBytes() / 2, do ++g_frame.failedDraws and return, with a "NOT RETAIL:" comment saying that D3D11 reads 0 past a null or short IB while Vulkan without robustBufferAccess is UB. This needs kZeroBufferBytes (resources.cpp:26) exposed in resources.h, for example as a ZeroBufferBytes() accessor beside ZeroBuffer(). The repro's case 6 shows this guard clears the VUID. A broader alternative is to set want2.features.robustBufferAccess = have2.features.robustBufferAccess in device.cpp, which also covers vertex streams read past the zero buffer (draw.cpp:1217) but costs performance on some drivers. Separately, consider plain hardening so that SerializeBuffer handles CreateBuffer's false result, though retail ignores the result as well.

verdict.severity: logic (the rain/snow ambient sound is missing; nothing crashes)
verdict.proof:
The Ghidra diff against origin/main fa150cf7f shows the port has dropped the audio arms. No merged PR touches this code: the "audio is out of scope" comments are still on main. No other F-* or S-* row covers it, so it is not a duplicate.

1. Retail WeatherSimulation_SetEffectEnabled 0x1400942c0, enable arm. After AddGlobalObject and `*(param_1+2)=0`, retail continues:
`if (*(*(*param_1+0x28) + 8 + slot*0x10) != 0) { local_30 = MemAlloc(0x48,8); ptr = ComponentEntity_CopyCtor(local_30, template); InternalBasePtr_Ctor(&local_38, ptr); *(param_1[0xc] + slot*8) = local_38; EntityList_RegisterEntity(*(gw+0xe8), &local_30, *(template+0x20)); ComponentEntity_FindComponent_AmbientEmitterComponent(...,&local_res20); AmbientEmitterComponent_MoveTo(local_res20, {0,0,0}); puVar2 = *(local_res20+0x38); if (*puVar2==0) puVar2[1]=0; else if (puVar2[1]!=0.0) { puVar2[1]=0; Audio::Scene::SetEmitterVolume(*(gw+0x78), *puVar2, local_res20+0x28, 0.0); } }`
The port's src/game/Game/weather_particles.cpp:363-365 ends at `field_0x10 = 0;` with "NOTE: the audio ambient entity (entry+8 template) is intentionally not spawned here — audio is out of scope". The whole template branch is missing.

2. Retail WeatherSimulation_Update 0x1400944e0, per-effect loop. After the geometry's Update, retail checks `if (*(param_1[0xc]+i*8) != 0)`. When it is set, it finds the AmbientEmitterComponent and sets the emitter volume to geometry+0xC0 (store into puVar4[1], then SetEmitterVolume if the volume changed). In the removal arm, after RemoveGlobalObject and the delete, retail does: `if (emitters[i]) { if (!(entity+0x40 >>10 &1)) { ComponentEntity_MarkForRemoval(e); DynArray8_ResizeFill(entityList+0xd0, size+1, &e); } emitters[i] = IBP(null); }`
The port's src/game/Game/weather_sim.cpp:250-275 has neither arm, only the comment "(audio IBP slot +0x60[i] stays null — no audio spawned)".

Effect: whenever a weather effect is on (rain in state 0 when the temperature is above 34, and the same on load through Serialize -> SetEffectEnabled), retail spawns the WeatherChoice's audio-template entity, which for Rain is Audio/Effects/RainEffect.rsc:ambient. Its volume follows the effect intensity, and it is retired when the effect fades. The port never creates that entity, so there is no weather ambient sound. Fixing this changes entity registration (the EntityList id/order) during rain, so the resave and sim bytes move toward retail.
verdict.minimal_fix:
Two changes, both mirroring retail.

1. In WeatherSimulation::SetEffectEnabled's enable arm (weather_particles.cpp), after `field_0x10 = 0`, add the retail template branch. When `arrayBase[slot]`'s audio template (+8) is non-null:
   - MemAlloc(0x48,8) and run the ComponentEntity copy ctor from the template.
   - Store the IBP into emitters[slot] (+0x60).
   - Call EntityList::RegisterEntity(gw+0xe8, ibp, template+0x20).
   - Call FindComponent<AmbientEmitterComponent> and MoveTo({0,0,0}).
   - Set the volume to 0 with the retail store/SetEmitterVolume pattern.

2. In WeatherSimulation::Update's per-effect loop (weather_sim.cpp):
   - When emitters[i] is set, set the emitter volume to geometry+0xC0 the same way.
   - In the removal arm, after the delete: if emitters[i] is set and its entity+0x40 bit 10 is clear, MarkForRemoval it and append it to entityList+0xd0. Then null emitters[i].

Title the commit `behaviour:`. Run the gate and the resave check, because entity registration changes during rain.

verdict.severity: logic (low): ext-only (ext.family_tree / ext.sharp_ui), hosts without Segoe UI installed (Wine, stripped Windows); not reachable on a stock Windows install
verdict.proof:
Line-by-line proof on origin/main fa150cf7f, src/platform/win/font_raster_win.cpp. No merged PR touches it (gh pr list on merged "font_raster": only #5 macOS).
1. Lines 35-36: `bool g_privateTried = false; bool g_privateLoaded = false;` are single file-scope globals with no face key.
2. Lines 75-77: `LoadPrivateFace(const wchar_t* face, ...)` begins `if (g_privateTried) return g_privateLoaded; g_privateTried = true;`. Only after that does it build `<exe dir>/<face>.ttf` (lines 84-85), so the path depends on the face but the cache does not.
3. Line 92: `g_privateLoaded = AddFontResourceExW(path, FR_PRIVATE, nullptr) > 0;` is reached only for the first face ever tried. The early returns on lines 81/83/87 (no such file) leave g_privateTried = true and g_privateLoaded = false.
4. AcquireFace (lines 96-106) calls LoadPrivateFace(face) whenever SelectFace on the installed face fails. FaceAvailable (line 116) and RasterizeFont (line 151) both go through AcquireFace.
5. Windows DefaultFaces (lines 110-114) = {"Segoe UI", "Arial", kGameFace="FrancophilSans"}, and family_raster.cpp:82-88 SystemGlyphSource::Glyphs tries them in that order. On a host without Segoe UI, LoadPrivateFace(L"Segoe UI") finds no "Segoe UI.ttf" beside the exe and returns false with tried=true. If Arial is also missing, it returns the cached false without looking for Arial.ttf. FrancophilSans then also returns the cached false, although tools/release/package.sh ships FrancophilSans.ttf beside the exe (tools/release/fonts/FrancophilSans.ttf). Result: the family tree gets no font. Any later FaceAvailable(kGameFace) from font_provider.cpp:91 (FaceOk, called once per process and cached in c.faceChecked) also returns false, so ext.sharp_ui logs "font variants off" and turns itself off for the session. This needs only Segoe UI to be missing and the family tree to rasterise before sharp_ui's first FaceOk.
6. In the reverse order, once FrancophilSans has loaded, a later missing face gets the cached true. AcquireFace then reports the misleading "private Segoe UI.ttf loaded but GDI selected ..." (line 102). It still returns null, so this half only affects the diagnostic text.
7. The contract in font_raster.h:68-70 says "the private load is remembered for the process" for `face`, and line 74 says other platforms look up face files "each face once per process". The intent is per face; the Windows cache is per process.
No runtime repro: stock Windows has Segoe UI, so the path needs Wine or a GDI mock. The defect is in the control flow and does not depend on the environment. This is the ext rasteriser (file banner "NOT RETAIL"), so there is no retail comparison.
verdict.minimal_fix: In font_raster_win.cpp, replace the two globals with a per-face cache guarded by the existing g_lock, e.g. `std::map<std::wstring, bool> g_privateFaces;`. LoadPrivateFace then does: `auto it = g_privateFaces.find(face); if (it != g_privateFaces.end()) return it->second;`, runs the existing file and AddFontResourceExW logic, and stores the result in `g_privateFaces[face]` on every exit path (including the not-found returns). No faithful code is touched and ext-off behaviour is unchanged. A unit test can cover it if LoadPrivateFace takes a directory argument (or an injected exe-dir), so that a missing face followed by a present face both resolve.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: low (logic; ext.sharp_ui / ext.family_tree only; reachable only where a DefaultFaces entry ahead of kGameFace is not installed, e.g. Wine/Proton or a stripped image; no faithful-path impact, NOT RETAIL file)
verdict.proof:
The bug is still present on origin/main fa150cf7f, in <worktree>/src/platform/win/font_raster_win.cpp. No merged PR touches LoadPrivateFace. PR #149 "face cache" is F-171-era work in font_provider and does not change this latch.

Line-by-line proof:
1. Lines 35-36 are the two process-wide globals `bool g_privateTried = false; bool g_privateLoaded = false;`. Neither is keyed by face.
2. LoadPrivateFace(face, why), lines 82-84, does `if (g_privateTried) return g_privateLoaded; g_privateTried = true;`. Only after that does it build `<exe dir>\<face>.ttf` from the `face` argument. So the first call, whatever its face, decides the answer for every later face.
3. AcquireFace (lines 101-111) calls LoadPrivateFace(face) only after SelectFace(face) fails, which means the face is not installed.
4. Windows DefaultFaces (line 111) is {"Segoe UI", "Arial", kGameFace}. SystemGlyphSource::Glyphs (src/ext/family_tree/family_raster.cpp:82-87) calls RasterizeFont, and so AcquireFace, for each of these faces in that order.
5. Failing case: Segoe UI is not installed (Wine/Proton) and the family-tree raster runs first. LoadPrivateFace("Segoe UI") sets g_privateTried=true, does not find "Segoe UI.ttf" and returns false, leaving g_privateLoaded=false. Later, FaceOk() (src/ext/resources/font_provider.cpp:91) calls FaceAvailable(kGameFace). In AcquireFace, SelectFace("FrancophilSans") fails because the face is not installed. LoadPrivateFace("FrancophilSans") then returns the cached false without ever probing FrancophilSans.ttf, which the release package ships beside the exe. FaceOk caches faceOk=false for the session, so ext.sharp_ui's variants stay off. The same thing happens inside Glyphs itself: the kGameFace fallback, third in the list, is never loaded privately.
6. Reverse case: FrancophilSans.ttf loads first (g_privateLoaded=true). A later missing face then gets `true` back. The re-select fails, and the reason reads "private Segoe UI.ttf loaded but GDI selected ...", which is wrong.

The header contract (font_raster.h:68-74) promises a private load per face: "the private load is remembered for the process" and "each face once per process". The code latches once per process for all faces. This is not a faithful-code question: the file banner says NOT RETAIL, so no Ghidra check is needed. On stock Win10/11 Segoe UI and Arial are installed, so SelectFace succeeds and LoadPrivateFace is reached only for kGameFace. That is why this only bites on hosts that lack those faces.
verdict.minimal_fix: Key the latch by face, under the g_lock that is already held. Replace the two bools with `std::map<std::wstring, bool> g_privateTried;`. In LoadPrivateFace: `auto it = g_privateTried.find(face); if (it != g_privateTried.end()) return it->second;` and record `g_privateTried[face] = result` on every return path, including the missing-file and exe-path-failure paths. Alternatively, keep the bools and latch only when `_wcsicmp(face, L"FrancophilSans") == 0` (kGameFace); for any other face, return false without touching the latch, since only kGameFace's .ttf ships. A unit test (tests/unit, Windows-only) could call FaceAvailable("NoSuchFace_S051") followed by FaceAvailable(kGameFace), with FrancophilSans.ttf placed beside the test exe, and assert the second call succeeds.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: logic (low-medium): exclusive fullscreen is kept on a minimized window; the on-screen effect is not verified
verdict.proof:
Checked on origin/main fa150cf7f; the code is unchanged and no merged PR touches it (merged PRs searched for "fullscreen"/"review": only #17, the topology-cache fix, is near it).

Retail VideoDX11-x64.dll 0x180004340 (DeviceData::Resize). Its CALL/branch skeleton:
- The only early-out is the window check: `180004371 CALL [0x1800134e0]` (IsWindowVisible) / `TEST EAX,EAX` / `JZ 0x1800044f7`.
- With no further window check, it runs `18000438e CALL [RAX+0x108]` (OMSetRenderTargets), `[RAX+0x378]` (ClearState), the buffer releases and AdjustDisplay (`180004417`).
- Then `180004464 CALL [RAX+0x70]` (ResizeTarget), `180004493 CALL [R10+0x68]` (ResizeBuffers) and `1800044af CALL [RAX+0x50]` (SetFullscreenState(cfg+0x40 != 0, NULL)).
- Retail has no IsIconic call.

Port (src/render/dx11/devicedata.cpp):
- Line 734 checks IsVisible (plus a boot-window exception).
- Lines 741-742 add `if (Platform::Window::IsIconic(dev->windowHandle)) return 0;` before the ClearState / ResizeTarget / ResizeBuffers / SetFullscreenState(line 872) chain. It carries no NOT RETAIL tag; the comment says it was added on purpose to avoid latching a 0x0 size.

DeviceData_OnActivate (lines 917-938) mirrors retail: on WA_INACTIVE it sets wasFullscreen=1 and cfg->fullscreen=0, then relies on Resize to call SetFullscreenState(FALSE). The port does run in exclusive fullscreen: desc->Windowed = cfg->fullscreen==0 at line 468, and the SetFullscreenState call is at line 872. Its WM_ACTIVATE comes from SDL focus events through window_messages.cpp:53 (the pump), so by the time the minimize focus loss is handled the window is already iconic.

Result: the port returns 0 and never leaves exclusive mode. Retail would drop it, because an iconic window still passes IsWindowVisible. That is a Ghidra-proven drift on the fullscreen focus-loss path. Only the user-visible result (mode held, or black screen until restore) is unverified, and it does not affect the drift verdict.

Retail itself, in this case, would run AdjustDisplay's windowed branch and latch the 0x0 client rect. The port's guard exists to prevent that, so the fix must keep the guard and only restore the fullscreen-state transition.
verdict.minimal_fix: In DeviceData_Resize, inside the IsIconic early-out (devicedata.cpp:741), before `return 0`, add: `if (ConfigOf()->fullscreen == 0 && self->swapChain != nullptr) self->swapChain->SetFullscreenState(FALSE, nullptr);`. Tag it as a NOT RETAIL guard that keeps retail's leave-exclusive-mode-on-deactivate step while still refusing to latch the minimized 0x0 size. This way kResetPending stays set and the full rebuild (and SetFullscreenState(TRUE) on reactivate) runs on restore as before. Also tag the IsIconic guard itself as NOT RETAIL.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: logic (GPU data race / torn texture on macOS Metal only; no crash, no sim or save effect)
verdict.proof:
Re-read on origin/main fa150cf7f (<worktree>/src/render/metal/backend.mm). Nothing has changed it, and no merged or open PR touches it: the only open review PRs are #159 (docs) and #160 (diag parse).
1) Update (backend.mm:1675-1691) writes straight into the live texture. After its guards it does only this:
   size_t row = width * (f == 3 || f == 4 ? 1 : 4);
   [texture replaceRegion:MTLRegionMake2D(0, 0, width, height) mipmapLevel:0 withBytes:data bytesPerRow:row];
   It has no completion wait, no rename and no blit encoded on `commands`.
2) The texture is CPU-visible shared memory. Create (backend.mm:1609) sets d.storageMode = MTLStorageModeShared, and Update refuses only `shared` (ext.share_gpu_data) and BC4 textures.
3) Up to three frames can still be reading it. BeginCommands (backend.mm:1180) waits on inFlight, which is created as dispatch_semaphore_create(kFramesInFlight = 3) (lines 101-104 and 916), so up to 3 committed command buffers can be queued or running. The only per-resource completion tracking is bufferUses (lines 137-146, pruned at 1189). It covers MTLBuffers only. No texture use gets a completion ticket, so Update cannot know whether an earlier frame still samples the texture.
4) Metal does not synchronise replaceRegion. It is a CPU write into the texture's storage. The caller must make sure no committed command buffer still accesses that texture (Apple documents this for MTLTexture replaceRegion:). Items 1-3 show this code never does, so this is an unsynchronised CPU write against GPU reads. A frame still executing samples half-written texels. Also, any draw already encoded into the current uncommitted buffer that binds the texture will see the new contents, not the contents at encode time.
5) The DX11 path of the same slot (retail VideoDX11 slot 5, port at src/render/dx11/imagebufferdata.cpp:883-903) is ordered. It uses Map(WRITE_DISCARD) for a dynamic owner, which the driver renames, and UpdateSubresource otherwise, which is queued in the context's command stream. The Vulkan twin records the upload. So the Metal behaviour departs from the reference semantics and is not an inherited retail behaviour.
6) The race is reachable in normal play: GameUpdateLoop::Update re-uploads the minimap overlay whenever overlayDirty is set (gameupdateloop.cpp:1351). Other callers: ext.terrain_edit UploadGroundTexture (brush_tool.cpp:755), noiseui.cpp:218/268 and moddialog.cpp:203.
This is a line-by-line proof of a violated API contract. Nothing was run: the Metal backend builds only on macOS, and torn texels are timing-dependent, so no runtime repro was attempted. Label ext: the Metal backend has no retail counterpart.
verdict.minimal_fix:
Put the write into the command stream, the way DX11 UpdateSubresource does. In ImageBufferData::Update, under DeviceLockScope, copy the rows into the current frame's upload arena (Upload()). Then, if `commands` is live, encode a blit copyFromBuffer:sourceOffset:sourceBytesPerRow:sourceBytesPerImage:sourceSize:toTexture:destinationSlice:0 destinationLevel:0 destinationOrigin:{0,0,0} on `commands`. If it is not, encode the blit on a private command buffer from the same queue and commit it before the frame's buffer, so it runs before later frames. Earlier frames finish reading the old contents first because the queue executes in order.
For a strict fix within the frame, encode the blit before the frame's render pass begins, or close the pass first. Otherwise draws already encoded in the pass would still see the new data, because a blit cannot run inside a render encoder: end the current encoder, blit, then reopen it with load actions that preserve the attachments.
Alternative: give textures completion tickets like bufferUses and rename (fresh texture, re-point the aliases) when the current one is busy. The texture cannot go to MTLStorageModePrivate unless all writes become blits.

verdict.label: port
verdict.severity: logic (low); macOS/Metal only, rendering glitch (wrong blend/layout pipeline), no memory corruption from the cache itself
verdict.proof:
Still present on origin/main fa150cf7f. No merged PR touches it: the only Metal PRs are #6 and #7, and tests/unit/metal_fast_pipeline_cache_test.cpp covers only Evict-after-Insert. The line numbers have moved: RenderStateData dtor/Create evict at backend.mm:2139/2142, Bind stores bound.blend at 2199, Pipeline() inserts at 399.

What the code proves:
(1) backend.cmake:32 builds backend.mm with -fobjc-arc, so `Bindings bound` (backend.mm:84-92: MTLVertexDescriptor* layout, MTLRenderPipelineColorAttachmentDescriptor* blend) holds STRONG references. After RenderStateData::Create runs EvictPipelineOwner(old blend A) and assigns `blend = [... new]`, A stays alive while bound.blend == A. The same holds for the dtor, and for VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate/dtor with bound.layout.
(2) Pipeline() (backend.mm:339-402) keys on the raw (__bridge void*)bound.blend/layout/function. On a miss it calls Insert(key, state, {vf,pf,layout,blendKey}) after the synchronous CachedPipeline compile. Nothing stops an Insert under address A after Evict(A) has already run.
(3) In fast_pipeline_cache.h, Insert records owners and Evict drops only entries that exist at that moment. An entry inserted after the eviction lives until someone evicts A again. Once A is released (bound.blend reassigned), a new descriptor at address A with the same vf/pf/layout/strides/formats gets the stale pipeline from Find().

What is NOT proven is reachability. Pipeline() has to run with bound.blend/layout still set to the evicted object:
- The engine sets context state through compare-then-dirty (video_program.cpp:154 Apply; context_bind.cpp:368 rebinds the render state only when bit 0x20 is set). A RenderState re-created in place while it is the context's current state would therefore skip the rebind.
- But no runtime caller re-creates a live RenderState: RenderState::Initialize has no callers, and PlatformCreate runs only from Serialize(read) on load or from device restore, which Metal does not get.
- The dtor-while-bound case needs a resource unloaded while it is still bound, then a draw before any rebind. The likelier route is the ext.render_pipe loader thread destroying or re-creating an owner while the render thread is between key computation and Insert. That is a timing race and needs a macOS run (or an instrumented build) to show it happens.
- The P8 model test only exercises the cache's own semantics (Evict then Insert then Find hits), which is true by construction. It does not show the backend reaching that sequence.

Side note, not this finding: VertexProgramData/PixelProgramData::PlatformCreate call shaders.clear() while bound.vs/bound.ps are raw Shader* into that vector. A re-create while bound leaves a dangling pointer, which is a stronger issue than the stale cache entry for functions.
verdict.minimal_fix: Make the cache entry keep its owners alive so their address cannot be reused while the entry exists. Store strong refs (vertex function, pixel function, layout descriptor, blend descriptor) in the cached value next to the pipeline state, e.g. struct CachedState { id<MTLRenderPipelineState> state; id<MTLFunction> vf, pf; MTLVertexDescriptor* layout; MTLRenderPipelineColorAttachmentDescriptor* blend; }. An address in a key then cannot be recycled until the entry is evicted. Keep the existing evictions so entries are freed when the owners die. The alternative is to key on a monotonically increasing id assigned at Create/PlatformCreate instead of the raw address. Add a unit case: Evict(A), then Insert(key{A}), then the entry must hold A alive (or must not match a different object).

proof_run.proof:
S-054 stays SUSPECTED. The backend's order of operations is now shown with a failing model test. The engine path that would reach that order has not been observed, and the Metal backend cannot be built or run on this Windows bed.

1) Failing model of the backend order: scratchpad/phase2/proofs/S-054/backend_order_model.cpp
- It includes the real src/render/metal/fast_pipeline_cache.h from origin/main fa150cf7f.
- It mirrors three things in backend.mm: `bound.blend` holds a strong reference, as under ARC (backend.mm:86); `~RenderStateData` evicts its blend's address while it is still bound (2139); `Pipeline()` keys on the raw bound.blend address and inserts after a miss (343/399).
- A recycling allocator plays the part of malloc handing out the freed address again.
- Sequence: bind X; destroy X (evicts A); draw before any render-state rebind (Insert under A after the evict); bind Y (A released); create Z (its descriptor lands at A); bind Z; draw.
- Output (exit 1, saved in model_run.txt): `A=00007ff6326060f8 z.blend=00007ff6326060f8 reused=1` and `z wants factor 7, pipeline compiled with factor 1 -> STALE`.
- Built with `g++ -std=c++17 -O1 -static -I <openba-review>/src/render/metal`.

So if any draw reaches Pipeline() while bound.blend or bound.layout is an owner that has already been evicted, the cache returns a pipeline with the wrong blend or layout once the address is reused.

2) The engine-side precondition is plausible but not observed. This is a static finding (not in the triage), and it is why the probe was worth running:
- Context::ClearResources (context_lifecycle.cpp:287) runs on every loop transition (mainloop_run.cpp:262 sets `_contextDirty`). It clears image and vertex buffers only, never `_renderState` or `_vertexLayout`.
- The only full Context::Reset is on BeginCommands failure (loops.cpp:1086).
- So the context can keep a pointer to a RenderState or VertexLayout destroyed by a world unload. If a new one is allocated at the same engine address, the compare-then-dirty in Apply skips the 0x20/0x4 rebind. The next draw then runs Pipeline() with the old, already-evicted bound.blend/layout, and that is exactly the Insert-after-Evict in the model.
- The skipped rebind itself is engine behaviour that retail D3D11 shares. What only Metal adds is the stale cache entry outliving the address.

3) A reachability probe was written but has not run yet.
- Temporary, never committed: src/engine/Video/s054_probe.h plus hooks in context_bind.cpp, renderstate.cpp and vertexlayout.cpp of worktree <worktree>. The patch script is scratchpad/phase2/proofs/S-054/patch_probe.py.
- It bumps a per-address generation on create and destroy, and logs `[S054] STALE` when BindResources skips a render-state or layout rebind for an object whose generation changed since it was bound. This check is shared engine code, so a DX11 run answers the reachability question for Metal too.
- Its debug build is at about 270/1602 at -j2 on a loaded machine, so the game run (gate plus BANISHED_AUTOSTART_GAMES for the game -> menu -> game transitions) has not happened.

Next step to confirm: finish that build, run it through tools/game_dirs.sh functional with BANISHED_AUTOSTART_GAMES=3, and grep standalone_error.log for `[S054] STALE`. A hit confirms engine reachability; the model test above then supplies the failing half. The ext.render_pipe loader-thread race is still unproven and needs a macOS run.
proof_run.minimal_fix: Make each cache entry keep its owners alive, so an address in a key cannot be reused while the entry exists. In backend.mm, store strong references in the cached value: struct CachedPipeline { id<MTLRenderPipelineState> state; id<MTLFunction> vf, pf; MTLVertexDescriptor* layout; MTLRenderPipelineColorAttachmentDescriptor* blend; }. Keep the existing EvictPipelineOwner calls so entries are freed when their owners die; an Insert after the evict then pins A, and A cannot be recycled until a later evict. The alternative is to key on a monotonically increasing id assigned in RenderStateData::Create, VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate and Translate, instead of the raw address. Comment: "NOT RETAIL: the Metal fast cache must not key on a recyclable address". Add a unit case built on backend_order_model.cpp: Evict(A), Insert(key{A}), release A, allocate a new owner at A, then Find must miss or return the new owner's pipeline. Separately, VertexProgramData/PixelProgramData::PlatformCreate call shaders.clear() while bound.vs/bound.ps are raw Shader* pointers into that vector. That dangling pointer is a separate, stronger issue and should get its own finding.

verdict.label: ext
verdict.severity: resource (low): log spam only after a GPU fault; no sim or save effect
verdict.proof:
Checked against origin/main fa150cf7f in <worktree>. The code is unchanged and no merged PR touches it: the only open PRs are #158 and #159, and neither changes src/render/metal.

What the code proves on its own: in src/render/metal/backend.mm:779-784, Present adds a completion handler to every frame's command buffer. That handler runs `fprintf(stderr, "[Metal] command error: %s\n", ...)` whenever `cb.error` is set. Nothing limits the line: there is no count cap, no `_DEBUG` guard and no `Opt()` gate. The readback handler at line 1775 has the same shape. A grep of src/render/metal, src/render/common and src/platform/darwin finds no device-removed handling (no MTLDeviceWasRemovedNotification and no OnVideoError route). `DeviceLive()` (line 818) is just `gpu != nil`, so it stays true after a fault.

What still needs a run: the finding says the line prints every frame, and that only holds if Metal keeps failing every later command buffer after a fault, timeout or eGPU removal. That depends on how Metal behaves at run time (the blacklisted, not-permitted and device-removed errors), so neither the code nor Ghidra can show it. A Metal backend has no retail counterpart. Until a macOS run (a forced GPU timeout or an injected failing command buffer) shows the line repeating, the spam claim stays SUSPECTED. While no errors occur, the line costs nothing. One error prints one line, which AGENTS.md section 3 allows.
verdict.minimal_fix: Put a hard cap on the stderr lines in the completion handler of backend.mm:780 (and in the readback handler at line 1775). For example, a function-local `static std::atomic<unsigned> errors` that prints the first 8 lines, then one "further errors suppressed" line, then nothing. The handlers run on a Metal completion thread, so the counter must be atomic. A device-lost route (set a flag on a removed or blacklisted error, refuse frames in BeginCommands and request a restart like DX11's OnVideoError) is a separate ext feature, not part of the minimal fix.
